> दे॒वासः॑ शृ॒णव॒न्हि क॑म् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । नः । ऊर्जे । वि । अव्ययम् । पवित्रम् । धाव । धारया ।  
> देवासः । शृणवन् । हि । कम् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सुतः अभिषुतस्त्वं नः अस्माकम् ऊर्जे अन्नाय अव्ययम् अविमयं पवित्रं धारया संपातेन वि धाव प्राप्नुहि। देवासः देवा अपि हि कं शृणवन् गमनवेलायामुत्पन्नं तव शब्द शृण्वंतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who are pressed (सुतः (*sutaḥ*)), run (धाव (*dhāva*)), that is, reach, in a stream (धारया (*dhārayā*)) the woollen (अव्ययं (*avyayaṃ*), made of sheep's wool) filter (पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)) for our food (ऊर्जे (*ūrje*)). Let the gods also hear (शृणवन् (*śṛṇavan*)) your sound that arises at the time of your going.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- सः (*saḥ*)—you who are pressed
- नः (*naḥ*)—for us
- ऊर्जे (*ūrje*)—for the gaining of food
- अव्ययं (*avyayaṃ*)—made of wool
- पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)—to the ten-fold filter
- धारया (*dhārayā*)—in the form of a stream
- विधाव (*vidhāva*)—go and join
- देवासः हि (*devāsaḥ hi*)—as for the gods
- कं (*kaṃ*)—the sound of your going to the pure vessel
- शृणवन् (*śṛṇavan*)—let them hear

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are pressed, for our gaining of food go and join, in the form of a stream, the ten-fold filter made of wool. As for the gods, let them hear the sound of your going to the pure vessel.

The divine Soma, the purifier, flows, slaying and destroying the Asuras and making his own radiances shine as before.

## Sūkta 50 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘उत्ते' इति पंचर्चं षड्विंशं सूक्तमांगिरसस्योचथ्यस्यार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रांतम्---’ उत्ते शुष्मास उचथ्यः' इति । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning उत्ते (*utte*) has five ṛks and is the twenty-sixth sūkta. Its seer is Ucathya Āṅgirasa, its metre is Gāyatrī, and its deity is Pavamāna Soma. So the Anukramaṇī says उत्ते शुष्मास उचथ्यः (*utte śuṣmāsa ucathyaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

This sūkta beginning उत्ते (*utte*) is the twenty-sixth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains five ṛks. Ucathya Āṅgirasa is the seer of this sūkta; Pavamāna Soma is the deity; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said उत्ते शुष्मासः उचथ्यः (*utte śuṣmāsaḥ ucathyaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

Sūkta 50. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 50. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 1, Varga 7. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Ucathya. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ते॒ शुष्मा॑स ईरते॒ सिंधो॑रू॒र्मेरि॑व स्व॒नः ।  
> वा॒णस्य॑ चोदया प॒विम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ते । शुष्मासः । ईरते । सिंधोः । ऊर्मेःऽइव । स्वनः ।  
> वाणस्य । चोदय । पविम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते तव शुष्मासः शुष्मा वेगाः उत् ईरते उद्गच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । सिंधोः समुद्रस्य ऊर्मेरिव यथा तरंगात् स्वनः ध्वनिरुद्गच्छति तद्वदित्यर्थः । सः त्वं वाणस्य विसृष्टस्य बाणस्य नालस्य वा वादित्रविशेषस्य पविं शब्दम् । पविः भारती ' इति वाङ्नामसु पाठात् । चोदय प्रेरय । वेगेन स्यंदमानस्त्वं विसृष्टबाणशब्दसदृशं शब्दं कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, your शुष्मासः (*śuṣmāsaḥ*), that is, your impetuous rushes, rise up. The illustration: as the sound rises from a wave of the sea, so it is meant. You, then, are to send forth the sound (पविं (*paviṃ*)) of a discharged arrow, or of a reed, or of a particular musical instrument; for "pavi" is read as a name of speech ("Pavi is Bhāratī") among the speech-names. Sāyaṇa's sense: flowing with speed, make a sound like that of a discharged arrow.

### Printed p. 132

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- सिंधोः (*siṃdhoḥ*)—of the sea
- ऊर्मेः (*ūrmeḥ*)—from the stroke of the waves
- स्वनः इव (*svanaḥ iva*)—like the sound arising
- ते (*te*)—your
- शुष्मासः (*śuṣmāsaḥ*)—the sound of the speed of the current
- उदीरते (*udīrate*)—arises and spreads
- वाणस्य (*vāṇasya*)—like the sound arising from the speed of an arrow
- पविं (*paviṃ*)—the sound of your current
- चोदय (*codaya*)—impel

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, like the sound arising from the stroke of the waves of the sea, the sound of the speed of your current arises and spreads; impel the sound of your current like the sound arising from the speed of an arrow or of a particular musical instrument.

##### English translation
Forth flow your mighty (streams), like the roar (issuing) from the ocean wave: emit your sound like that of a (rushing) arrow.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र॒स॒वे त॒ उदी॑रते ति॒स्रो वाचो॑ मख॒स्युवः॑ ।  
> यदव्य॒ एषि॒ सान॑वि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रऽसवे । ते । उत् । ईरते । तिस्रः । वाचः । मखस्युवः ।  
> यत् । अव्ये । एषि । सानवि ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते तव प्रसवे सति मखस्युवः यज्ञमिच्छतो यजमानस्य तिस्रो वाचः ऋग्यजुःसामात्मकानि त्रीणि वाक्यानि उदीरते उद्गच्छंति । कदेत्यत आह । यत् यदा सानवि व्युच्छ्रिते अव्ये अविभये पवित्रे एषि त्वं गच्छसि ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, when you come into being, the three voices (तिस्रो वाचः (*tisro vācaḥ*)), that is, the three kinds of utterance consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, of the sacrificer who desires the sacrifice rise up. When is that? He says: when you go to the raised (सानवि (*sānavi*)) sheep's-wool (अव्ये (*avye*)) filter, that is, the one free from danger.

### Printed p. 133

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- ते (*te*)—your
- प्रसवे (*prasave*)—at the time of birth
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- सानवि (*sānavi*)—placed on a raised place
- अव्ये (*avye*)—made of wool, to the ten-fold filter
- एषि (*eṣi*)—you go and join, then
- मखस्युवः (*makhasyuvaḥ*)—of the sacrificer who has resolved on the sacrifice
- तिस्रः वाचः (*tisraḥ vācaḥ*)—the voices of three kinds, in the forms of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman
- उदीरते (*udīrate*)—are recited and become manifest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, at the time of your birth, when you go and join the ten-fold filter, which is placed on a raised place and made of wool, then the voices of the sacrificer who has resolved on the sacrifice, of three kinds in the forms of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman, are recited.

##### English translation
At your birth the three voices of the worshipper are uttered when you go to the summit of the fleece.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अव्यो॒ वारे॒ परि॑ प्रि॒यं हरिं॑ हिन्वं॒त्यद्रि॑भिः ।  
> पव॑मानं मधु॒श्चुत॑म् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अव्यः । वारे । परि । प्रियम् । हरिम् । हिन्वंति । अद्रिऽभिः ।  
> पवमानम् । मधुऽश्चुतम् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्रियं देवानां प्रीतिकरं हरिं हरितवर्णम् अद्रिभिः ग्रावभिरभिषुतं मधुश्चुतं मधुनो रसस्य च्यावयितारं पवमानं सोमम् अव्यः अवेः वारे वाले परि हिन्वंति ऋत्विजः परिप्रेरयंति ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests (ṛtvij) impel (परि हिन्वंति (*pari hinvaṃti*)) Pavamāna Soma onto the hair (वारे (*vāre*)) of the sheep (अव्यः (*avyaḥ*)): Soma who is dear (प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)), that is, pleasing to the gods; green-tinted (हरिं (*hariṃ*)); pressed with the stones (अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)), that is, the pressing-stones; and honey-dropping (मधुश्चुतं (*madhuścutaṃ*)), that is, one who makes the sweet juice flow.

### Printed p. 134

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- प्रियं (*priyaṃ*)—that which is pleasing to the gods
- हरिं (*hariṃ*)—that which is green in colour
- अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)—that which is pressed with stones
- मधुश्चुतं (*madhuścutaṃ*)—that which makes the sweet juice flow
- पवमानं (*pavamānaṃ*)—and that which purifies, the Soma juice
- अव्यः (*avyaḥ*)—of the wool
- वारे (*vāre*)—in the fibres (in the ten-fold filter)
- परि हिन्वंति (*pari hinvaṃti*)—the priests pour for purification

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma juice, which is pleasing to the gods, green in colour, pressed with stones, makes the sweet juice flow and purifies, is poured by the priests, for purification, on the wool fibres of the ten-fold filter.

##### English translation
(The priests)effuse with the stones into the fleece the beloved green-tinted purifying honey-dropping (Soma).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ प॑वस्व मदिंतम प॒वित्रं॒ धार॑या कवे ।  
> अ॒र्कस्य॒ योनि॑मा॒सद॑म् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । पवस्व । मदिन्ऽतम । पवित्रम् । धारया । कवे ।  
> अर्कस्य । योनिम् । आऽसदम् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदिंतम मादयितृतम कवे क्रांतकर्मन् सोम अर्कस्य अर्चनीयस्येंद्रस्य योनिं स्थानम् आसदं प्राप्तुं पवित्रम् अतीत्य धारया संपातेन आ पवस्व आभिमुख्येन क्षर । यद्यप्येषा पूर्वस्मिन्नध्याये ( ऋ. सं. ९.२५.६ ) व्याकृता तथापि मंदमतीनां विस्मरणशंकया पुनर्व्याख्याता ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O most exhilarating (मदिंतम (*madiṃtama*)) one, O sage (कवे (*kave*)), one of far-reaching works, Soma: in order to reach (आसदं (*āsadaṃ*)) the abode (योनिं (*yoniṃ*)) of Indra, the one to be worshipped (अर्कस्य (*arkasya*)), pass beyond the filter (पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)) and flow (आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)) towards him, that is, stream forth, in a current (धारया (*dhārayā*)), that is, in a continuous fall. Although this ṛk was explained in the previous adhyāya (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9.25.6), it is explained again for fear that those of slow wit have forgotten it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदिंतम (*madiṃtama*)—O one who gives gladness in the highest degree
- कवे (*kave*)—and who is of wise works, O divine Soma
- अर्कस्य (*arkasya*)—of the worshipful Indra
- योनिं (*yoniṃ*)—the abode
- आसदं (*āsadaṃ*)—in order to go
- पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)—passing beyond the ten-fold filter
- धारयो (*dhārayo*)—in the form of a current **NOTE**
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—flow

### Printed p. 135

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, giver of gladness in the highest degree, of wise works, in order to reach the abode of the worshipful Indra (his belly), pass beyond the ten-fold filter and flow in the form of a current.

##### English translation
Most exilarating sage (Soma), flow in a stream to the filter to sit on Indra's lap.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स प॑वस्व मदिंतम॒ गोभि॑रंजा॒नो अ॒क्तुभिः॑ ।  
> इंद॒विंद्रा॑य पी॒तये॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । पवस्व । मदिन्ऽतम । गोभिः । अंजानः । अक्तुऽभिः ।  
> इंदो इति । इंद्राय । पीतये ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे मदिंतम मादयितृतम इंदो सोम अक्तुभिः अंजनसाधनभूतैः गोभिः गोविकारैः पयोभिः अंजानः अज्यमानः संस्क्रियमाणः सः त्वम् इंद्राय इंद्रस्य पीतये पानाय पवस्व

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O most exhilarating (मदिंतम (*madiṃtama*)) Indu, Soma: being anointed (अंजानः (*aṃjānaḥ*)), that is, refined, with the cows' products (गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)), that is, with milk, which are the means of anointing (अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*)), you flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)) for Indra's drinking (पीतये (*pītaye*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदिंतम (*madiṃtama*)—O most excellent giver of gladness
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- अक्तुभिः (*aktubhiḥ*)—which are like unguents
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the other admixture substances
- अंजानः (*aṃjānaḥ*)—united and well refined
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—of Indra
- वीतये (*vītaye*)—for drinking **NOTE**
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, most excellent giver of gladness, united with milk and the other admixture substances that are like unguents, and well refined, flow for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Most exhilarating Indu. being anointed with the unguents of milk and curds, flow forth for Indra's drinking.

## Sūkta 51 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘अध्वर्यो ' इति पंचर्चं सप्तविंशं सूक्तमांगिरसस्योचथ्यस्यार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रम्यते-' अध्वर्यो ' इति । गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*) has five ṛks and is the twenty-seventh sūkta. Its seer is Ucathya Āṅgirasa, its metre is Gāyatrī, and its deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*). The use of the sūkta in the rite has been stated.

This sūkta beginning अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*) is the twenty-seventh sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains five ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Ucathya, the son of Aṅgiras; Pavamāna Soma is the deity; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*). The use of the sūkta has been stated before.

Sūkta 51. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 51. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 1, Varga 8. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Uṣadhyaḥ **NOTE**. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अध्व॑र्यो॒ अद्रि॑भिः सु॒तं सोमं॑ प॒वित्र॒ आ सृ॑ज ।  
> पु॒नी॒हींद्रा॑य॒ पात॑वे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अध्वर्यो इति । अद्रिऽभिः । सुतम् । सोमम् । पवित्रे । आ । सृज ।  
> पुनीहि । इंद्राय । पातवे ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यो अद्रिभिः ग्रावभिः सुतम् अभिषुतं सोमं पवित्र आ सृज । एतदेव दर्शयति । इंद्राय इंद्रस्य पातवे पानाय पुनीहि पावय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adhvaryu, pour out the Soma pressed (सुतम् (*sutam*)) with the stones (अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)), that is, the pressing-stones, onto the filter. He shows this very thing: purify it, that is, cleanse it, for Indra's drinking (पातवे (*pātave*)).

### Printed p. 137

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अध्वर्यो (*adhvaryo*)—O Adhvaryu
- अद्रिभिः (*adribhiḥ*)—with the pressing stones
- सुतं (*sutaṃ*)—pressed
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma
- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—in the ten-fold filter
- आ सृज (*ā sṛja*)—pour for purification
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—of Indra
- पातवे (*pātave*)—for drinking
- पुनीहि (*punīhi*)—purify

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryu, pour the Soma pressed with the stones onto the ten-fold filter. Purify it for Indra's drinking.

##### English translation
Adhwaryu pour upon the filter the Soma that has been expresscd with the stones, purify it for Indra's drinking.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वः पी॒यूष॑मुत्त॒मं सोम॒मिंद्रा॑य व॒ज्रिणे॑ ।  
> सु॒नोता॒ मधु॑मत्तमम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवः । पीयूषम् । उत्ऽतमम् । सोमम् । इंद्राय । वज्रिणे ।  
> सुनोत । मधुमत्ऽतमम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अध्वर्यवः यूयं मधुमत्तमम् अतिशयेन मधुमंतं दिवः द्युलोकस्य पीयूषम् अमृतम् उत्तमं श्रेष्ठं सोमं वज्रिणे वज्रवते इंद्राय सुनोत अभिषुणुत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Adhvaryus, press (सुनोत (*sunota*)) for Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt (वज्रिणे (*vajriṇe*)), that is, the one who has the thunderbolt, the Soma that is most honeyed (मधुमत्तमम् (*madhumattamam*)), that is, possessed of sweetness in the highest degree: the ambrosia (पीयूषम् (*pīyūṣam*)), the nectar, of heaven (दिवः (*divaḥ*)), the best (उत्तमं (*uttamaṃ*)), the most excellent.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Adhvaryus)
- मधुमत्तमं (*madhumattamaṃ*)—that which is exceedingly tasty
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—in the heavenly world
- पीयूषं (*pīyūṣaṃ*)—that which is of the nature of nectar
- उत्तमं (*uttamaṃ*)—and that which is best
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—the Soma juice
- वज्रिणे (*vajriṇe*)—who bears the thunderbolt as weapon
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- सुनोत (*sunota*)—press

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Adhvaryus, press the Soma juice, which is extremely pure **NOTE** and of the nature of nectar in the heavenly world, for Indra the wielder of the thunderbolt.

### Printed p. 138

##### English translation
(Adhwaryus), effuse the most sweet-flavoured Soma, the best ambrosia of heaven for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॒ त्य इं॑दो॒ अंध॑सो दे॒वा मधो॒र्व्य॑श्नते ।  
> पव॑मानस्य म॒रुतः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । त्ये । इंदो इति । अंधसः । देवाः । मधोः । वि । अश्नते ।  
> पवमानस्य । मरुतः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम तव संबंधिनं मधोः मदकरस्य पवमानस्य पूयमानम् अंधसः अन्नम् । कर्मणि षष्ठी । त्ये त इमे देवाः इंद्रादयः मरुतः च व्यश्नते व्याप्नुवंति प्राप्नुवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma: these well-known gods, Indra and the others, and the Maruts, pervade (व्यश्नते (*vyaśnate*)), that is, obtain, your food (अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)), the purifying (पवमानस्य (*pavamānasya*)), that is, being purified, juice that is of the gladdening (मधोः (*madhoḥ*)) kind. The genitive is used in the sense of the object.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- तव (*tava*)—your
- मधोः (*madhoḥ*)—that which gives gladness
- षवमानस्य (*ṣavamānasya*)—and that which purifies **NOTE**
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—the food in the form of juice
- त्ये (*tye*)—the well-known
- देवाः (*devāḥ*)—gods, Indra and the others
- मरुतः (*marutaḥ*)—and the Maruts
- व्यक्तते (*vyaktate*)—obtain **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, the well-known gods, Indra and the others, and the Maruts, obtain your food in the form of juice, which gives gladness and purifies. (They drink it.) **NOTE**

##### English translation
Indu, tne gods and the Maruts partake of your sweet purifying beverage.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वं हि सो॑म व॒र्धय॑न्सु॒तो मदा॑य॒ भूर्ण॑ये ।  
> वृष॑न्स्तो॒तार॑मू॒तये॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वृषन् । स्तोतारम् । ऊतये ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम सुतः अभिषुतः त्वं वर्धयन् देवान प्रवृद्धान् कुर्वन् वृषन् कामान् वर्षन् भूर्णये क्षिप्राय मदाय ऊतये रक्षणाय च स्तोतारम् अभिगच्छसीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who are pressed (सुतः (*sutaḥ*)), that is, expressed, making the gods grow (वर्धयन् (*vardhayan*)), that is, causing them to increase, and showering (वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)) desires, go to the worshipper (स्तोतारम् (*stotāram*)) for swift (भूर्णये (*bhūrṇaye*)) exhilaration (मदाय (*madāya*)) and for protection (ऊतये (*ūtaye*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—pressed for the sacrifice
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- वर्धयन् (*vardhayan*)—making the gods flourish
- वृषन् (*vṛṣan*)—and being a shower of desires
- भूर्णये (*bhūrṇaye*)—arising swiftly
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for gladness
- ऊतये (*ūtaye*)—and for protection
- स्तोतारं (*stotāraṃ*)—you go to the praiser and join him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are pressed for the sacrifice, making the gods flourish and being a shower of desires, go to the praiser and join him, for the gladness that arises as soon as you are drunk and for protection.

##### English translation
For you, Soma, being effused, approach the worshipper for speedy exhilaration ane protection.

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भ्य॑र्ष विचक्षण प॒वित्रं॒ धार॑या सु॒तः ।

### Printed p. 140

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । अर्ष । विऽचक्षण । पवित्रम् । धारया । सुतः ।  
> अभि । वाजम् । उत । श्रवः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विचक्षण सोम सुतः अभिषुतस्त्वं पवित्रम् अभि प्रति धारया अर्ष गच्छ। उत अपि चास्माकं वाजम् अन्नं श्रव: कीर्तिं च अभि क्षरेत्यर्थः॥ ॥ ८ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O far-seeing (विचक्षण (*vicakṣaṇa*)) Soma, you who are pressed (सुतः (*sutaḥ*)), go (अर्ष (*arṣa*)) in a stream (धारया (*dhārayā*)) towards (अभि (*abhi*)) the filter (पवित्रम् (*pavitram*)). And also (उत (*uta*)) flow towards us food (वाजम् (*vājam*)) and fame (श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विचक्षण (*vicakṣaṇa*)—O divine Soma of subtle sight
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—you who are pressed for the sacrifice
- पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)—towards the ten-fold filter **NOTE**

- अर्ष (*arṣa*)—flow
- उत (*uta*)—and

- श्रवः (*śravaḥ*)—and fame
- अभि (*abhi*)—make them flow towards us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma of subtle sight, you who are pressed for the sacrifice, flow in the form of a current towards the ten-fold filter. Make food and fame flow towards us.

##### English translation
Hasten, sagacious (Soma), when you are effused, to the filter in a stream ; bestow upon us food and fame.

## Sūkta 52 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘परि द्युक्षः' इति पंचर्चमष्टाविंशं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । परि द्युक्षः' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning परि द्युक्षः (*pari dyukṣaḥ*) has five ṛks and is the twenty-eighth sūkta. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says परि द्युक्षः (*pari dyukṣaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

This sūkta beginning परि द्युक्षः (*pari dyukṣaḥ*) is the twenty-eighth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains five ṛks. The seer, deity and metre of this sūkta are the same as those of the previous sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said परि द्युक्षः (*pari dyukṣaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

Sūkta 52. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 52. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 1, Varga 9. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Ucathya. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

### Printed p. 141

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ द्यु॒क्षः स॒नद्र॑यि॒र्भर॒द्वाजं॑ नो॒ अंध॑सा ।  
> सु॒वा॒नो अ॑र्ष प॒वित्र॒ आ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । द्युक्षः । सनत्ऽरयिः । भरत् । वाजम् । नः । अंधसा ।  
> सुवानः । अर्ष । पवित्रे । आ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> द्युक्षः दीप्तः सनद्रयिः दीयमानधनः सोमः नः अस्माकं वाजं बलम् अंधसा अन्नेन सह  परि भरत् परिभरतु प्रयच्छतु। अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । हे सोम सुवानः अभिषूयमाणस्त्वं पवित्रे  आ अर्ष क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

May Soma, the radiant (द्युक्षः (*dyukṣaḥ*)), that is, shining, the giver of wealth (सनद्रयिः (*sanadrayiḥ*)), that is, one whose wealth is given, bring (परि भरत् (*pari bharat*)) to us strength (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)) together with food (अंधसा (*aṃdhasā*)), that is, bestow it. Now a direct address: O Soma, being pressed (सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*)), flow (अर्ष (*arṣa*)) to the filter (पवित्रे (*pavitre*)), that is, stream forth.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- द्युक्षः (*dyukṣaḥ*)—the radiant
- सनद्रयिः (*sanadrayiḥ*)—the giver of wealth, the divine Soma
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- अंधसा (*aṃdhasā*)—together with food
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—strength
- परिभरत् (*paribharat*)—may he give fully (O divine Soma)
- सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*)—you who are pressed
- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—towards the ten-fold filter
- आर्ष (*ārṣa*)—flow **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May Soma, the radiant giver of wealth, give us strength joined with food. O divine Soma, you who are pressed for the sacrifice, flow towards the ten-fold filter for purification.

##### English translation
May glittering (Soma), the acquirer of wealth, bestow upon us strength together with food; hasten, when effused to the filter.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॑ प्र॒त्नेभि॒रध्व॑भि॒रव्यो॒ वारे॒ परि॑ प्रि॒यः ।  
> स॒हस्र॑धारो या॒त्तना॑ ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 142

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । प्रत्नेभिः । अध्वऽभिः । अव्यः । वारे । परि । प्रियः ।  
> सहस्रऽधारः । यात् । तना ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम तव संबंधी प्रियः देवानां प्रीतिकरः सहस्रधारः बहुधारः तना विस्तृतसारो रसः प्रत्नेभिः पुराणैः अध्वभिः मार्गैः अव्यः अवेः वारे वाले दशापवित्रे परि यात् परिगच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, your juice, which is dear (प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)), that is, pleasing to the gods, thousand-streamed (सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*)), that is, of many streams, and of widely spread essence (तना (*tanā*)), goes (परि यात् (*pari yāt*)) round by the ancient (प्रत्नेभिः (*pratnebhiḥ*)), old paths (अध्वभिः (*adhvabhiḥ*)) to the hair (वारे (*vāre*)) of the sheep (अव्यः (*avyaḥ*)), the ten-fold filter.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- प्रियः (*priyaḥ*)—that which is pleasing to the gods
- सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*)—that which has a thousand streams
- तना (*tanā*)—and that which spreads widely
- तव (*tava*)—your juice
- प्रत्नेभिः (*pratnebhiḥ*)—by ancient
- अध्वभिः (*adhvabhiḥ*)—paths
- अव्यः (*avyaḥ*)—made of wool
- वारे (*vāre*)—in the meshes of the ten-fold filter
- परि यात् (*pari yāt*)—goes and joins for purification

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, your juice, which is pleasing to the gods, has a thousand streams and spreads widely, goes by ancient paths into the woollen meshes of the ten-fold filter for purification.

##### English translation
Your juice dear (to the gods), flowing in a thousand streams, proceeds by ancient paths to the fleecy filter.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> च॒रुर्न यस्तमीं॑ख॒येंदो॒ न दान॑मींखय ।  
> व॒धैर्व॑धस्नवींखय ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चरुः । न । यः । तम् । ईंखय । इंदो इति । न । दानम् । ईंखय ।  
> वधैः । वधस्नो इति वधऽस्नो । ईंखय ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 143

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम चरुर्न चरुरिव यः पूर्णोदनो भवति तमींखय अस्मान् प्रापय । अपि च हे इंदो न इदानीं दानं देयम् ईंखय । हे वधस्नो प्रहारेण प्रस्रवणशील सोम वधैः ग्राव्णां प्रहारैः ईंखय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, send to us (ईंखय (*īṃkhaya*)), that is, make us reach, the one who is like a cooked-rice offering (चरुर्न (*carurna*)), namely the one who is full of boiled rice. And further, O Indu, now send (ईंखय (*īṃkhaya*)) the gift (दानं (*dānaṃ*)), that which is fit to be given. O Soma (वधस्नो (*vadhasno*)), you who are by nature streaming forth through a blow, send it with blows (वधैः (*vadhaiḥ*)), that is, with the strokes of the pressing-stones.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- चरुः न (*caruḥ na*)—like the cooked-rice offering made in the sacrifice
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which is full of food
- तं (*taṃ*)—that vessel of food
- ईंखिय (*īṃkhiya*)—send to us **NOTE**
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- न (*na*)—now
- दानं (*dānaṃ*)—that which is fit to be given to us
- ईंखिय (*īṃkhiya*)—send and give
- वधस्नो (*vadhasno*)—O divine Soma, whose nature is to stream forth through the blows of the stones
- वध्यैः (*vadhyaiḥ*)—that which is born of the blows of those same pressing-stones **NOTE**
- ईंखिय (*īṃkhiya*)—send to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, like the cooked-rice offering made in the sacrifice, send to us that vessel which is full of food. O divine Soma, send us right now that which is fit to be given to us. O divine Soma, whose nature is to stream forth as the result of the blows of the stones, send to us what is born of the blows of those same pressing-stones.

##### English translation
(Soma), send (us) him who is like a pot; Indu, send us now wealth; swift-flowing (Soma), send it with blows (of the stones).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नि शुष्म॑मिंदवेषां॒ पुरु॑हूत॒ जना॑नाम् ।  
> यो अ॒स्माँ आ॒दिदे॑शति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नि । शुष्मम् । इंदो इति । एषाम् । पुरुऽहूत । जनानाम् ।  
> यः । अस्मान् । आऽदिदेशति ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 144

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूत इंदो सोम त्वं यः शुष्मो येषां शत्रुजनानां बलम् अस्मान् आदिदेशति बाधार्थमाह्वयति एषां शत्रुजनानां तं शुष्मं बलं नि न्यक् कुर्विति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, invoked of many (पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)), that is, called by many: whatever strength (शुष्मो (*śuṣmo*)) of those enemy people summons us (आदिदेशति (*ādideśati*)) in order to harm us, that strength (शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*)) of these enemy people, bring down (नि (*ni*)): the word "bring down" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुहूत (*puruhūta*)—worthy of the invocation of many
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever enemy's strength
- अस्मान् (*asmān*)—us
- आदिदेशति (*ādideśati*)—harms
- एषां जनानां (*eṣāṃ janānāṃ*)—of those enemy people
- शुष्मं (*śuṣmaṃ*)—the strength
- नि (*ni*)—destroy completely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, worthy of the invocation of many, whichever enemy's strength harms us, destroy completely the strength of those enemy people.

##### English translation
Indu, the invoked of many, overthrow the strength of those people who challenge us.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तं न॑ इंद ऊ॒तिभिः॑ स॒हस्रं॑ वा॒ शुची॑नाम् ।  
> पव॑स्व मंह॒यद्र॑यिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतम् । नः । इंदो इति । ऊतिऽभिः । सहस्रम् । वा । शुचीनाम् ।  
> पवस्व । मंहयत्ऽरयिः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम मंहयद्रयिः प्रदीयमानधनस्त्वं नः अस्माकम् ऊतिभिः ऊतिभ्यः । विभक्तिव्यत्ययः । रक्षार्थं शुचीनां शुद्धानां तव अंशभूतानां सोमानां शतं सहस्रं वा पवस्व क्षर ॥ ॥ ९ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, you who give wealth (मंहयद्रयिः (*maṃhayadrayiḥ*)), that is, one whose wealth is bestowed, flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)), that is, stream forth, for our protection (ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*): the instrumental stands for the dative), a hundred or a thousand (शतं सहस्रं वा (*śataṃ sahasraṃ vā*)) of your pure (शुचीनां (*śucīnāṃ*)), that is, clean, Somas that are parts of you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- मंहयद्रयिः (*maṃhayadrayiḥ*)—you who give wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- ऊतिभिः (*ūtibhiḥ*)—for protection
- शुचीनां (*śucīnāṃ*)—of the thoroughly pure juices
- शतं सहस्रं वा (*śataṃ sahasraṃ vā*)—together with streams of many numbers
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who give wealth, for our protection make your thoroughly pure juices, of many streams, flow.

##### English translation
Indu, do you who are the distributor of riches, pour forth for our protection a hundred or a thousand of your pure (streams.)

## Sūkta 53 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘उत्ते' इति चतुर्ऋचमेकोनत्रिंशं सूक्तं काश्यपस्यावत्सारस्यार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । तथा चानुकांतम्-- उत्ते चतुष्कमवत्सारः' इति । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning उत्ते (*utte*) has four ṛks and is the twenty-ninth sūkta. Its seer is Avatsāra Kāśyapa, its metre is Gāyatrī, and its deity is Pavamāna Soma. So the Anukramaṇī says उत्ते चतुष्कमवत्सारः (*utte catuṣkamavatsāraḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

This sūkta beginning उत्ते (*utte*) is the twenty-ninth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains four ṛks. Avatsāra, the son of the sage Kaśyapa, is the seer of this sūkta; Pavamāna Soma is the deity; the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said उत्ते चतुष्कमवत्सारः (*utte catuṣkamavatsāraḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

Sūkta 53. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 2, Sūkta 53. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 1, Varga 10. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Seer: Avatsāra. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

### Printed p. 146

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उत्ते॒ शुष्मा॑सो अस्थू॒ रक्षो॑ भिं॒दंतो॑ अद्रिवः ।  
> नु॒दस्व॒ याः प॑रि॒स्पृधः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत् । ते । शुष्मासः । अस्थुः । रक्षः । भिंदंतः । अद्रिऽवः ।  
> नुदस्व । याः । परिऽस्पृधः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे अद्रिवः ग्राववन् सोम ते तव शुष्मासः शुष्मा वेगाः रक्षः राक्षसान् भिंदंतः विदारयंतः उत अस्थुः उत्तिष्ठंति । याः स्पृधः स्पर्धमानाः शत्रुसेना अस्मान् प्रतिबाधंते तास्त्वं नुदस्व प्रेरय । बाधस्वेत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who are armed with stones (अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)), your rushes (शुष्मासः (*śuṣmāsaḥ*)), that is, your impetuous movements, rise up (अस्थुः (*asthuḥ*)), splitting (भिंदंतः (*bhiṃdaṃtaḥ*)), that is, tearing apart, the Rākṣasas (रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)). Drive away (नुदस्व (*nudasva*)), that is, impel, crush, those contending (स्पृधः (*spṛdhaḥ*)) enemy armies that press upon us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अद्रिवः (*adrivaḥ*)—O divine Soma, joined with the stones
- ते (*te*)—your
- शुष्मासः (*śuṣmāsaḥ*)—mighty powers
- रक्षः (*rakṣaḥ*)—the Rākṣasas
- भिंदंतः (*bhiṃdaṃtaḥ*)—destroying
- उदस्थुः (*udasthuḥ*)—become manifest
- परिस्पृधः (*parispṛdhaḥ*)—that fall upon us
- याः (*yāḥ*)—whatever enemy armies there are, all of them
- नुदस्व (*nudasva*)—drive far away

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, joined with the stones, your mighty powers become manifest, destroying the Rākṣasas. Drive far away all the enemy armies that fall upon us.

##### English translation
(Soma) armed with the stones, your powerful ( streams ) rise up scattering the Rakshasas; drive away those who are our adversaries.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒या नि॑ज॒घ्निरोज॑सा रथसं॒गे धने॑ हि॒ते ।  
> स्तवा॒ अबि॑भ्युषा हृ॒दा ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 147

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अया । निऽजघ्निः । ओजसा । रथऽसंगे । धने । हिते ।  
> स्तवै । अबिभ्युषा । हृदा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वम् अया अनेन कृतेन ओजसा बलेन निजघ्निः शत्रून् हंतुं शीलवान् । तं त्वाम् अबिभ्युषा अभीतेन हृदा मनसा युक्तोऽहं रथसंगे अस्माकं रथानां संगे हिते शत्रुषु निहिते धने च निमित्ते स्तवै स्तौमि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are by nature a slayer (निजघ्निः (*nijaghniḥ*)) of enemies, through this (अया (*ayā*)) strength (ओजसा (*ojasā*)) that has been produced. I, joined with a fearless (अबिभ्युषा (*abibhyuṣā*)) heart (हृदा (*hṛdā*)), that is, mind, praise you (स्तवै (*stavai*)) in the meeting of our chariots (रथसंगे (*rathasaṃge*)), and for the sake of the wealth (धने (*dhane*)) that is lodged (हिते (*hite*)) among the enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- आया (*āyā*)—in this way manifested **NOTE**
- ओजसा (*ojasā*)—by strength
- निजघ्निः (*nijaghniḥ*)—you are the destroyer of enemies
- अभिभ्युषा (*abhibhyuṣā*)—fearless **NOTE**
- हृदा (*hṛdā*)—I, joined with a heart (with devotion)
- रथसंगे (*rathasaṃge*)—for the protection of the lines of our chariots
- हिते (*hite*)—lodged among the enemies
- धने (*dhane*)—and for the sake of wealth
- स्तवै (*stavai*)—I praise you

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, by the strength manifested as described above, you are the destroyer of enemies. I, joined with fearless devotion, praise you for the protection of our chariots and for the gain of the wealth lodged among the enemies.

##### English translation
(You are), by this strength the discomfiter (of foes): I praise you with a fearless heart for the sake of (our) line of chariots ranged ( against the foe ) and for the sake of wealth.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस्य॑ व्र॒तानि॒ नाधृषे॒ पव॑मानस्य दू॒ढ्या॑ ।  
> रु॒ज यस्त्वा॑ पृत॒न्यति॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्य । व्रतानि । न । आऽधृषे । पवमानस्य । दुःऽध्या ।  
> रुज । यः । त्वा । पृतन्यति ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 148

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम पवमानस्य क्षरतो यस्य अस्य तव व्रतानि कर्माणि दूढ्या दुर्बुद्धिना राक्षसेन नाधृषे आधर्षयितुमशक्यानि स त्वं त्वां यः दुर्बुद्धिः शत्रुः पृतन्यति योद्भुमिच्छति तं रुज बाधस्व॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who flow (पवमानस्य (*pavamānasya*)), whose works (व्रतानि (*vratāni*)) cannot be assailed (नाधृषे (*nādhṛṣe*)), that is, cannot be overpowered, by an evil-minded (दूढ्या (*dūḍhyā*)) Rākṣasa: shatter (रुज (*ruja*)), that is, crush, the evil-minded enemy who wishes to fight (पृतन्यति (*pṛtanyati*)) you.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma)
- पवमानस्य (*pavamānasya*)—of you who are of the nature of a pure current
- अस्य (*asya*)—your
- व्रतानि (*vratāni*)—works
- दूढ्या (*dūḍhyā*)—by an Asura of evil mind
- नाधृषे (*nādhṛṣe*)—are impossible to bear
- यः (*yaḥ*)—whichever evil-minded enemy
- त्वा (*tvā*)—with you
- पृतन्यति (*pṛtanyati*)—wishes to fight, him
- रुज (*ruja*)—harm and destroy

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, the works of you, who are joined with a pure current, an evil-minded Asura cannot withstand. Harm and destroy whichever evil-minded enemy wishes to fight with you.

##### English translation
The prowess of you (Soma) as you are poured forth is irresistible against the malignant (Rakshasa) : destroy him who defies you to battle.

> इंदुम् । इंद्राय । मत्सरम् ॥ ४ ॥

> मदच्युतं मदस्य च्यावयितारं हरिं हरितवर्णं वाजिनं बलिनं मत्सरं मदकरं तम् इंदुं सोमं नदीषु वसतीवरीषु इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं हिन्वंति ऋत्विजः प्रेरयंति ॥ ॥ १० ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests (ṛtvij) impel (हिन्वंति (*hinvaṃti*)) for Indra (इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)) that Indu, Soma, among the rivers (नदीषु (*nadīṣu*)), that is, the waters called vasatīvarī: the one who makes the exhilaration flow (मदच्युतं (*madacyutaṃ*)), green-tinted (हरिं (*hariṃ*)), strong (वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)), and gladdening (मत्सरं (*matsaraṃ*)).

- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—that which is full of strength

## Sūkta 54 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य प्रत्नाम्' इति चतुर्ऋचं त्रिंशं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । ‘ अस्य प्रत्नाम्' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning अस्य प्रत्नाम् (*asya pratnām*) has four ṛks and is the thirtieth sūkta. The seer and the rest are as before. So the Anukramaṇī says अस्य प्रत्नाम् (*asya pratnām*). The use in the rite has been stated.

### Printed p. 150

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒स्य प्र॒त्नामनु॒ द्युतं॑ शु॒क्रं दु॑दुह्रे॒ अह्र॑यः ।  
> पयः॑ सहस्र॒सामृषि॑म् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अस्य । प्रत्नाम् । अनु । द्युतम् । शुक्रम् । दुदुह्रे । अह्रयः ।  
> पयः । सहस्रऽसाम् । ऋषिम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अस्य सोमस्य प्रत्नां पुराणां द्युतं द्योतमानां तनुम् अनु शुक्रं दीप्तं सहस्रसाम् अभिलषितस्यापरिमितस्य दातारम् ऋषिम् अतींद्रियस्य कर्मफलस्य द्रष्टारं पयः पातव्यं रसम् अह्रयः कवयः दुदुहे दुहंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of this Soma, towards his ancient, shining body, the poets (kavis) milk the bright, radiant juice, the drink to be drunk, which gives without measure what is desired and is the seer (ṛṣi), the beholder of the fruit of rites beyond the senses.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Soma-deva
- प्रश्नां (*praśnāṃ*)—ancient **NOTE**
- द्युतं (*dyutaṃ*)—shining; from the body that is both
- अनुशुक्रं (*anuśukraṃ*)—radiant
- सहस्रसां (*sahasrasāṃ*)—giver of unlimited desired objects
- ऋषिं (*ṛṣiṃ*)—having vision of things beyond the senses
- पयः (*payaḥ*)—fit for drinking; the juice
- अह्रयुः (*ahrayuḥ*)—the poets
- मधुहे (*madhuhe*)—they milk **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the ancient, shining body of this Soma-deva the poets milk the juice that is radiant, that gives unlimited desired objects, that has vision of things beyond the senses and that is fit for drinking.

##### English translation
Towards Soma's ancient body the seers milk the flashing fluid, the sage who grants a thousand boons,

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं सूर्य॑ इवोप॒दृग॒यं सरां॑सि धावति ।  
> स॒प्त प्र॒वत॒ आ दिव॑म् ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 151

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयम् । सूर्यःऽइव । उपऽदृक् । अयम् । सरांसि । धावति ।  
> सप्त । प्रऽवतः । आ । दिवम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सोमः सूर्यइव यथा सूर्यः सर्वस्य लोकस्योपद्रष्टा तद्वत् कर्मणाम् उपदृक् उपद्रष्टा । अपि च अयं सोमः सरांसि । त्रिंशदुक्थपात्राणीति केचिद्वर्णयंति । अपरे तु त्रिंशदहोरात्राणि सरांसीति । तानि धावति गच्छति । तथा च यास्कः-’ तत्रैतद्याज्ञिका वेदयंते त्रिंशदुक्थपात्राणि माध्यंदिने सवन एकदेवतानि तान्येतस्मिन्काल एकेन प्रतिधानेन पिबंति तान्यत्र सरांस्युच्यंते । त्रिंशदपरपक्षस्याहोरात्रास्त्रिंशत्पूर्वपक्षस्येति नैरुक्ताः' (निरु. ५ . ११ ) इति । अपि चायं सोमः दिवम् अधिकृत्य सप्त प्रवतः सप्त नदीः आ तिष्ठति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma is like the sun: as the sun is the overseer of the whole world, so he is the overseer of rites. Further, this Soma runs to the "lakes" (sarāṃsi). Some explain these as the thirty uktha vessels, others as the thirty days and nights. Yāska accordingly says (Ni. 5.11): the performers of sacrifice hold that there are thirty uktha vessels at the midday pressing, all with one deity, which at that time are drunk with a single pratidhāna, and these are here called lakes; the etymologists (Nairuktas) say that they are the thirty days and nights of the dark fortnight and the thirty of the bright fortnight. Moreover this Soma, turning to heaven, goes to the seven flowing rivers.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Soma-deva
- सूर्य इव (*sūrya iva*)—like the sun, the eye of the world
- उपदृक् (*upadṛk*)—is one who has the power to see everything
- अयं (*ayaṃ*)—this Soma-deva
- सरांसि (*sarāṃsi*)—the lakes in the form of the vessels
- धावति (*dhāvati*)—he enters swiftly
- दिवं (*divaṃ*)—facing the sky
- प्रवतः (*pravataḥ*)—flowing
- सप्त (*sapta*)—the seven rivers
- आ (तिष्ठति) (*ā (tiṣṭhati)*)—goes and joins

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like the sun, the eye of the world, this Soma-deva has the power to see everything. This Soma-deva goes and joins the vessels that are like lakes. He goes and joins the seven rivers that flow towards the sky.

##### English translation
He like the sun is the supervisor (of all acts) : he hastens to the lakes, he unites with the seven down-descending rivers from heaven.

> सोमः । दिवः । न । सूर्यः ॥ ३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, being purified, stands above all the worlds. He gives the illustration: like the divine sun. As the sun, a god, stands above all the worlds, so does this Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुनान' (*punāna '*)—the purifier

- उपरि (*upari*)—in the highest region
- तिष्ठति (*tiṣṭhati*)—he stands

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The purified Soma, like the divine sun, abides above all regions. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 55 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यवंयवं नः' इति चतुर्ऋचमेकत्रिंशं सूक्तं काश्यपस्यावत्सारस्यार्षं गायत्रं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । ‘यवंयवम्' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning यवंयवं (*yavaṃyavaṃ*) has four ṛks and is the thirty-first sūkta. Its seer is Avatsāra, of the Kāśyapa line; its metre is Gāyatra and its deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says यवंयवं (*yavaṃyavaṃ*). The use in the rite has already been stated.

Translation: This sūkta beginning यवंयवं (*yavaṃyavaṃ*) is the thirty-first sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains four ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is one called Kāśyapa Avatsāra; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Gāyatrī. The Anukramaṇī says यवंयवं (*yavaṃyavaṃ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

Sūkta 55. Maṇḍala 9. Anuvāka 2. Sūkta 55. Aṣṭaka 7. Adhyāya 1. Varga 12. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Seer: Avatsāra. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

### Printed p. 154

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यवं॑यवं नो॒ अंध॑सा पु॒ष्टंपु॑ष्टं॒ परि॑ स्रव ।  
> सोम॒ विश्वा॑ च॒ सौभ॑गा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यवम्ऽयवम् । नः । अंधसा । पुष्टम्ऽपुष्टम् । परि । स्रव ।  
> सोम । विश्वा । च । सौभगा ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वं नः अस्माकं पुष्टंपुष्टं बहुलं यवंयवं पुनःपुनर्युतं रसम् अंधसा अन्नात्मना परि स्रव धारया क्षर ॥ अत्र प्रार्थयितुस्तृष्णयात्यंतं पीडितत्वात्  आबाधे च ' (पा. सू. ८.१.१०) इति द्विर्भावः । पीडा प्रयोक्तृधर्मो नाभिधेयधर्म इत्युक्तम् ॥ अपि च विश्वा विश्वानि सौभगा सौभगानि धनानि परि स्रव ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, flow for us, in the form of food, the abundant, again and again gathered juice; let it stream in a flow. Here the doubling (of यवं (*yavaṃ*) and पुष्टं (*puṣṭaṃ*)) is by the rule "also in the sense of distress" (Pā. Sū. 8.1.10), because the petitioner is greatly afflicted by thirst; the affliction belongs to the one who uses the word, not to what is denoted, as has been said. Further, flow all the good fortunes, that is, the riches.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- पुष्टंपुष्टं (*puṣṭaṃpuṣṭaṃ*)—exceedingly abundant
- यवं (*yavaṃ*)—**NOTE**
- यवं (*yavaṃ*)—the juice that has been gathered many times
- अंधसा (*aṃdhasā*)—in the form of food
- परिस्रव (*parisrava*)—cause to flow
- विश्वा च (*viśvā ca*)—all
- सौभगा (*saubhagā*)—blessings; provide them as well

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, cause the exceedingly abundant juice that has been gathered many times to flow for us in the form of food. Provide all blessings as well.

##### English translation
Soma, pour forth (in a stream of) food, abundant oft-collected (juice), and all good things

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंदो॒ यथा॒ तव॒ स्तवो॒ यथा॑ ते जा॒तमंध॑सः ।  
> नि ब॒र्हिषि॑ प्रि॒ये स॑दः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंदो इति । यथा । तव । स्तवः । यथा । ते । जातम् । अंधसः ।  
> नि । बर्हिषि । प्रिये । सदः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम अंधसः अन्नरूपस्य तव संबंधी स्तवः स्तवनं स्तोत्रं तथा ते तव जातं जन्म यथा प्रादुर्भूतमस्ति तथा त्वं प्रिये प्रीणयितरि बर्हिषि अस्मद्यागे नि षदः निषण्णो भव॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, as the praise (stava) of you, who are of the nature of food, and your birth have come about, so do you sit down on our sacrifice's grass (barhis) that gives you pleasure.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—who are in the form of food
- तव (*tava*)—addressed to you
- स्तवः (*stavaḥ*)—the praise
- ते (*te*)—your
- जातं (*jātaṃ*)—manifestation
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever manner they are accomplished at one and the same time, so
- प्रिये (*priye*)—that gives you pleasure
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—on the seat of darbha grass
- नि षदः (*ni ṣadaḥ*)—sit down

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, in whatever manner the praise addressed to you, who are in the form of food, and your manifestation are accomplished at one and the same time, in that manner sit down on the seat of darbha grass that gives you pleasure.

##### English translation
Indu, since the praise of you as food, since your birth (has appeared), sit down upon the grass that pleases (you).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त नो॑ गो॒विद॑श्व॒वित्पव॑स्व सो॒मांध॑सा ।  
> म॒क्षूत॑मेभि॒रह॑भिः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । नः । गोऽवित् । अश्वऽवित् । पवस्व । सोम । अंधसा ।  
> मक्षुऽतमेभिः । अहऽभिः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 157

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत अपि च हे सोम नः अस्माकं गोवित् गोप्रदः अश्ववित् अश्वप्रदश्च त्वं मक्षूतमेभिः मक्षुतमैरतिशयेन शीघ्रैः अहभिः अहोभिर्हेतुभिः अंधसा अन्नेन पवस्व धारया क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And, O Soma, you who give cows and give horses to us, flow with food in a stream, by reason of the exceedingly swift days.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- उत (*uta*)—and
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- गोवित् (*govit*)—you who give cows
- अश्ववित् (*aśvavit*)—and who give horses
- मक्षूतमेभिः (*makṣūtamebhiḥ*)—swiftly going
- अहभिः (*ahabhiḥ*)—on account of the days
- अंधसा (*aṃdhasā*)—in the form of food
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow in the form of a stream

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who give us cows and give horses, flow in the form of a stream on account of those swift-moving oblations. **NOTE**

##### English translation
And Soma, do you who are the giver of cattle, the giver of horses, flow to us in (a stream of) food as the days quickly pass.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यो जि॒नाति॒ न जीय॑ते॒ हंति॒ शत्रु॑म॒भीत्य॑ ।  
> स प॑वस्व सहस्रजित् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यः । जिनाति । न । जीयते । हंति । शत्रुम् । अभिऽइत्य ।  
> सः । पवस्व । सहस्रऽजित् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सहस्रजित् असंख्यानां शत्रूणां जेतः सोम यः भवान् जिनाति शत्रून् हंति न जीयते स्वयं शत्रुभिर्न जीयते । न हन्यत इत्यर्थः । शत्रुमभीत्य शत्रुं स्वयमभ्येत्य हंति न च स्वयं शत्रुभिरभिभूयते सः त्वं पवस्व क्षर ॥ ॥ १२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, conqueror of thousands, that is, of countless enemies, you who conquer, slay enemies and are not yourself conquered by enemies, that is, are not slain; who come upon the enemy yourself and slay him and are not overcome by enemies: such as you flow.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सहस्रजित् (*sahasrajit*)—O Soma who conquer countless enemies
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who
- जिनाति (*jināti*)—conquer enemies
- न जीयते (*na jīyate*)—but are not conquered by any enemies
- शत्रुमभीत्य (*śatrumabhītya*)—fall upon the enemies
- हंति (*haṃti*)—and slay
- सः (*saḥ*)—such a you
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow in the form of a stream

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, conqueror of countless enemies, you who conquer enemies, are not conquered by any enemies, and fall upon enemies and slay them: such as you flow in the form of a stream.

##### English translation
Flow forth, O conqueror of thousands, who conquers but is not conquered, and attacking slays his foe.

## Sūkta 56 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘परि सोमः' इति चतुर्ऋचं द्वात्रिंशं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । परि सोमः' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning परि सोमः (*pari somaḥ*) has four ṛks and is the thirty-second sūkta. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says परि सोमः (*pari somaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

### Printed p. 158

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ सोम॑ ऋ॒तं बृ॒हदा॒शुः प॒वित्रे॑ अर्षति ।  
> वि॒घ्नन्रक्षां॑सि देव॒युः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । सोमः । ऋतम् । बृहत् । आशुः । पवित्रे । अर्षति ।  
> विऽघ्नन् । रक्षांसि । देवऽयुः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> आशुः क्षिप्रकारी देवयुः देवकामः सोमः पवित्रे स्थित्वा रक्षांसि राक्षसान् विघ्नन् निघ्नन् बृहत् महत् ऋतम् अन्नं परि अर्षति परिगमयति । अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, swift (āśu, quick in action) and desiring the gods, standing in the filter, destroys the Rākṣasas and brings around abundant, great food (ṛta, that is, annaṃ); the sense is that he gives it to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- आशुः (*āśuḥ*)—swift-going
- देवयुः (*devayuḥ*)—and desiring to satisfy the gods
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—while he is in the ten-fold filter
- रक्षांसि (*rakṣāṃsi*)—the Rākṣasas
- विघ्नन् (*vighnan*)—destroying
- बृहत् (*bṛhat*)—abundant
- ऋतं (*ṛtaṃ*)—food
- पर्यर्षति (*paryarṣati*)—he provides around us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, who goes swiftly and desires to satisfy the gods, while he is in the ten-fold filter destroys the Rākṣasas and provides abundant food all around us.

##### English translation
The switt Soma devoted to the gods destroying the Rakshasas in the filter bestows abundant food (on us).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> यत्सोमो॒ वाज॒मर्ष॑ति श॒तं धारा॑ अप॒स्युवः॑ ।  
> इंद्र॑स्य स॒ख्यमा॑वि॒शन् ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 159

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> यत् । सोमः । वाजम् । अर्षति । शतम् । धाराः । अपस्युवः ।  
> इंद्रस्य । सख्यम् । आऽविशन् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत् यदा अपस्युवः कर्मकामाः शतं शतसंख्याकाः धाराः सोमस्य धाराः इंद्रस्य सख्यं सखित्वम् आविशन् प्राप्नुवंति तदा सोमः वाजम् अन्नम् अर्षति गमयति । अस्मभ्यं प्रयच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When the hundred streams of Soma, desiring the rite (apasyu), attain the friendship of Indra, then Soma brings food; the sense is that he gives it to us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत् (*yat*)—when
- अपस्युवः (*apasyuvaḥ*)—desiring the sacrificial rite
- शतं (*śataṃ*)—being a hundred in number
- धाराः (*dhārāḥ*)—the streams of the Soma juice
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- सख्यं (*sakhyaṃ*)—the friendship
- आविशन् (*āviśan*)—attain, then
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- अर्षति (*arṣati*)—provides to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

When the hundred streams of Soma juice, which desire the sacrificial rite, attain the friendship of Indra, then Soma-deva provides food for all of us.

##### English translation
When the hundred rite-loving streams (of the Soma) obtain the the friendship of Indra, then the Soma brings us food.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒भि त्वा॒ योष॑णो॒ दश॑ जा॒रं न क॒न्या॑नूषत ।  
> मृ॒ज्यसे॑ सोम सा॒तये॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अभि । त्वा । योषणः । दश । जारम् । न । कन्या । अनूषत ।  
> मृज्यसे । सोम । सातये ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 160

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम त्वा त्वां याः दश दशसंख्याकाः योषणः अंगुलयः कन्या पितृमती कन्यका जारं न यथा प्रियमभिशब्दायते तद्वत् अभि अनूषत अभिशब्दायंते ताभिः सातये अस्माकं धनस्य लाभाय मृज्यसे इंद्रार्थं शोध्यसे ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, the ten women (yoṣaṇaḥ), that is, the ten fingers, call out to you as a maiden (kanyā, a girl who has a father) calls out to her lover (jāra) with a sound of love; with them, for the winning (sātaye) of wealth for us, you are cleansed for Indra.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- कन्या (*kanyā*)—as a young girl
- जारं न (*jāraṃ na*)—calls her lover with a loving sound
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- दश योषणः (*daśa yoṣaṇaḥ*)—the ten fingers
- अभ्यनूषत (*abhyanūṣata*)—which honour with a sound; joined with them
- सातये (*sātaye*)—for the gain of our wealth
- मृज्यसे (*mṛjyase*)—you receive purification

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, as a young girl calls her lover with a loving sound, so the ten fingers honour you with a sound (squeeze you); joined with them, for the gain of our wealth, you receive purification.

##### English translation
The ten fingers commend you, Soma, as a maiden her lover, you are cleansed in order to bestow (wealth on us).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> त्वमिंद्रा॑य॒ विष्ण॑वे स्वा॒दुरिं॑दो॒ परि॑ स्रव ।  
> नॄन्स्तो॒तॄन्पा॒ह्यंह॑सः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> त्वम् । इंद्राय । विष्णवे । स्वादुः । इंदो इति । परि । स्रव ।  
> नॄन् । स्तोतॄन् । पाहि । अंहसः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम स्वादुः प्रियरसस्त्वम् इंद्राय इंद्रार्थं विष्णवे विष्ण्वर्थं च परि स्रव परिक्षर । नॄन् कर्मणां नेतॄन स्तोतॄन् त्वद्विषयाणां स्तुतीनां कर्तॄन् अंहसः दुरितात् पाहि रक्ष च ॥ ॥ १३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, sweet, of pleasant juice, flow all around for Indra and for Viṣṇu. Protect from sin the leaders of the rites (nṛ) and the praisers who make praises addressed to you.

### Printed p. 161

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- स्वादुः (*svāduḥ*)—having a tasty juice
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra
- विष्णुवे (*viṣṇuve*)—and for Viṣṇu
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow in the form of a stream
- नृन् (*nṛn*)—the sacrificers, leaders of the rites
- स्तोत्थान् (*stotthān*)—and the praisers
- अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)—from sin
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—protect

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you of tasty juice, flow in the form of a stream for Indra and for Viṣṇu. Protect from sin the sacrificers who lead the rites and the praisers.

##### English translation
Do you, Indu, who are sweet-flavoured flow for Indra and Vishnu, preserve the worshippers, your praisers from sin.

## Sūkta 57 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘प्र ते धाराः' इति चतुर्ऋचं त्रयस्त्रिंशं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । ‘प्र ते धाराः ' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्र ते धाराः (*pra te dhārāḥ*) has four ṛks and is the thirty-third sūkta. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says प्र ते धाराः (*pra te dhārāḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

Translation: This sūkta beginning प्र ते धाराः (*pra te dhārāḥ*) is the thirty-third sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains four ṛks. The seer, deity and metre of this sūkta are the same as in the preceding sūkta. The Anukramaṇī says प्र ते धाराः (*pra te dhārāḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

Sūkta 57. Maṇḍala 9. Anuvāka 2. Sūkta 57. Aṣṭaka 7. Adhyāya 1. Varga 14. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Seer: Avatsāra. Deity: Pavamāna Soma.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र ते॒ धारा॑ अस॒श्चतो॑ दि॒वो न यं॑ति वृ॒ष्टयः॑ ।  
> अच्छा॒ वाजं॑ सह॒स्रिण॑म् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

### Printed p. 162

> प्र । ते । धाराः । असश्चतः । दिवः । न । यंति । वृष्टयः ।  
> अच्छ । वाजम् । सहस्रिणम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम ते तव असश्चतः संगरहिताः धाराः सहस्रिणम् अपरिमितसंख्याकं वाजम् अन्नम् अच्छ अस्मदर्थं प्र यंति प्रगच्छंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । दिवो न वृष्टयः । यथा द्युलोकात् वर्षधारा निःसंगाः प्रजानामपरिमितमन्नं प्रयच्छंति तद्वदित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, your unobstructed (asaścataḥ, unattached) streams go forth towards us, towards a thousandfold, that is, countless, food. The illustration: like the rains from heaven. As the streams of rain from the world of heaven, free of attachment, give the people countless food, so do your streams.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—pouring from the sky
- वृष्टयः न (*vṛṣṭayaḥ na*)—as streams of rain provide abundant foods
- ते (*te*)—your
- असश्चतः (*asaścataḥ*)—separate
- धाराः (*dhārāḥ*)—flows
- सहस्रिणं (*sahasriṇaṃ*)—countless (abundant)
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- अच्छ (*accha*)—towards us
- प्रयंति (*prayaṃti*)—they provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, as streams of rain pouring from the sky provide abundant foods, so your streams, flowing separately, provide us with exceedingly abundant foods.

##### English translation
Your unconnected streams advance towards infinite food ( for us ) like the showers from heaven,

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हरि॑स्तुंजा॒न आयु॑धा ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हरिः । तुंजानः । आयुधा ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 163

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हरिः हरितवर्णः सोमः विश्वा विश्वानि प्रियाणि देवानां प्रीतिकराणि काव्या काव्यानि कर्माणि चक्षाणः पश्यन् आयुधा स्वकीयान्यायुधानि तुंजानः राक्षसान् प्रति प्रेरयंश्च अभि अर्षति यागं प्रति गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Hari, the green-coloured Soma, beholding all the pleasing, poetic acts (kāvya) that delight the gods, and hurling his own weapons at the Rākṣasas, goes towards the sacrifice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—Soma, who is of green colour
- प्रियाणि (*priyāṇi*)—pleasing to the gods
- विश्वा काव्या (*viśvā kāvyā*)—all the sacrificial acts
- चक्षाणः (*cakṣāṇaḥ*)—beholding
- आयुधा (*āyudhā*)—his weapons
- तुंजानः (*tuṃjānaḥ*)—hurling towards the Rākṣasas
- अभ्यर्षति (*abhyarṣati*)—he comes towards the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, who is of green colour, beholding all the sacrificial acts that please the gods and hurling his weapons towards the Rākṣasas, comes towards the sacrifice.

##### English translation
The greeu-tinted Soma contemplating all the holy acts that are pleasing to the gods rushes (to the sacrifice) brandishing his weapons (against the Rakshasas).

> श्येनः । न । वंसु । सीदति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुव्रतः सुकर्मा सः सोमः आयुभिः मनुष्यैर्ऋत्विग्भिः मर्मृजानः शोध्यमानः इभः गतभयः राजेव यथा राजा श्येनो न यथा च श्येनस्तथा वंसु उदकेषु वसतीवरीषु सीदति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Soma, of good works (suvrata), being cleansed by men (āyu), that is, by the priests, fearless (ibha) like a king, and like a hawk, settles in the waters called vasatīvarī.

He, the object of pious observances, cleansed by the priests, fearless as a king, sits on the waters like a hawk.

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

## Sūkta 58 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘तरत्सः' इति चतुर्ऋचं चतुस्त्रिंशं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । तरत्सः' इत्यनुक्रांतम् ॥ उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning तरत्सः (*taratsaḥ*) has four ṛks and is the thirty-fourth sūkta. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says तरत्सः (*taratsaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

Translation: This sūkta beginning तरत्सः (*taratsaḥ*) is the thirty-fourth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It contains four ṛks. The seer, deity and metre of this sūkta are the same as in the preceding sūkta. The Anukramaṇī says तरत्सः (*taratsaḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

Sūkta 58. Maṇḍala 9. Anuvāka 2. Sūkta 58. Aṣṭaka 7. Adhyāya 1. Varga 15. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 4. Seer: Avatsāra. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Gāyatrī.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तर॒त्स मं॒दी धा॑वति॒ धारा॑ सु॒तस्यांध॑सः ।  
> तर॒त्स मं॒दी धा॑वति ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 166

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तरत् । सः । मंदी । धावति । धारा । सुतस्य । अंधसः ।  
> तरत् । सः । मंदी । धावति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मंदी देवानां हर्षकरः सः सोमः तरत् स्तोतॄन् पाप्मनः सकाशात् तारयन् धावति पवते । तदेव दर्शयति । सुतस्य अभिषुतस्य अंधसः देवानामन्नात्मकस्य सोमस्य धारा धावतीति । पुनरपि तदेवाह अत्यंतादरार्थं तरत्स मंदी धावति इति । यद्वा । अस्या ऋचो यास्केनोक्तोऽर्थो द्रष्टव्यः । तद्यथा-‘तरति स पापं सर्वं मंदी यः स्तौति धावति गच्छत्यूर्ध्वाँ गतिम् । धारा सुतस्यांधसो धारयाभिषुतस्य सोमस्य मंत्रपूतस्य वाचा स्तुतस्य ' (निरु. १३.६ ) इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Soma, the delighter (mandī) of the gods, runs on, that is, flows, carrying the praisers across from sin. He shows just this: the stream (dhārā) of the pressed (suta) food-like (andhas) Soma of the gods runs. Again he says the same, for the sake of great emphasis: "he crosses, the delighter runs". Or else, the meaning stated by Yāska is to be seen for this ṛk, namely (Ni. 13.6): he crosses all sin who, delighted, praises; "runs" means goes to the upward path; the stream of the pressed andhas means the stream of the Soma that is pressed, purified by mantra and praised by speech.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मंदी (*maṃdī*)—the delighter of the gods
- सः (*saḥ*)—Soma-deva
- तरत् (*tarat*)—carrying the praisers across from sin
- धावति (*dhāvati*)—he flows swiftly
- सुतस्य (*sutasya*)—of the pressed
- अंधसः (*aṃdhasaḥ*)—Soma
- धारा (*dhārā*)—the flow runs swiftly
- तरत् (*tarat*)—carrying the sacrificers across from hardship **NOTE**
- सः (*saḥ*)—Soma-deva
- मंदी (*maṃdī*)—causing gladness
- धावति (*dhāvati*)—he moves quickly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, the delighter of the gods, flows swiftly, carrying the praisers across from sin. The flow of the pressed Soma runs swiftly.

##### English translation
He the delighter (of the gods) flows rescuing (his worshippers from sin); the stream of the effused beverage (flows); he the delighter (of the gods) flows rescuing (his worshippers from sin).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒स्रा वे॑द॒ वसू॑नां॒ मर्त॑स्य दे॒व्यव॑सः ।  
> तर॒त्स मं॒दी धा॑वति ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 167

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उस्रा । वेद । वसूनाम् । मर्तस्य । देवी । अवसः ।  
> तरत् । सः । मंदी । धावति ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वसूनां धनानाम् उस्रा उत्सरणशीला प्रदात्री देवी द्योतमाना स्तूयमाना वा यस्य सोमस्य धारा मर्तस्य मनुष्यं यजमानम् अवसः रक्षितुं वेद जानाति । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The stream of that Soma, which gives the riches (vasu), is moving (uṣrā) and bountiful, and is shining (devī) or praised, knows how to protect (avasaḥ) the mortal (martya), the human sacrificer. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*)—the riches
- उस्रा (*usrā*)—that gives abundantly
- देवी (*devī*)—and radiant stream of Soma
- मर्तस्य (*martasya*)—the human sacrificer
- अवसः (*avasaḥ*)—to protect
- वेद (*veda*)—it knows
- मंदी (*maṃdī*)—the delighter of the gods
- सः (*saḥ*)—Soma-deva
- तरत् (*tarat*)—carrying the sacrificers across from sin
- धावति (*dhāvati*)—he moves quickly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The radiant stream of Soma, which gives riches abundantly, knows that it must protect the human sacrificer. Soma-deva, the delighter of the gods, moves quickly, carrying the sacrificer across from sin.

##### English translation
The brilliant (stream), the bestower of riches, knows how to protect the worshipper : he the delighter (of the gods) flows rescuing (his worshippers from sin).

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ध्व॒स्रयोः॑ पुरु॒षंत्यो॒रा स॒हस्रा॑णि दद्महे ।  
> तर॒त्स मं॒दी धा॑वति ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ध्वस्रयोः । पुरुऽसंत्योः । आ । सहस्राणि । दद्महे ।  
> तरत् । सः । मंदी । धावति ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 168

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ध्वस्रयोः पुरुषंत्योः । ध्वस्रः कश्चिद्राजा पुरुषंतिः कश्चित् । तयोरुभयोः । अत्र इतरेतरयोगविवक्षया द्विवचनं द्रष्टव्यम् । सहस्राणि धनानां सहस्राणि आ दद्महे वयं प्रतिगृह्णीमः । तदस्माभिः प्रतिगृहीतं धनमुत्तममस्त्विति ऋषिः सोमं प्रार्थयत इति सोमस्य स्तुतिः । सिद्धमन्यत् । यथावत्सार एतयोर्धनानि प्रतिजग्राह एवं तरंतपुरुमीळ्हौ प्रतिजगृहतुः । तथा च शाट्यायनकम्--- ‘ अथ ह वै तरंत पुरुमीळ्हौ वैददश्वी ध्वस्रयोः पुरुषंत्योर्बहु प्रतिगृह्य गरगिराविव मेनाते तौ ह स्मांगुल्या सातं प्रतिममृशाते तावकामयेतामसातं नाविवेदं सातं स्यादात्तमिवैव न प्रतिगृहीतमिति तावेतंचतुर्ऋचमपश्यतां तेन प्रत्यैतां ततो वै तयोरसातं सातमभवदात्तमिवैव न प्रतिगृहीतं स यः  प्रतिगृह्य कामयेत' इत्यादि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of Dhvasra and Puruṣanti: Dhvasra is a certain king and Puruṣanti is another; of those two. The dual is to be understood here as intending a combination of one with the other (itaretarayoga). We receive thousands of riches. The seer prays to Soma that the wealth received by us may be excellent; thus it is praise of Soma. The rest is established. As Vatsāra received the riches of these two, so Taranta and Purumīḷha received them. And so the Śāṭyāyanaka says: Taranta and Purumīḷha, the Vaidadaśvis, having received much from Dhvasra and Puruṣanti, thought it like poison; they touched the gain with a finger and wished that the ungained become gained and that what was received become as if not received; they saw this four-ṛk hymn and went to it; thereupon the ungained became gained and what was received as if not received; and so on. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ध्वस्रयोः (*dhvasrayoḥ*)—from the king called Dhvasra
- पुरुषंत्योः (*puruṣaṃtyoḥ*)—and from the king called Puruṣanti
- सहस्राणि (*sahasrāṇi*)—unlimited riches
- आ दद्महे (*ā dadmahe*)—we have received
- मंदी (*maṃdī*)—the gladdener
- सः (*saḥ*)—Soma-deva
- तरत् (*tarat*)—carrying the sacrificers across from sin
- धावति (*dhāvati*)—he moves quickly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

We have received unlimited riches from the king called Dhvasra and from the king called Puruṣanti. Soma-deva, the gladdener, moves quickly, carrying the sacrificers across from sin.

##### English translation
We have received thousands from Dhwasra and Purushanti: he the delighter (of the gods) flows rescuing (his worshippers from sin).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ ययो॑स्त्रिं॒शतं॒ तना॑ स॒हस्रा॑णि च॒ दद्म॑हे ।  
> तर॒त्स मं॒दी धा॑वति ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 169

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ । ययोः । त्रिंशतम् । तना । सहस्राणि । च । दद्महे ।  
> तरत् । सः । मंदी । धावति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ययोः ध्वस्रपुरुषंत्योः त्रिंशतं त्रिशतानि सहस्राणि तना वस्त्राणि आ दद्महे वयं प्रतिगृह्णीमः तयोरस्माभिः प्रतिगृहीतं तत्सर्वमप्रतिगृहीतमस्त्विति सोमऋषिः प्रार्थयत इति सोमस्यैव स्तुतिः । सिद्धमन्यत् ॥ ॥ १५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Of those two, Dhvasra and Puruṣanti, we receive thirty hundreds of thousands of garments (tanā); the seer of Soma prays that all that has been received by us from them may be as if not received; thus it is only praise of Soma. The rest is established.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ययोः (*yayoḥ*)—from those two kings, Dhvasra and Puruṣanti
- त्रिंशतिं (*triṃśatiṃ*)—multiplied by three hundred **NOTE**
- सहस्राणि (*sahasrāṇi*)—numbering thousands
- तना च (*tanā ca*)—and garments
- आ दद्महे (*ā dadmahe*)—we have received
- मंदी (*maṃdī*)—the gladdener
- सः (*saḥ*)—Soma-deva
- तरत् (*tarat*)—carrying the sacrificers across from sin
- धावति (*dhāvati*)—he moves quickly

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

From the two kings, Dhvasra and Puruṣanti, we have received garments numbering thousands multiplied by three hundred (1000 x 300). Soma-deva, the gladdener, moves quickly, carrying the sacrificers across from sin.

##### English translation
We have received from those two three hundred thousand garments; he the delighter ( of the gods ) flows rescuing ( his worshippers from sin ).

## Sūkta 59 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘पवस्व ' इति चतुर्ऋचं पंचत्रिंशं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । ' पवस्व' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning पवस्व (*pavasva*) has four ṛks and is the thirty-fifth sūkta. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇī says पवस्व (*pavasva*). The use in the rite has been stated.

## Sūkta 60 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘प्र गायत्रेण' इति चतुर्ऋचं षट्त्रिंशं सूक्तं काश्यपस्यावत्सारस्यार्षम्। तृतीया पुरउष्णिगाद्यद्वादशका द्व्यष्टका । शिष्टा गायत्र्यः । पवमानः सोमो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतं- प्र गायत्रेणोपांत्या पुरउष्णिक्' इति । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्र गायत्रेण (*pra gāyatreṇa*) has four ṛks and is the thirty-sixth sūkta; it is the vision of Kāśyapa Avatsāra. The third ṛk is a Puraūṣṇih, of which the first pāda has twelve syllables and the other two eight each. The remaining ṛks are Gāyatrī. The deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says: प्र गायत्रेणोपांत्या पुर उष्णिक् (*pra gāyatreṇopāṃtyā pura uṣṇik*). The use in the rite has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

This sūkta beginning प्र गायत्रेण (*pra gāyatreṇa*) is the thirty-sixth sūkta in the second anuvāka. It has four ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the one called काश्यपः अवत्सारः (*kāśyapaḥ avatsāraḥ*); the deity is Pavamāna Soma. The third ṛk of this sūkta is of the metre called Puraūṣṇih. If a ṛk has three pādas, with twelve syllables in the first pāda and eight syllables each in the other two pādas, it is called of Puraūṣṇih metre. The remaining ṛks are of Gāyatrī metre. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: प्र गायत्रेणोपांत्या पुर उष्णिक् (*pra gāyatreṇopāṃtyā pura uṣṇik*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

##### English translation
All-beholding Soma, flow pleasantly for Indra's gratification ; bring (us) food with male offspring.

## Sūkta 61 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तृतीयेऽनुवाके सप्त सूक्तानि । तत्र ‘अया वीती' इति त्रिंशदृचं प्रथमं सूक्तम् । अमहीयुर्नामांगिरस ऋषिः । गायत्री छंदः । पवमानः सोमो देवता । तथा चानुक्रांतम्- अया वीती त्रिंशदमहीयुः' इति । उक्तो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the third anuvāka there are seven sūktas. Among them the sūkta beginning अया वीती (*ayā vītī*) has thirty ṛks and is the first. The seer is Amahīyu, of the Āṅgirasa family; the metre is Gāyatrī; the deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says: अया वीती त्रिंशदमहीयुः (*ayā vītī triṃśadamahīyuḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

In the third anuvāka of the ninth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā there are seven sūktas. Among them this sūkta beginning अयावीती (*ayāvītī*) is the first. It has thirty ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is the one called अमहीयुः (*amahīyuḥ*), son of the seer Aṅgiras. The deity is called पवमानः सोम (*pavamānaḥ soma*); the metre is Gāyatrī. In the Anukramaṇī it is said: अया वीती त्रिंशदमहीयुः (*ayā vītī triṃśadamahīyuḥ*). The use in the rite has been stated before.

### Printed p. 178
Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 3 **NOTE**, Sūkta 61. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 1, Vargas 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 30. Seer: अमहीयुः (*amahīyuḥ*). Deity: पवमानः सोमः (*pavamānaḥ somaḥ*). Metre: गायत्री (*gāyatrī*).

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒या वी॒ती परि॑ स्रव॒ यस्त॑ इंदो॒ मदे॒ष्वा ।  
> अ॒वाह॑न्नव॒तीर्नव॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अया । वीती । परि । स्रव । यः । ते । इंदो इति । मदेषु । आ ।  
> अवऽअहन् । नवतीः । नव ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम अया अनेन रसेन वीती वीत्या इंद्रस्य भक्षणाय परि स्रव परिक्षर । कीदृशेन रसेनेत्यत आह । ते तव यः रसः मदेषु संग्रामेषु नवतीर्नव इति नवनवतिसंख्याकाश्च शत्रुपुरीः अवाहन जघान । अमुं सोमरसं पीत्वा मत्तः सन्निंद्र उक्तलक्षणाः शत्रुपुरीर्जघानेति कृत्वा रसो जघानेत्युपचारः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, with this juice flow around, for Indra's enjoyment, by way of entering his body. With what kind of juice? He says: your juice which in the battles struck down ninety-nine cities of the enemy. Having drunk this Soma juice and become exhilarated, Indra struck down the enemy cities of the stated kind; therefore the striking is attributed to the juice in a figurative way.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- ते (*te*)—your
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which juice
- मदेषु (*madeṣu*)—in the battles
- नवतीर्नव (*navatīrnava*)—ninety-nine enemy cities
- अवाहन् (*avāhan*)—destroyed
- आया (*āyā*)—with a juice of such power **NOTE**
- वीती (*vītī*)—for Indra's drinking
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—flow in the form of a stream

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, with that juice of yours, of such power, which in the battles destroyed ninety-nine enemy cities, flow in the form of a stream for Indra's drinking.

### Printed p. 179

##### English translation
Flow, Indu, for (Indra's) food with that (juice) of yours which in battles overthrew ninety and nine (cities of the foe).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पुरः॑ स॒द्य इ॒त्थाधि॑ये॒ दिवो॑दासाय॒ शंब॑रम् ।  
> अध॒ त्यं तु॒र्वशं॒ यदु॑म् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पुरः । सद्यः । इत्थाऽधिये । दिवःऽदासाय । शंबरम् ।  
> अध । त्यम् । तुर्वशम् । यदुम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सद्यः एकस्मिन्नेवाह्नि पुरः शत्रूणां पुराणि सोमरसोऽवाहन् । इत्थाधिये सत्यकर्मणे दिवोदासाय राज्ञे शंबरं शत्रुपुराणां स्वामिनम् अध अथ त्यं तं तुर्वशं तुर्वशनामकं राजानं दिवोदासशत्रुं यदुं यदुनामकं राजानं च वशमानयंच । अत्रापि सोमरसं पीत्वा मत्तः सन्निंद्रः सर्वमेतदकार्षीदिति सोमरसे कर्तृत्वमुपचर्यते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In a single day, at once, the Soma juice struck down the cities of the enemies. For King Divodāsa, whose action is true, it brought under control Śambara, the lord of the enemy cities, and then that Turvaśa, the king so named, an enemy of Divodāsa, and Yadu, the king so named. Here too, it is figuratively that agency is attributed to the Soma juice, since Indra, having drunk it and become exhilarated, did all this.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सद्यः (*sadyaḥ*)—at one time
- पुरः (*puraḥ*)—the Soma juice destroyed all the enemy cities
- इत्थाधिये (*itthādhiye*)—whose action is true
- दिवोदासाय (*divodāsāya*)—to help the king called Divodāsa
- शंबरं (*śaṃbaraṃ*)—the demon Śambara
- अध (*adha*)—afterwards
- त्यं (*tyaṃ*)—renowned
- तुर्वशं (*turvaśaṃ*)—the king called Turvaśa
- यदुं (*yaduṃ*)—and the king called Yadu, it defeated

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma juice, which gladdens Indra, helped Indra to destroy all the enemy cities at one time. To help the king called Divodāsa, it helped to defeat the demon Śambara, then the renowned Turvaśa, and likewise Yadu.

##### English translation
(Which overturned) the cities in a moment, and for the sake of the devout Divodasa (subdued) Shambara and then that Turvasha and Yadu.

> क्षर । सहस्रिणीः । इषः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम अश्ववित् अश्वस्य लंभकस्त्वं नः अस्माकम् अश्वं गोमत् गोयुक्तं हिरण्यवत् हिरण्योपेतं धनं च परि क्षर । अपि च सहस्रिणीः बहूनि इषः अन्नानि क्षर ॥

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are possessed of horses, provide to us all around horses, wealth with cattle and of gold, and very abundant foods.

> चारुः । मित्रे । वरुणे । च ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम मधुमान् मधुररसः चारुः कल्याणस्वरूपश्च सः अभिषुतस्त्वं नः अस्माकं यज्ञे भगाय भगाख्याय देवाय वायवे च पूष्णे च मित्रे मित्राय देवाय वरुणे वरुणाय च पवस्व क्षर ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, sweet-juiced and beautiful, pressed as you are, flow for us in our sacrifice for the god called Bhaga, for Vāyu, for Pūṣan, for the god Mitra and for Varuṇa.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O divine Soma) मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—possessed of sweet juice
- चारुः (*cāruḥ*)—of attractive form
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—in our sacrifice
- मित्रे (*mitre*)—for Mitra
- भगाय (*bhagāya*)—for the divine Bhaga
- नायवे (*nāyave*)—with Vāyu as the aim **NOTE**
- पूष्पे (*pūṣpe*)—for the divine Pūṣan **NOTE**
- वरुणे च (*varuṇe ca*)—and for the satisfaction of Varuṇa
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are possessed of sweet juice and of attractive form, flow in our sacrifice for Mitra, for the satisfaction of Bhaga, with Vāyu as the aim, for Pūṣan, and for the satisfaction of Varuṇa.
