#### Ṛk 46

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अस॑र्जि स्कं॒भो दि॒व उद्य॑तो॒ मदः॒ परि॑ त्रि॒धातु॒र्भुव॑नान्यर्षति ।  
> अं॒शुं रि॑हंति म॒तयः॒ पनि॑प्नतं गि॒रा यदि॑ नि॒र्णिज॑मृ॒ग्मिणो॑ य॒युः ॥ ४६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> असर्जि । स्कंभः । दिवः । उत्ऽयतः । मदः । परि । त्रिऽधातुः । भुवनानि । अर्षति ।  
> अंशुम् । रिहंति । मतयः । पनिप्नतम् । गिरा । यदि । निःऽनिजम् । ऋग्मिणः । ययुः ॥ ४६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवः द्युलोकस्य स्कंभः स्कंभयिता धारकः उद्यतः सोमः असर्जि सृज्यते । अभिषूयते इत्यर्थः । किंच त्रिधातुः । द्रोणकलशाधवनीयपूतभृदाख्यास्त्रयो धातवो यस्य स तथोक्तः । तादृशो भुवनानि उदकानि अर्षति गच्छति । अंशुं सोमं पनिप्नतं शब्दायमानं मतयः पूजकाः रिहंति लिहंति आस्वादयंति । कदा। यदि निर्णिजं निर्णिक्तम् । यद्वा । निर्णिगिति रूपनाम। रूपवंतमित्यर्थः । तम् ऋग्मिणः स्तोतारः गिरा स्तुत्या ययुः गच्छंति तदा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, the supporter (स्कंभः (*skaṃbhaḥ*), one who props up) of heaven, the sustainer, uplifted, is let loose (असर्जि (*asarji*) means is pressed). Further, he is threefold in substance (त्रिधातुः (*tridhātuḥ*)): the three substances called Droṇa-kalaśa, Ādhavanīya and Pūtabhṛt belong to him; such as he is, he goes to the waters. The worshippers (मतयः (*matayaḥ*)) lick, that is, taste, the sounding Soma. When? When the singers of Ṛks, the praisers, approach with praise (गिरा (*girā*)) him who is purified (निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*)); or else, निर्णिक् (*nirṇik*) is a name of form, and the meaning is the one who has form. Then they go to him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मदः (*madaḥ*)—the giver of joy
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—to the world of Dyaus
- स्कंभः (*skaṃbhaḥ*)—the supporter
- उद्यतः (*udyataḥ*)—and restrained for the sacrifice, Soma
- असर्जि (*asarji*)—is pressed
- त्रिधातुः (*tridhātuḥ*)—Soma who has the three vessels, the Droṇa-kalaśa and others
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—the waters
- परि अर्षति (*pari arṣati*)—enters
- यदि (*yadi*)—when
- निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*)—Soma who has form
- ऋग्मिणः (*ṛgmiṇaḥ*)—the praisers
- गिरा (*girā*)—with praise
- ययुः (*yayuḥ*)—approach, then
- मतयः (*matayaḥ*)—the reciters of praise
- पनिष्कृतं (*paniṣkṛtaṃ*)—sounding **NOTE**
- अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)—Soma
- रिहंति (*rihaṃti*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, the giver of joy, the supporter of the world of Dyaus, restrained for the sacrifice, is pressed. Soma, who has the three vessels, the Droṇa-kalaśa and others, enters the waters. When the praisers approach with praise the Soma who has form, then the reciters of praise drink the sounding Soma.

The supporter of heaven the prepared cxhilarating (Soma) is let loose, the triple (liquor) rushes to the waters ; the worshippers taste the sounding Soma juice, when the reciters of holy texts approach the embodied (beverage) with praise. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 47

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र ते॒ धारा॒ अत्यण्वा॑नि मे॒ष्यः॑ पुना॒नस्य॑ सं॒यतो॑ यंति॒ रंह॑यः ।  
> यद्गोभि॑रिंदो च॒म्वोः॑ सम॒ज्यस॒ आ सु॑वा॒नः सो॑म क॒लशे॑षु सीदसि ॥ ४७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । ते । धाराः । अति । अण्वानि । मेष्यः । पुनानस्य । सम्ऽयतः । यंति । रंहयः ।  
> यत् । गोभिः । इंदो इति । चम्वोः । सम्ऽअज्यसे । आ । सुवानः । सोम । कलशेषु । सीदसि ॥ ४७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पुनानस्य पूयमानस्य संयतः संगृह्यमाणाः रंहयः रंहणस्वभावाः धाराः मेष्यः अण्वानि अणूनि लोमानि अति यंति अतिक्रम्य गच्छंति । हे इंदो सोम यत् यदा गोभिः उदकैः चम्वोः अधिषवणफलकयोरुपरि समज्यसे तदानीं हे सोम सुवानः सूयमानस्त्वं कलशेषु आ सीदसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, when you are mixed with the waters over the two boards (चम्वोः (*camvoḥ*), the pressing boards), then, O Soma, being pressed, you settle in the pitchers.

- कलशेषु (*kalaśeṣu*)—in the pitchers
- आ सीदसि (*ā sīdasi*)—are established

O Soma-deva, your streams, which are purified, gathered together and of the nature of a flow, pass beyond the threads of the wool. When you are mixed together with the waters in the ladles, then you, who are pressed, are established in the pitchers.

#### Ṛk 48

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> पव॑स्व सोम क्रतु॒विन्न॑ उ॒क्थ्योऽव्यो॒ वारे॒ परि॑ धाव॒ मधु॑ प्रि॒यम् ।  
> ज॒हि विश्वा॑न्र॒क्षस॑ इंदो अ॒त्रिणो॑ बृ॒हद्व॑देम वि॒दथे॑ सु॒वीराः॑ ॥ ४८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> पवस्व । सोम । क्रतुऽवित् । नः । उक्थ्यः । अव्यः । वारे । परि । धाव । मधु । प्रियम् ।  
> जहि । विश्वान् । रक्षसः । इंदो इति । अत्रिणः । बृहत् । वदेम । विदथे । सुऽवीराः ॥ ४८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम नः अस्माकं ऋतुवित् कर्मज्ञः । स्तुतिज्ञ इत्यर्थः । उक्थ्यः स्तुत्यः । यतः स्तुत्योऽतः क्रतुविदित्यभिप्रायः । ईदृशस्त्वं नोऽस्माकं यागाय पवस्व स्रव रसम् । अव्यो वारे दशापवित्रे प्रियं मधु परि धाव परिक्षर । हे इंदो दीप्त सोम अत्रिणः भक्षकान् विश्वान रक्षसः जहि । सुवीराः सुपुत्रा वयं विदथे यज्ञे बृहत् महद्धनं वदेम उच्चारयेम । याचेमेत्यर्थः । यद्वा प्रभूतं स्तोत्रं वदेम ॥ ॥ २१ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you who know the rite for us (ऋतुवित् (*ṛtuvit*) is glossed as one who knows the rite, that is, who knows praise) and are worthy of praise (उक्थ्यः (*ukthyaḥ*)): because you are praiseworthy, you are one who knows the rite, such is the intention. Such as you are, flow your juice for our sacrifice; in the woollen ten-fold filter run around the dear sweet juice. O Indu, shining Soma, slay all the devouring Rākṣasas. We, with good sons, in the sacrifice (विदथे (*vidathe*)) would utter great (बृहत् (*bṛhat*)) wealth, that is, we would ask for it; or else we would utter abundant praise. **NOTE**

- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- अव्यः वारे (*avyaḥ vāre*)—in the woollen threads of the ten-fold filter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who know our rite and are worthy of praise, flow. In the woollen threads of the ten-fold filter make the dear and tasty juice flow. O Soma-deva, destroy all the devouring Rākṣasas. We, who have excellent heroic sons, recite abundant praise in the sacrificial house.

## Sūkta 87 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘प्र तु द्रव' इति नवर्चं द्वितीयं सूक्तं काव्यस्योशनस आर्षमनादेशपरिभाषया त्रैष्टुभं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । तथा चानुक्रांतं -- प्र तु नवोशना ' इति । 'जागतमूर्ध्वं प्रागुशनसः' (अनु. ९. ६७ ) इति वचनाज्जगत्यधिकारो निवृत्तः । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The second sūkta, beginning प्र तु द्रव (*pra tu drava*), has nine Ṛks. Its seer is Uśanā, of the line of Kavi; by the rule that a metre not stated is understood, the metre is Triṣṭubh; the deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇikā is cited accordingly: प्र तु नवोशना (*pra tu navośanā*). By the statement जागतमूर्ध्वं प्रागुशनसः (*jāgatamūrdhvaṃ prāguśanasaḥ*) (Anu. 9-67) the governing rule of Jagatī ceases here. The application (viniyoga) has been stated.

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning प्र तु द्रव (*pra tu drava*) is the second sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has nine Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Uśanā, the son of Kavi; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: प्र तु नवोशना (*pra tu navośanā*). Since it is said जागतमूर्ध्वं प्रागुशनसः (*jāgatamūrdhvaṃ prāguśanasaḥ*) (Anu. 9-67), from here onward there are no mantras of the Jagatī metre, only the Triṣṭup metre. The application (viniyoga) has been stated before. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र तु द्र॑व॒ परि॒ कोशं॒ नि षी॑द॒ नृभिः॑ पुना॒नो अ॒भि वाज॑मर्ष ।  
> अश्वं॒ न त्वा॑ वा॒जिनं॑ म॒र्जयं॒तोऽच्छा॑ ब॒र्ही र॑श॒नाभि॑र्नयंति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । तु । द्रव । परि । कोशम् । नि । सीद । नृऽभिः । पुनानः । अभि । वाजम् । अर्ष ।  
> अश्वम् । न । त्वा । वाजिनम् । मर्जयंतः । अच्छ । बर्हिः । रशनाभिः । नयंति ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम तु क्षिप्रं प्र द्रव प्रगच्छ । गत्वा च कोशं द्रोणकलशं परि नि षीद निषण्णो  भव । नृभिः नेतृभिः पुनानः पूयमानः वाजम् अन्नं यजमानार्थमुद्दिश्य अभि अर्ष अभिगच्छ । वाजिनं बलवंतम् अश्वं न अश्वमिव तं यथा मार्जयंति तद्वत् वाजिनं त्वां मार्जयंतः शोधयंतः बर्हिः यज्ञम् अच्छ प्रति रशनाभिः रशनावदायताभिरंगुलीभिः नयंति अध्वर्युप्रमुखाः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, run forth swiftly, and having gone, settle round the receptacle, the Droṇa-kalaśa. Purified by the leaders, flow towards the food intended for the sacrificer. Just as they cleanse a strong horse, so the Adhvaryu and the others, cleansing you, the strong one, lead you towards the sacrifice with the fingers, which are long like girths.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- तु (*tu*)—swiftly (O Soma-deva)
- प्र द्रव (*pra drava*)—flow
- कोशं (*kośaṃ*)—in the Droṇa-kalaśa
- परि नि षीद (*pari ni ṣīda*)—sit down
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—being purified
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food for the sacrificer
- अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)—procure **NOTE**
- वाजिनं त्वा (*vājinaṃ tvā*)—you who are endowed with strength
- अश्वं न (*aśvaṃ na*)—as one washes a horse
- मार्जयंतः (*mārjayaṃtaḥ*)—cleansing (the priests) **NOTE**
- रशनाभिः (*raśanābhiḥ*)—with their fingers
- बर्हिः अच्छ (*barhiḥ accha*)—towards the sacrifice
- नयंति (*nayaṃti*)—lead

### Printed p. 613

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, flow swiftly. Sit in the Droṇa-kalaśa. Being purified by the priests, procure food for the sacrificer. The Adhvaryus, cleansing you, the strong one, as one washes a horse, lead you with their fingers towards the sacrifice.

##### English translation
Flow fast (Soma), sit down on the receptacle, purified by the priests hasten (showing) food (to the sacrificer); cleansing you like a strong horse, they guide you with (their fingers for) reins to the sacred grass.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स्वा॒यु॒धः प॑वते दे॒व इंदु॑रशस्ति॒हा वृ॒जनं॒ रक्ष॑माणः ।  
> पि॒ता दे॒वानां॑ जनि॒ता सु॒दक्षो॑ विष्टं॒भो दि॒वो ध॒रुणः॑ पृथि॒व्याः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सुऽआयुधः । पवते । देवः । इंदुः । अशस्तिऽहा । वृजनम् । रक्षमाणः ।  
> पिता । देवानाम् । जनिता । सुऽदक्षः । विष्टंभः । दिवः । धरुणः । पृथिव्याः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स्वायुधः शोभनायुधः इंदुः सोमः देवः पवते । स च देवः अशस्तिहा रक्षोहा वृजनम् उपद्रवं रक्षमाणः पिता पालकः देवानां तथा जनिता उत्पादकः सुदक्षः सुबलः दिवः विष्टंभः विशेषेण स्तंभयिता पृथिव्याः च धरुण धारकः । एवंमहानुभावः पवते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Indu, Soma, the god with excellent weapons (स्वायुधः (*svāyudhaḥ*)), flows. That god is the destroyer of Rākṣasas (अशस्तिहा (*aśastihā*), the slayer of Rakṣas), and protects against trouble (वृजनम् (*vṛjanam*) is glossed as affliction). He is the protector of the gods and also their begetter, of excellent strength, the one who firmly props up (विष्टंभः (*viṣṭaṃbhaḥ*)) heaven, and the supporter of the earth (धरुण (*dharuṇa*), the holder). Of such greatness he flows.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवः (*devaḥ*)—of divine nature
- स्वायुधः (*svāyudhaḥ*)—having an excellent weapon
- अशस्तिहा (*aśastihā*)—the destroyer of evil-doers
- वृजनं (*vṛjanaṃ*)—from obstacle
- रक्षमाणः (*rakṣamāṇaḥ*)—the protector
- पिता (*pitā*)—the guardian of the world
- देवानां जनिता (*devānāṃ janitā*)—the begetter of the gods
- सुदक्षः (*sudakṣaḥ*)—having excellent strength
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the world of Dyaus

### Printed p. 614

- विष्टंभः (*viṣṭaṃbhaḥ*)—the supporter
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—of the earth
- धरुणः (*dharuṇaḥ*)—the foundation
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma-deva
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, of divine nature, having an excellent weapon, the destroyer of evil-doers, the protector from obstacles, the guardian of the world, the begetter of the gods, having excellent strength, the supporter of the world of Dyaus and of the earth, flows.

##### English translation
The divine Indu well armed flows forth, the destroyer of Rakshasas, averting calamity, the protector of the gods, the progenitor, the powerfur one, the prop of heaven, the support of the earth. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ऋषि॒र्विप्रः॑ पुरए॒ता जना॑नामृ॒भुर्धीर॑ उ॒शना॒ काव्ये॑न ।  
> स चि॑द्विवेद॒ निहि॑तं॒ यदा॑सामपी॒च्यं१॒॑ गुह्यं॒ नाम॒ गोना॑म् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> ऋषिः । विप्रः । पुरःऽएता । जनानाम् । ऋभुः । धीरः । उशना । काव्येन ।  
> सः । चित् । विवेद । निऽहितम् । यत् । आसाम् । अपीच्यम् । गुह्यम् । नाम । गोनाम् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ऋषिः अतींद्रियद्रष्टा विप्रः मेधावी पुरएता पुरतो गंता जनानां मनुष्याणाम् ऋभुः उरु भासमानः धीरः धीमान् उशना एतन्नामर्षिः यः स चित् स एव काव्येन कवित्वेन स्तोत्रेण विवेद लभते । किम् । यदासां गोनां गवाम् अपीच्यम् । अंतर्हितनामैतत् । अंतर्हितं गुह्यं गोपनीयं नाम नामकमुदकं पयोलक्षणम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The seer (ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*), one who sees beyond the senses), the wise, the leader of men going before them, shining widely (ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*)), the steadfast, the seer named Uśanā: that same one by his poetic power (काव्येन (*kāvyena*), by poetic skill, by praise) obtains it. What? Of these cows (गोनां (*gonāṃ*)) the अपीच्यम् (*apīcyam*), which is a word for hidden; the hidden, secret, to be guarded नाम (*nāma*), that is, water having the nature of milk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—one who has supersensuous vision
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the wise
- जनानां पुरएता (*janānāṃ puraetā*)—the guide of men
- ऋभुः (*ṛbhuḥ*)—the shining **NOTE**
- धीरः (*dhīraḥ*)—the learned
- उशना (*uśanā*)—and the one named Uśanas
- स चित् (*sa cit*)—that same seer
- आसां गोनां (*āsāṃ gonāṃ*)—of these cows
- अपीच्यः (*apīcyaḥ*)—which is concealed **NOTE**
- गुह्यं (*guhyaṃ*)—and kept secret
- नाम (*nāma*)—the water in the form of milk
- काव्येन (*kāvyena*)—by his own greatness endowed with poetic power
- विवेद (*viveda*)—obtained

### Printed p. 615

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The seer, who has supersensuous vision, is wise, the guide of men, shining, learned and named Uśanas, obtained the water in the form of milk, concealed and kept secret, of the cows, by his own greatness endowed with poetic power.

##### English translation
The rishi, the sage, the foremost of men, the farshining intelligent U'shanas—he verily by his poetic gift discovered the secret milk of those cows which was hidden and concealed.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष स्य ते॒ मधु॑माँ इंद्र॒ सोमो॒ वृषा॒ वृष्णे॒ परि॑ प॒वित्रे॑ अक्षाः ।  
> स॒ह॒स्र॒साः श॑त॒सा भू॑रि॒दावा॑ शश्वत्त॒मं ब॒र्हिरा वा॒ज्य॑स्थात् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । स्यः । ते । मधुऽमान् । इंद्र । सोमः । वृषा । वृष्णे । परि । पवित्रे । अक्षारिति ।  
> सहस्रऽसाः । शतऽसाः । भूरिऽदावा । शश्वत्ऽतमम् । बर्हिः । आ । वाजी । अस्थात् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र वृष्णे वर्षकाय ते तुभ्यम् एष स्यः सः सोमः मधुमान् माधुर्योपेतः वृषा वर्षकः पवित्रे परि अक्षाः परिक्षरति । क्षरतेर्लुङि रूपम् । स एव सहस्रसाः सहस्रसंख्याकधनस्य दाता शतसाः शतसंख्याकस्य दाता भूरिदावा ततोऽपि भूरेर्दाता वाजी बलवान् शश्वत्तमं नित्यं बर्हिः यज्ञम् आ अस्थात् अतिष्ठति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, for you the showerer, that same Soma, sweet (endowed with sweetness), showering, flows around (अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*)) in the filter. He is the giver of a thousand-fold wealth (सहस्रसाः (*sahasrasāḥ*)), the giver of a hundred-fold (शतसाः (*śatasāḥ*)), the giver of even more abundance (भूरिदावा (*bhūridāvā*)), strong (वाजी (*vājī*)), and he stays (अस्थात् (*asthāt*)) ever (शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)) at the sacrifice (बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- वृष्णे (*vṛṣṇe*)—who grants desired objects
- ते (*te*)—for you
- मधुमान् (*madhumān*)—which is endowed with sweetness
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—and grants desired objects
- एषः स्यः सोमः (*eṣaḥ syaḥ somaḥ*)—this Soma

### Printed p. 616

- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—in the ten-fold filter
- पर्यक्षाः (*paryakṣāḥ*)—flows
- सहस्रसाः (*sahasrasāḥ*)—who gives wealth by the thousand
- शतसाः (*śatasāḥ*)—who gives in many forms
- भूरिदावा (*bhūridāvā*)—who gives abundantly
- वाजी (*vājī*)—and is endowed with strength, Indra **NOTE**
- शश्वत्तमं (*śaśvattamaṃ*)—always
- बर्हिः (*barhiḥ*)—in the sacrifice
- अस्थात् (*asthāt*)—sits

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, for you, who grant desired objects, this Soma, which is endowed with sweetness and grants desired objects, flows in the ten-fold filter. Indra, who gives wealth by the thousand, in many forms and abundantly, and is endowed with strength, always sits in the sacrifice.

##### English translation
For you Indra, the showerer, this sweet flavoured Soma the showerer, has been poured into the filter ; the giver of thousand-fold wealth, the giver of hundredfold wealth, the giver of abundant wealth, the powerful is present at the eternal sacrifice.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ते सोमा॑ अ॒भि ग॒व्या स॒हस्रा॑ म॒हे वाजा॑या॒मृता॑य॒ श्रवां॑सि ।  
> प॒वित्रे॑भिः॒ पव॑माना असृग्रंछ्रव॒स्यवो॒ न पृ॑त॒नाजो॒ अत्याः॑ ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एते । सोमाः । अभि । गव्या । सहस्रा । महे । वाजाय । अमृताय । श्रवांसि ।  
> पवित्रेभिः । पवमानाः । असृग्रन् । श्रवस्यवः । न । पृतनाजः । अत्याः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एते सोमाः गव्या गव्यानि सहस्रा सहस्राणि श्रवांसि अन्नानि आशिरलक्षणानि लक्षीकृत्य पवित्रेभिः पवित्रच्छिद्रैः पवमानाः पूयमानाः महे महते वाजाय अन्नाय अमृताय अमृतत्वाय अभि असृग्रन् सृज्यंते । किमिव । श्रवस्यवः अन्नेच्छवः पृतनाजः सेनाजेतारः अत्याः न अश्वा इव ॥ ॥ २२ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These Soma-juices, aiming at (लक्षीकृत्य (*lakṣīkṛtya*)) thousands of cow-products (गव्या (*gavyā*)) and foods (श्रवांसि (*śravāṃsi*)) that have the character of admixture with milk, being purified by the holes of the filter, are let loose for great food and for immortality. Like what? Like horses (अत्याः (*atyāḥ*)) that desire food (श्रवस्यवः (*śravasyavaḥ*)) and are winners of armies (पृतनाजः (*pṛtanājaḥ*)).

### Printed p. 617

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एते सोमाः (*ete somāḥ*)—these Soma-juices
- गव्या (*gavyā*)—obtained from cows
- सहस्रा श्रवांसि (*sahasrā śravāṃsi*)—with a view to many kinds of food
- पवित्रेभिः (*pavitrebhiḥ*)—by the ten-fold filters
- पवमानाः (*pavamānāḥ*)—being purified
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- वाजाय (*vājāya*)—for food
- अमृतायु (*amṛtāyu*)—for the gaining of immortality **NOTE**
- श्रवस्यवः (*śravasyavaḥ*)—desiring food
- पृतनाजः (*pṛtanājaḥ*)—and victorious in battle
- अत्याः न (*atyāḥ na*)—like horses
- अभ्यसृग्रन् (*abhyasṛgran*)—are let loose freely

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

These Soma-juices are let loose freely, like horses that are victorious in battle and desire food, with a view to many kinds of food obtained from cows, being purified by the ten-fold filters, for great food and for the gaining of immortality.

##### English translation
These Soma-juices, (going towards) the thousand viands produced by cows, purified by the filters, are let loose for ample food and ambrosia, desiring food like horses victorius over a host. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ हि ष्मा॑ पुरुहू॒तो जना॑नां॒ विश्वास॑र॒द्भोज॑ना पू॒यमा॑नः ।  
> अथा भ॑र श्येनभृत॒ प्रयां॑सि र॒यिं तुंजा॑नो अ॒भि वाज॑मर्ष ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । हि । स्म । पुरुऽहूतः । जनानाम् । विश्वा । असरत् । भोजना । पूयमानः ।  
> अथ । आ । भर । श्येनऽभृत । प्रयांसि । रयिम् । तुंजानः । अभि । वाजम् । अर्ष ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 618

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं परि असरत् परिसरति जनानाम् अर्थाय विश्वा सर्वाणि भोजना भोजनान्यन्नानि धनानि वा । कीदृशः। पुरुहूतः बहुभिराहूतः पूयमानः शोध्यमानः । अथ प्रत्यक्षकृतः । अथ इदानीं हे श्येनभृत श्येनेनाहृत सोम त्वं प्रयांसि अन्नानि आ भर आहर । रयिं धनं तुंजानः ददानः वाजम् अन्नं रसम् अभि अर्ष अभिगच्छ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma moves round (असरत् (*asarat*)) for the benefit of men all foods (भोजना (*bhojanā*)), that is, foods or wealth. Of what kind is he? Called by many (पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)), being purified. Then (अथ (*atha*)), now, the address becomes direct: O Soma, carried by the falcon (श्येनभृत (*śyenabhṛta*), brought by the falcon), bring foods; giving wealth, flow towards the food, the juice.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पुरुहूतः (*puruhūtaḥ*)—worthy to be invoked by many
- पूयमानः (*pūyamānaḥ*)—and purified, Soma-deva
- जनानां (*janānāṃ*)—for the good of men
- विश्वा भोजना (*viśvā bhojanā*)—all the wealth fit to be enjoyed
- पर्यसरत् (*paryasarat*)—spreads and distributes
- श्येनभृत (*śyenabhṛta*)—O Soma-deva, borne by the falcon
- प्रयांसि (*prayāṃsi*)—foods
- आ भर (*ā bhara*)—provide
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- तुंजानः (*tuṃjānaḥ*)—providing
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—the food in the form of juice
- अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)—make flow **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, worthy to be invoked by many and purified, spreads and distributes for the good of men all the wealth fit to be enjoyed. O Soma-deva, borne by the falcon, provide us foods. Providing us wealth, make flow the food in the form of juice.

##### English translation
Invoked by many, the Soma, undergoing purification, pours forth all food (for the sake of men) ; falcon-borne, bring us food, conveying wealth, send forth your juice.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ष सु॑वा॒नः परि॒ सोमः॑ प॒वित्रे॒ सर्गो॒ न सृ॒ष्टो अ॑दधाव॒दर्वा॑ ।  
> ति॒ग्मे शिशा॑नो महि॒षो न शृंगे॒ गा ग॒व्यन्न॒भि शूरो॒ न सत्वा॑ ॥ ७ ॥

### Printed p. 619

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषः । सुवानः । परि । सोमः । पवित्रे । सर्गः । न । सृष्टः । अदधावत् । अर्वा ।  
> तिग्मे इति । शिशानः । महिषः । न । शृंगे इति । गाः । गव्यन् । अभि । शूरः । न । सत्वा ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एष सुवानः सूयमानः अर्वा अरणकुशलः सोमः सर्गो न सृष्टः विसृष्टोऽश्व इव पवित्रे परि अदधावत् परिधावति । किंच तिग्मे तीक्ष्णे शृंगे शिशानः तीक्ष्णीकुर्वन् महिषो न महान् महिषाख्यो मृग इव । तथान्यदृष्टांतः। गा गव्यन् प्रभूता गा इच्छन् शूरो न शूर इव । एतौ महिषशूरौ यथा प्रतिबुद्धौ शीघ्रं धावतः तद्वत् सत्वा सदनशीलोऽयं गच्छतीति शेषः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, being pressed, swift in going (अर्वा (*arvā*)), runs around in the filter like a horse let loose (सर्गो न सृष्टः (*sargo na sṛṣṭaḥ*)). Further, he is like a great buffalo (महिषो न (*mahiṣo na*)), the animal called buffalo, sharpening his two sharp horns (शृंगे (*śṛṃge*)); another comparison: like a hero (शूरो न (*śūro na*)) desiring abundant cows (गा गव्यन् (*gā gavyan*)). As the buffalo and the hero, when awakened, run swiftly, so he, of settling nature (सत्वा (*satvā*)), goes; the word "goes" is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*)—when pressed
- अर्वा (*arvā*)—swift-going
- एषः सोमः (*eṣaḥ somaḥ*)—this Soma
- सृष्टः (*sṛṣṭaḥ*)—let loose freely
- सर्गः न (*sargaḥ na*)—like a horse
- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—in the ten-fold filter
- परदधावत् (*paradadhāvat*)—runs **NOTE**
- तिग्मी (*tigmī*)—sharp **NOTE**
- शृंगे (*śṛṃge*)—horns
- शिशानः (*śiśānaḥ*)—which he has whetted
- महिषो न (*mahiṣo na*)—like a buffalo
- गा गव्यन् (*gā gavyan*)—desiring abundant cows
- शूरो न (*śūro na*)—like a hero
- सत्वा (*satvā*)—Soma who has attained a state, appears **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Swift-going Soma, when pressed, runs to the ten-fold filter like a horse let loose freely. When he has attained a state, he appears like a buffalo that has whetted its sharp horns and like a hero who desires abundant cows.

##### English translation
When effused, this quick-flowing Soma hastens to the filter like a steed let loose ; whilst alighting (he moves) like a buffalo sharpening his pointed horns, like a warrior on a foray for cattle.

### Printed p. 620

#### Ṛk 8

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒षा य॑यौ पर॒मादं॒तरद्रेः॒ कूचि॑त्स॒तीरू॒र्वे गा वि॑वेद ।  
> दि॒वो न वि॒द्युत्स्त॒नयं॑त्य॒भ्रैः सोम॑स्य ते पवत इंद्र॒ धारा॑ ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एषा । आ । ययौ । परमात् । अंतः । अद्रेः । कूऽचित् । सतीः । ऊर्वे । गाः । विवेद ।  
> दिवः । न । विऽद्युत् । स्तनयंती । अभ्रैः । सोमस्य । ते । पवते । इंद्र । धारा ॥ ८ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एषा सोमधारा परमात् उच्छ्रितात् स्थानात् ययौ जगाम पात्रं स्वयंप्राप्तव्यं देशं वा । किंच अद्रेः पणीनां निवासस्थानस्य पर्वतस्य अंतः कूचित् क्वचित् कुत्रचिद्गूढे ऊर्वे देशे सतीः वर्तमानाः पणिभिरपहृताः गाः विवेद लब्धवती । यत्र पणयो गा अपहृत्य  स्थापितवंतः स देश ऊर्वः। 'ऊर्वं गव्यं महि गृणानः' (ऋ. सं. ६,१७,१ ) इति हि मंत्रांतरम् । दिवो न विद्युत् दिवः सकाशाद्विद्युदिव स्तनयंती शब्दयंती । विद्युत् विशेष्यते । अभ्रैः प्रेरितेति शेषः । सा यथा शब्दं करोति तद्वच्छब्दं कुर्वती । सोमस्य संबंधिनी सेयं धारा हे इंद्र ते त्वदर्थं त्वत्पानाय पवते पूयते । क्षरति वा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This stream of Soma went (ययौ (*yayau*)) from the highest, lofty place to the vessel, or to the place to be reached of itself. Further, within the mountain (अद्रेः (*adreḥ*)), the dwelling place of the Paṇis, somewhere, in a hidden wide place (ऊर्वे (*ūrve*)), it found the cows (गाः (*gāḥ*)) that were there, stolen by the Paṇis. The place where the Paṇis stole the cows and put them is ऊर्वः (*ūrvaḥ*); for there is another mantra, ऊर्वं गव्यं महि गृणानः (*ūrvaṃ gavyaṃ mahi gṛṇānaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6,17,1). Sounding like lightning from heaven, sent forth by the clouds (that is to be supplied), as that makes a sound so this makes a sound. This stream, belonging to Soma, O Indra, is purified, or flows, for you, for your drinking.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- एषा (*eṣā*)—this stream of Soma
- परमात् (*paramāt*)—from the highest place
- युयौ (*yuyau*)—has come **NOTE**
- अद्रेः (*adreḥ*)—of the mountain
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—inside
- क्वचित् ऊर्वे (*kvacit ūrve*)—in a place that no one sees **NOTE**
- सतीः (*satīḥ*)—that were hidden
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- विवेद (*viveda*)—has found out
- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अभ्रैः (*abhraiḥ*)—impelled by the clouds
- विद्युत् (*vidyut*)—lightning
- स्तनयंती (*stanayaṃtī*)—sounding
- दिवो न (*divo na*)—as falling from the atmosphere
- सोमस्य (*somasya*)—of the Soma-juice
- धारा (*dhārā*)—the stream
- ते (*te*)—for you
- पवते (*pavate*)—flows

### Printed p. 621

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

This Soma-deity has come from a very high place. It has found the cows that were hidden in a place inside the mountain that no one sees. O Indra, like lightning impelled by the cloud, falling sounding from the atmosphere, the stream of the Soma-juice flows towards you.

##### English translation
This Soma stream has come from on high and has detected the cattle which were in a stall (hidden) somewhere within the mountain ; the stream of the Soma flows for you, Indra, thundering like lightning emitted by the clouds from heaven.

#### Ṛk 9

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त स्म॑ रा॒शिं परि॑ यासि॒ गोना॒मिंद्रे॑ण सोम स॒रथं॑ पुना॒नः ।  
> पू॒र्वीरिषो॑ बृह॒तीर्जी॑रदानो॒ शिक्षा॑ शचीव॒स्तव॒ ता उ॑प॒ष्टुत् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । स्म । राशिम् । परि । यासि । गोनाम् । इंद्रेण । सोम । सऽरथम् । पुनानः ।  
> पूर्वीः । इषः । बृहतीः । जीरदानो इति जीरऽदानो । शिक्ष । शचीऽवः । तव । ताः । उपऽस्तुत् ॥ ९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत स्म अपि च खलु हे सोम पुनानः पूयमानः गोनां गवां राशिं समूहं पणिभिरपहृतं परि यासि परिगच्छसि । कथंभूतः सन् उच्यते । इंद्रेण सह सरथम् एकमेव रथमास्थाय । हे जीरदानो क्षिप्रदान सोम उपस्तुत् उपस्तूयमानस्त्वं पूर्वीः बह्वीः बृहतीः महतीः इषः उक्तलक्षणान्यन्नानि शिक्ष देहि । हे शचीवः अन्नवन् ताः इषः तव स्वभूता इति शेषः ॥ ॥ २३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

And indeed, O Soma, being purified, you go round the herd (गोनां राशिं (*gonāṃ rāśiṃ*), the mass) of cows stolen by the Paṇis. In what manner? Riding together with Indra in one and the same chariot (सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)). O Soma, quick giver (जीरदानो (*jīradāno*)), being praised, give many (पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)) and great (बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)) foods (इषः (*iṣaḥ*)) of the kind stated. O शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*), possessor of food, those foods are your own, that is to be supplied.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who have attained purity
- इंद्रेण सह (*iṃdreṇa saha*)—together with Indra
- सरथं (*sarathaṃ*)—mounting one and the same chariot
- गोनां राशिं (*gonāṃ rāśiṃ*)—the herd of cows

### Printed p. 622

- परि यासि (*pari yāsi*)—you set out seeking
- जीरदानो (*jīradāno*)—O Soma-deva, who give quickly
- उपस्तुत् (*upastut*)—you who are praised by us
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—abundant
- बृहतीः (*bṛhatīḥ*)—and of great fruit
- इषः (*iṣaḥ*)—foods
- शिक्ष (*śikṣa*)—give
- शचीवः (*śacīvaḥ*)—O Soma, possessor of food
- ताति (*tāti*)—those foods **NOTE**
- तव (*tava*)—are your possessions

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who have attained purity set out seeking the herd of cows, mounting one and the same chariot together with Indra. O Soma-deva, who give quickly, you who are praised by us, give abundant foods of great fruit. O Soma, possessor of food, those foods are your possessions.

##### English translation
And being purified, Soma, you pursue the herd of (stolen) cattle in the same chariot with Indra ; O you who give quickly, give (us) when invoked plentiful and abundant viands, for they are your (property), O you who abund in food. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 88 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> 'अयं सोमः' इत्यष्टर्चं तृतीयं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । अयं सोमोऽष्टौ ' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The third sūkta, beginning अयं सोमः (*ayaṃ somaḥ*), has eight Ṛks. The seer and the rest are as before. The Anukramaṇikā is cited: अयं सोमोऽष्टौ (*ayaṃ somo 'ṣṭau*). The application (viniyoga) has been stated.

Anuvāda: This sūkta beginning अयं सोमः (*ayaṃ somaḥ*) is the third sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has eight Ṛks. The seer, deity and metre of this sūkta are the same as in the previous sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said: आयं सोमोऽष्टौ (*āyaṃ somo 'ṣṭau*). The application (viniyoga) has been stated before. **NOTE**

- Maṇḍala 9; Anuvāka 5; Sūkta 88
- Aṣṭaka 7; Adhyāya 3; Varga 24
- Number of Ṛks in the sūkta: 8
- Seer: उशनाः (*uśanāḥ*)
- Deity: पवमानः सोमः (*pavamānaḥ somaḥ*)
- Metre: त्रिष्टुप् (*triṣṭup*)

### Printed p. 623

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒यं सोम॑ इंद्र॒ तुभ्यं॑ सुन्वे॒ तुभ्यं॑ पवते॒ त्वम॑स्य पाहि ।  
> त्वं ह॒ यं च॑कृ॒षे त्वं व॑वृ॒ष इंदुं॒ मदा॑य॒ युज्या॑य॒ सोम॑म् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अयम् । सोमः । इंद्र । तुभ्यम् । सुन्वे । तुभ्यम् । पवते । त्वम् । अस्य । पाहि ।  
> त्वम् । ह । यम् । चकृषे । त्वम् । ववृषे । इंदुम् । मदाय । युज्याय । सोमम् ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंद्र अयं सोमः तुभ्यं त्वदर्थं सुन्वे सूयते ॥ सुनोतेः कर्मार्थे लटि ‘ लोपस्त आत्मनेपदेषु' इति तलोपः ॥ तुभ्यं त्वदर्थमेव पवते पूयते । त्वं च अस्य अमुं पाहि पिब । त्वं ह यम् इंदुं सोमं चकृषे करोषि । त्वं च यं ववृषे वृतवानसि । किमर्थम् । मदाय युज्याय सहायाय । सोम इंद्राय बलकरत्वात् सहाय इति प्रसिद्धम् । यमेवं करोषि त्वं तं पाहीति समन्वयः॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indra, this Soma is pressed (सुन्वे (*sunve*)) for you; for you alone it is purified. Drink it. That Indu, Soma, which you have made (चकृषे (*cakṛṣe*)) and which you have chosen (ववृषे (*vavṛṣe*)): for what purpose? For exhilaration (मदाय (*madāya*)) and for companionship (युज्याय (*yujyāya*), glossed as help). It is well known that Soma is a helper of Indra, because it gives strength. The construction is: drink him whom you thus treat.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंद्र (*iṃdra*)—O Indra
- अयं सोमः (*ayaṃ somaḥ*)—this Soma
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- सुन्वे (*sunve*)—is pressed
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—for you
- पवते (*pavate*)—is purified
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- इंदुं (*iṃduṃ*)—in the form of a stream
- यं सोमं (*yaṃ somaṃ*)—which Soma
- चकृषे (*cakṛṣe*)—you create
- मदाय (*madāya*)—for your joy
- युज्याय (*yujyāya*)—and for help
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- ववृषे (*vavṛṣe*)—which Soma you desire
- अस्य (*asya*)—such a Soma
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- पाहि (*pāhi*)—drink

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Indra, this Soma is pressed for you. It is purified for you. The Soma in the form of a stream, which you create, which you desire for your joy and for help, such a Soma drink.

##### English translation
This Soma is expressed ror you, Indra ; for you it is filtered ; drink of it ; it is the Indu Soma which you have made, which you have chosen for your exhilaration, your companion. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 624

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स ईं॒ रथो॒ न भु॑रि॒षाळ॑योजि म॒हः पु॒रूणि॑ सा॒तये॒ वसू॑नि ।  
> आदीं॒ विश्वा॑ नहु॒ष्या॑णि जा॒ता स्व॑र्षाता॒ वन॑ ऊ॒र्ध्वा न॑वंत ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । ईमिति । रथः । न । भुरिषाट् । अयोजि । महः । पुरूणि । सातये । वसूनि ।  
> आत् । ईमिति । विश्वा । नहुष्याणि । जाता । स्वःऽसाता । वने । ऊर्ध्वा । नवंत ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स ईं सोऽयं सोमः भुरिषाट् भूरिभारस्य सोढा रथो न रथ इव भुरिषाट्  प्रभूतस्य भारस्य सोढा अयोजि युज्यते । कीदृशः सः । महः महान् । किमर्थमयोजि । पुरूणि बहूनि वसूनि धनानि सातये अस्मभ्यं दातुम् । आदीं योगानंतरं विश्वा विश्वानि सर्वाणि नहुष्याणि । नहुषो मनुष्याः । तेषां संबंधीनि जाता जातान्यस्मद्विरोधीनि ऊर्ध्वा उन्मुखानि वने वननीये स्वर्षाता स्वर्षातौ । संग्रामनामैतत् । स्वर्गलाभयुक्ते संग्रामे नवंत गच्छंतु । नवतिर्गतिकर्मा । यद्वा। सोमं संग्रामे युद्धार्थिनः संगच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma, like a chariot that bears a heavy load (भुरिषाट् (*bhuriṣāṭ*), the bearer of much burden), is yoked (अयोजि (*ayoji*)). Of what kind? Great. For what purpose is he yoked? To give us many riches (सातये (*sātaye*)). After the yoking, let all (विश्वा (*viśvā*)) the born (जाता (*jātā*)) belonging to men (नहुष्याणि (*nahuṣyāṇi*); नहुषो मनुष्याः (*nahuṣo manuṣyāḥ*), that is, men), who are hostile to us, looking upward (ऊर्ध्वा (*ūrdhvā*), with faces turned up), go (नवंत (*navaṃta*); the root नवति (*navati*) is in the sense of going) to the desirable (वने (*vane*)) battle (स्वर्षाता (*svarṣātā*) is a name of battle) that brings the gain of heaven. Or else, those who seek battle assemble at Soma in the battle.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- महः (*mahaḥ*)—the great one
- सईं (*saīṃ*)—that same Soma **NOTE**
- भूरिषाट् (*bhūriṣāṭ*)—which bears a heavy burden **NOTE**
- रथो न (*ratho na*)—like a chariot
- पुरूणि (*purūṇi*)—abundant
- वसूनि (*vasūni*)—riches
- सातये (*sātaye*)—to give us
- अयोजि (*ayoji*)—is yoked
- आदीं (*ādīṃ*)—immediately after
- नहुष्याणि (*nahuṣyāṇi*)—in the group of men
- जाता (*jātā*)—born
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all our enemies
- ऊर्ध्वा (*ūrdhvā*)—facing us
- वने (*vane*)—which gives enthusiasm
- स्वर्षाता (*svarṣātā*)—in the battle
- नवंत (*navaṃta*)—let them come and join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The great Soma is appointed to give us abundant riches, like a chariot that bears a heavy burden. Immediately after, let all our enemies, born in the group of men, come and join, facing us, in the battle that gives enthusiasm.

### Printed p. 625

##### English translation
It has been harnessed like a great wagon that bears heavy burdens in order to bring us many treasures ; after this may all the races of men expecting our (attack) go to the desirable battle.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वा॒युर्न यो नि॒युत्वाँ॑ इ॒ष्टया॑मा॒ नास॑त्येव॒ हव॒ आ शंभ॑विष्ठः ।  
> वि॒श्ववा॑रो द्रविणो॒दा इ॑व॒ त्मन्पू॒षेव॑ धी॒जव॑नोऽसि सोम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> वायुः । न । यः । नियुत्वान् । इष्टऽयामा । नासत्याऽइव । हवे । आ । शम्ऽभविष्ठः ।  
> विश्वऽवारः । द्रविणोदाःऽइव । त्मन् । पूषाऽइव । धीऽजवनः । असि । सोम ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यः सोमः नियुत्वान् । नियुतो वायोरश्वाः । तद्वान् वायुर्न वायुरिव इष्टयामा इष्टगमनः । नासत्येव अश्विनाविव हवम् आह्वानमाकर्ण्य आ सर्वतः शंभविष्ठः सुखस्य भावयितृतमः । द्रविणोदाइव धनदातेव' त्मन् आत्मनि विश्ववारः विश्वैर्वरणीयो भवति तद्वद्विश्ववारोऽसि । पूषेव पोषकः सवितेव धीजवनः मनोवेगः असि । यद्वा कर्मणां प्रवर्तयितासि हे सोम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Soma who has the नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*), the horses of Vāyu, like Vāyu, is of desired going (इष्टयामा (*iṣṭayāmā*)). Like the Aśvins (नासत्येव (*nāsatyeva*)), hearing the invocation (हवम् (*havam*)), he is on every side the greatest producer of happiness (शंभविष्ठः (*śaṃbhaviṣṭhaḥ*)). As a giver of wealth is to be chosen by all in himself (त्मन् (*tman*)), so you are विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*), chosen by all. Like Pūṣan (पूषेव (*pūṣeva*)), the nourisher, like Savitṛ, you are swift as thought (धीजवनः (*dhījavanaḥ*), having the speed of the mind). Or else you, O Soma, are the one who sets the rites in motion.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you who
- नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*)—possessing the horses called Niyut
- वायुर्न (*vāyurna*)—like Vāyu
- इष्टयामा (*iṣṭayāmā*)—of free movement
- नासत्येव (*nāsatyeva*)—like the Aśvin-devatās
- हवं (*havaṃ*)—hearing our invocation
- आ (*ā*)—everywhere
- शंभविष्यः (*śaṃbhaviṣyaḥ*)—the giver of happiness **NOTE**
- द्रविणोदाइव (*draviṇodāiva*)—like a giver of wealth
- त्मन् (*tman*)—you yourself
- विश्ववारः (*viśvavāraḥ*)—desired by all
- पूषेव (*pūṣeva*)—like Savitṛ, the nourisher of the world
- धीजवनः (*dhījavanaḥ*)—having the speed of the mind
- असि (*asi*)—you are

### Printed p. 626

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you are like Vāyu with his horses called Niyut, of unimpeded movement; like the Aśvin deities, hearing our invocation, you give happiness everywhere; like a giver of wealth, you are desired by all; and like Savitṛ, the nourisher of the world, you are swift as the mind.

##### English translation
You, Soma, who like Vayu with his Niyut steeds go where you list,
who like the Nasatyas on hearing the invocation grant abundant felicity,
you are of yourself desired by all like the giver of wealth, you are like Pushan,
swift as thought.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इंद्रो॒ न यो म॒हा कर्मा॑णि॒ चक्रि॑र्हं॒ता वृ॒त्राणा॑मसि सोम पू॒र्भित् ।  
> पै॒द्वो न हि त्वमहि॑नाम्नां हं॒ता विश्व॑स्यासि सोम॒ दस्योः॑ ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इंद्रः । न । यः । महा । कर्माणि । चक्रिः । हंता । वृत्राणाम् । असि । सोम । पूःऽभित् ।  
> पैद्वः । न । हि । त्वम् । अहिऽनाम्नाम् । हंता । विश्वस्य । असि । सोम । दस्योः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> इंद्रो न इंद्र इव यः त्वं महा महांति कर्माणि चक्रिः ताच्छील्येन करोषि स त्वं हे सोम वृत्राणां शत्रूणां हंता असि भवसि । तथा पूर्भित् पुरां भेत्तासि । किंच पैद्वो न अश्व इव खलु अहिनाम्नां हंता भवसि । आगत्य हंतीत्यहिः । तन्नामकानामित्यर्थः । न केवलं तेषामेव अपि तु विश्वस्य अपि सर्वस्यापि दस्योः उपक्षपयितुः शत्रोर्हंता असि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Like Indra, you who habitually perform great acts are, O Soma, the slayer of the Vṛtras, that is, of enemies; likewise you are the splitter of cities. Further, like a horse of Paidva, you are the slayer of those called Ahi (one who comes and strikes is Ahi; the meaning is: those so named). Not only of these, but of every Dasyu, the destroyer, the enemy, you are the slayer.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- यः (*yaḥ*)—you
- इंदो न (*iṃdo na*)—like Indra **NOTE**
- महा कर्माणि (*mahā karmāṇi*)—great acts
- चक्रिः (*cakriḥ*)—you are the doer
- वृत्राणां (*vṛtrāṇāṃ*)—of enemies

### Printed p. 627

- हंता (*haṃtā*)—as the destroyer
- असि (*asi*)—you are
- पूर्भित् (*pūrbhit*)—you split the enemy cities
- पैद्वो न (*paidvo na*)—like the horse of Pedu
- अहिनाम्यां (*ahināmyāṃ*)—of the demons called Ahi **NOTE**
- हंता (*haṃtā*)—you are the destroyer
- त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you
- विश्वस्य दस्योः (*viśvasya dasyoḥ*)—as the destroyer of every Dasyu
- असि (*asi*)—you are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, like Indra you are the doer of great deeds. You are the destroyer of enemies. You split the cities of the enemy. Like the horse of Pedu, you are the destroyer of the demons called Ahi. You are also the destroyer of every Dasyu.

##### English translation
You, Soma, who like Indra perform mighty acts, are the slayer of the
Vritras, the destroyer of strong-holds ; like the horse of Pedu you are the
slayer of those who are called serpents ; you are the slayer of every Dasyu.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒ग्निर्न यो वन॒ आ सृ॒ज्यमा॑नो॒ वृथा॒ पाजां॑सि कृणुते न॒दीषु॑ ।  
> जनो॒ न युध्वा॑ मह॒त उ॑प॒ब्दिरिय॑र्ति॒ सोमः॒ पव॑मान ऊ॒र्मिम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अग्निः । न । यः । वने । आ । सृज्यमानः । वृथा । पाजांसि । कृणुते । नदीषु ।  
> जनः । न । युध्वा । महतः । उपब्दिः । इयर्ति । सोमः । पवमानः । ऊर्मिम् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अग्निर्न अग्निरिव यः सोमः वने अरण्ये आ सृज्यमानः वनसंबंध्यग्निर्यथा बलानि कुरुते' एवं यः सोमः वृथा अनायासेन नदीषु आंतरिक्षाणि पाजांसि कृणुते कुरुते । किंच युध्वा युद्धस्य कत जनो न शूरो मनुष्य इव महतः शत्रोः उपब्दिः । वाङ्नामैतत् । शब्दयिता सन् पवमानः पूयमानः सोमः ऊर्मिं प्रवृद्धं रसम् इयर्ति प्रेरयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma is like Agni, let loose in the forest: as a fire of the forest makes its forces, so Soma, without effort, makes his powers in the rivers, that is, in the waters of the atmosphere. Further, like a man, a warrior, who fights, being a sounder (the word उपब्दिः (*upabdiḥ*) is a name of speech) against a mighty enemy, Soma, being purified, urges on the wave, that is, the swollen juice. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 628

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यः (*yaḥ*)—Soma
- वने (*vane*)—in the forest
- आ सृज्यमानः (*ā sṛjyamānaḥ*)—placed freely
- अग्निः न (*agniḥ na*)—like fire
- उपब्धिः (*upabdhiḥ*)—making a sound **NOTE**
- महतः (*mahataḥ*)—facing a mighty enemy
- युध्वा (*yudhvā*)—who fights
- जनो न (*jano na*)—like a hero
- वृथा (*vṛthā*)—without effort
- नदीषु (*nadīṣu*)—in the atmospheric regions
- पाजांसि (*pājāṃsi*)—his powers
- कृणुते (*kṛṇute*)—he manifests
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—purified
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)—the juice that is like a wave
- इयर्ति (*iyarti*)—he urges on

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like fire let loose freely in the forest, and like a hero who, shouting, faces a mighty enemy and fights, Soma without effort manifests his powers in the atmosphere. The purified Soma makes his wave-like juice flow.

##### English translation
Soma who, like Agni let loose in a forest, easily manifests his might in
the waters like a man who fights shouting against his mighty (foe)—so Soma
when purified urges on his wave.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒ते सोमा॒ अति॒ वारा॒ण्यव्या॑ दि॒व्या न कोशा॑सो अ॒भ्रव॑र्षाः ।  
> वृथा॑ समु॒द्रं सिंध॑वो॒ न नीचीः॑ सु॒तासो॑ अ॒भि क॒लशाँ॑ असृग्रन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एते । सोमाः । अति । वाराणि । अव्या । दिव्या । न । कोशासः । अभ्रऽवर्षाः ।  
> वृथा । समुद्रम् । सिंधवः । न । नीचीः । सुतासः । अभि । कलशान् । असृग्रन् ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> एते पूयमानाः सोमाः अव्या अविमयानि वाराणि वालानि अति गच्छंतीति शेषः । तत्र दृष्टांतः । दिव्या न कोशासः दिवि भवाः कोशा आप इव । ता विशेष्यंते । अभ्रवर्षाः अभ्रैर्वृष्यमाणाः । किंच वृथा अनायासेन समुद्रं सिंधवो न नद्य इव नीचीः नीचीनाग्राः सुतासः अभिषुताः सोमाः कलशान् अभि असृग्रन् अभिगच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These Soma-juices, being purified, pass over the woollen fibres, the hairs made of wool (the verb "pass over" is to be supplied). The illustration: like the heavenly streams, that is, the waters that are in heaven; these are qualified as showered by clouds, rained down by the clouds. Further, without effort, like rivers going to the ocean with their fronts turned downward, the pressed Soma-juices go towards the vessels.

### Printed p. 629

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अभ्रवर्षाः (*abhravarṣāḥ*)—showered by the clouds
- दिव्याः (*divyāḥ*)—born in the heavenly world **NOTE**
- कोशासः न (*kośāsaḥ na*)—like streams of rain
- एते सोमाः (*ete somāḥ*)—these streams of Soma
- अव्या वाराणि (*avyā vārāṇi*)—the woollen fibres of the ten-fold filter
- अति (गच्छंति) (*ati (gacchaṃti)*)—they pass over
- नीचीः (*nīcīḥ*)—flowing in low-lying regions
- सिंधवः (*siṃdhavaḥ*)—rivers
- वृथा (*vṛthā*)—without effort
- समुद्रं न (*samudraṃ na*)—as they enter the ocean
- सुतासः (*sutāsaḥ*)—pressed Soma-juices
- कलशान् अभि (*kalaśān abhi*)—into the Droṇa vessels
- अस्यग्रन् (*asyagran*)—they enter **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Like streams of rain showered by the clouds and born in the heavenly world, these streams of Soma pass over the woollen fibres of the ten-fold filter. As rivers flowing in low-lying regions enter the ocean without effort, the pressed Soma-juices enter the Droṇa vessels.

##### English translation
These Soma-juices pass through the woollen fleece, like the rains of heaven showered by the clouds; the effused juices flow promptly to the pitchers as rivers running downwards (flow) into the ocean.

#### Ṛk 7

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> शु॒ष्मी शर्धो॒ न मारु॑तं पव॒स्वान॑भिशस्ता दि॒व्या यथा॒ विट् ।  
> आपो॒ न म॒क्षू सु॑म॒तिर्भ॑वा नः स॒हस्रा॑प्साः पृतना॒षाण्न य॒ज्ञः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शुष्मी । शर्धः । न । मारुतम् । पवस्व । अनभिऽशस्ता । दिव्या । यथा । विट् ।  
> आपः । न । मक्षु । सुऽमतिः । भव । नः । सहस्रऽअप्साः । पृतनाषाट् । न । यज्ञः ॥ ७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम शुष्मी । शुष्मं बलं शोषणात् । बलवांस्त्वं मारुतं शर्धो न मरुतां बलमिव पवस्व । तत्र दृष्टांतमेव स्पष्टयति । यथा दिव्या विट् प्रजा अनभिशस्ता । अभिशासो निंदा । अनिंदिता पवते । ‘ मरुतो वै देवानां विशः '(तै. सं. २. २. ५, ७) इति हि ब्राह्मणम् । किंच आपो न उदकानीव मक्षु क्षिप्रं पवमानस्त्वं सुमतिः भव नः अस्माकम् । किंच सहस्राप्साः। अप्स इति रूपनाम । बहुरूपस्त्वं पृतनाषाट् पृतनानामभिभवितेंद्र इव यज्ञः यष्टव्यो भवसीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, you are powerful (śuṣma is strength, so called from drying up); being strong, flow like the might of the Maruts. He makes the illustration clear: as the heavenly folk are blameless (abhiśāsa is censure, so the uncensured folk) and flow; for the Brāhmaṇa says मरुतो वै देवानां विशः (*maruto vai devānāṃ viśaḥ*) (Tai. Saṃ. 2. 2. 5, 7). Further, like waters, being purified, be quickly well-disposed towards us. Further, you are of a thousand forms (apsa is a name for form), of many forms; you are the overcomer of battles, like Indra, and you are to be worshipped.

- शुष्मी (*śuṣmī*)—endowed with strength
- दिव्या विट् यथा (*divyā viṭ yathā*)—like the folk of the heavenly world
- अनभिशस्ता (*anabhiśastā*)—blameless
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow

- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- नः (*naḥ*)—in regard to us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, flow endowed with strength like the host of the Maruts, and blameless like the folk of the heavenly world. Like water, quickly be of a gracious mind towards us. You who have many forms are, like Indra, worthy of worship.

Flow strong as the army of the Maruts, like the divine blameless folk ;

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम वरुणस्य वारकस्य ते तव व्रतानि कर्माणि नु क्षिप्रं करोमीति शेषः । हे सोम तव धाम तेजःस्थानं बृहत् महत् गभीरं च । प्रियः मित्रः इव त्वं शुचिः दीप्तः शुद्धो वा असि । अर्यमेव अर्यमा देव इव त्वं दक्षाय्यः असि ॥ ॥ २४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, of you, the restrainer Varuṇa, the vratas, that is, the rites: "I quickly perform" is to be supplied. O Soma, your abode, the place of radiance, is vast and deep. Like a dear friend (Mitra), you are bright or pure. Like Aryaman, the god, you are दक्षाय्यः (*dakṣāyyaḥ*). **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, your deeds, as lord, are as great as the deeds of Varuṇa. O Soma-deva, your abode is vast and deep. Like a dear friend you are radiant, and like the god Aryaman you are generous.

##### English translation
Your acts are (like) those of the royal Varuna, vast and profound,
Soma, is your abode ; you are pure as the beloved Mitra, munificent are you,
Soma, as Aryaman.

## Sūkta 89 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘प्रो स्य वह्निः' इति सप्तर्चं चतुर्थं सूक्तम् । ऋष्याद्याः पूर्ववत् । ‘प्रो स्य सप्त' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्रो स्य वह्निः (*pro sya vahniḥ*) has seven Ṛks and is the fourth sūkta. The seer and the other particulars are as before. It is recorded in the Anukramaṇī as प्रो स्य सप्त (*pro sya sapta*). The viniyoga has been stated.

Anuvāda— This sūkta beginning प्रो स्य वह्निं (*pro sya vahniṃ*) is the fourth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has seven Ṛks. The seer, deity and metre of this sūkta are the same as in the preceding sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated as प्रो स्य सप्त (*pro sya sapta*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

### Printed p. 632

Sūkta 89. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 89. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 3, Varga 25. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 7. Seer: Uśanā. Deity: Pavamāna Soma **NOTE**. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्रो स्य वह्निः॑ प॒थ्या॑भिरस्यांदि॒वो न वृ॒ष्टिः पव॑मानो अक्षाः ।  
> स॒हस्र॑धारो असद॒न्न्य१॒॑स्मे मा॒तुरु॒पस्थे॒ वन॒ आ च॒ सोमः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्रो इति । स्यः । वह्निः । पथ्याभिः । अस्यान् । दिवः । न । वृष्टिः । पवमानः । अक्षारिति ।  
> सहस्रऽधारः । असदत् । नि । अस्मे इति । मातुः । उपऽस्थे । वने । आ । च । सोमः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र ऊ इति निपातद्वयसमुदाय एको निपातितः । प्रो अस्यान् प्रस्यंदते स्यः सः वह्निः वोढा पथ्याभिः यज्ञमार्गैः । दिवो न वृष्टिः दिवः सकाशात् वृष्टिरिव पवमानः पूयमानः सन् अक्षाः व्याप्नोषि । सोऽयं सोमः सहस्रधारः बहुधारः सन् अस्मे अस्मासु नि असदत् निषीदति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The two particles pra and ū are joined into one by nipātana. That Soma, the bearer (the carrier), flows forth by the paths of the sacrifice. Like rain from heaven, being purified, you pervade. This Soma, thousand-streamed, that is, many-streamed, sits down among us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—the one who bears the burden
- स्यः (*syaḥ*)—Soma
- पथ्याभिः (*pathyābhiḥ*)—by the paths of sacrifice
- प्रो अस्यान् (*pro asyān*)—he flows forth
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—O Soma, you who have attained purity
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—falling from the atmosphere
- वृष्टिः न (*vṛṣṭiḥ na*)—like rain
- अक्षाः (*akṣāḥ*)—you pervade
- सहस्रधारः (*sahasradhāraḥ*)—having many kinds of streams
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- वने (*vane*)—in the water
- मातुः उपस्थे (*mātuḥ upasthe*)—on the lap of his mother
- अस्मे (*asme*)—among us
- न्यासदत् (*nyāsadat*)—he sits **NOTE**

### Printed p. 633

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma who bears the burden flows forth by the paths of the sacrifice. O Soma, you who have attained purity pervade like rain falling from the atmosphere. Soma-deva, with many kinds of streams, sits among us in the water, on the lap of his mother.

##### English translation
This horse of burden moves forth by the (sacrificial) paths ; when purified you flow like the rain from heaven ; the thousand-streamed Soma sits down amongst us on his mother's lap in the water.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> राजा॒ सिंधू॑नामवसिष्ट॒ वास॑ ऋ॒तस्य॒ नाव॒मारु॑ह॒द्रजि॑ष्ठाम् ।  
> अ॒प्सु द्र॒प्सो वा॑वृधे श्ये॒नजू॑तो दु॒ह ईं॑ पि॒ता दु॒ह ईं॑ पि॒तुर्जाम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> राजा । सिंधूनाम् । अवसिष्ट । वासः । ऋतस्य । नावम् । आ । अरुहत् । रजिष्ठाम् ।  
> अप्ऽसु । द्रप्सः । ववृधे । श्येनऽजूतः । दुहे । ईम् । पिता । दुहे । ईम् । पितुः । जाम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं राजा सोमः सिंधूनाम् उदकानां क्षीरादिस्यंदिनीनां गवां वा वासः वसनस्थानीयं क्षीराख्यं श्रयणद्रव्यम् अवसिष्ट आच्छादयति । तथा कृत्वा रजिष्ठाम् ऋजुतराम् ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य नावमारुहत् आरोहति । सः द्रप्सः सोमरसः श्येनजूतः श्येनेनापहृतो रसः अप्सु वसतीवरीषु ववृधे वर्धते। ईं तमिमं पितुः पालकात् पितृस्थानीयात् द्युलोकात् जां जातमपत्यं सोमम् ईम् अयं पिता पालको लोकः दुहे दोग्धि रसम् । तथाध्वर्युरपि दुहे दोग्धि । अथवा । उक्तलक्षणमेतं सोमं पिता पालकः स्वामी यजमानो दोग्धि फलं तथा दुहेऽध्वर्युरपि रसं दुहे। यद्वा । दुह ईमिति पुनरुक्तिरादरार्था ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This king Soma puts on, covers himself with, the garment of the rivers, that is, of the waters, or of the cows that flow with milk and so on: the mixing substance called milk, which stands as a garment. Having done so, he mounts the straightest ship of the ṛta, the sacrifice. That drop, the Soma juice, brought by the falcon, grows in the waters, the Vasatīvarī waters. Him, the child born of the father, the protecting world of heaven, this father, the protecting world, milks, that is, milks out the juice; so also the Adhvaryu milks. Or else: the father, the protector, the master, the sacrificer, milks this Soma of the stated character, that is, the fruit; and in the same way the Adhvaryu milks out the juice. Or else: the repetition दुह ईमिति (*duha īmiti*) is for emphasis.

- राजा (*rājā*)—Soma-deva, the lord
- सिंधूनां (*siṃdhūnāṃ*)—of the flowing milk and the rest
- वासः (*vāsaḥ*)—the mixing substances that are like a covering
- अवसिष्ट (*avasiṣṭa*)—he has put on

- रजिष्ठां (*rajiṣṭhāṃ*)—of straight course
- नावं (*nāvaṃ*)—the boat
- अरुहत् (*aruhat*)—he has ascended
- श्येनजूतः (*śyenajūtaḥ*)—brought by the falcon
- द्रप्पः (*drappaḥ*)—the Soma juice **NOTE**
- अप्सु (*apsu*)—in the Vasatīvarī waters and the rest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The lord Soma-deva is mixed with the mixing substances, like a covering, of the flowing milk and the rest. He has ascended the boat of the sacrifice, of straight course. The Soma juice brought by the falcon grows in the Vasatīvarī waters and the rest. This world milks the juice from the Soma born of the protecting world of heaven.

##### English translation
The sovereign Soma has put on the vestment of the waters, he has ascended the most straight-going ship of sacrifice ; the dripping juice brought by the falcon has increased in the waters ; the father milks him--milks him the son of the father.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सिं॒हं न॑संत॒ मध्वो॑ अ॒यासं॒ हरि॑मरु॒षं दि॒वो अ॒स्य पति॑म् ।

> शूरः । युत्ऽसु । प्रथमः । पृच्छते । गाः । अस्य । चक्षसा । परि । पाति । उक्षा ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 635

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सिंहं शत्रूणां हिंसकं सिंहसदृशं मध्वः उदकस्य अयासं प्रेरकं हरिं हरितवर्णम् अस्य दिवः द्युलोकस्य पतिं पालकं सोमं नसंत व्याप्नुवंति यजमानाः। युत्सु संग्रामेषु शूरः प्रथमः देवानां मध्ये मुख्यः सोमः गाः पणिभिरपहृताः पृच्छते मार्गज्ञान् । पणीन् हत्वा गा लब्धुं गोमार्गं पृच्छतीत्यर्थः । किंच अस्य चक्षसा सामर्थ्येन उक्षा सेक्ता देवेंद्रः परि पाति विश्वम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma is the lion, the destroyer of enemies, like a lion; the impeller of the water (madhu); the green-coloured; the lord, the protector, of this world of heaven. The sacrificers reach him. In battles Soma, the hero, first, that is, chief among the gods, asks after the cows carried off by the Paṇis, asks those who know the way: the meaning is that, having slain the Paṇis, he asks for the cows' path in order to obtain the cows. Further, by his sight, that is, by his power, the sprinkler, Devendra, protects the universe.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*)—golden-hued (attractive)
- अस्य दिवः (*asya divaḥ*)—of this world of heaven
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—the protector
- सिंहं (*siṃhaṃ*)—of the nature of a lion to enemies
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—to the sweet water
- अयासं (*ayāsaṃ*)—the impeller
- हरिं (*hariṃ*)—the Soma-deva who is of green colour
- नसंत (*nasaṃta*)—the sacrificers approach
- युत्सु (*yutsu*)—in battles
- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—valiant
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—chief among the gods; this Soma
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the cows
- पृच्छते (*pṛcchate*)—seeks (tries to learn the path of the cows)
- अस्य (*asya*)—of this Soma
- चक्षसा (*cakṣasā*)—by the power
- उक्षा (*ukṣā*)—Indra, the giver of what is desired
- परि पाति (*pari pāti*)—protects the world

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificers approach Soma-deva, who is attractive and golden-hued, the protector of the world of heaven, of the nature of a lion to enemies, the impeller of the sweet water, and green-coloured. Soma, who is valiant in battles and chief among the gods, asks in order to learn the path of the cows. By the power of this Soma, Indra, the giver of what is desired, protects the world.

##### English translation
(The worshippers) reach the lion-like (Soma) the dispenser of water, green-tinted, red, the protector of this heaven ; a hero in battles, first (among the gods) he seeks the (stolen) cows; by his might the sprinkler (Indra) protects (the universe).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> मधु॑पृष्ठं घो॒रम॒यास॒मश्वं॒ रथे॑ युंजंत्युरुच॒क्र ऋ॒ष्वम् ।  
> स्वसा॑र ईं जा॒मयो॑ मर्जयंति॒ सना॑भयो वा॒जिन॑मूर्जयंति ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 636

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> मधुऽपृष्ठम् । घोरम् । अयासम् । अश्वम् । रथे । युंजंति । उरुऽचक्रे । ऋष्वम् ।  
> स्वसारः । ईम् । जामयः । मर्जयंति । सऽनाभयः । वाजिनम् । ऊर्जयंति ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मधुपृष्ठं मधुरपृष्ठभागं घोरं भयानकम् अयासं गंतारम् ऋष्वं दर्शनीयमुक्तलक्षणाश्वस्थानीयं व्याप्तं सोमम् उरुचक्रे प्रभूतचक्रे रथे यथाश्वं रथे युंजंति रथिकास्तद्वत् प्रभूतचरणे रथे रंहस्य साधने यज्ञाख्ये रथे युंजंति । योजयंत्यध्वर्य्वादयः । किंच ईम् एनं सोमं स्वसारः स्वयंसारिण्यः परस्परं स्वसृभूता वा जामयः बंधुभूता अंगुलयः । एकहस्तनिष्पन्नत्वात् स्वसृत्वं जामित्वं च । एवंभूताः मार्जयंति शोधयंति । तदेवाह । सनाभयः समानबंधनाः वाजिनं बलवंतं सोमम् ऊर्जयंति बलिनं कुर्वंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, with a honeyed (sweet) back, terrible, a goer, ṛṣva (beautiful), pervading, standing in the place of a horse of the stated character: as charioteers yoke a horse to a broad-wheeled car, so the Adhvaryu and the others yoke him to the car called the sacrifice, which has many feet and is the means of speed. Further, the fingers, which move of themselves, or are sisters to one another, and are kinsfolk (being produced from one hand they are sisters and kin), cleanse this Soma. He says the same: the fingers, having a common bond, invigorate the strong Soma, make him strong.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मधुपृष्ठः (*madhupṛṣṭhaḥ*)—having a back of the form of water **NOTE**
- घोरं (*ghoraṃ*)—terrible
- अयासं (*ayāsaṃ*)—swift-going
- ऋष्टं (*ṛṣṭaṃ*)—attractive; the horse in the form of Soma **NOTE**
- उरुचक्रे (*urucakre*)—with wide wheels
- रथे (*rathe*)—in the car in the form of the sacrifice
- युंजंति (*yuṃjaṃti*)—the priests yoke
- जामयति (*jāmayati*)—kindred **NOTE**
- स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—the fingers
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Soma
- मार्जयंति (*mārjayaṃti*)—they purify
- सनाभयः (*sanābhayaḥ*)—these fingers, with equal kinship
- वाजिनं (*vājinaṃ*)—the Soma endowed with strength
- ऊर्जयंति (*ūrjayaṃti*)—they make strong

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The horse in the form of Soma, having a back of the form of water, terrible, swift-going and attractive, the priests yoke in the car called the sacrifice, which has wide wheels. The fingers, who are kinsfolk, purify this Soma. These fingers, with equal kinship, make the Soma endowed with strength strong.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> चत॑स्र ईं घृत॒दुहः॑ सचंते समा॒ने अं॒तर्ध॒रुणे॒ निष॑त्ताः ।  
> ता ई॑मर्षंति॒ नम॑सा पुना॒नास्ता ईं॑ वि॒श्वतः॒ परि॑ षंति पू॒र्वीः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> चतस्रः । ईम् । घृतऽदुहः । सचंते । समाने । अंतः । धरुणे । निऽसत्ताः ।  
> ताः । ईम् । अर्षंति । नमसा । पुनानाः । ताः । ईम् । विश्वतः । परि । संति । पूर्वीः ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> चतस्रः घृतदुहः घृतदोग्ध्र्यो गावः ईम एनं सोमं सचंते सेवंते । कीदृश्यस्ताः । समाने एकस्मिन् धरुणे सर्वेषां धारकेऽंतरिक्षे निषत्ताः निषण्णाः । ताः घृतदुहः ईम एनम् अर्षंति प्राप्नुवंति नमसा अन्नेन पुनानाः पूयमानाः सत्यः। ताः पूर्वीः बह्व्यः प्रभूता गावः विश्वतः सर्वतः परि षंति परिभवंति ॥  विष्टंभो दिवो धुरुणः पृथिव्या विश्व उत क्षितयो हस्ते अस्य ।

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Four ghee-milking cows serve this Soma. How are they? Seated in the one supporter of all, the atmosphere. Those ghee-milking cows reach him, being purified by namas, that is, by food. Those many cows, numerous, surround him on all sides. The block continues with विष्टंभो दिवो धुरुणः पृथिव्या विश्व उत क्षितयो हस्ते अस्य । (*viṣṭaṃbho divo dhuruṇaḥ pṛthivyā viśva uta kṣitayo haste asya |*) **GLOSS** **NOTE**

- घृतदुहः (*ghṛtaduhaḥ*)—that milk ghee
- चतस्रः (*catasraḥ*)—the four cows
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Soma
- सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—they serve
- पुनानाः (*punānāḥ*)—having attained purity
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—they
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Soma
- नमसा (*namasā*)—with food
- अर्षंति (*arṣaṃti*)—they approach
- पूर्वीः (*pūrvīḥ*)—numerous
- ताः (*tāḥ*)—they
- विश्वतः (*viśvataḥ*)—on all sides
- परि षंति (*pari ṣaṃti*)—they stand surrounding

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The four cows that milk ghee, seated in the atmosphere, the one supporter of the whole world, serve this Soma. Having attained purity, they approach this Soma with food. Numerous, they stand surrounding on all sides.

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वि॒ष्टं॒भो दि॒वो ध॒रुणः॑ पृथि॒व्या विश्वा॑ उ॒त क्षि॒तयो॒ हस्ते॑ अस्य ।  
> अस॑त्त॒ उत्सो॑ गृण॒ते नि॒युत्वा॒न्मध्वो॑ अं॒शुः प॑वत इंद्रि॒याय॑ ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> विष्टंभः । दिवः । धरुणः । पृथिव्याः । विश्वाः । उत । क्षितयः । हस्ते । अस्य ।  
> असत् । ते । उत्सः । गृणते । नियुत्वान् । मध्वः । अंशुः । पवते । इंद्रियाय ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अयं सोमः दिवः द्युलोकस्य विष्टंभभूतः । यथा गृहस्थ स्तंभस्तद्वत्। तथा पृथिव्याः धरुणः धारकः । उत अपि च विश्वाः सर्वाः क्षितयः प्रजाः अस्य सोमस्य हस्ते भवंति । उत्सः । उत्सरंत्यस्मात् कामा इत्युत्सः सोमः। सः गृणते स्तुवते ते तुभ्यं नियुत्वान् अश्ववान् असत् भवतु । स सोमः मध्वः मधु । कर्मणि षष्ठी । मधुररसः अंशुः सोमः । ‘ अंशुः शमष्टमात्रो भवति' (निरु. २. ५) इति यास्कः । इंद्रियाय पवते पूयते अभिषूयते ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

This Soma is the prop of heaven, the world of Dyu: as a pillar is to a house, so he is the supporter of the earth. Also all beings, the subjects, are in the hand of this Soma. Utsa: that from which desires gush forth, so Soma is Utsa. May he, possessed of horses, be so for you who praise. That Soma is sweet (madhu; the genitive is in the sense of the object), the sweet-flavoured filament, Soma. Yāska says: अंशुः शमष्टमात्रो भवति (*aṃśuḥ śamaṣṭamātro bhavati*) (Ni. 2. 5) **GLOSS** He is pressed, purified, for strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विष्टंभः (*viṣṭaṃbhaḥ*)—is the support
- पृथिव्याः (*pṛthivyāḥ*)—to the earth
- धरुणः (*dharuṇaḥ*)—the upholder
- अस्य हस्ते (*asya haste*)—in the power of this Soma-deva
- विश्वाः क्षितयः (*viśvāḥ kṣitayaḥ*)—all beings are
- उत्सः (*utsaḥ*)—Soma, the showerer of desires
- गृणते (*gṛṇate*)—who praise
- ते (*te*)—to you, to give
- नियुत्वान् (*niyutvān*)—possessed of horses
- असत् (*asat*)—let him be
- मध्वः (*madhvaḥ*)—of sweet juice
- अंशुः (*aṃśuḥ*)—Soma
- इंद्रियाय (*iṃdriyāya*)—for increase of strength
- पवते (*pavate*)—is pressed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva is the support of the world of heaven and the upholder of the earth. All beings are in the power of this Soma-deva. May Soma, the showerer of desires, be possessed of horses in order to give to you who praise. Soma of the sweet juice is pressed for increase of strength.

## Sūkta 90 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र हिन्वान इति षडृचं पंचमं सूक्तं मैत्रावरुणेर्वसिष्ठस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं
> पवमानसोमदेवताकं ॥ तथा चानुक्रांतं । प्र हिन्वानः षड्वसिष्ठ इति ॥ गतो
> विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning प्र हिन्वान (*pra hinvāna*) has six Ṛks and is the fifth sūkta. It is the hymn of Vasiṣṭha, of Maitrāvaruṇa descent, in the Triṣṭubh metre, with Pavamāna Soma as deity. So it is recorded in the Anukramaṇī: प्र हिन्वानः षड्वसिष्ठ (*pra hinvānaḥ ṣaḍvasiṣṭha*). The viniyoga has been stated.

Anuvāda— This sūkta beginning प्र हिन्वा नः (*pra hinvā naḥ*) is the fifth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. Vasiṣṭha is the seer of this sūkta; Pavamāna Soma is the deity; Triṣṭup is the metre. In the Anukramaṇikā it is stated as प्र हिन्वानः षड्वसिष्ठः (*pra hinvānaḥ ṣaḍvasiṣṭhaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 90. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 90. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 3, Varga 26. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Vasiṣṭha. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र हि॑न्वा॒नो ज॑नि॒ता रोद॑स्यो॒ रथो॒ न वाजं॑ सन्नि॒ष्यन्न॑यासीत् ।

### Printed p. 641

> इंद्रं गच्छन्नायुधा संशिशानो विश्वा वसु हस्तयोरादधानः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । हिन्वानः । जनिता । रोदस्योः । रथः । न । वाजं । सनिष्यन् । अयासीत् ।  
> इंद्रं । गच्छन् ! आयुधा । संशिशानः । विश्वा । वसु । हस्तयोः । आदधानः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हिन्वानः प्रेयमाणोऽध्वर्यादिभिर्जुनितोत्पादयिता रोदस्योर्द्यावापृथिव्योः । तयोर्जनयितृत्वं वृष्टिप्रदानहविष्ट्रापणाभ्यां । तादृक्षोमो वाजमन्नं सनिष्यन्दास्यन् प्रायासीत् । प्रयच्छति । इंद्रं गच्छन्द्राप्नुवन्नायुधायुधानि संशिशानः सम्यक् तीक्ष्णीकुर्वन्निंद्रसाहाय्यगमनार्थं तीक्ष्णायुधः सन् विश्वा
> सर्वाणि वसु वसूनि हस्तयोरादधानोऽस्मभ्यं दानाय। एवं कुर्वन् प्रायासीत्॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being urged by the Adhvaryu and the others, is the begetter, the producer, of the two worlds, heaven and earth; his begetting them is by the giving of rain and by conveying the offerings. Such a Soma, wishing to give vāja, food, advances, that is, gives. Going to Indra, reaching him, sharpening his weapons well, that is, becoming one of sharp weapons in order to go to Indra's help, holding all riches in his hands to give to us, so doing he advances.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रोदस्योः (*rodasyoḥ*)—to heaven and earth
- जनिता (*janitā*)—the producer
- हिन्वानः (*hinvānaḥ*)—Soma, urged by the priests
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- गच्छन् (*gacchan*)—approaching
- आयुधा संशिशानः (*āyudhā saṃśiśānaḥ*)—having sharp weapons
- हस्तयोः (*hastayoḥ*)—in the hands
- विश्वा (*viśvā*)—all
- वसु (*vasu*)—riches
- आदधानः (*ādadhānaḥ*)—holding
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—food
- सनिष्यन् (*saniṣyan*)—with the wish to give to the sacrificers

> त्रिपृष्ठं । त्रीणि पृष्टानि स्तोत्राणि द्रोणकलशादिस्थानानि वा सवनानि वा यस्य

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Tripṛṣṭha: he who has three pṛṣṭhas, that is, three stotras, or places such as the Droṇakalaśa, or three savanas. The voices of the praisers who make a loud sound resound around him, the showerer, the giver of food, Soma. Wearing the waters, covering them, as Varuṇa covers the rivers, so Soma, the giver of jewels, grants desirable riches to the praisers.

- सिंधून् न (*siṃdhūn na*)—as he wraps himself in the flowing waters

- वना (*vanā*)—the waters
- वसानः (*vasānaḥ*)—having wrapped himself in
- वार्याणि (*vāryāṇi*)—desirable riches
- दयते (*dayate*)—gives

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The voices of the praisers surround and praise Soma, who is in three places such as the Droṇakalaśa, the giver of what is desired, and the giver of food. As the god Varuṇa joins himself to the flowing waters, so Soma, the giver of wealth, mixing himself with the waters, gives desirable riches.

## Sūkta 91 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्रासर्जीति षडृचं षष्ठं सूक्तं मारीचस्य कश्यपस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं
> पवमानसोमदेवताकं । असर्जि कश्यप इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning तत्रासर्जीति (*tatrāsarjīti*) has six Ṛks and is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is Kaśyapa, of Marīci's line; its metre is Triṣṭubh; its deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says असर्जि कश्यप (*asarji kaśyapa*). The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, called असर्जि (*asarji*), is the sixth in the fifth anuvāka of the ninth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as असर्जि कश्यपः (*asarji kaśyapaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

> इंदो इति । सुउक्ताय । वचसे । वयः । धाः । यूयं । पात । स्वस्तिभिः ।  
> सदा । नः ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अनया स्तुतिमुपसंहरन् फलमाशास्त्रे । हे सोम एवैवं स्तुत इति शेषः ।
> क्रतुमांस्त्वं राजेवामेन बलेन विश्वा सर्वाणि दुरिता दुरितानि घनिघ्नद्विनाशयन्
> पवस्व । हे इंदो दीप्त सोम सूक्ताय शोभनमुदिताय वचसेऽस्माकं
> स्तोत्राय तद्वचो विमृष्यार्थवदवगत्य वयो धाः । अन्नं धेहि । अन्नलाभस्य
> स्तुतिनिमित्तकत्वात्तस्य स्तुतिवचसः प्राधान्येनोक्तिः । शिष्टं सिद्धं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Concluding the praise with this Ṛk, he asks for the fruit; "thus praised" is to be supplied. O Soma, you who are endowed with will, like a king, destroying with your strength all evils, flow. O Indu, shining Soma, for our well-spoken praise, having considered its words as full of meaning and understood them, वयो धाः (*vayo dhāḥ*): give food. Since the gaining of food is caused by praise, the praise-speech is mentioned as the chief thing. The rest is established.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The authors of the Nirukta have explained the meaning of the word svasti with an example from a Ṛk:

स नः पितेव सूनवेऽग्ने सूपायनो भव । सचस्वा नः स्वस्तये । (*sa naḥ piteva sūnave 'gne sūpāyano bhava | sacasvā naḥ svastaye |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-1-F) **NOTE**

Here the word svasti is explained as स्वस्तीति अविनाशिनाम अस्तियभिपूजितः सु अस्तीति । (*svastīti avināśināma astiyabhipūjitaḥ su astīti |*) The word asti is used in the sense of "worship". The prefix su joins and relates to it, and the form su asti results. "Avināśi: that which is without destruction" is the meaning he has explained; so Durgācārya has commented. And:

स्वस्तिरिद्दि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्ण स्वत्यभि या वाममेति । सा.नो अमा सो अरणे नि पातु स्वावेशा भवतु देवगोपा । (*svastiriddi prapathe śreṣṭhā rekṇa svatyabhi yā vāmameti | sā.no amā so araṇe ni pātu svāveśā bhavatu devagopā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-63-4)

A deity renowned as Svasti, since she dwells in the antarikṣa, is a deity of the middle region, and the greatness of that goddess is described in this Ṛk in this way.

### Printed p. 648

स्वस्तिरेव हि प्रपथे श्रेष्ठा रेक्लस्वति धनवत्यभ्येति या वसूनि वननीयानि सा नोऽमा गृहे सानिरमणे सा निर्गमने पातु स्वावेशा भवतु देवी गोप््री देवान् गॊपायत्विति देवा एनां गोपायंत्वि ना । (*svastireva hi prapathe śreṣṭhā reklasvati dhanavatyabhyeti yā vasūni vananīyāni sā no 'mā gṛhe sāniramaṇe sā nirgamane pātu svāveśā bhavatu devī goprī devān gòpāyatviti devā enāṃ gopāyaṃtvi nā |*) (Ni. 12-48)

On this Durgācārya has explained the meaning thus: The goddess Svasti is the most worthy of praise in the antarikṣa among all the gods. Like those who have filled themselves with wealth for all, she always moves about, accompanied by indispensable water. May that goddess protect us who dwell in the forest and in the house. May she protect us so that we move about happily. May this goddess protect the oblations offered to the gods, the gods, and us. May the gods of the middle region who stand in the heaven-place, or the rays also, protect this goddess.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> तत्रासर्जीति षडृचं षष्ठं सूक्तं मारीचस्य कश्यपस्यार्यं त्रैष्टुभं
> पवमानसोमदेवताकं । असर्जि कश्यप इत्यनुक्रांतं ॥ गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning तत्रासर्जीति (*tatrāsarjīti*) has six Ṛks and is the sixth sūkta. Its seer is Kaśyapa, of Marīci's line; its metre is Triṣṭubh; its deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says असर्जि कश्यप (*asarji kaśyapa*). The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, called असर्जि (*asarji*), is the sixth in the fifth anuvāka of the ninth maṇḍala of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇī it is stated as असर्जि कश्यपः (*asarji kaśyapaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दश॒ स्वसा॑रो॒ अधि॒ सानो॒ अव्येजं॑ति॒ वह्निं॒ सद॑ना॒न्यच्छ॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दश । स्वसारः । अधि । सानौ । अव्ये । अजंति । वह्निं । सदनानि । अच्छ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वक्त्वा शब्दायमानः ॥ वच परिभाषणे । वनिप् ॥ एतादृशः पवमानः सोम
> आजौ । अजंति कर्मार्थमृत्विज इत्याजिर्यज्ञः । तस्मिन्दिया कर्मणा स्तोत्रेण वा
> साकमसर्जि । सृज्यते पात्रेष्विति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथ्ये यथा रथार्ह आजौ । संग्रामनामैतत् अजंति प्रक्षिपंत्यायुधान्यत्रेति । तस्मिन्नश्वो यथा धियांगुल्या सृज्यते
> तद्वत् । कीदृशः । मनोता यस्मिन्देवानां मनांस्योतानि प्रोतानि सः । तथा च
> ब्राह्मणं । तस्मिन् हि तेषां मनांस्योतानि । ऐ. ब्रा- २-१० । इति । प्रथमः सर्वॆषां
> देवानां मुख्यः मनीषी । मनस ईषा मनीषा स्तुतिः । तद्वान् । दश स्वसारो
> दशसंख्याका अंगुलयः सदनानि यज्ञगृहाण्यच्छाभिमुखीक्रत्य वह्निं वोढारं
> सोमं सान् समुच्च्रिते । अधिः सप्तम्यर्थानुवादकः । अव्येऽविभवेऽविनालेन
> कृते पवित्रेजंति । प्रेरयंति ॥ अज गतिक्षेपणयोः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वक्वा (*vakvā*) means sounding (the root वच (*vaca*), to speak). Such is Pavamāna Soma. In the आजौ (*ājau*) — अजंति (*ajaṃti*): the priests drive for the rite — so the word for sacrifice is derived; in it, together with धिया (*dhiyā*), action or praise, he is let loose, असर्जि (*asarji*), into the vessels. An example is given: as in an आजौ (*ājau*) worthy of chariots, which is a name for battle, because weapons are thrown there, a horse is let loose by the finger (धिया (*dhiyā*) understood as the finger), so is he. What sort is he? मनोता (*manotā*): he in whom the minds of the gods are threaded. And so the Brāhmaṇa says तस्मिन् हि तेषां मनांस्योतानि । (*tasmin hi teṣāṃ manāṃsyotāni |*) (Ai. Brā. 2-10). प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*): chief among all the gods. मनीषी (*manīṣī*): मनीषा (*manīṣā*) is praise, the impulse of the mind; he who has it. दश स्वसारः (*daśa svasāraḥ*): the ten fingers, turning toward the sacrificial houses (सदनानि अच्छ (*sadanāni accha*)) the carrier (वह्निं (*vahniṃ*)) Soma on the raised place (सानौ (*sānau*)); अधि (*adhi*) only restates the locative sense; on the अव्ये (*avye*), the filter made of woollen thread, they अजंति (*ajaṃti*), urge him on; the root अज (*aja*) has the sense of going and throwing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- रथ्ये यथा (*rathye yathā*)—as horses are driven by the fingers when fighting mounted on a chariot
- मनोता (*manotā*)—the recipient of the gods' meditation
- प्रथमः (*prathamaḥ*)—chief among all the gods
- मनीषी (*manīṣī*)—possessed of praise

### Printed p. 651

- वक्वा (*vakvā*)—the Soma that makes a sound
- आजौ (*ājau*)—in the sacrifice
- धिया (*dhiyā*)—with praise
- असर्जि (*asarji*)—is pressed
- दश स्वसारः (*daśa svasāraḥ*)—the ten fingers
- सदनानि अच्छ (*sadanāni accha*)—toward the sacrificial houses
- वह्निं (*vahniṃ*)—Soma, the carrier of the oblation
- सानौ (*sānau*)—on the raised place
- अव्ये अधि (*avye adhi*)—on the woollen ten-fold filter
- अजंति (*ajaṃti*)—urge

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As horses are urged by the fingers when fighting together with a chariot, the Soma, which is the recipient of the gods' meditation, chief among all the gods, possessed of praise and sounding, is pressed in the sacrifice with praise. The ten fingers too, turned toward the sacrificial houses, urge Soma, the carrier of the oblation, onto the woollen ten-fold filter on the raised place.

##### English translation
(Soma) on whom the minds of the gods are fixed, chief (of the gods), recipient of praise, is let loose with a shout by ceremony as (a horse is let loose by the finger) in a battle of chariots ; the ten sister (fingers) drive the bearer (of the oblation) on the elevated place to the halls (of sacrifice).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> वी॒ती जन॑स्य दि॒व्यस्य॑ क॒व्यैरधि॑ सुवा॒नो न॑हु॒ष्ये॑भि॒रिंदुः॑ ।  
> प्र यो नृभि॑र॒मृतो॒ मर्त्ये॑भिर्ममृजा॒नोऽवि॑भि॒र्गोभि॑र॒द्भिः ॥ २ ॥

> प्र । यः । नृभिः । अमृतः । मर्त्येभिः । मर्मृजानः । अविभिः । गोभिः । अत्भिः ॥

> इंदुः सोमो दिव्यस्य दिवि भवस्य जनस्य देवगणस्य वीती ॥ सुपां सुलुगिति
> चतुर्थ्याः पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः ॥ सोमभक्षणार्थं यज्ञमधिगच्छति । किंचामृतो

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma Indu, being pressed (सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*)) by the good praisers (कव्यैः (*kavyaiḥ*)), by men (नहुष्येभिः (*nahuṣyebhiḥ*)), goes to the sacrifice for the drinking (वीती (*vītī*)) of the divine people (the divine people), that is, of the host of the gods born in heaven, for the eating of Soma. And further, immortal **NOTE**

### Printed p. 652

> मरणधर्मरहितो यः सोमो नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्मर्त्येभिर्मर्त्यैरविभिरविमय्यैः
> पवित्रैः तथा गोभिरानडुहैरधिषवणचर्मभिः यद्वा गोविकारैः क्षीरादिभिः
> अद्भिवर्ततीवर्यादिभिरुदकैश्च मर्मृजानो भृशं शोध्यमानः सन् यज्ञं प्रति
> गच्छति । उपसर्गश्रुतेर्योग्यक्रियाध्याहारः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Soma who is free from the law of death, with the men who lead the rite, with mortals, with the filters made of wool, likewise with the ox-hides on the pressing-place, or else with the products of the cow, milk and the rest, and with the waters, being thoroughly purified, goes toward the sacrifice. Because the preverb is heard, a suitable verb is to be supplied. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमृतः (*amṛtaḥ*)—free from the law of death **NOTE**
- यः (*yaḥ*)—which Soma
- कव्यैः (*kavyaiḥ*)—by the praisers
- नहुष्येभिः (*nahuṣyebhiḥ*)—by men
- सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*)—pressed
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the leaders of the rite
- मर्त्येभिः (*martyebhiḥ*)—by men
- अविभिः (*avibhiḥ*)—in the ten-fold filters
- गोभिः (*gobhiḥ*)—with milk and the rest
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—with the waters
- मर्मृजानः (*marmṛjānaḥ*)—who is purified
- इंदुः (*iṃduḥ*)—Soma
- दिवस्य जनस्यॆ (*divasya janasyè*)—to the host of gods born in the heaven-world **NOTE**
- वीती (*vītī*)—for drinking
- अधि (*adhi*)—comes to the sacrificial house

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma who is free from the law of death, pressed by men who are praisers, and purified by men who lead the rite, in the ten-fold filters, with milk and the rest and with the waters, such a Soma comes to the sacrificial house for the drinking of the host of gods born in the heaven-world.

##### English translation
The Soma juice effused by pious mortals (comes) down (to the sacrifice) for the food of the celestial people ; which immortal (liquor) is purified by mortal (priests) with the filter, the curds and milk and the waters.

> सोमः पवमानः पूयमानः सन्नस्मै वृष्णे वर्षकायेंद्राय तदर्थं रुशत् ॥
> रोचतेरिदं रूपं ॥ आरोचमानं श्वेतं गोः पय आश्रयणद्रव्यमिर्तॆ । गच्छति ॥
> ईर गत् । आदादिकः ॥ किंच ऋक्वा ॥ छंदसीवनिपाविति मत्वर्थीयो वनिप् ॥
> स्तोत्रवान् अत एव वचोवित् स्तुतीनां ज्ञाता सूरः सुवीर्यः सर्वेषामग्निष्टोमादिकर्मणि प्रेरकः सोमोऽध्वस्मभिर्ध्वंसनवर्जितैर्हिंसारहितैः सहस्रं
> पथिभिर्बहुभिमार्गैरण्वं सूक्ष्मच्छिद्रं पवित्रं वि याति । अतीत्य द्रोणकलशं गच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

वृषा (*vṛṣā*): the showerer of desires, or one acting like a bull; रोरुवत् (*roruvat*): sounding loudly; अंशुः (*aṃśuḥ*): Soma, being purified, goes for this showerer, Indra, and for his sake to the shining white milk of the cow, the substance that serves as a support; ईर्ते (*īrte*) means goes. Further, ऋक्वा (*ṛkvā*) is the possessor of praise, in the Vedic form with the affix meaning possession; hence वचोवित् (*vacovit*), the knower of praises; सूरः (*sūraḥ*): of good valour, the impeller of all in the Agniṣṭoma and the other rites. That Soma, with a thousand paths, many, free from destruction and harm, passes through the filter with its fine holes; having crossed it, he goes to the Droṇakalaśa.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the giver of desired things
- रोरुवत् (*roruvat*)—and one who makes sound
- अंशुः (*aṃśuḥ*)—Soma
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—having attained purity
- अस्मै वृष्णे (*asmai vṛṣṇe*)—for this Indra
- रुशत् (*ruśat*)—shining
- गोः पयः (*goḥ payaḥ*)—toward the milk and the other substances that serve as a support
- ईर्ते (*īrte*)—goes
- ऋक्वा (*ṛkvā*)—possessed of praise
- वचोवित् (*vacovit*)—knower of praise
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—Soma, the impeller
- अध्वस्मभिः (*adhvasmabhiḥ*)—free from harm
- सहस्रं पथिभिः (*sahasraṃ pathibhiḥ*)—by many paths
- अण्वं (*aṇvaṃ*)—to the ten-fold filter
- वि याति (*vi yāti*)—comes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, the giver of desired things and one who makes sound, having attained purity, goes for Indra toward the shining milk and the other substances that serve as a support. Soma, who is possessed of praise, a knower of praise and an impeller, comes to the ten-fold filter by many paths free from harm.

##### English translation
The Soma juice the showerer (of benefits) roaring to the showerer (Indra) goes when being purified to (mix with) the glistening milk of the cow; greeted with laudation, cognizant of sacred praise, the hero passes through the filter by a thousand imperishable paths.

> रु॒जा दृ॒ळ्हा चि॑द्र॒क्षसः॒ सदां॑सि पुना॒न इं॑द उर्णुहि॒ वि  ॑
> वाजान् ।

> वृश्चोपरिस्पात्तुजता वधेन ये अंति दूरारुपनायमेषां ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)
