##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम दृळ्हा चिद्दृढान्यपि परैरगंतव्यत्वेन रक्षसो राक्षसस्य सदांसि
> स्थानानि पुराणि रुज । विनाशय ॥ रुजो भंगे तौदादिकः ॥ किंच हे इंदो पवमानः
> पुनानः पवित्रादिभिः पूयमानस्त्वं . वाजांस्तस्यान्नानि तस्य बलानि वोर्णुहि ।
> आच्छादय । आहरेत्यर्थः । तथा ये राक्षसा उपरिष्टादूर्ध्वदेशादागच्छंति ये
> वांत्यंतिके समीप आगच्छंति ये च दूराद्दूरदेशाद्वागच्छंति तेषां राक्षसानामुपनायमुपनेतारं स्वामिनं तुजता । तुजतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । हिंसकेन वधेन
> हननसाधनेनायुधेन त्वं वृश्च । छिंधि ॥ ओव्रश्च छेदने तौदादिकः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, break the dwellings, the strongholds, of the Rākṣasa, सदांसि (*sadāṃsi*), even though they are firm and not to be entered by others; destroy them. Further, O Indu, purified by the filters and the rest, put on, that is, cover yourself with, or bring, the strengths, the foods, of that one. Likewise, those Rākṣasas who come from above, from the upper region, or who come from near, or who come from afar: their leader and master (उपनायं (*upanāyaṃ*)), cut down with a harming weapon, a means of killing (तुजता (*tujatā*): the root means harm); cut, cleave (वृश्च (*vṛśca*)).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma-deva)
- रक्षसः (*rakṣasaḥ*)—of the Rākṣasa
- सदांसि (*sadāṃsi*)—the dwelling-places
- दृळ्हाचित् (*dṛḷhācit*)—though they are exceedingly firm
- रुज (*ruja*)—destroy
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who have attained purity
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—strength
- वि ऊर्णुहि (*vi ūrṇuhi*)—put on
- ये (*ye*)—which Rākṣasas
- उपरिष्टात् (*upariṣṭāt*)—from above
- अंति (*aṃti*)—from near
- दूरात् (*dūrāt*)—and from a distant region come, those Rākṣasas
- एषां उपनायं (*eṣāṃ upanāyaṃ*)—and their leaders
- तुजता (*tujatā*)—harming
- वधेन (*vadhena*)—with a weapon
- वृश्च (*vṛśca*)—cut

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, destroy the dwelling-places of the Rākṣasa, though they are exceedingly firm. O Soma, you who have attained purity, put on strength. Those asuras **NOTE** who come from above, from near, and from a distant region, those Rākṣasas and their leaders too, cut with a harming weapon.

### Printed p. 655

##### English translation
Demolish the strong dwellings of the Rakshasa ; Indu, when purified put on his strength; cut to pieces with your destructive weapon (the Rakshasas) who come from above, from nigh, or from afar and their leader.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स प्र॑श्न॒वन्नव्य॑से विश्ववार सू॒क्ताय॑ प॒थः कृ॑णुहि॒ प्राचः॑ ।  
> ये दुः॒षहा॑सो व॒नुषा॑ बृ॒हंत॒स्तांस्ते॑ अश्याम पुरुकृत्पुरुक्षो ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । प्रश्नवत् । नव्यसे । विश्ववार । सुउक्ताय । पथः । कृणुहि । प्राचः ।  
> ये । दुःसहासः । वनुषा । बृहंतः । तान् । शे । अश्याम । पुरुकृत् । पुरुक्षो  
> इति पुरुषोत्तम ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे विश्ववार विश्वै सर्वैर्वर्णेय हे सोम स तादृशस्त्वं प्रत्नवत् पुराण
> इव स्थितस्त्वं नव्यसे नवीयसे नवतराय ॥ नवशब्दादीयसुनीकारलोपश्रांदसः ॥
> तस्यॆ सूक्ताय शोभनस्तुतिकाय मह्यं पथो मार्गान् प्राचः प्राचीनान्
> कृणुहि । कुरु । सर्वत्र गमनं प्रयच्छेत्यर्थः ॥ कृवि हिंसाकरणयोः । धिन्विकृण्वोरच्चेत्युप्रत्ययः ॥ हे पुरुकृद्बहुकर्मन् हे पुरुषो ॥ टुक्षु शब्दे । मितद्वादिश्वाद्दु प्रत्ययः । पा. ३-२-१४०-१ ॥ बहुविधॆं शब्दायमान हे सोम दुःसहासो
> रक्षोभिः सोधुमशक्याः अत एव वनुषा । वनतिर्हिंसार्थः । हिंसया युक्ता
> बृहंतो महांतो ये त्वदीयाः अंताः संति तांस्ते तव स्वभूतानंशान्वयं
> यष्टेऽत्याम ! प्राप्युयाम ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O विश्ववार (*viśvavāra*), one to be chosen by all, O Soma, such as you are, standing as if ancient (प्रत्नवत् (*pratnavat*)), for the newer, the very new one (नव्यसे (*navyase*)), that is, for me, the well-praising सूक्ताय (*sūktāya*), make the paths forward, the ancient ones; the meaning is: grant movement everywhere. O पुरुकृत् (*purukṛt*), doer of many works, O पुरुक्षो (*purukṣo*), one who sounds in many ways, O Soma: those of your parts which are दुःसहासो (*duḥsahāso*), impossible for the Rākṣasas to overcome, and therefore वनुषा (*vanuṣā*), accompanied by harming, great, which are yours, those portions of you which belong to you, may we obtain. **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- विश्ववार (*viśvavāra*)—O Soma-deva, worthy of all worship
- सः (*saḥ*)—you who are renowned
- प्रत्नवत् (*pratnavat*)—being ancient
- नव्यसे (*navyase*)—and the present one
- सूक्ताय (*sūktāya*)—to me, who am an excellent praiser
- पथः (*pathaḥ*)—excellent paths
- प्राजिः (*prājiḥ*)—so that they face me **NOTE**
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—make

- पुरुकृत् (*purukṛt*)—one who does many works
- पुरुक्षो (*purukṣo*)—one who sounds greatly, O Soma
- दुःसहासः (*duḥsahāsaḥ*)—which cannot be withstood by enemies
- वनुषा (*vanuṣā*)—harming enemies
- बृहंतः (*bṛhaṃtaḥ*)—and of great form
- ये (*ye*)—which powers of yours there are
- तान् (*tān*)—those
- ते (*te*)—we **NOTE**
- अश्याम (*aśyāma*)—may we obtain

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, worthy of the worship of all, you who are renowned, being ancient, make known excellent paths to me, who am the present one and an excellent praiser. O Soma, doer of many works and one who sounds greatly, may we obtain those powers of yours which cannot be withstood by enemies, which harm enemies and are of great form.

##### English translation
Adorable (Soma), you as of old grant the ancient paths to your new worshipper ; doer of many acts, utterer of many sounds, may we obtain those (portions) of you which are difficult to defeat, inflicting injury (on foes) and mighty.

> शं नः॒ क्षेत्र॑मु॒रु ज्योतीं॑षि सोम॒ ज्योज्न्॒यः सूर्यं॑

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । पुनानः । अपः । स्वः । गाः । अस्मभ्यं । तोका । तनयानि । भूरि ।  
> शं । नः । क्षेत्रं । उरु । ज्योतींषि । सोम । ज्योक् । नः । सूर्यं । दृशये ।  
> रिरीहि ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम एवैवं पुनानः पूयमानः पवित्रादिभिरस्मभ्यं रिरीहि । प्रापय ।
> प्रयच्छ । किं तत् । अपः । अप इत्यंतरिक्ष नाम । आप्नोति सर्वमपि । अंतरिक्षं स्वः
> अ. ७. आ. ४. व. २. ] ऋग्वेदसंहिता 657.
> स्वर्गं द्युलोकं गाः । सर्वैर्गम्यतेऽत्रेति गावः पृथिव्यः । ताः पृथिवीश्च भूरि ॥
> सुपां सुलुगति द्वितीयाया लुक् ॥ बहूंस्तोका पुत्रांस्तनयानि । तन्वंति कुलमिति
> तनयाः पौत्राः । तांश्च तथा नोऽस्मभ्यं क्षेत्रं शं सुखकरं कुरु । हे सोम
> जोतींषि नक्षत्राण्युरूरूण्यंतरिक्षे विस्तीर्णानि कुरु तथा नोऽस्मभ्यं सूर्यमादित्यं ज्योक् । चिरनामैतत् । चिरकालं दृशये द्रष्टुं कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, thus purified by the filters and the rest, रिरीहि (*rirīhi*): bring to us, give. What? अपः (*apaḥ*): this is a name of the antarikṣa, because it pervades everything; स्वः (*svaḥ*): heaven, the world of the sky; गाः (*gāḥ*): the earths, because all go over them; and these earths in abundance (भूरि (*bhūri*)). Many sons (तोका (*tokā*)) and grandsons (तनयानि (*tanayāni*): those who extend the family are the tanayas, the grandsons). And likewise make our field pleasant (शं (*śaṃ*)). O Soma, make the luminaries, the stars, wide (उरु (*uru*)) in the antarikṣa; and likewise make us see the sun, the Āditya, for a long time (ज्योक् (*jyok*) is a name meaning long), दृशये (*dṛśaye*), to see.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- (O Soma-deva)
- एव (*eva*)—thus
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who have attained purity
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the atmosphere
- स्वः (*svaḥ*)—the heaven-world
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—the earths
- भूरि (*bhūri*)—in abundance
- तोका (*tokā*)—sons
- तनयानि (*tanayāni*)—grandsons
- रिरीहि (*rirīhi*)—provide
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- क्षेत्रं (*kṣetraṃ*)—the field
- शं (*śaṃ*)—make pleasant
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- ज्योतींषि (*jyotīṃṣi*)—the stars
- उरु (*uru*)—make them shine in the wide atmosphere
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सूर्यं (*sūryaṃ*)—the Āditya
- ज्योक् (*jyok*)—for a long time
- दृशये (*dṛśaye*)—make visible

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who have attained purity, provide us the atmosphere, the heaven-world, the earths, and in abundance sons and grandsons. Make our field pleasant. Make the stars shine in the atmosphere; may we see the Āditya for a long time.

##### English translation
Thus, being purified. bestow upon us the firmament and heaven and earth and many sons and grandsons ; make our land prosper, diffuse the luminaries widely (in the firmament) and grant us long life to see the sun- **NOTE**

The ninety-second sūkta.

## Sūkta 92 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘परि सुवानः' इति षडृचं सप्तमं सूक्तं मारीचस्य कश्यपस्यार्षं त्रैष्टुभं पवमानसोमदेवताकम् । ‘ परि सुवानः' इत्यनुक्रांतम् । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sūkta beginning परि सुवानः (*pari suvānaḥ*) has six Ṛks and is the seventh sūkta. Its seer is Kaśyapa, of Marīci's line; its metre is Triṣṭubh; its deity is Pavamāna Soma. The Anukramaṇī says परि सुवानः (*pari suvānaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, परि सुवानः (*pari suvānaḥ*), is the seventh sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has six Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kaśyapa, the son of Marīci; the deity is Pavamāna

### Printed p. 658

Soma; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said परि सुवानः (*pari suvānaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 92. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 92. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 4, Varga 2. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 6. Seer: Kaśyapa. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॑ सुवा॒नो हरि॑रं॒शुः प॒वित्रे॒ रथो॒ न स॑र्जि स॒नये॑ हिया॒नः ।  
> आप॒च्छ्लोक॑मिंद्रि॒यं पू॒यमा॑नः॒ प्रति॑ दे॒वाँ अ॑जुषत॒ प्रयो॑भिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । सुवानः । हरिः । अंशुः । पवित्रे । रथः । न । सर्जि । सनये । हियानः ।  
> आपत् । श्लोकम् । इंद्रियम् । पूयमानः । प्रति । देवान् । अजुषत । प्रयःऽभिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुवानः' अभिषूयमाणः हियानः ऋत्विग्भिः प्रेर्यमाणः हरिः हरितवर्णः अंशुः सोमः पवित्रे अविवालेन कृते दशापवित्रे परि सर्जि परिसृज्यते । किमर्थम् । सनये धनलाभाय देवानां संभजनाय वा । तत्र दृष्टांतः । रथो न । रथो यथा युद्धे शत्रुवधार्थं शत्रुधनहरणार्थं वा सृज्यते तद्वत् । किंच पूयमानः पवित्रेण सोऽयं सोमः इंद्रियम् इंद्रलिंगमिंद्रस्य पर्याप्तं वा श्लोकं स्तोत्रम् आपत् आप्नोति । आप्लृ व्याप्तौ ' । लेट्यडागमः । तथा स सोमः प्रयोभिः प्रीणयितृभिः हवीरूपैरन्नैः देवान् प्रति अजुषत प्रतिसेवते । ‘जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः' ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*): being pressed; हियानः (*hiyānaḥ*): driven on by the priests; हरिः (*hariḥ*): of green colour; अंशुः (*aṃśuḥ*): Soma. On the filter, the ten-fold filter made of woollen threads, he is released all around (परि सर्जि (*pari sarji*)). For what purpose? सनये (*sanaye*): for the gain of wealth, or for the sharing with the gods. An example is given: रथो न (*ratho na*), as a chariot is sent forth in battle to kill enemies or to carry off the enemies' wealth, so he is sent. Further, being purified by the filter, this Soma obtains (आपत् (*āpat*)) इंद्रियम् (*iṃdriyam*), the mark of Indra or what is sufficient for Indra, and praise, श्लोकं (*ślokaṃ*). Likewise that Soma, with the gladdening foods in the form of oblations (प्रयोभिः (*prayobhiḥ*)), serves the gods (अजुषत (*ajuṣata*); the root means pleasing and serving).

- सुवानः (*suvānaḥ*)—pressed
- हियानः (*hiyānaḥ*)—driven on by the priests
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—of green colour

- रथो न (*ratho na*)—like a chariot
- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—on the ten-fold filter

- इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*)—being gratifying to Indra

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Soma, which is pressed, driven on by the priests, and of green colour, is let loose like a chariot on the ten-fold filter for the gain of wealth. Having attained purity, since it is gratifying to Indra, it is praised. With gladdening oblations it serves the gods.

##### English translation
The green-tinted Soma effused and sent forth (by the priests) is let loose, like a chariot upon the filter, for the acquisition (of riches); being filtered he acquires (Indra's) praise, he gratifies the gods with conciliatory (oblations).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अंशु. सनये रथो न सर्जि (*aṃśu. sanaye ratho na sarji*)—अयं सोमः धनलाभाय देवानां संभजनाय वा परिसृज्यते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । यथा रथः युद्धे शत्रुवधार्थं शत्रुधनहरणार्थं वा सृज्यते तद्वत् । (*ayaṃ somaḥ dhanalābhāya devānāṃ saṃbhajanāya vā parisṛjyate | tatra dṛṣṭāṃtaḥ | yathā rathaḥ yuddhe śatruvadhārthaṃ śatrudhanaharaṇārthaṃ vā sṛjyate tadvat |*) Here the Soma juice that streams out from the crushed Soma plants is compared to a chariot that sets out for battle. A chariot that sets out for battle is helpful in killing the enemies in the battle, and after the enemies have been conquered in the battle it also helps in bringing the wealth and other things that were with them. In the same way the pressed Soma juice is used in the sacrifices and other rites that are performed for the gain of wealth, for the pleasure of Indra, and for the attainment of strength and capacity. In the sense that refers to Soma, the word सनये (*sanaye*) indicates the idea: for the gain of wealth, or for the gods to come to the sacrifice. Likewise the word इंद्रियं (*iṃdriyaṃ*) indicates the meaning virility, strength, or else the hymn recited addressing Indra.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अच्छा॑ नृ॒चक्षा॑ असरत्प॒वित्रे॒ नाम॒ दधा॑नः क॒विर॑स्य॒ योनौ॑ ।  
> सीद॒न्होते॑व॒ सद॑ने च॒मूषूपे॑मग्म॒न्नृष॑यः स॒प्त विप्राः॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अच्छ । नृऽचक्षाः । असरत् । पवित्रे । नाम । दधानः । कविः । अस्य । योनौ ।  
> सीदन् । होताऽइव । सदने । चमूषु । उप । ईम् । अग्मन् । ऋषयः । सप्त । विप्राः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> नृचक्षाः नृणां द्रष्टा कविः क्रांतप्रज्ञः सोमः नाम वसतीवर्याख्यमुदकं दधानः धारयन् अस्य एतादृशस्यात्मनः योनौ स्थाने पवित्रे अच्छ असरत् अभितः सरति । ततः सदने । सीदंत्यत्रेति सदनो यज्ञः । तस्मिन् होतेव होता यथा देवान् स्तोतुमुपविशति तद्वद्देवानागंतुमुपविशन् सोमः चमूषु । चमंति चम्वो ग्रहादयः । तेष्वभिसरति । अनंतरं सप्तसंख्याकाः विप्राः मेधाविनो भरद्वाजः कश्यप गोतमोऽत्रिर्विश्वामित्रो जमदग्निर्वसिष्ठ इत्येते ऋषयः ईम् एनं सोमम् उप अग्मन् स्तोत्रैरुपगच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*): the seer of men; कविः (*kaviḥ*): one of surpassing wisdom: this Soma, holding the water called vasatīvarī, flows all around, अच्छ असरत् (*accha asarat*), in the filter, which is the place of himself, such as he is. Then at the sacrifice, the place where they sit: as a Hotṛ sits in order to praise the gods, so Soma sits in order that the gods may come, in the चमूषु (*camūṣu*), the cups, that is, the vessels of the grahas and the rest, which are sipped from; he flows toward them. After that the seven wise ones, men of intelligence, the seers Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gotama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha, approach (अग्मन् (*agman*)) him, ईम् (*īm*), this Soma, with praises.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- नृचक्षाः (*nṛcakṣāḥ*)—one who can see men
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—Soma, of surpassing wisdom
- नाम (*nāma*)—water
- दधानः (*dadhānaḥ*)—holding
- अस्य योन्सौ (*asya yonsau*)—in his own place **NOTE**
- पवित्रे (*pavitre*)—on the ten-fold filter
- अच्छ (*accha*)—everywhere
- असरत् (*asarat*)—flows
- सदने सीदन् (*sadane sīdan*)—sitting at the sacrifice
- होतेव (*hoteva*)—like a Hotṛ who praises the gods
- चमूषु (*camūṣu*)—in the camū vessels Soma gathers to serve the gods
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise
- सप्त ऋषयः (*sapta ṛṣayaḥ*)—the seven seers beginning with Bharadvāja
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Soma
- उपाग्मन् (*upāgman*)—approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who can see men and is of surpassing wisdom, mixed with water, flows everywhere in the ten-fold filter, his own place. Like the Hotṛ who sits at the sacrifice and praises the gods, Soma enters the camū vessels to serve the gods. The seven wise seers beginning with Bharadvāja approach this Soma.

### Printed p. 661

##### English translation
The sage, the observer of men, retaining the water proceeds to his place on the filter ; like a ministrant priest sitting at the sacrifice (the Soma flows) into the cups ; the seven wise rishis approach him with praise.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

नाम दधानः—वसतीवर्याख्यमुदकं धारयन् । (*nāma dadhānaḥ—vasatīvaryākhyamudakaṃ dhārayan |*) Here the word नाम (*nāma*) means water (Ni. 2-24). When the pressed Soma juice is being prepared, it is the rule to mix with it the water that is in the vessels called vasatīvarī. Therefore the meaning of the words नाम दधानः (*nāma dadhānaḥ*) is: the Soma juice mixed with such vasatīvarī waters.

योनौ—स्वस्थाने पवित्रे । (*yonau—svasthāne pavitre |*) योनि (*yoni*) means place. Since the Soma is poured into the vessel for straining called the ten-fold filter and is strained, that straining vessel, the filter, is what is indicated here by the word योनि (*yoni*).

सीदन् होतेव चमूषु—होता यथा यज्ञे देवान् स्तोतुमुपविशति तथा सोमः ग्रहादिचमसपात्रॆषु उपविशति (*sīdan hoteva camūṣu—hotā yathā yajñe devān stotumupaviśati tathā somaḥ grahādicamasapātrèṣu upaviśati*) The meaning is: as the priest called Hotṛ sits in his own place on the sacrificial altar in order to praise the gods, so the Soma juice is placed in the camasa, graha and other vessels that are made ready for it.

होता— होमनिष्पादको अयमग्निः । (*hotā— homaniṣpādako ayamagniḥ |*) Although the word hotṛ designates the priest who invites the gods in order that they may accept the oblations, it applies also to Agni, who in order to bring the oblations that the sacrificers offer in the sacrifice to the gods, brings the gods, offers them the oblations, and so carries out the sacrifice: this meaning has been explained. A meaning of this kind is employed especially with regard to Agni. And further: होमनिष्पादकं आह्वातारं वा । (*homaniṣpādakaṃ āhvātāraṃ vā |*) "one who accomplishes the homa by the offering of oblations and the rest, or one who invites the gods": thus two kinds of activity of the Hotṛ are given as the meaning of the word hotṛ. The same idea is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa in the form of a discussion, as follows. It shows the position of the Hotṛ in the sacrifice.

यज्ञो वै देवेभ्य उदक्रामत्तमिष्टिभिः प्रैषमैच्छन्यदिष्टिभिः प्रैषमैच्छंस्तदिष्टीनामिष्टित्वं तमन्वविंदन् । अनुवित्तयज्ञो राध्योति य एवं वेद । आहुतयो वै नामृता यदाहुतॆय एताभिर्नै देवान्यजमानो ह्वयति तदाहुतीनामाहुतित्वं । ऊतयः खलु वै ता नाम याभिर्देवा (*yajño vai devebhya udakrāmattamiṣṭibhiḥ praiṣamaicchanyadiṣṭibhiḥ praiṣamaicchaṃstadiṣṭīnāmiṣṭitvaṃ tamanvaviṃdan | anuvittayajño rādhyoti ya evaṃ veda | āhutayo vai nāmṛtā yadāhutèya etābhirnai devānyajamāno hvayati tadāhutīnāmāhutitvaṃ | ūtayaḥ khalu vai tā nāma yābhirdevā*)

### Printed p. 662

यजमानस्य ह्यवमायंतिये वै पंथानो याः स्तुतयस्ता ना ऊतयस्त उ एवैतत्सर्गयाणा यजमानस्य भवंति ॥ (*yajamānasya hyavamāyaṃtiye vai paṃthāno yāḥ stutayastā nā ūtayasta u evaitatsargayāṇā yajamānasya bhavaṃti ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1-2)

Once the sacrifice went away from the gods. Then they got it back by offering oblations. An oblation (āhuti) is an offering made by invoking a deity by name. When it is said that the one who offers such an oblation is called the Hotṛ, another question arises.

तदाहुर्यदन्यो जुहोत्यथ योऽनु चाह यजति च कस्मात्तं होतेत्याचक्षत इति। यद्वाव स तत्र यथाभाजनं देवता अमुमावहामुमावहेत्यावाहयति तदेव होतुर्होतृत्वं होता भवति । होतेत्येनमाचक्षते य एवं वेद ॥ (*tadāhuryadanyo juhotyatha yo 'nu cāha yajati ca kasmāttaṃ hotetyācakṣata iti| yadvāva sa tatra yathābhājanaṃ devatā amumāvahāmumāvahetyāvāhayati tadeva hoturhotṛtvaṃ hotā bhavati | hotetyenamācakṣate ya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1-2)

To the question how the name Hotṛ is proper for one who utters the mantra of offering, where the one who offers the oblation is one person and the one who gives the invitation and utters the mantra is another, it is answered that since the one who recites this mantra calls the respective deities according to the respective measure of the offerings, the name Hotṛ is proper for him as well; and then:

मनो वै यज्ञस्य मैत्रावरुणो वाग्यज्ञस्य होता ! (*mano vai yajñasya maitrāvaruṇo vāgyajñasya hotā !*) (Ai. Brā. 6-5)

By this sentence the identity of speech, which recites the mantra, and the Hotṛ is stated. And:

सीद होतः स्व उ लोके चिकित्वानित्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैष स्वो लोको यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिः...................नि होता होतृषदने विदान इत्यग्निर्वै देवानां होता तस्यैतद्धोतृषदनं यदुत्तरवेदी नाभिः ॥ (*sīda hotaḥ sva u loke cikitvānityagnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaiṣa svo loko yaduttaravedī nābhiḥ...................ni hotā hotṛṣadane vidāna ityagnirvai devānāṃ hotā tasyaitaddhotṛṣadanaṃ yaduttaravedī nābhiḥ ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 5-2)

These and similar sentences address Agni, the accomplisher of the homa, as Hotṛ; therefore in the Ṛk at hand two kinds of meaning can be given to the word होतारं (*hotāraṃ*): होमनिष्पादकं आह्वातारं ना (*homaniṣpādakaṃ āhvātāraṃ nā*) **NOTE**.

ऋषियः सप्त विप्रा अग्मन्—सप्त ऋषय एनं सोमं स्तोत्रैरुपगच्छंति ! (*ṛṣiyaḥ sapta viprā agman—sapta ṛṣaya enaṃ somaṃ stotrairupagacchaṃti !*) The seven wise seers approach Soma, reciting hymn-mantras. Here Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gotama, Atri, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni and Vasiṣṭha are said to be the seven seers.

### Printed p. 663

ऋयषः— ऋषिः अतींद्रियद्रष्टा । (*ṛyaṣaḥ— ṛṣiḥ atīṃdriyadraṣṭā |*) One who, by the power of his austerity, can know what other ordinary people cannot know, the past, future and present, and the nature of Brahman, is called a ṛṣi.

The derivation of the word ṛṣi is given in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa in this way; at the same time the relation between creation and the seers is also shown.

असद्वा इदमग्र आसीत् । तदाहुः किं तदसदासीदित्यषयो नाव तेऽग्रेऽ सदासीत्तदाहुः के त ऋषय इति प्राणा ना ऋषयस्ते यत्पुरास्मात्सर्वस्मादिदमिच्छंतः क्रमेण तपसारिषंस्तस्मादृषयः (*asadvā idamagra āsīt | tadāhuḥ kiṃ tadasadāsīdityaṣayo nāva te 'gre ' sadāsīttadāhuḥ ke ta ṛṣaya iti prāṇā nā ṛṣayaste yatpurāsmātsarvasmādidamicchaṃtaḥ krameṇa tapasāriṣaṃstasmādṛṣayaḥ*) (Śa. Brā. 6-1-1-1)

Before creation there was only non-being. These seers were in that form. Who are the seers? They are the chief vital breaths. Before creation, desiring the creation of the world, they practised austerity for it and toiled. Therefore they are called seers: thus the derivation of the word ṛṣi is stated (तपसारिषंस्तस्मादृषयः (*tapasāriṣaṃstasmādṛṣayaḥ*)). And:

............त्वयि तंतुमेतमिति योऽसावृषिभिस्तंतुस्तु तस्तमेतदाह (*............tvayi taṃtumetamiti yo 'sāvṛṣibhistaṃtustu tastametadāha*) (Śa. Brā. 8-6 3-22) **NOTE**

They spun the sacrificial thread that is of the nature of the universe; they became the cause of the expansion of the world: thus the power of the seers is praised. For that very reason they are also said to be of the nature of Brahman, the root of creation:

प्राणा ना यषयः प्रथमजास्तद्धि ब्रह्म प्रथमजं (*prāṇā nā yaṣayaḥ prathamajāstaddhi brahma prathamajaṃ*) (Śa. Brā. 8-6-1-5)

Thus the identity of the seers and Brahman is shown. If this is one kind of derivation, another derivation is possible in contrast to it, as stated in the Vācaspatya:

यमति ज्ञानेन संसारपारं (*yamati jñānena saṃsārapāraṃ*)

Because one crosses to the far shore of saṃsāra through knowledge, the word ṛṣi, formed from the root ṛṣ, means the knowers. Thus according to one derivation the seers are the root cause of the creation of the world, and according to the other derivation the cause of the cessation of saṃsāra. The description of the Ṛk at hand is that both these powers were in the seers. In the words उभौ वर्ण पुपोष (*ubhau varṇa pupoṣa*), through obtaining Rāma-satisfaction **NOTE** the power of creation is described, and through obtaining spiritual knowledge the power that is the means of the cessation of saṃsāra is described.

### Printed p. 664

The derivation given above shows that the word ṛṣi is formed from the root ऋषी (ऋष्) गत् । (*ṛṣī (ṛṣ) gat |*), a root of the sense of non-going. **NOTE** Further, the scholar Monier Williams states in his Sanskrit-English Dictionary that the word ṛṣi can also be formed from the root dṛś, and, giving the meaning of the word ऋषिकृत् (*ṛṣikṛt*) with two authorities, has stated the meaning Causing to see, enlightening. In this example, firstly:

इमामग्ने शरणिं मीमृषो न इममध्वानं यमगाम दूरात् । आपिः पिता प्रमतिः सोम्यानां भृमिरस्यृषिकृन्मर्त्यानां ॥ (*imāmagne śaraṇiṃ mīmṛṣo na imamadhvānaṃ yamagāma dūrāt | āpiḥ pitā pramatiḥ somyānāṃ bhṛmirasyṛṣikṛnmartyānāṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-31-16)

In this Ṛk the word ऋषिकृत् (*ṛṣikṛt*) is an epithet of Agni. Sāyaṇa has given this word the meaning दर्शनकारी (*darśanakārī*). Similarly:

ऋषिमना य ऋषिकृत्स्वर्षाः सहस्रणीथः पदवीः कवीनां । तृतीयं धाम महिषः सिषासन्मो विराजमनु राजति ष्टुप् ॥ (*ṛṣimanā ya ṛṣikṛtsvarṣāḥ sahasraṇīthaḥ padavīḥ kavīnāṃ | tṛtīyaṃ dhāma mahiṣaḥ siṣāsanmo virājamanu rājati ṣṭup ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-96-18)

in this Ṛk too the word ऋषिमानाः (*ṛṣimānāḥ*) has been explained as सर्वदर्शनशील मनस्यः (*sarvadarśanaśīla manasyaḥ*) and ऋषिकृत् (*ṛṣikṛt*) as सर्वस्य दर्शनकर्ता (*sarvasya darśanakartā*). In worldly usage too, the synonym darśana for knowledge of the truth indicates these ideas.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र सु॑मे॒धा गा॑तु॒विद्वि॒श्वदे॑वः॒ सोमः॑ पुना॒नः सद॑ एति॒ नित्य॑म् ।  
> भुव॒द्विश्वे॑षु॒ काव्ये॑षु॒ रंतानु॒ जना॑न्यतते॒ पंच॒ धीरः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सुऽमेधाः । गातुऽवित् । विश्वऽदेवः । सोमः । पुनानः । सदः । एति । नित्यम् ।  
> भुवत् । विश्वेषु । काव्येषु । रंता । अनु । जनान् । यतते । पंच । धीरः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सुमेधाः । ‘ नित्यमसिच् प्रजामेधयोः' ( पा. सू. ५. ४. १२२) इत्यसिच्समासांतः । शोभनप्रज्ञः गातुवित् मार्गस्य वेत्ता । यद्वा । गातवः स्तोतारः । तेषां धनस्य लंभयिता । विश्वदेवः सर्वदेवोपगतः । यद्वा । देवो देवनं दीप्तिः । व्यापकदीप्तियुक्तः । एतादृशः सोमः पुनानः पूयमानः सन् नित्यम् अविनश्वरं सदः स्थानं द्रोणकलशं प्र एति प्रगच्छति । ततः विश्वेषु सर्वेषु काव्येषु कविकर्मसु स्तोत्रेषु रंता भुवत् रमणशीलो भवति । रमेस्ताच्छीलिकस्तृन् । तथा धीरः प्राज्ञः सोऽयं पंच जनान् निषादपंचमांश्चतुरो वर्णान् अनु यतते अनुगंतुं प्रयत्नं करोति । अनुगच्छतीति यावत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*): of good wisdom; गातुवित् (*gātuvit*): the knower of the path; or else, the gātus are the praisers, and he causes them to obtain wealth; विश्वदेवः (*viśvadevaḥ*): attended by all the gods; or else, deva is devana, light: possessed of pervading light. Such a Soma, being purified, goes forth continually to the imperishable सदः (*sadaḥ*), place, the Droṇakalaśa. Then among all the काव्येषु (*kāvyeṣu*), the works of poets, the hymns, he becomes delighted. Likewise, being धीरः (*dhīraḥ*), wise, he strives to follow the पंच जनान् (*paṃca janān*), the four classes together with the Niṣādas as the fifth; the meaning is that he goes after them.

### Printed p. 665

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—one of excellent wisdom
- गातुविन् (*gātuvin*)—the knower of the right path **NOTE**
- विश्वदेवः (*viśvadevaḥ*)—one accompanied by all the gods
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma, the god
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—having attained purification
- नित्यं (*nityaṃ*)—constant (imperishable)
- सदः (*sadaḥ*)—the Droṇakalaśa
- प्र एति (*pra eti*)—enters
- विश्वेषु काव्येषु (*viśveṣu kāvyeṣu*)—in all acts of praise
- रंता भुवत् (*raṃtā bhuvat*)—attains delight
- धीरः (*dhīraḥ*)—Soma, the wise
- पंच जनान् (*paṃca janān*)—the five peoples beginning with the Niṣādas
- अनु यतते (*anu yatate*)—strives to approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, the god, who has excellent wisdom, who knows the right path and who is accompanied by all the gods, having attained purification, enters the imperishable Droṇakalaśa. He attains delight in all acts of praise. Soma, the wise, strives to approach the five peoples beginning with the Niṣādas.

##### English translation
Soma, the intelligent, the knower of the right path, accompanied by all the gods, undergoing purification goes to his constant abode ; he is one who delights in all sacred praises ; the sage endeavourrs to approach the five classes of beings. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पंच जनान् (*paṃca janān*)—In the Ṛgveda the words पंच जनाः (*paṃca janāḥ*) and पंच क्षितयः (*paṃca kṣitayaḥ*) are seen to be used here and there. Both kinds of words have one meaning. Therefore, as to who these पंचजनाः (*paṃcajanāḥ*) or पंचक्षितयः (*paṃcakṣitayaḥ*) are, Sāyaṇa has given two kinds of meaning. First,

1. देवा मनुष्याः पितरः पशवः पक्षिणश्चेति पंच जनाः । (*devā manuṣyāḥ pitaraḥ paśavaḥ pakṣiṇaśceti paṃca janāḥ |*) The five kinds are the gods, men, fathers, animals and birds; and second,

### Printed p. 666

2. चत्वारो वर्णाः निषादपंचमाः पंच जना इत्यन्ये (*catvāro varṇāḥ niṣādapaṃcamāḥ paṃca janā ityanye*)—he has explained in another way as well: the people of the four classes together with the Niṣādas. For both these meanings the authority of Vedic statements can be shown. First the derivation of the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) may be examined, and afterwards it may be considered what meaning can be given to पंचक्षिति (*paṃcakṣiti*) in the present context.

क्षितीनां (*kṣitīnāṃ*)—क्षियंति निवसंति गच्छंति ना क्षितयो मनुष्याः । (*kṣiyaṃti nivasaṃti gacchaṃti nā kṣitayo manuṣyāḥ |*) Sāyaṇa has explained that men have this epithet because they dwell or move about. The Nirukta authors have read the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*) among the twenty-five names of man beginning with नरः (*naraḥ*). (Ni. 3-7)

अग्निर्नेता भग इव क्षितीनां दैवीनां देव ऋतुपा ऋतावा । स वृत्रहा सनयो विश्ववेदाः पर्षद्विश्वाति दुरिता गृणंतं ॥ (*agnirnetā bhaga iva kṣitīnāṃ daivīnāṃ deva ṛtupā ṛtāvā | sa vṛtrahā sanayo viśvavedāḥ parṣadviśvāti duritā gṛṇaṃtaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-20-4)

In such Ṛks, when the difference between men and the subjects belonging to the gods is shown, men, the subjects of the earth, are indicated by the word क्षिति (*kṣiti*). But in the present Ṛk it cannot be said precisely that earthly men are meant, because Indra's wealth pervades the earth and the atmosphere altogether.

न यस्य देवा देवता न मर्ता आपश्चन शवसो अंतमापुः । स परिक्षा त्वक्षसा क्ष्मो दिवश्च मरुत्वान्नो भवत्विंद्र ऊती ॥ ( (*na yasya devā devatā na martā āpaścana śavaso aṃtamāpuḥ | sa parikṣā tvakṣasā kṣmo divaśca marutvānno bhavatviṃdra ūtī ‖ (*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-100 15)

In such Ṛks it is described that the power of Indra, who is endowed with the qualities of generosity and the like and is of the nature of a god, surpasses the power of all others in the world; that neither gods nor men could reach its end; and that Indra with his own power, which destroys enemies and is full of majesty, makes the earth and heaven both shine together. Because of this, and because in the present Ṛk too Indra's wealth is described as all-pervading, पंचक्षितीनां (*paṃcakṣitīnāṃ*) cannot be said to mean merely the four classes together with the Niṣādas as the fifth. In this matter the Nirukta authors have not said what their own view is, and have only stated the opinions of others.

पंचजना “मम होत्रं जुषध्वं” गंधर्वाः पितरो देवा असुरा रक्षांसीत्येके । चत्वारो वर्णा निषादः पंचम इत्यौपमन्यवः ॥ (*paṃcajanā “mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ” gaṃdharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsītyeke | catvāro varṇā niṣādaḥ paṃcama ityaupamanyavaḥ ‖*) (Ni. 3-8)

Some hold that they are five kinds of groups: Gandharvas, fathers, gods, Asuras and Rākṣasas; and Upamanyu and others are of the opinion that the people of the four classes beginning with the Brāhmaṇas, together with the fifth group called Niṣādas, are the five peoples. Thus only the opinions of others have been stated.

### Printed p. 667

Formerly, when all the gods prayed to Agni to accept the oblation offered in the sacrifice for them and to distribute it among all, Agni agreed, and

तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुरा अभि देवा असाम । ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पंच जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वं ॥ (*tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurā abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ paṃca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvaṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-53-4)

gave the answer that the five peoples together should enjoy this oblation. The authors of the Bṛhaddevatā have quoted this statement and discussed the differences of opinion about the five peoples.

प्रत्युवाचाथ तानग्निर्विश्वेदेवा यदूच मां । तत्करिष्ये जुषंतां तु होत्रं पंचजना मम ॥ (*pratyuvācātha tānagnirviśvedevā yadūca māṃ | tatkariṣye juṣaṃtāṃ tu hotraṃ paṃcajanā mama ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-66)

In this verse the answer that Agni gave to the gods is told, and afterwards the word पंचजन (*paṃcajana*) is explained.

शालामुख्यः प्रणीतश्च पुत्रो गृहपतेश्च यः । उत्तरो दक्षिणश्चाग्निरेते पंचजनाः स्मृताः ॥ (*śālāmukhyaḥ praṇītaśca putro gṛhapateśca yaḥ | uttaro dakṣiṇaścāgnirete paṃcajanāḥ smṛtāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-67)

That is, the fire at the entrance of the hall, the prepared Āhavanīya fire, the Gārhapatya fire which is as a son of the sacrificer, and the southern and the northern fires: these five kinds of fires together are the five kinds of groups, according to the traditional usage. Besides this view,

मनुष्याः पितरो देवा गंधर्वोरगराक्षसाः । गंधर्वा पितरो देवा असुरा यक्षराक्षसाः ॥ (*manuṣyāḥ pitaro devā gaṃdharvoragarākṣasāḥ | gaṃdharvā pitaro devā asurā yakṣarākṣasāḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-68)

According to the first opinion the Uragas and Rākṣasas are one group; according to the second opinion the Yakṣas and Rākṣasas are one group.

यास्कौपमन्यवावेतानाहतुः पंच वै जनान् । निषादपंचमान्वर्णा मन्यते शाकटायनः ॥ (*yāskaupamanyavāvetānāhatuḥ paṃca vai janān | niṣādapaṃcamānvarṇā manyate śākaṭāyanaḥ ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-69)

In this statement the authors of the Bṛhaddevatā say that Yāska's view is the first. But in the Nirukta only the views of others are stated, and Yāska has not stated his own view precisely. Perhaps he may have accepted that one.

### Printed p. 668

ऋत्विजो यजमानं च शाकपूणिस्तु मन्यते । (*ṛtvijo yajamānaṃ ca śākapūṇistu manyate |*) (Bṛ. De. 7-20)

It is the view of Śākapūṇi that the four priests beginning with the Hotṛ, together with the sacrificer, make five groups.

चक्षुःश्रोत्रं मनो वाक् च प्राणश्चेत्यात्मवादिनः ॥ गंधर्वाप्सरसो देवा मनुष्याः पितरस्तथा ॥ सर्पाश्च ब्राह्मणे चैव श्रूयंते हैतरेयके ॥ (*cakṣuḥśrotraṃ mano vāk ca prāṇaścetyātmavādinaḥ ‖ gaṃdharvāpsaraso devā manuṣyāḥ pitarastathā ‖ sarpāśca brāhmaṇe caiva śrūyaṃte haitareyake ‖*) (Bṛ. De. 7-71,72)

Eye, ear, mind, speech and breath: these five are the five peoples, according to those who hold the spiritual view. That they are Gandharvas and the rest is explained in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa (Ai. Brā. 3-31-5). That Agni gave the gods the answer that such five peoples should enjoy the oblation is said, and in the explanation of the Bṛhaddevatā also the differences of opinion are stated.

पंच क्षितीनां विश्वानि वसु इंद्रस्य हस्तयोः । (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ viśvāni vasu iṃdrasya hastayoḥ |*) Thus it is described in the Ṛk 1-176-3. Since the whole world is under the protection of Indra, all the above opinions fit the expression पंच क्षितीनां (*paṃca kṣitīnāṃ*).

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तव॒ त्ये सो॑म पवमान नि॒ण्ये विश्वे॑ दे॒वास्त्रय॑ एकाद॒शासः॑ ।  
> दश॑ स्व॒धाभि॒रधि॒ सानो॒ अव्ये॑ मृ॒जंति॑ त्वा न॒द्यः॑ स॒प्त य॒ह्वीः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तव । त्ये । सोम । पवमान । निण्ये । विश्वे । देवाः । त्रयः । एकादशासः ।  
> दश । स्वधाभिः । अधि । सानौ । अव्ये । मृजंति । त्वा । नद्यः । सप्त । यह्वीः ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान पूयमान हे सोम तव स्वभूताः त्ये ते प्रसिद्धाः त्रय एकादशासः । पूरणार्थे डट् प्रत्ययः । त्रयस्त्रिंशत्संख्याकाः विश्वे सर्वे देवाः निण्ये । अंतर्हितनामैतत् । अंतर्हिते स्थाने द्युलोके वर्तंते । तादृशं त्वां दशसंख्याका अंगुलयः अधि सानौ अधिकं समुच्छ्रिते अव्ये अविमये पवित्रे स्वधाभिः उदकैः मृजंति शोधयंति । किंच यह्वीः ।' वा छंदसि । इति पूर्वसवर्णदीर्घः । यह्वयो महत्यः सप्त सप्तसंख्याका गंगाद्याः नद्यः त्वा त्वां मृजंति । वसतीवर्यात्मकैरेकधनात्मकैश्च स्वीयैरुदकैस्त्वां मार्जयंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Pavamāna, O Soma, those well-known त्रय एकादशासः (*traya ekādaśāsaḥ*), who belong to you, are thirty-three in number: all the gods. निण्ये (*niṇye*) is a name for what is concealed; they abide in the concealed place, the heavenly world. You, such as you are, the ten fingers purify with स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*), that is, with waters, on the lofty fleece, raised up high, in the अव्ये (*avye*), the strainer made of wool. Further, यह्वीः (*yahvīḥ*) means the great ones: the seven great rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, purify you; the meaning is that they cleanse you with their own waters, which are of the nature of वसतीवर्यात्मकैरेकधनात्मकैश्च (*vasatīvaryātmakairekadhanātmakaiśca*).

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—named Pavamāna
- सोम (*soma*)—O god Soma
- तव (*tava*)—related to you
- त्ये (*tye*)—well-known
- त्रय एकादशासः (*traya ekādaśāsaḥ*)—of the number thirty-three
- विश्वे देवाः (*viśve devāḥ*)—all the gods
- निण्ये (*niṇye*)—are in the secret heavenly world
- दश (*daśa*)—the ten fingers
- अधि सान्सौ (*adhi sānsau*)—being in the elevated place **NOTE**
- अव्ये (*avye*)—in the daśāpavitra
- स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)—with waters
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—purify you
- यह्वीः (*yahvīḥ*)—having great forms
- सप्त नद्यः (*sapta nadyaḥ*)—the seven rivers
- त्वा (*tvā*)—you
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—cleanse

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O god Soma, named Pavamāna, all the gods who are related to you, well-known, thirty-three in number, are in the secret heavenly world. In the daśāpavitra, which is in the elevated place, the ten fingers of the Adhvaryu and the other priests purify you. The seven rivers, of great form, cleanse you.

##### English translation
O Soma Pavamana, your are the thrice eleven universal gods abiding in the secret (heaven) ; the ten (fingers) cleanse you with the waters upon the elevated fleece, the seven great rivers (cleanse you). **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

त्रय एकादशासः विश्वे देवाः (*traya ekādaśāsaḥ viśve devāḥ*)—the meaning is thirty-three gods. In the Ṛk beginning ये देवासो दिव्येकादशस्थ (*ye devāso divyekādaśastha*) it is told who the thirty-three gods are. Addressing all the gods of the three worlds, it says: you, who are all the gods, accept this sacrifice of ours. By दिवि एकादश, पृथिव्यां एकादश, अप्सुक्षितो एकादश (*divi ekādaśa, pṛthivyāṃ ekādaśa, apsukṣito ekādaśa*) it is said that the total number of gods from the three worlds is thirty-three. Sāyaṇa, quoting the Nirukta statement यद्यपि तिस्र एव देवताः (*yadyapi tisra eva devatāḥ*) (Ni. 7-5), has explained: क्षित्याद्यभिमानिन्यो . देवतास्तिस्र एव तथापि महिता महत्वेन स्वस्वविभूत्या त्रयस्त्रिंशत्संख्याता भवंति । तत्तत्स्थाना अन्यास्तद्विभूतय इत्युक्तत्वात् । (*kṣityādyabhimāninyo . devatāstisra eva tathāpi mahitā mahatvena svasvavibhūtyā trayastriṃśatsaṃkhyātā bhavaṃti | tattatsthānā anyāstadvibhūtaya ityuktatvāt |*) That is, although the presiding deities of the earth, the atmosphere and heaven are only three in number, they appear as thirty-three in number by their respective greatness; all the remaining gods in those worlds are their manifestations. The Nirukta authors also—

### Printed p. 670

तिस्र एव देवता इति नैरुक्ताः । अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानः । वायुर्वा इंद्रो वा अंतरिक्षस्थानः । सूर्यो द्युस्थानः । तासां महाभाग्यात् एकैकस्या अपि बहूनि नामधेयानि भवंति । अपि ना कर्मपृथक्त्वात् । (*tisra eva devatā iti nairuktāḥ | agniḥ pṛthivīsthānaḥ | vāyurvā iṃdro vā aṃtarikṣasthānaḥ | sūryo dyusthānaḥ | tāsāṃ mahābhāgyāt ekaikasyā api bahūni nāmadheyāni bhavaṃti | api nā karmapṛthaktvāt |*) (Ni. 7-5)

According to the view of the Nirukta authors, these three deities, Agni, Vāyu or Indra, and Sūrya **NOTE**, are the presiding deities of the three worlds, the earth, the atmosphere and heaven. Having said that these deities have many kinds of names, in accordance with their respective greatness or because of the variety of their actions, it has stated, with अथातोऽनुक्रमिष्याम अग्निः पृथिवीस्थानः तं प्रथमं व्याख्यास्यामः। (*athāto 'nukramiṣyāma agniḥ pṛthivīsthānaḥ taṃ prathamaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ|*), the nature of the deities of the earth from Ni. 7-14 to 9-43; with अथातो मध्यस्थाना देवताः । तासां वायुः प्रथमागामि भवति । (*athāto madhyasthānā devatāḥ | tāsāṃ vāyuḥ prathamāgāmi bhavati |*), the nature of the deities of the middle region, the atmosphere, from 10-1 to 11-50; and with अथातो द्युस्थाना देवताः (*athāto dyusthānā devatāḥ*), the nature of the deities of the heavenly world from 12-1 to the end of the chapter. Although there are differences of opinion on how many deities there are in this division, in many places of the Ṛksaṃhitā one and the same view is seen.

आ नासत्या त्रिभिरेकादशैरिह देवेभिर्यातं मधुपेयमश्विना । प्रायुस्तारिष्टं नी रपांसि मृक्षतं सेधतं द्वेषो भवतं सचाभुवा ॥ (*ā nāsatyā tribhirekādaśairiha devebhiryātaṃ madhupeyamaśvinā | prāyustāriṣṭaṃ nī rapāṃsi mṛkṣataṃ sedhataṃ dveṣo bhavataṃ sacābhuvā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 134-11) **NOTE**

(11-3) Thus the Aśvin deities are prayed to: come here with the thirty-three gods, desiring the drink of mead.

श्रुष्टीवानो हि दाशुषे देवा अग्ने विचेतसः । तान्रोहिदश्व गिर्वणस्रयस्त्रिंशतमा वह ॥ (*śruṣṭīvāno hi dāśuṣe devā agne vicetasaḥ | tānrohidaśva girvaṇasrayastriṃśatamā vaha ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-45-2)

Agni is prayed to in the same way as in the present Ṛk: bring the thirty-three gods.

ऐभिरग्ने सरथं याह्यर्वाज् नानारथं ना विभवो ह्यश्वाः । पत्नीवतस्त्रिंशतं त्रींश्च देवाननुष्पधमा वह मादयस्व ॥ (*aibhiragne sarathaṃ yāhyarvāj nānārathaṃ nā vibhavo hyaśvāḥ | patnīvatastriṃśataṃ trīṃśca devānanuṣpadhamā vaha mādayasva ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-6-9) **GLOSS**

इति स्तुतासो असथा रिशादसो ये स्थ त्रयश्च त्रिंशच्च । मनोर्देना यज्ञियासः ॥ (*iti stutāso asathā riśādaso ye stha trayaśca triṃśacca | manordenā yajñiyāsaḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-30-2) **GLOSS**

विश्वैर्देवैस्त्रिभिरेकादशैरिहाद्भिर्मरुद्भिर्भृगुभिः सचाभुवा । (*viśvairdevaistribhirekādaśairihādbhirmarudbhirbhṛgubhiḥ sacābhuvā |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-35-3) **GLOSS**

### Printed p. 671

तव त्ये सोम पवमान निण्ये विश्वे देवास्त्रय एकादशासः । दश स्वधाभिरधि सानो अव्ये मृजंति त्वा नद्यः सप्त यह्वीः । (*tava tye soma pavamāna niṇye viśve devāstraya ekādaśāsaḥ | daśa svadhābhiradhi sāno avye mṛjaṃti tvā nadyaḥ sapta yahvīḥ |*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-92-4)

In such Ṛks too it is clear that the number of the gods is thirty-three. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa too,

अष्टौ वसवः । एकादश रुद्राः । द्वादशादित्या' इमे एव द्यावापृथिवी त्रयस्त्रिंशद्वै देवाः प्रजापतिश्च तुस्त्रिंशः । (*aṣṭau vasavaḥ | ekādaśa rudrāḥ | dvādaśādityā ' ime eva dyāvāpṛthivī trayastriṃśadvai devāḥ prajāpatiśca tustriṃśaḥ |*) (Śa. Badra, 4-5-7-2) **NOTE**

the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras, the twelve Ādityas and Dyāvāpṛthivī together are thirty-three gods; Prajāpati, besides these, is the thirty-fourth: thus it is said in one place. But in another place, although the number is the same thirty-three, Indra and Prajāpati are included in place of Dyāvāpṛthivī.

ते त्रयस्त्रिंशदित्यष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्यास्त एकत्रिंशदिंद्रश्चैव प्रजापतिश्च त्रयस्त्रिंशाविति । (*te trayastriṃśadityaṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāsta ekatriṃśadiṃdraścaiva prajāpatiśca trayastriṃśāviti |*) (Śa. Brā. 11-6-3-5)

In the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too,

त्रयस्त्रिंशद्वै देवाः सोमपास्त्रयस्त्रिंशदसोमपा अष्टौ वसव एकादश रुद्रा द्वादशादित्याः प्रजापतिश्च वषट्कारश्चते देवाः सोमपाः । (*trayastriṃśadvai devāḥ somapāstrayastriṃśadasomapā aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ prajāpatiśca vaṣaṭkāraścate devāḥ somapāḥ |*) (Ai. Bā. 2-18) **NOTE**

The gods who drink the Soma are thirty-three: they are the eight Vasus, the eleven Rudras and the twelve Ādityas; with them Prajāpati and Vaṣaṭkāra. Thus in the Saṃhitā and in the Brāhmaṇas there is one and the same opinion about this number. But,

त्रीणि शता श्री सहस्राण्यग्निं त्रिंशच्च देवा नव चासपर्यन् । औक्षन् धृतैरस्त्रृणन्बर्हिरस्मा आदिद्दोतारं न्यसादयंत ॥ (*trīṇi śatā śrī sahasrāṇyagniṃ triṃśacca devā nava cāsaparyan | aukṣan dhṛtairastrṛṇanbarhirasmā ādiddotāraṃ nyasādayaṃta ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-9-9)

in this Ṛk, and likewise in the Ṛk Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-52-6, it is said that three thousand three hundred and thirty-nine gods worshipped Agni. The same order is found in the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā too (33-7). Besides this,

नमो महद्भो नमो अर्भकेभ्यो नमो युवभ्यो नम आशिनेभ्यः । यजाम देवान्यदि शक्नवाम मा ज्यायसः शंसमा वृक्षि देवाः ॥ (*namo mahadbho namo arbhakebhyo namo yuvabhyo nama āśinebhyaḥ | yajāma devānyadi śaknavāma mā jyāyasaḥ śaṃsamā vṛkṣi devāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-26-1)

### Printed p. 672

When salutation is said to all kinds of gods, those of exceeding qualities, those of lesser qualities, the young and the old, it is understood that there is variety of nature among the gods. This very mantra **NOTE** is recited in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa too (7-16), in the Śunaḥśepa narrative, in the context of the prayer to the Viśvedevas. But,

नहि वो अस्त्यर्भको देवासो न कुमारकः । विश्वे सतोमहांत इत् (*nahi vo astyarbhako devāso na kumārakaḥ | viśve satomahāṃta it*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-20-1) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 8-30-1) **NOTE**

here there is no distinction at all of great and small among the gods; there is the praise that all the gods are great.

नद्यः सप्त यह्वीः (*nadyaḥ sapta yahvīḥ*)—Here seven great rivers are mentioned. Which are these seven great rivers? What are their names? and the like: the discussion of these matters we shall make in the introduction to the 75th sūkta of the tenth maṇḍala. In the 5th Ṛk of that same sūkta the names of these principal rivers are stated in this way—

इमं मे गंगे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि स्तोमं सचता परुष्णा । असिक्किया मरुद्वृधे वितस्तयार्जीकीये शृणुह्या सुषोमया ॥ (*imaṃ me gaṃge yamune sarasvati śutudri stomaṃ sacatā paruṣṇā | asikkiyā marudvṛdhe vitastayārjīkīye śṛṇuhyā suṣomayā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-75-5)

In this Ṛk there are the names of ten principal rivers: Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudri, Paruṣṭhī, Asiknī, Marudvṛdhā, Vitastā, Ārjīkī and Suṣomā. Leaving aside the three rivers that are not much in use, Vitastā, Asiknī and Ārjīkī, the remaining seven rivers are famous as great rivers, and the matter of these seven rivers is mentioned here and there. Since in the Nirukta written by Yāska on the above Ṛk there is an explanation how these rivers came to have these names, we have explained just that here.

इमं मे गंगे यमुने सरस्वति शुतुद्रि परुष्ठि स्तोममासेवध्वमसिक्ना च सह मरुद्वृधे वितस्तया चार्जिकीय आशृणुहि सुसोमया चेति समस्तार्थः ॥ (*imaṃ me gaṃge yamune sarasvati śutudri paruṣṭhi stomamāsevadhvamasiknā ca saha marudvṛdhe vitastayā cārjikīya āśṛṇuhi susomayā ceti samastārthaḥ ‖*)

अथैकपदनिरुक्तं- गंगा गमनात् ॥ (*athaikapadaniruktaṃ- gaṃgā gamanāt ‖*)

यमुना प्रयुवती गच्छतीति ना प्रवियुतं गच्छतीति वा ॥ (*yamunā prayuvatī gacchatīti nā praviyutaṃ gacchatīti vā ‖*)

सरस्वती सॆर इत्यदकनाम सर्तॆस्तद्वती ॥ (*sarasvatī sèra ityadakanāma sartèstadvatī ‖*)

शुतुद्रीशुद्राविणी क्षिप्रद्राविण्याशु तुन्नेव द्रवतीति वा ॥ (*śutudrīśudrāviṇī kṣipradrāviṇyāśu tunneva dravatīti vā ‖*)

इरावतीं परुष्ठीत्याहुः—पर्ववती भास्वती कुटिलगामिनी ॥ (*irāvatīṃ paruṣṭhītyāhuḥ—parvavatī bhāsvatī kuṭilagāminī ‖*)

असिक्न्यशुक्लाशिता--सितमिति वर्णनाम तत्प्रतिषेधोऽसितं ॥ (*asiknyaśuklāśitā--sitamiti varṇanāma tatpratiṣedho 'sitaṃ ‖*)

### Printed p. 673

मरुद्वधाः सर्वा नद्यो मरुत एना वर्धयंति वितस्ता विदग्धा विवृद्धा महाकूला ॥ (*marudvadhāḥ sarvā nadyo maruta enā vardhayaṃti vitastā vidagdhā vivṛddhā mahākūlā ‖*)

आर्जीकीयां विपाडित्याहुः । ऋजीकप्रभवा वर्जुगामिनी वा विपाड्विपाटनाद्वा विप्राशनाद्वा विप्रापणाद्वा पाशा अस्यां व्यपाश्यंत वसिष्ठस्य मुमूर्षतस्तस्माद्विपाडुच्यते ॥ पूर्वमासीदुरुंजिरा ॥ (*ārjīkīyāṃ vipāḍityāhuḥ | ṛjīkaprabhavā varjugāminī vā vipāḍvipāṭanādvā viprāśanādvā viprāpaṇādvā pāśā asyāṃ vyapāśyaṃta vasiṣṭhasya mumūrṣatastasmādvipāḍucyate ‖ pūrvamāsīduruṃjirā ‖*)

सुषोमा सिंधुर्यदेनामभिप्रसुवंति नद्यः ॥ (*suṣomā siṃdhuryadenāmabhiprasuvaṃti nadyaḥ ‖*)

सिंधुः स्यंदनात् ॥ (*siṃdhuḥ syaṃdanāt ‖*) (Ni. 9-26)

"O Gaṅgā, Yamunā, Sarasvatī, Śutudri together with Paruṣṭhī, Marudvṛdhā together with Asikkī, Ārjīkīyā together with Vitastā: all of you, listen to this hymn that I am reciting": this is the total meaning of this Ṛk. For each of these words, Gaṅgā and the rest, the nirukta, that is, the meaning of the parts, will be stated—

गंगा (*gaṃgā*)—The word Gaṅgā is derived from a word expressing going, formed from the root गम्लृ (*gamlṛ*), which has the meaning "to go" (to flow).

यमुना (*yamunā*)—Because it flows mixed with (joined to) other rivers, or slowly, or without sound, this river is called Yamunā.

सरस्वति (*sarasvati*)—सरः (*saraḥ*) means water. "Possessing water" means that, because it has plenty of water, or because it keeps moving without stopping (flowing on), this river is called Sarasvatī.

शुतुद्रि (*śutudri*)—Because it runs away swiftly, or flows swiftly, or flows swiftly like those who run when urged by others, this river is called Śutudri.

परुष्टी (*paruṣṭī*)—The river Irāvatī itself is called the river Paruṣṭī. Paruṣṭī means that which has पर्व (*parva*) or joints (knots). Because this river flows in windings, this river has come to have the name Paruṣṭī.

असिक्नी (*asiknī*)—It means that which is not white, that which is black. सितं (*sitaṃ*) means that which is white. असित (*asita*) means that which is not white, that which is black. Because the water of this river is not clear but has a slight dark tinge, this river has got the name Asiknī.

मरुध्वधे (*marudhvadhe*)—Because this river grows through all the other rivers (its tributaries) and through the wind, and flows overflowing, it is called Marudvadhā.

### Printed p. 674

वितस्ता (*vitastā*)—It means a river with high banks formed of unburnt, that is, raw sticky clay.

आर्जीकीया (*ārjīkīyā*)—This has also the name विपाड् (*vipāḍ*). Because this river rises and flows in the country called Ṛjuka, or because it flows straight without bends (turns), this river is called Ārjīkīyā.

विपाट् (*vipāṭ*)—Because this river, when flowing, flows crossing over its banks, or flows bursting through the two banks that confine it, or flows spreading widely beyond the banks, this river is called Vipāṭ. Formerly, when the sons of the sage Vasiṣṭha had died, the sage, unable to bear the grief for his sons, wished to kill himself, tied his hands and feet with ropes and sank in this river Vipāṭ. But the river, not wishing to kill him, tore off his ropes and saved him. Because it tore off the ropes in this way, this river came to have the name Vipāṭ. Formerly this river had the name उरुंजिरा (*uruṃjirā*), a river with abundant water.

सुषोमा (*suṣomā*)—This river has also the name of the river Sindhu, because all the rivers (its tributaries) flow to it in order to join it (confluence). The word सिंधु (*siṃdhu*) means flowing. Some are of the opinion that, because excellent soma creepers grew on the bank of this river, the name Suṣomā (सु+सोम (*su+soma*)) may have come to this river.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तन्नु स॒त्यं पव॑मानस्यास्तु॒ यत्र॒ विश्वे॑ का॒रवः॑ सं॒नसं॑त ।  
> ज्योति॒र्यदह्ने॒ अकृ॑णोदु लो॒कं प्राव॒न्मनुं॒ दस्य॑वे कर॒भीक॑म् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तत् । नु । सत्यम् । पवमानस्य । अस्तु । यत्र । विश्वे । कारवः । सम्ऽनसंत ।  
> ज्योतिः । यत् । अह्ने । अकृणोत् । ऊं इति । लोकम् । प्र । आवत् । मनुम् । दस्यवे । कः । अभीकम् ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 675

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सत्यं सत्यभूतं तत् प्रसिद्धं पवमानस्य सोमस्य स्थानं नु क्षिप्रमस्माकम् अस्तु । यत्र यस्मिन् स्थाने विश्वे सर्वे कारवः स्तोतारः संनसंत स्तोतुं संगच्छंते तत्स्थानमस्तु । अस्य सोमस्य यत् ज्योतिः अह्ने दिवसाय लोकम् आलोकं प्रकाशम् अकृणोत् करोति । उ इत्यवधारणे । तज्ज्योतिः मनुम् एतन्नामानं राजर्षिं प्रावत् प्रकर्षेणारक्षत् । तथा सोमः स्वयं तेजः दस्यवे सर्वस्योपक्षपयित्रेऽसुराय अभीकम् अभिगमनशीलं कः अकार्षीत् । करोतेर्लुङि  मंत्रे घस° ' इति च्लेर्लुक् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That well-known place of Pavamāna, Soma, which is of the nature of truth, let it quickly be ours: the place in which all the praisers assemble to praise; let that place be ours. The light of this Soma which makes लोकम् (*lokam*), that is, brightness, light, for the day; here उ (*u*) is in the sense of emphasis. That light protected Manu, the royal sage so named, exceedingly. Likewise Soma himself made his energy such as to approach, to confront, the Dasyu, the Asura who wastes away everything: who made it? कः (*kaḥ*), he made it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- यत्र (*yatra*)—in the divine place of which Soma
- विश्वे कारवः (*viśve kāravaḥ*)—all the praisers
- संनसंत (*saṃnasaṃta*)—are gathered together; of such
- पवमानस्य (*pavamānasya*)—of the god Soma
- तत् (*tat*)—well-known
- सत्यं (*satyaṃ*)—of the nature of truth, the place
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- अस्तु (*astu*)—let it be ours
- यत् ज्योतिः (*yat jyotiḥ*)—the light of which Soma
- अह्ने (*ahne*)—for the day
- लोकं (*lokaṃ*)—brightness
- अकृणोत् (*akṛṇot*)—produces, that light
- मनुं (*manuṃ*)—Manu, the royal sage
- प्रावत् (*prāvat*)—protected (that same energy)
- दस्यवे (*dasyave*)—the Asura
- अभीकं (*abhīkaṃ*)—so as to confront and defeat
- कः (*kaḥ*)—Soma made

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Let the well-known place of the god Soma, of the nature of truth, in whose divine place all the praisers are gathered together, quickly become ours. The light of Soma which produces brightness for the day protected the royal sage called Manu; Soma made that same energy such as to confront and defeat the Asura.

##### English translation
May that place of the truthful Pavamana be quickly ours, where all the worshippers assemble (to praise him); the light (of the Soma) which gave manifestation to the day protected Manu—Soma made it triumphant over the Dasyu.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

मनुं (*manuṃ*)—Although the name of Manu is read in many places in the Ṛgveda, no further description is found anywhere. Manu may be understood as the primal ancestor of the human race and as the guide in the method of performing sacrifices and the like. In many contexts, with the words "as Manu did" (मनुष्यत् (*manuṣyat*)) **NOTE**, the work done by Manu is also praised. When he was distributing his property among his children,

### Printed p. 676

his youngest son, named Nābhānediṣṭha, was studying in the guru's house in celibacy and so was not near his father. His father at that time divided his property among all the other children who were near him. Nābhānediṣṭha received no share of inheritance. He, having completed his studies, came to his father and asked about his share; then Manu told him everything that had happened, and said that he now had nothing, but taught him a device for obtaining wealth. "O son, do not think about wealth. The Āṅgirasa sages are now performing a sacrifice. If you go to that place and teach them some mantras, their sacrifice will proceed in perfect order and they will give you wealth as much as you wish," and sent him off. Nābhānediṣṭha, according to his father's word, went to the sacrificial ground of the Aṅgirasa sages, taught them the mantras and obtained wealth from them as much as he wished. This account is explained at length in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa and in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā of the Yajurveda. Chiefly because the sacrifice performed by this Manu is famous, the matter of the sacrifice performed by Manu is mentioned here and there in the Ṛgveda. The matter of this Manu is told not only in the Ṛgveda but in places such as the Atharvaveda (14-2-41) and the Taittirīya Saṃhitā (Tai. Saṃ. 3-1-9-4, 5).

मनुः (*manuḥ*)—Since the usage occurs also when men in general are intended, as "Manu" or "Manus", it is difficult to know when men are intended and when the person called Manu. In the second sense, the usage occurs about twenty times in the singular as "Manu" and about as many times in the plural; Manu is called "father" five times, and in two of these still more clearly "our father" (2-33-13: and the like). (विशः (*viśaḥ*) 4-37-1;) **NOTE** Agni dwells in the progeny of Manu (1-68-4). It is Manu who began the sacrifices. Having kindled Agni, together with the seven sages, he gave the first offering to the gods (10-63-7). The very sacrifice practised by Manu is what everyone practises now. The present sacrifice is compared to the sacrifice that the Manus performed with reference to the gods (1-76-5). By the adverb मनुस्वत् (*manusvat*) (like Manu) the sacrificial acts are compared again and again. Like the Manus, the worshippers complete the sacrifice with Agni (1-44-11). Like the Manus, they kindle Agni (5-21-1 and the like). They praise Agni, kindled by Manu, just like Manu (7-2-3). Like the Manus, they offer the Soma juice (4-37-3). Soma is prayed to flow for them now, as he flowed formerly for Manu (9-96-12). Manu established Agni so that he might be a light for all people (1-36-19). With the ancient sacrificers, the Aṅgirases and the Yayātis (1-31-17), Bhṛgu and Aṅgirasa

### Printed p. 677

Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases (8-43-13), with Atharvan and Dadhyañc (1-80-16), and with Dadhyañc, the Aṅgirases, Atri and the Kaṇvas (1-139-1) Manu too is included. The gods (1-36-10), Mātariśvan (1-128-2), Mātariśvan and the gods (1-46-9) or the poet Uśanas (8-23-17,): these gave Agni to Manu **NOTE** or appointed him as the priest of Manu. In four contexts Manu must mean a man.

Indra drank Soma together with Manu, the son of Vivasvant (Vā. 4-1) **NOTE**, or with Manu Sāṃvaraṇi (Vā. 3-1). To obtain the strength needed for fighting with the Asura Vṛtra, Indra drank the soma juice belonging to the Manus, as much as three lakes (5-29-7). A bird brought the soma juice to Manu (4-26-4). In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā and the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇas Manu is described as the patron of religious rites.

Manu is conceived as the son of Vivasvant; he has the name Vaivasvata Manu (4-1; compare 3-1). In the Atharvaveda (A. Ve. 8-10-24) **NOTE**, the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 13-4-3-3) and the Purāṇas and the like, the name Vaivasvata has become customary for Manu. Among the children of Vivasvant Yama is one, and he is the first among men. That is, Manu and Yama may be called the two primal progenitors of men. But while Manu is the first among the living, Yama became the first among the dead and the lord of the world of the dead. In the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, Vaivasvata Manu is called the king of men and Yama the king of the dead (Śa. Brā. 13-4-3-3 5) **NOTE**. In the Nirukta (Ni. 12-10), Manu is explained as the son of the Āditya called Vivasvant and of the woman called Savarṇā (which may have been used in the place of Saraṇyu) (compare 10-17-2), and he is indicated as one of the deities of the heavenly world (Ni. 5-6) (Ni. 12-34).

There is a story in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa (Śa. Brā. 1-8-1-1 to 10) that at the time of the deluge, although all other creatures were drowned, Manu alone was saved in a ship by a fish (an incarnation of Viṣṇu). It was then that Manu became the cause of the human race through his daughter named Iḍā (Iḷā), born of oblations. This story of the deluge is found in the Atharvaveda too (A. Ve. 19-39-8).

#### Ṛk 6

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ सद्मे॑व पशु॒मांति॒ होता॒ राजा॒ न स॒त्यः समि॑तीरिया॒नः ।  
> सोमः॑ पुना॒नः क॒लशाँ॑ अयासी॒त्सीद॑न्मृ॒गो न म॑हि॒षो वने॑षु ॥ ६ ॥

### Printed p. 678

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । सद्मऽइव । पशुऽमंति । होता । राजा । न । सत्यः । सम्ऽइतीः । इयानः ।  
> सोमः । पुनानः । कलशान् । अयासीत् । सीदन् । मृगः । न । महिषः । वनेषु ॥ ६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> होता देवानामाह्वातर्त्विक् पशुमंति पशुमतः सद्मेव यज्ञगृहान् यथोपगच्छति । किंच राजा न यथा राजा सत्यः सत्यकर्मा सन् समितीः । संग्रामनामैतत् सम्यक् प्राप्यते योद्धृभिरत्रेति । तान् संग्रामान् इयानः गच्छन् भवति तथा पुनानः सोमः वनेषु वननीयेषु वसतीवर्याख्येषूदकेषु सीदन् मृगो न महिषः महिषाख्यो मृग इवोदकेषु तिष्ठन् कलशान् द्रोणाभिधानान् अयासीत् परियाति । यद्वा । महिषो महान् पूज्यो वा सोमः कलशान् परिगच्छतीति ॥ ॥ २ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The Hotṛ, the priest who summons the gods, goes to the sacrificial houses पशुमंति (*paśumaṃti*), those that have animals, as one goes to one's own house. Further, as a king, being of true action, goes to समितीः (*samitīḥ*), which is a name for battle (that in which warriors properly (सम्यक् (*samyak*)) attain), going to those battles, so Soma, being purified, abiding in वनेषु (*vaneṣu*), the lovable waters called vasatīvarī, like the wild beast called महिषः (*mahiṣaḥ*) staying in water, goes round the vessels called Droṇa. Or else, महिषः (*mahiṣaḥ*) means great or worthy of worship: Soma goes round the vessels.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- होता (*hotā*)—the Hotṛ
- पशुमंति (*paśumaṃti*)—possessed of sacrificial animals
- सद्मेव (*sadmeva*)—as he enters the sacrificial house
- सत्यः (*satyaḥ*)—of true action
- राजा (*rājā*)—the king
- समितीः न इयानः (*samitīḥ na iyānaḥ*)—as he enters the field of battle
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—the purifier
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- महिषः मृगो न (*mahiṣaḥ mṛgo na*)—as the wild beast called mahiṣa enters the water
- वनेषु (*vaneṣu*)—in the vasatīvarī and the rest
- सीदन् (*sīdan*)—being stationed
- कलशान् (*kalaśān*)—into the Droṇakalaśa
- अयासीत् (*ayāsīt*)—enters

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the Hotṛ enters the sacrificial house provided with sacrificial animals, as the king of true action enters the field of battle, Soma, the purifier, stationed in the vasatīvarī and the rest, enters the Droṇakalaśa, as the wild beast called mahiṣa (the buffalo) enters the water.

##### English translation
As the ministrant priest proceeds to the hall where the victim is stationed, as a just king marches to battle, the Soma undergoing purification enters the pitchers like the wild buffalo in the waters, **NOTE**

The ninety-third sūkta.

## Sūkta 93 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> साकमुक्षः' इति पंचर्चमष्टमं सूक्तं गौतमस्य नोधस आर्षम् । पूर्ववच्छंदोदेवते । तथा चानुक्रम्यते- साकमुक्षः पंच नोधाः' इति । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eighth sūkta, of five Ṛks, beginning साकमुक्षः (*sākamukṣaḥ*), is the ārṣa of Nodhas Gautama. Its metre and deity are as before. And so the Anukramaṇī says साकमुक्षः पंच नोधाः (*sākamukṣaḥ paṃca nodhāḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated.

### Printed p. 679

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, साकमुक्षः (*sākamukṣaḥ*), is the eighth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Nodhas, the son of the sage Gotama; Pavamāna Soma is the deity; the metre is Triṣṭup. That it is said in the Anukramaṇikā साकमुक्षः पंच नोधाः (*sākamukṣaḥ paṃca nodhāḥ*): the viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 93. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 93. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 4, Varga 3. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Nodhas. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सा॒क॒मुक्षो॑ मर्जयंत॒ स्वसा॑रो॒ दश॒ धीर॑स्य धी॒तयो॒ धनु॑त्रीः ।  
> हरिः॒ पर्य॑द्रव॒ज्जाः सूर्य॑स्य॒ द्रोणं॑ ननक्षे॒ अत्यो॒ न वा॒जी ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> साकम्ऽउक्षः । मर्जयंत । स्वसारः । दश । धीरस्य । धीतयः । धनुत्रीः ।  
> हरिः । परि । अद्रवत् । जाः । सूर्यस्य । द्रोणम् । ननक्षे । अत्यः । न । वाजी ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> साकमुक्षः सह युगपत् सिंचंत्यः । उक्ष सेचने'। क्विपि रूपम् । तादृश्यः स्वसारः कर्मकरणार्थमितस्ततः सुष्ठु गच्छंत्योऽंगुल्यः मर्जयंत सोमं शोधयंति। ‘ मृजू शौचालंकारयोः' । तथा दश दशसंख्याकाः धीतयः । अंगुलिनामैतत् । अंगुलयः धीरस्य समर्थस्य प्राज्ञस्य वा देवैर्ध्यातव्यस्य काम्यमानस्य वा सोमस्य धनुत्रीः प्रेरयित्र्यो भवंति । ततः हरिः हरितवर्णः सोमः सूर्यस्य जाः प्रादुर्भूता जाया दिशस्ताः पर्यद्रवत् परितो गच्छति । सूर्यतेजसा ह्याविर्भवतीति दिशां तस्य जात्वम् । अत्यः अतनशीलः वाजी न अश्व इव स्थितः सोमः द्रोणं कलशं ननक्षे व्याप्नोति । नक्षतिर्व्याप्तिकर्मा ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

साकमुक्षः (*sākamukṣaḥ*): sprinkling together, at one time (the root उक्ष (*ukṣa*) has the sense of sprinkling). Such sisters, the fingers, moving well hither and thither in order to perform the rite, मर्जयंत (*marjayaṃta*), purify the Soma (the root मृजू (*mṛjū*) has the sense of cleansing and adorning). Likewise the ten, ten in number, धीतयः (*dhītayaḥ*), which is a name of the fingers, the fingers, are धनुत्रीः (*dhanutrīḥ*), impellers, of the धीरस्य (*dhīrasya*) Soma, who is able or wise, or is to be meditated upon by the gods, or is desired. Then हरिः (*hariḥ*), the green-hued Soma, goes round on all sides the जाः (*jāḥ*) of the Sun, the manifested wives, the directions; for they become manifest through the Sun's light, and so the directions are said to be born of him. Staying like a अत्यः (*atyaḥ*), one who keeps moving, a swift horse, Soma pervades the Droṇa, the vessel, ननक्षे (*nanakṣe*). नक्षति (*nakṣati*) has the sense of pervading.
