##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- साकमुक्षः (*sākamukṣaḥ*)—gathered together and pressing
- स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*)—the fingers
- मर्जयंत (*marjayaṃta*)—purify the Soma
- दश धीतयः (*daśa dhītayaḥ*)—the ten fingers also
- धीरस्य (*dhīrasya*)—for the wise Soma
- धनुत्रीः (*dhanutrīḥ*)—are impellers
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—Soma, of green colour
- सूर्यस्य जाः परि (*sūryasya jāḥ pari*)—in all the directions lighted by the sun
- अद्रवत् (*adravat*)—moves
- अत्यः (*atyaḥ*)—swift-going
- वाजी न (*vājī na*)—like a horse
- द्रोणं (*droṇaṃ*)—into the Droṇakalaśa
- ननक्षे (*nanakṣe*)—enters

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The fingers, which gather together and press, purify the Soma. The ten fingers also are impellers of the wise Soma. Soma, of green colour, moves in all the directions lighted by the sun. Like a swift-going horse he enters the Droṇakalaśa.

##### English translation
The sister (fingers) sprinkling together cleanse (the Soma), the ten fingers (are) the effusers of the sagacious (Soma); the green-tinted one flows round the wives of the sun, he hastens like a swift horse to the pitcher.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दश स्वसारः (*daśa svasāraḥ*)—कर्मकरणार्थमितस्ततः सुष्टु गच्छंत्योऽज्जुलयः । (*karmakaraṇārthamitastataḥ suṣṭu gacchaṃtyo 'jjulayaḥ |*) Because they keep moving hither and thither while working, the fingers have the name स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*). Besides, स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) also has the meaning sisters: since the fingers have gone forth from the hand, the hand is the common place of origin of the fingers. Women who have one and the same place of origin are called sisters of one another. Here, since the hand is the common place of origin of the fingers, it has become customary to call these fingers by the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*). In the present Ṛk it is indicated that the ten fingers on the hands of the priests, the Adhvaryu and the others, are engaged in the work of crushing the soma creeper with stones and pressing out the juice. The description of this work has been given in many Ṛks of this maṇḍala. Yāska in his Nirukta has read the word स्वसारः (*svasāraḥ*) among the twenty-two names of the fingers beginning with आग्रुवः (*āgruvaḥ*). (Ni. 3-9)

### Printed p. 681

सूर्यस्य जाः (*sūryasya jāḥ*)—सूर्यस्य प्रादुर्भूता जाया दिशः । सूर्यतेजसा ह्याविर्भवंतीति दिशां तस्य जात्वं ॥ (*sūryasya prādurbhūtā jāyā diśaḥ | sūryatejasā hyāvirbhavaṃtīti diśāṃ tasya jātvaṃ ‖*) Here जाः (*jāḥ*) has been taken to mean the directions: since by the light of the sun the directions all around become visible to everyone, the seer has described the directions as produced (illumined) by the sun.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सं मा॒तृभि॒र्न शिशु॑र्वावशा॒नो वृषा॑ दधन्वे पुरु॒वारो॑ अ॒द्भिः ।  
> मर्यो॒ न योषा॑म॒भि नि॑ष्कृ॒तं यन्सं ग॑च्छते क॒लश॑ उ॒स्रिया॑भिः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सम् । मातृऽभिः । न । शिशुः । वावशानः । वृषा । दधन्वे । पुरुऽवारः । अत्ऽभिः ।  
> मर्यः । न । योषाम् । अभि । निःऽकृतम् । यन् । सम् । गच्छते । कलशे । उस्रियाभिः ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वावशानः देवान् कामयमानः वृषा कामानां वर्षकोऽत एव पुरुवारः बहुभिर्वरणीयः सोमः अद्भिः मातृभूताभिर्वसतीवरीभिः सं दधन्वे संधार्यते । तत्र दृष्टांतः । मातृभिर्न शिशुः । कामयमानः पुत्री यथा मातृभिः पयःप्रदानेन संधार्यते । धविर्गत्यर्थः । कर्मणि लिटि रूपम् । मर्यो न मनुष्यो यथा योषां युवतिमभिगच्छति तद्वत् निष्कृतं संस्कृतं स्वस्थानम् अभि यन् अभिगच्छन् कलशे द्रोणाभिधाने उस्रियाभिः अद्भिर्गोविकारैः क्षीरादिभिर्वा सं गच्छते । गमेरकर्मकात् ' समो गम्यृच्छि' इत्यात्मनेपदम् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Longing for the gods, वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*), the showerer of desires, वृषा (*vṛṣā*), and therefore पुरुवारः (*puruvāraḥ*), to be chosen by many, Soma is held together with the waters, अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*), the vasatīvarī waters who are like mothers. An illustration for this: मातृभिर्न शिशुः (*mātṛbhirna śiśuḥ*), as a longing child is sustained by its mothers through the giving of milk. मर्यो न (*maryo na*): as a man goes to a young woman, so going to his own prepared place, in the vessel called Droṇa he unites with उस्रियाभिः (*usriyābhiḥ*), with waters, or with products of the cow, milk and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शिशुः (*śiśuḥ*)—the child
- मातृभिः न (*mātṛbhiḥ na*)—as it joins its mothers
- वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*)—one who longs for the gods
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—the granter of desires
- पुरुवारः (*puruvāraḥ*)—desired by many; Soma, the god, being such
- अद्भिः (*adbhiḥ*)—with the vasatīvarīs
- सं दधन्वे (*saṃ dadhanve*)—joins
- मर्यः (*maryaḥ*)—a man
- योषां न (*yoṣāṃ na*)—as he goes near a young woman
- निष्कृतं (*niṣkṛtaṃ*)—to his well-refined place
- अभि यन् (*abhi yan*)—going
- कलशे (*kalaśe*)—in the Droṇakalaśa
- उस्रियाभिः (*usriyābhiḥ*)—with milk and the like
- सॆं गच्छते (*sèṃ gacchate*)—joins **NOTE**

### Printed p. 682

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a child joins its mother, Soma, the god, who longs for the gods, grants desires and is desired by many, joins the vasatīvarīs. As a man goes near a young woman, going to his well-refined place he joins in the Droṇakalaśa with milk and the like.

##### English translation
Longing (for the deities) the showerer (of benefits) the desired of many (the Soma) is sustained by the (consecrated) waters as the infant by its mother; going to his station like a bridegroom to his bride, he combines in the pitcher with the curds and milk.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The soma juice, pressed out of the creepers, flows away and goes and falls into the vessel called the Droṇakalaśa, placed for it. The seer has described this by two kinds of illustrations. One kind of illustration is this: as a small child goes to its mother's side for suckling, the soma juice goes in order to join the वसतीवरी (*vasatīvarī*) water, which is like a mother to it. The soma juice just pressed is compared to a small child. It is natural for a child to go to its mother. In the same way, as a preliminary to offering the pressed soma to the gods, it is to be purified in the दशापवित्र (*daśāpavitra*) and refined by rites such as mixing it with the water of the vessel called वसतीवरी (*vasatīvarī*). That is what is said here in the comparison: the soma juice goes in order to be mixed with the वसतीवरी (*vasatīvarī*) water. The second comparison is this: in the way a young man goes eagerly to the young woman dear to him, this soma juice goes to the Droṇakalaśa in order to join the substances such as milk with which it is mingled **NOTE**. This is the second illustration. In order that the soma juice may have taste, substances called आशिर (*āśira*), milk, curds and flour, are added to it. The soma juice to which milk is added has the name गवाशिर (*gavāśira*), that to which curds are added दध्याशिर (*dadhyāśira*), and that to which flour is added यवाशिर (*yavāśira*): different names. The seer has described the soma juice flowing to be mixed with आशिर (*āśira*) substances of this kind, comparing it to a young man going to unite with a young woman.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> उ॒त प्र पि॑प्य॒ ऊध॒रघ्न्या॑या॒ इंदु॒र्धारा॑भिः सचते सुमे॒धाः ।  
> मू॒र्धानं॒ गावः॒ पय॑सा च॒मूष्व॒भि श्री॑णंति॒ वसु॑भि॒र्न नि॒क्तैः ॥ ३ ॥

### Printed p. 683

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> उत । प्र । पिप्ये । ऊधः । अघ्न्यायाः । इंदुः । धाराभिः । सचते । सुऽमेधाः ।  
> मूर्धानम् । गावः । पयसा । चमूषु । अभि । श्रीणंति । वसुऽभिः । न । निक्तैः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> उत अपि च अघ्न्यायाः । अघ्न्येति गोनाम । अहंतव्याया गोः ऊधः पयःस्थानं सोमः प्र पिप्ये । ओषध्यादिषु सोमः प्रविश्य प्रकर्षेणाप्याययति । प्यायतेर्लिटि लिड्यङोश्च ' इति पीभावः । सुमेधाः शोभनप्रज्ञः सोऽयम् इंदुः सोमः धाराभिः सचते समवैति संगच्छते । ततः गावः चमूषु । चमंति भक्षयन्यत्र सोममिति चम्वो ग्रहादयः । तेषु स्थितं मूर्धानं समुच्छ्रितमिमं सोमं पयसा श्वेतेन अभि श्रीणंति अभित आच्छादयंति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । निक्तैः प्रक्षालितैः वसुभिर्न वस्त्रैर्यथाच्छादयंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"Also" (उत (*uta*)): the udder of the cow अघ्न्यायाः (*aghnyāyāḥ*) — अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*) is a name of the cow, one not to be killed — that is, the place of the milk, is nourished by Soma (प्र पिप्ये (*pra pipye*)): Soma enters the plants and the like and nourishes them greatly. The wise Indu, Soma, is united with his streams (सचते (*sacate*): comes together, joins). Then the cows clothe this elevated Soma, standing in the चमूषु (*camūṣu*) (the vessels in which the Soma is drunk, the Graha cups and the rest, called camvaḥ because they take in the Soma), with white milk, covering him on all sides. The illustration: as people cover themselves with washed garments (वसुभिर्न (*vasubhirna*), the word vasubhiḥ meaning garments), so the cows cover the Soma.

##### English translation
And he nourishes the cow's udder ; the intelligent Indu is associated with his streams ; the cows clothe the elevated Soma in the ladies with their milk as with newly washed robes. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 684

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अघ्नायाः (*aghnāyāḥ*)—अहंतव्या गोः । (*ahaṃtavyā goḥ |*) The cow, which is not fit to be killed, that is, which is to be revered, is called अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*). The word अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*) is read among the nine names of the cow. (Ni. 3-9). **NOTE**

अघ्न्यायाः ऊधः प्र पिप्ये (*aghnyāyāḥ ūdhaḥ pra pipye*)—गोः पयःस्थानं ओषध्यादिशु सोमः प्रविश्य आप्याययति । (*goḥ payaḥsthānaṃ oṣadhyādiśu somaḥ praviśya āpyāyayati |*) The meaning is that this god Soma nourishes the milk in the udders of the cows and makes it increase. What relation is there between Soma and the cows? How does Soma make the milk increase in the cows? According to the Śruti sentence सोमो वनस्पतीनामधिपतिः (*somo vanaspatīnāmadhipatiḥ*), the deity Soma is the lord of the plants and trees. Therefore he nourishes well the grass and the like, the food of cattle such as cows, makes it full of sap, and by that means is the cause of the cows' thriving. Because the cows eat food full of sap, they give milk abundantly. The meaning is that the deity Soma is thus the indirect (indirectly) cause of the cows giving much milk.

निक्तै वसुभिर्न चमूषु मूर्धनि स्थितं पयसा अभि श्रीणंति । (*niktai vasubhirna camūṣu mūrdhani sthitaṃ payasā abhi śrīṇaṃti |*) When people put on clean, well-washed, shining garments, they look white; in the same way, when the milk of the cows is mixed with the Soma juice filled in the Camasa vessels, the Soma juice looks white, like people wrapped in white cloth. The meaning is that when the cows mix their white milk with the Soma juice, they make that Soma juice look white. In this way the seer has described it in another manner.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स नो॑ दे॒वेभिः॑ पवमान र॒देंदो॑ र॒यिम॒श्विनं॑ वावशा॒नः ।  
> र॒थि॒रा॒यता॑मुश॒ती पुरं॑धिरस्म॒द्र्य१॒॑गा दा॒वने॒ वसू॑नाम् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । नः । देवेभिः । पवमान । रद । इंदो इति । रयिम् । अश्विनम् । वावशानः ।  
> रथिरायताम् । उशती । पुरम्ऽधिः । अस्मद्र्यक् । आ । दावने । वसूनाम् ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे पवमान पूयमान सोम सः तादृशस्त्वं नः अस्मभ्यं देवेभिः देवैः सह रद प्रयच्छ । किं तत् उच्यते । हे इंदो पात्रेषु क्षरन् सोम वावशानः कामयमानः सन् अश्विनम् अश्ववंतं रयिं धनं प्रयच्छति । किंच रथिरायताम् । रथो येषामस्तीति रथिराः । ‘ मेधारथाभ्याम्' इतीरच्प्रत्ययः । तद्वदाचरतस्तानिच्छतो वा पुरुषान् उशती कामयमाना पुरंधिः त्वदीया बहुविधा धीः वसूनां धनानां दावने दानाय अस्मद्र्यक् अस्मदभिमुखी आ आगच्छतु । यद्वा । रथिरायितामिति धनानां विशेषणम् । बलवतां धनानामिति । अस्मद्र्यक् । 'विष्वग्देवयोश्च टेरद्र्यंचतावप्रत्यये । (पा. सू. ६. ३. ९२ ) इत्यद्र्यादेशः । अद्रिसध्र्योरंतोदात्तत्वनिपातनात् ' उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यणः । इति स्वरितः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Pavamāna, Soma who art being purified, such as thou art, give (रद (*rada*)) to us together with the gods." What is it that he gives? "O Indu, Soma flowing in the vessels, desiring (वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*)), thou bestowest wealth, riches with horses (अश्विनम् (*aśvinam*))." Further, रथिरायताम् (*rathirāyatām*): those who have a chariot are रथिराः (*rathirāḥ*); men who behave like them or who wish for them. Thy manifold intelligence (पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)), desiring (उशती (*uśatī*)) such men, should come (आ (*ā*)) towards us (अस्मद्र्यक् (*asmadryak*)) for the giving (दावने (*dāvane*)) of riches (वसूनाम् (*vasūnām*)). Or else: rathirāyitām is an epithet of riches, meaning mighty riches.

### Printed p. 685

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- पवमान इंदो (*pavamāna iṃdo*)—O Soma named Pavamāna
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- देवेभिः (*devebhiḥ*)—with the gods
- वावशानः (*vāvaśānaḥ*)—desiring their company
- अश्विनं (*aśvinaṃ*)—possessed of horses
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- रद (*rada*)—give
- रथिरायतां (*rathirāyatāṃ*)—men possessing a chariot
- उशती (*uśatī*)—desiring
- पुरंधिः (*puraṃdhiḥ*)—your intelligence
- वसूनां दावने (*vasūnāṃ dāvane*)—for the giving of wealth
- अस्मध्यक् (*asmadhyak*)—towards us **NOTE**
- आ (*ā*)—may it come

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva named Pavamāna, desiring the company of the gods, give us wealth possessed of horses. May your intelligence, which desires men possessing chariots, come towards us for the giving of wealth.

##### English translation
Indu Pavamana, do you with the gods, who do long for (our good) bestow upon us riches comprising horses ; may your capacious mind longing for those possess chariots (come) towards us to bestow treasures (upon us).

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

रथिरायतां (*rathirāyatāṃ*)—रथो येषामस्तीति रथिराः । (*ratho yeṣāmastīti rathirāḥ |*) तद्वदाचरतस्तानिच्छतो वा पुरुषान् । (*tadvadācaratastānicchato vā puruṣān |*) Those who possess a chariot are called रथिराः (*rathirāḥ*). The meaning of this word is: desiring such men who are charioteers. Or: रथिरायतामिति वसूनां विशेषणं बलवतां धनानामिति । (*rathirāyatāmiti vasūnāṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ balavatāṃ dhanānāmiti |*) The word रथिरायतां (*rathirāyatāṃ*) may also be said to be an epithet of the word वसूनां (*vasūnāṃ*). In this case the meaning can be said to be: of riches and the like that are possessed of chariots, loaded in chariots, or that give strength.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> नू नो॑ र॒यिमुप॑ मास्व नृ॒वंतं॑ पुना॒नो वा॒ताप्यं॑ वि॒श्वश्चं॑द्रम् ।  
> प्र वं॑दि॒तुरिं॑दो ता॒र्यायुः॑ प्रा॒तर्म॒क्षू धि॒याव॑सुर्जगम्यात् ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 686

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> नु । नः । रयिम् । उप । मास्व । नृऽवंतम् । पुनानः । वाताप्यम् । विश्वऽचंद्रम् ।  
> प्र । वंदितुः । इंदो इति । तारि । आयुः । प्रातः । मक्षु । धियाऽवसुः । जगम्यात् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम पुनानः पूयमानस्त्वं नः अस्मभ्यं नु क्षिप्रं नृवंतं मनुष्यैर्युक्तम् । छांदसं मतुपो वत्वम् । तादृशं रयिं धनम् उप मास्व उपनिर्मिमीष्व । उपकुर्वित्यर्थः । किं च विश्वचंद्रं सर्वेषामाह्लादकं वाताप्यम्। उदकनामैतत् । उदकं च कुरु । तथा हे इंदो सोम वंदितुः तव स्तोतुः आयुः जीवनं प्र तारि त्वया वर्धितमस्तु । सोऽयं सोमः धियावसुः बुद्ध्या  कर्मणा वा प्राप्तधनः प्रातः काले वा सवने वा मक्षु शीघ्रमस्मदीयं यज्ञं प्रति जगम्यात् आगच्छेत् । गमेर्लिङि ‘ बहुलं छंदसि ' इति शपः श्लुः ॥ ॥ ३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

"O Soma, being purified, quickly (नु (*nu*)) fashion for us (उप मास्व (*upa māsva*): bring about, do us the favour of) riches, rich in men (नृवंतं (*nṛvaṃtaṃ*): possessed of men)." Further, make the वाताप्यम् (*vātāpyam*) — this is a name of water — that gladdens all (विश्वचंद्रं (*viśvacaṃdraṃ*)). Likewise, O Indu, Soma, may the life of thee, thy praiser (वंदितुः (*vaṃdituḥ*)), be lengthened (प्र तारि (*pra tāri*)) by thee. May this Soma, who has obtained wealth (धियावसुः (*dhiyāvasuḥ*)) by intelligence or by rite, come (जगम्यात् (*jagamyāt*)) quickly (मक्षु (*makṣu*)) to our sacrifice in the morning (प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)), that is, at the morning pressing.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who have obtained purity
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- नु (*nu*)—quickly
- नृवंतं (*nṛvaṃtaṃ*)—together with men
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- उप मास्व (*upa māsva*)—provide
- विश्वचंद्रं (*viśvacaṃdraṃ*)—delightful to the whole world
- वाताप्यं (*vātāpyaṃ*)—provide water
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma
- वंदितुः (*vaṃdituḥ*)—of your praiser
- आयुः (*āyuḥ*)—life
- प्र तारि (*pra tāri*)—may it grow long
- धियावसुः (*dhiyāvasuḥ*)—Soma, who has wealth in the form of rites
- प्रातः (*prātaḥ*)—in the morning
- मक्षु (*makṣu*)—quickly
- जगम्यात् (*jagamyāt*)—may he come to the house of the sacrifice

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, you who have obtained purity, quickly provide us with wealth together with sons and the like. Provide us water that is delightful to the whole world. O Soma, may the life of him who praises you grow long. May Soma, who has wealth in the form of rites, come quickly in the morning to the house of the sacrifice. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 687

##### English translation
Soma, when you are purified, measure out to us riches and dependents and all-gratifying water. Indu, may the life of your praiser be prolonged ; may (Soma) who acquires wealth by his intelligence come quickly at dawn.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk, which is a conclusion, Soma-deva is prayed to bestow wealth and the like, offspring such as sons, and long life on those who praise him, and to come in the morning to the sacrificial ground of the praiser.

The ninety-fourth sūkta.

## Sūkta 94 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘ अधि यत्' इति पंचर्चं नवमं सूक्तमांगिरसस्य कण्वस्यार्षम् । तथानुक्रम्यते---- अधि यत्कण्वः' इति । पूर्ववच्छंदोदेवते । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The ninth sūkta, of five Ṛks, beginning अधि यत् (*adhi yat*), is the ārṣa of Kaṇva of the Āṅgirasa line. And so the Anukramaṇī says अधि यत्कण्वः (*adhi yatkaṇvaḥ*). Metre and deity are as before. The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, अधि यत् (*adhi yat*), is the ninth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Kaṇva of the Aṅgirasa gotra; the deity and metre of this sūkta are as in the preceding sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said अधि यत्कण्वः (*adhi yatkaṇvaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 94. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 94. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 4, Varga 4. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Kaṇva. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अधि॒ यद॑स्मिन्वा॒जिनी॑व॒ शुभ॒ स्पर्धं॑ते॒ धियः॒ सूर्ये॒ न विशः॑ ।  
> अ॒पो वृ॑णा॒नः प॑वते कवी॒यन्व्र॒जं न प॑शु॒वर्ध॑नाय॒ मन्म॑ ॥ १ ॥

### Printed p. 688

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अधि । यत् । अस्मिन् । वाजिनिऽइव । शुभः । स्पर्धंते । धियः । सूर्ये । न । विशः ।  
> अपः । वृणानः । पवते । कविऽयन् । व्रजम् । न । पशुऽवर्धनाय । मन्म ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> यत् यदा अस्मिन् सोमे वाजिनीव शुभः अश्वे यथा वस्त्रप्रभृत्यलंकारा भवंति । यदा वास्मिन् सोमे सूर्ये न यथा सूर्ये विशः रश्मय उदिता भवंति । तदा धियः अंगुलयः अधि स्पर्धंते । अहं पुरस्ताच्छोधयाम्यहं पुरः शोधयामीत्यहमहमिकयोपतिष्ठंति । ततोऽयं सोमः अपः वसतीवरीः वृणानः आच्छादयन् पवते पात्रेषु क्षरति । कलशानधिगच्छति। कीदृशः । कवीयन् कविरिवाचरन् । यद्वा । कवयः स्तोतारः । तानिच्छन् । तत्र दृष्टांतः। व्रजं न मन्म मननीयं गवां गोष्ठं पशुवर्धनाय पशूनां वर्धनाय गोपालः परिगच्छति । तथा देवानां प्रीणनाय पात्राणि प्रति पवत इति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

When (यत् (*yat*)) on this Soma the trappings (शुभः (*śubhaḥ*)) such as garments are, as on a horse (वाजिनीव (*vājinīva*)); or when on this Soma, as in the sun (सूर्ये न (*sūrye na*)), the rays (विशः (*viśaḥ*)) have risen — then the fingers (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)) vie (अधि स्पर्धंते (*adhi spardhaṃte*)), each coming forward with "I shall purify first, I shall purify first". Then this Soma, covering (वृणानः (*vṛṇānaḥ*)) the waters (अपः (*apaḥ*), the वसतीवरीः (*vasatīvarīḥ*)), flows (पवते (*pavate*)) into the vessels and goes to the kalaśas. How? Acting like a poet (कवीयन् (*kavīyan*)); or else desiring the poets, the praisers. The illustration: as a cowherd goes round to the cow-pen (व्रजं न (*vrajaṃ na*)), the desirable (मन्म (*manma*), worthy of thought) stall of the cows, for the increase of cattle (पशुवर्धनाय (*paśuvardhanāya*)), so Soma flows towards the vessels to please the gods.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शुभः (*śubhaḥ*)—ornaments and the like
- वाजनीव (*vājanīva*)—as horses are adorned **NOTE**
- विशः (*viśaḥ*)—rays
- सूर्ये न (*sūrye na*)—as they rise in the sun
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—fingers
- अस्मिन् (*asmin*)—in this Soma
- अधि स्पर्धंते (*adhi spardhaṃte*)—are eager, in rivalry, to purify, then
- कवीयान् (*kavīyān*)—Soma, who desires the welfare of the praisers **NOTE**
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the वसतीवरी (*vasatīvarī*) waters
- वृणानः (*vṛṇānaḥ*)—wrapping himself
- पशुवर्धनाय (*paśuvardhanāya*)—for the nourishing of cattle
- मन्म (*manma*)—having excellent cows
- व्रजं न (*vrajaṃ na*)—as (the cowherd) enters the cow-pen
- पवते (*pavate*)—enters the vessels

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As ornaments and the like lie on horses and adorn them, and as the rays envelop the sun and adorn it, so when the fingers, in mutual rivalry, are eager to envelop Soma and purify him, Soma, who desires the welfare of the praisers, mingled with the वसतीवरी (*vasatīvarī*) waters, enters the vessels, as a cowherd enters, for the nourishing of the cattle, a cow-pen having excellent cows.

##### English translation
When the fingers vie with each other in this (Soma), as the trappings on a horse or the rays in the sun, clothed in the waters he flows desiring his

### Printed p. 689

worshippers like (a cowhered going to) a pleasant cow-stall for the nourishment of his cattle. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> द्वि॒ता व्यू॒र्ण्वन्न॒मृत॑स्य॒ धाम॑ स्व॒र्विदे॒ भुव॑नानि प्रथंत ।  
> धियः॑ पिन्वा॒नाः स्वस॑रे॒ न गाव॑ ऋता॒यंती॑र॒भि वा॑वश्र॒ इंदु॑म् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> द्विता । विऽऊर्ण्वन् । अमृतस्य । धाम । स्वःऽविदे । भुवनानि । प्रथंत ।  
> धियः । पिन्वानाः । स्वसरे । न । गावः । ऋतऽयंतीः । अभि । वावश्रे । इंदुम् ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अमृतस्य उदकस्य धाम धारकं स्थानमंतरिक्षं सोमः द्विता द्विधा व्यूर्ण्वन् उभयतः स्वतेजसाच्छादयन् मध्येन गच्छति । ततः स्वर्विदे सर्वज्ञाय तस्मै सोमाय भुवनानि प्रथंत विस्तीर्णानि भवंति । तस्य रश्मीनां संचरणार्थं प्रथंत इत्यर्थः । अथ पिन्वानाः प्रीणयित्र्यः धियः स्तुतिलक्षणा वाचः ऋतायंतीः यज्ञमिच्छंत्यः सत्यस्तमिमम् इंदुं सोममभिलक्ष्य स्वसरे यागाहनि वावश्रे शब्दायंते । यद्वा । सोमं कामयंते । तत्र दृष्टांतः। गावो न यथा पिन्वमानाः पयः क्षरंत्यो गावः स्वसरे । सुष्ठु अस्यंते प्रेर्यंते गावोऽत्रेति स्वसरो गोष्ठम् । तस्मिन्नच्छाभिलक्ष्य शब्दं कुर्वंति तद्वत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, covering on both sides (द्विता व्यूर्ण्वन् (*dvitā vyūrṇvan*)) with his own lustre the धाम (*dhāma*) of the अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*) — that is, the sky, the place that holds the water — goes through the middle. Then for him, the omniscient (स्वर्विदे (*svarvide*)), the worlds expand (प्रथंत (*prathaṃta*)): they expand for the movement of his rays. Then the gratifying (पिन्वानाः (*pinvānāḥ*)) praises (धियः (*dhiyaḥ*), words of the nature of laudation), desiring the sacrifice (ऋतायंतीः (*ṛtāyaṃtīḥ*)), call out (वावश्रे (*vāvaśre*)) towards this Indu, Soma, on the day of the sacrifice (स्वसरे (*svasare*)); or else they desire Soma. **NOTE**  The illustration: as cows (गावो न (*gāvo na*)), yielding milk and being gratified, call out in the स्वसरे (*svasare*) — स्वसर (*svasara*) is the cow-stall, where the cows are well driven — so they call out in it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अमृतस्य (*amṛtasya*)—to the water
- धाम (*dhāma*)—the sky, which holds it
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—making it two
- व्यूर्णन् (*vyūrṇan*)—pervading that part with his lustre (Soma moves) **NOTE**
- स्वर्विदे (*svarvide*)—for him, the omniscient
- भुवनानि (*bhuvanāni*)—the worlds
- प्रथंत (*prathaṃta*)—attain expansion
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—cows
- स्वसरे न (*svasare na*)—as they call out to go to their stall
- पिन्याना (*pinyānā*)—gratifying **NOTE**
- धियः (*dhiyaḥ*)—words of praise
- ऋतायंतीः (*ṛtāyaṃtīḥ*)—desiring the sacrifice
- इंदुं अभि (*iṃduṃ abhi*)—towards Soma
- वावश्रे (*vāvaśre*)—call out

### Printed p. 690

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, making the sky that holds the water two and pervading that part with his lustre, moves in the middle of them. For him, the omniscient, the worlds expand. As cows call out to go to their stall, gratifying words of praise, desiring the sacrifice, call out towards Soma.

##### English translation
Opening out the abode of the ambrosia on both sides (he passes between) ; for him, the omniscient, the worlds expand. Gratifying laudations eager for the sacrifice, call upon Indu, like cows (lowing) towards their stall,

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> परि॒ यत्क॒विः काव्या॒ भर॑ते॒ शूरो॒ न रथो॒ भुव॑नानि॒ विश्वा॑ ।  
> दे॒वेषु॒ यशो॒ मर्ता॑य॒ भूषं॒दक्षा॑य रा॒यः पु॑रु॒भूषु॒ नव्यः॑ ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> परि । यत् । कविः । काव्या । भरते । शूरः । न । रथः । भुवनानि । विश्वा ।  
> देवेषु । यशः । मर्ताय । भूषन् । दक्षाय । रायः । पुरुऽभूषु । नव्यः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> कविः क्रांतप्रज्ञः सोमः काव्या काव्यानि कवेः कर्माणि स्तोत्राणि यत् यदा परि भरते परितो बिभर्ति । परिगच्छतीति यावत् । कथमिव । शूरो न यथा शूरः शत्रूणां बाधकः रथः तदीयः विश्वा भुवनानि सांग्रामिकाणि भूतानि परियाति तद्वत् । तदानीं देवेषु स्थितं यशः व्यापकं धनं मर्ताय मनुष्याय स्तोत्रे भूषन् । भवतेरंतर्भावितण्यर्थात् सनि रूपम् । भावयितुमिच्छन् सोमः रायः आत्मना दत्तस्य धनस्य दक्षाय वृद्ध्यर्थं पुरुभूषु बहुषु यज्ञभवनेषु नव्यः स्तोतव्यो भवति । ‘णु स्तुतौ' । अचो यत् ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The sage (कविः (*kaviḥ*): one of far-reaching wisdom), Soma, when (यत् (*yat*)) he bears round (परि भरते (*pari bharate*): goes round) the काव्या (*kāvyā*) — the works, the praises, of the sage. How? As a hero (शूरो न (*śūro na*)), a smiter of enemies, his chariot goes round all the worlds, that is, all the beings of the battle. Then the glory (यशः (*yaśaḥ*)), the pervading wealth that abides among the gods, desiring (भूषन् (*bhūṣan*)) to bring it about for the mortal, the praiser — Soma, wishing to cause it to be, becomes worthy to be praised (नव्यः (*navyaḥ*)) in many houses of sacrifice (पुरुभूषु (*purubhūṣu*)) for the growth (दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*)) of the wealth (रायः (*rāyaḥ*)) given by himself.

### Printed p. 691

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—destroying enemies
- रथः (*rathaḥ*)—the chariot
- विश्वा भुवनानि न (*viśvā bhuvanāni na*)—as it takes up all its implements of war
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—Soma, of far-reaching wisdom
- काव्या (*kāvyā*)—praises
- परि भरते (*pari bharate*)—takes up, then
- देवेषु (*deveṣu*)—among the gods
- यशः (*yaśaḥ*)—the wealth
- मर्ताय (*martāya*)—to the mortal praiser
- भूषन् (*bhūṣan*)—desiring to give
- रायः (*rāyaḥ*)—of the wealth given by himself
- दक्षाय (*dakṣāya*)—for the growth
- पुरुभूषु (*purubhūṣu*)—in many houses of sacrifice
- नव्यः (*navyaḥ*)—becomes worthy of praise

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a chariot that destroys enemies takes up all its implements of war, so when Soma, of far-reaching wisdom, takes up the praises, he, desiring to give the wealth that is among the gods to the mortal praiser, becomes worthy of praise in many sacrifices for the growth of the wealth given by himself.

##### English translation
When the sagc Soma goes round praises (of the wise) like a hostile chariot (going round) all the regions (of the battle-field), then desirous of bestowing upon mortals the wealth that abides with the gods, he (is) to be glorified in the many places of sacrifice for the preservation of the riches he has given. **NOTE**

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श्रि॒ये जा॒तः श्रि॒य आ निरि॑याय॒ श्रियं॒ वयो॑ जरि॒तृभ्यो॑ दधाति ।  
> श्रियं॒ वसा॑ना अमृत॒त्वमा॑य॒न्भवं॑ति स॒त्या स॑मि॒था मि॒तद्रौ॑ ॥ ४ ॥

> श्रिये । जातः । श्रिये । आ । निः । इयाय । श्रियम् । वयः । जरितृऽभ्यः । दधाति ।  
> श्रियम् । वसानाः । अमृतऽत्वम् । आयन् । भवंति । सत्या । सम्ऽइथा । मितऽद्रौ ॥ ४ ॥

### Printed p. 692

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> स सोमः श्रिये जातः संपदर्थं प्रादुर्भूतो भवति । तदेवाह । श्रिये श्र्यर्थमेव आ निरियाय । अंशुभ्य आभिमुख्येन निर्गच्छति । निर्गतश्च स सोमः जरितृभ्यः स्तोतृभ्यः श्रियं वयः अन्नं जीवनं वा दधाति विदधाति प्रयच्छति । तेन दत्तां श्रियं वसानाः आच्छादयंतः स्तोतारः अमृतत्वं देवत्वममरणं वा आयन प्राप्नुवन् । तस्मिन् मितद्रौ मितगमने सोमे समिथा । युद्धनामैतत् सम्यक् प्राप्यतेऽत्रेति । ‘ समीणः ' ( उ. सू. २. ११ ) इत्येतेः संपूर्वस्य थक्प्रत्ययः । तानि युद्धानि सत्या सत्यानि यथार्थानि भवंति न तु वितथानि । तेन सोमेन पराजितानि भवंतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

That Soma is born for prosperity, that is, he comes forth for the sake of wealth. This is what he says: श्रिये (*śriye*) — for the sake of prosperity — he issues forth (आ निरियाय (*ā niriyāya*)), going out from the stalks facing us. And having issued forth he gives (दधाति (*dadhāti*)) to the praisers (जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)) prosperity and वयः (*vayaḥ*), that is, food or life. The praisers, clothing themselves in the prosperity given by him, attained (आयन (*āyana*)) immortality, which is divinity or deathlessness. Under him, मितद्रौ (*mitadrau*), who moves with measured tread, the समिथा (*samithā*) — this is a name of battle, where one is rightly reached — those battles become true (सत्या (*satyā*)), real and not false: the meaning is that they are won by that Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—for prosperity
- जातः (*jātaḥ*)—has been born
- श्रिये (*śriye*)—for prosperity
- आ निरियाय (*ā niriyāya*)—goes out
- जरितृभ्यः (*jaritṛbhyaḥ*)—to the praisers
- श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*)—prosperity
- वयः (*vayaḥ*)—and food
- दधाति (*dadhāti*)—gives
- श्रियं (*śriyaṃ*)—the prosperity given by Soma
- वसानाः (*vasānāḥ*)—the praisers who have put it on
- अमृतत्वं (*amṛtatvaṃ*)—freedom from death
- आयन् (*āyan*)—attained (attain)
- मितद्रौ (*mitadrau*)—when there is the help of Soma, who moves with measure
- समिथा (*samithā*)—the battle-acts of the praisers
- सत्या (*satyā*)—true, with good fruit
- भवंति (*bhavaṃti*)—become

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva has been born for prosperity. He goes out for prosperity. He gives the praisers prosperity and food. The praisers who have put on (obtained) the prosperity given by Soma attain freedom from death. When there is the help of Soma, who moves with measure, the battle-acts of the praisers become true, with good fruit.

##### English translation
He (is) generated for prosperity, for prosperity he issues forth, he gives prosperity (and) sustenance to those who praise him ; clothing themselves in (his) prosperity, they obtain immortality ; their eonflicts are successful through the aid of (the Soma) who moves with measured tread. **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इष॒मूर्ज॑म॒भ्य१॒॑र्षाश्वं॒ गामु॒रु ज्योतिः॑ कृणुहि॒ मत्सि॑ दे॒वान् ।  
> विश्वा॑नि॒ हि सु॒षहा॒ तानि॒ तुभ्यं॒ पव॑मान॒ बाध॑से सोम॒ शत्रू॑न् ॥ ५ ॥

### Printed p. 693

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इषम् । ऊर्जम् । अभि । अर्ष । अश्वम् । गाम् । उरु । ज्योतिः । कृणुहि । मत्सि । देवान् ।  
> विश्वानि । हि । सुऽसहा । तानि । तुभ्यम् । पवमान । बाधसे । सोम । शत्रून् ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम इषम् अन्नम् ऊर्जम् अन्नरसं च अस्मभ्यम् अभ्यर्ष अभिगमय । किंच अश्वं वाहनं गां पयःप्रदानेन यज्ञस्य साधनभूतां गां च । तथा उरु महत् ज्योतिः सूर्याख्यं कृणुहि जगदालोकनार्थं कुरु । किंच देवान् इंद्रादीन् मत्सि सोमेन तर्पय । मदेर्लटि ‘बहुलं छंदसि' इति विकरणस्य लुक् । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः । अपि च हे सोम तुभ्यं विश्वानि सर्वाणि रक्षांसि सुषहा सुसहान्यनायासेनैवाभिभवितुं शक्यानि भवंति । हिरवधारणे । अत एव हे पवमान पूयमान हे सोम सर्वान् शत्रून् बाधसे जहि ॥ ॥ ४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, bring to us (अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)) food (इषम् (*iṣam*)) and the juice of food (ऊर्जम् (*ūrjam*)). Further, a horse (अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)), a vehicle, and a cow (गां (*gāṃ*)), the cow that is a means of the sacrifice by giving milk. Likewise make (कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)) the great (उरु (*uru*)) light (ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)) called the sun, for the viewing of the world. Further, delight (मत्सि (*matsi*)) the gods, Indra and the others, with Soma. And, O Soma, for you all the Rākṣasas are easy to overcome (सुषहा (*suṣahā*)): they can be overcome without effort; the word हि (*hi*) is for emphasis. Therefore, O Pavamāna, O Soma who art being purified, smite (बाधसे (*bādhase*): slay) all enemies.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इषं (*iṣaṃ*)—food
- ऊर्जं (*ūrjaṃ*)—and the juice of food
- अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)—provide for us
- अश्वं (*aśvaṃ*)—a horse
- गां (*gāṃ*)—a cow
- उरु (*uru*)—extensive
- ज्योतिः (*jyotiḥ*)—and lustre
- कृणुहि (*kṛṇuhi*)—produce
- देवान् (*devān*)—the gods Indra and the others
- मत्सि (*matsi*)—gratify
- तुभ्यं (*tubhyaṃ*)—to you
- विश्वानि तानि (*viśvāni tāni*)—all the powers of the Rākṣasas
- सुषहा (*suṣahā*)—are easily subdued
- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—purifying
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- शत्रून् (*śatrūn*)—enemies
- भाधसे (*bhādhase*)—you smite **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, give us food and the juice of food. Produce a horse, a cow and extensive lustre. Gratify the gods, Indra and the others. You can easily defeat all the powers of the Rākṣasas. O Soma-deva, the purifier, you smite all enemies.

##### English translation
Bring us food and drink, horses, cattle and ample light, exhilarate the gods ; for all (the Rakshasas) are easily subdued by you ; Soma Pavamana, destroy (all) foes.

The ninety-fifth sūkta.

## Sūkta 95 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ‘कनिक्रंति' इति पंचर्चं दशमं सूक्तं कण्वपुत्रस्य प्रस्कवस्यार्षम् । तथानुक्रम्यते--- कनिक्रंति प्रस्कण्वः' इति । पूर्ववच्छंदोदेवते । गतो विनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The tenth sūkta, of five Ṛks, beginning कनिक्रंति (*kanikraṃti*), is the ārṣa of Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva. And so the Anukramaṇī says कनिक्रंति प्रस्कण्वः (*kanikraṃti praskaṇvaḥ*). Metre and deity are as before. The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, कनिक्रंति (*kanikraṃti*), is the tenth sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has five Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Praskaṇva, the son of Kaṇva. The deity and metre of this sūkta are the same as in the preceding sūkta. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said कनिक्रंति प्रस्कण्वः (*kanikraṃti praskaṇvaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 95. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 95. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 4, Varga 5. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 5. Seer: Praskaṇva. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> कनि॑क्रंति॒ हरि॒रा सृ॒ज्यमा॑नः॒ सीद॒न्वन॑स्य ज॒ठरे॑ पुना॒नः ।  
> नृभि॑र्य॒तः कृ॑णुते नि॒र्णिजं॒ गा अतो॑ म॒तीर्ज॑नयत स्व॒धाभिः॑ ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> कनिक्रंति । हरिः । आ । सृज्यमानः । सीदन् । वनस्य । जठरे । पुनानः ।  
> नृऽभिः । यतः । कृणुते । निःऽनिजम् । गाः । अतः । मतीः । जनयत । स्वधाभिः ॥ १ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सृज्यमानः आ समंताद्विसृज्यमानोऽभियूयमाणः हरिः हरितवर्णः सोमः कनिक्रंति पुनःपुनः शब्दायते । क्रंदतेर्यङ्लुकि तिपीडभावे ‘ दाधर्ति दर्धर्ति इत्यादिना निपातनादभ्यासस्य निगागमः । अभ्यस्तस्वरः । तथा पुनानः पूयमानः वनस्य वननीयस्य द्रोणकलशस्य जठरे सीदन् उपविशन् शब्दायते । किंच नृभिः कर्मनेतृभिर्ऋत्विग्भिः यतः संयतः सोमः गाः गोविकारान् क्षीरादीन्याच्छादयन् निर्णिजम् आत्मनो रूपं कृणुते ग्रहादिषु करोति । अतः अस्मै सोमाय मतीः मननीयाः स्तुतीः स्वधाभिः हविर्भिः सह जनयत स्तोतारः अजनयन्। झस्यांतादेशाभावः छांदसः। यद्वा । हे स्तोतारः अस्मै सोमाय स्तुतीर्जनयत उत्पादयत । कुरुतेति यावत्॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, the green one (हरिः (*hariḥ*)), being sent forth (सृज्यमानः (*sṛjyamānaḥ*)) on all sides, that is, pressed, cries out (कनिक्रंति (*kanikraṃti*)) again and again. And being purified (पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)) he makes a sound, sitting down (सीदन् (*sīdan*)) in the belly (जठरे (*jaṭhare*)) of the lovely (वनस्य (*vanasya*)) Droṇakalaśa. Further, Soma, held in check (यतः (*yataḥ*)) by the priests (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)), the leaders of the rite, covering the products of the cow (गाः (*gāḥ*)), milk and the rest, makes his own form (निर्णिजम् (*nirṇijam*)) in the Graha cups and the like. Therefore the praisers produce (जनयत (*janayata*)) for this Soma thoughts (मतीः (*matīḥ*)), praises worthy of thought, together with oblations (स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)). Or else: O praisers, produce praises for this Soma; that is, make them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सृज्यमानः (*sṛjyamānaḥ*)—the one who has been pressed
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—Soma, of green colour
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—having obtained purity
- वनस्य (*vanasya*)—of the attractive Droṇakalaśa
- जठरे (*jaṭhare*)—in the middle
- सीदन् (*sīdan*)—sitting
- कनिक्रंति (*kanikraṃti*)—makes a sound again and again
- नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*)—by the priests
- यतः (*yataḥ*)—being restrained
- गाः (*gāḥ*)—milk and the rest
- निर्णिजं (*nirṇijaṃ*)—to his own form
- कृणुते (*kṛṇute*)—makes
- अतः (*ataḥ*)—therefore (O praisers)
- मतीः (*matīḥ*)—praises addressed to him
- स्वधाभिः (*svadhābhiḥ*)—together with oblations
- जनयत (*janayata*)—produce

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who has been pressed and is of green colour, having obtained purity, sits in the middle of the attractive Droṇakalaśa and makes a sound again and again. Restrained by the priests, he mixes milk and the rest into his own form. O praisers, produce praises addressed to Soma, together with oblations.

##### English translation
The green-tinted Soma cries aloud when let loose, sitting when filtered in the belly of the pitcher ; collected by the priests, he assumes his shape, (putting on) the products of the cows ; therefore raise praises (to him) with oblations.

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> हरिः॑ सृजा॒नः प॒थ्या॑मृ॒तस्येय॑र्ति॒ वाच॑मरि॒तेव॒ नाव॑म् ।  
> दे॒वो दे॒वानां॒ गुह्या॑नि॒ नामा॒विष्कृ॑णोति ब॒र्हिषि॑ प्र॒वाचे॑ ॥ २ ॥

### Printed p. 696

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> हरिः । सृजानः । पथ्याम् । ऋतस्य । इयर्ति । वाचम् । अरिताऽइव । नावम् ।  
> देवः । देवानाम् । गुह्यानि । नाम । आविः । कृणोति । बर्हिषि । प्रऽवाचे ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सृजानः सृज्यमानः हरिः हरितवर्णः सोमः ऋतस्य सत्यभूतस्य पथ्यां पथि भवां वाचं दैवीम् इयर्ति प्रेरयति । तत्र दृष्टांतः । अरितेव जनांस्तीरं प्रापयन्नाविकः नावं यथा प्रेरयति तद्वत् । ‘ऋ  गतौ । जौहोत्यादिकः । ‘ अर्तिपिपर्त्योः ० इत्यभ्यासस्येत्वम् । ततः देवः दीप्यमानः सोमः देवानाम् इंद्रादीनां गुह्यानि अंतर्हितानि नाम नामानि शरीराणि प्रवाचे प्रकर्षेण वाचयित्रे स्तोत्रे बर्हिषि यज्ञे आविष्कृणोति स्तोतुमाविष्करोति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, the green one (हरिः (*hariḥ*)), being sent forth (सृजानः (*sṛjānaḥ*)), sends forth (इयर्ति (*iyarti*): impels) the divine speech that belongs to the path (पथ्यां (*pathyāṃ*): that is on the path) of truth (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)). The illustration: as a boatman (अरितेव (*ariteva*)), bringing people to the shore, impels his boat. Then the shining Soma reveals (आविष्कृणोति (*āviṣkṛṇoti*)), at the sacrifice (बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)), to the praiser (प्रवाचे (*pravāce*): to the one who makes the recitation proceed), for the sake of praising, the hidden (गुह्यानि (*guhyāni*)) names — that is, the bodies — of the gods, Indra and the rest.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अरिता इव (*aritā iva*)—as the boatman
- नावं (*nāvaṃ*)—impels the boat
- सृजानः (*sṛjānaḥ*)—the one who has been pressed
- हरिः (*hariḥ*)—Soma, of green colour
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—to truth
- पथ्यां (*pathyāṃ*)—guiding
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—speech
- इयर्ति (*iyarti*)—impels
- देवः (*devaḥ*)—the shining Soma
- बर्हिषि (*barhiṣi*)—at the sacrifice
- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—of the gods Indra and the rest
- गुह्यानि नाम (*guhyāni nāma*)—the hidden bodies
- प्रवाचे (*pravāce*)—to the praiser
- आविष्कृणोति (*āviṣkṛṇoti*)—makes manifest

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a boatman impels the boat to move, Soma, who has been pressed and is of green colour, impels the speech (the praise) that guides to truth. The shining Soma makes the hidden bodies of the gods, Indra and the rest, manifest to the praiser at the sacrifice.

##### English translation
The green-tinted Soma being let loose propels the voice that indicates the path of truth as the boatman (propels his) boat ; the bright Soma reveals to his worshipper od the sacred grass the secret names of the god. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 697

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒पामि॒वेदू॒र्मय॒स्तर्तु॑राणाः॒ प्र म॑नी॒षा ई॑रते॒ सोम॒मच्छ॑ ।  
> न॒म॒स्यंती॒रुप॑ च॒ यंति॒ सं चा च॑ विशंत्युश॒तीरु॒शंत॑म् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अपाम्ऽइव । इत् । ऊर्मयः । तर्तुराणाः । प्र । मनीषाः । ईरते । सोमम् । अच्छ ।  
> नमस्यंतीः । उप । च । यंति । सम् । च । आ । च । विशंति । उशतीः । उशंतम् ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अपामिव यथोदकानाम् ऊर्मयः त्वरंते । इत् इति पूरणः । तद्वत् तर्तुराणाः कर्मणि देवान् स्तोतुं त्वरमाणाः । ‘तुर त्वरणे' । जौहोत्यादिकः । यङ्लुगंतस्य शानचि रूपम् । अभ्यासस्यावर्णश्च रेफादेशश्छांदसः । अभ्यस्तस्वरः। तादृशा ऋत्विजः मनीषाः मनस ईशित्रीः स्तुतीः सोममच्छ सोमं प्रति प्र ईरते प्रेरयंति। नमस्यंतीः नमस्यंत्यः सोमं पूजयंत्यः सत्यः तम् उप यंति च उपगच्छंति तमेव सं यंति च । ‘ चवायोगे प्रथमा' इति न निघातः । ततः उशतीः कामयमानाः स्तुतयः उशंतं कामयमानं सोमम् आ विशंति च ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As the waves of the waters hasten, so the priests, eager (तर्तुराणाः (*tarturāṇāḥ*): hurrying to praise the gods in the rite), send out (ईरते (*īrate*)) their praises (मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*): those that rule the mind) towards Soma (सोममच्छ (*somamaccha*)). The word इत् (*it*) is a filler. Adoring (नमस्यंतीः (*namasyaṃtīḥ*)) Soma and worshipping him, the praises approach him and also come together with him. Then the praises, longing (उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*)), enter Soma, who longs for them.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- अपां इव (*apāṃ iva*)—of the waters
- ऊर्मय (*ūrmaya*)—like waves **NOTE**
- तर्तुराणाः (*tarturāṇāḥ*)—priests with a quick eagerness in the rite
- मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*)—their praises
- सोममच्छ (*somamaccha*)—towards Soma
- प्र ईरते (*pra īrate*)—send forth
- नमस्यंतीः (*namasyaṃtīḥ*)—those praises, worshipping Soma
- उप यंति (*upa yaṃti*)—approach him
- सं (यंति) (*saṃ (yaṃti)*)—join him
- उशंतं (*uśaṃtaṃ*)—him who longs for them
- उशतीः (*uśatīḥ*)—longing
- आ विशंति (*ā viśaṃti*)—enter him

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the waves of the waters move in succession, the priests, quick in their eagerness in the rite, send their praises towards Soma and recite them. Those praises approach Soma, worshipping him. Honouring Soma, who longs for those very praises, they join him.

### Printed p. 698

##### English translation
The priests hurrying like the waves of the waters despatch praises towards Soma ; adoring him they approach and come up together, longing for him who longs for them they enter him.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तं म॑र्मृजा॒नं म॑हि॒षं न साना॑वं॒शुं दु॑हंत्यु॒क्षणं॑ गिरि॒ष्ठाम् ।  
> तं वा॑वशा॒नं म॒तयः॑ सचंते त्रि॒तो बि॑भर्ति॒ वरु॑णं समु॒द्रे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तम् । मर्मृजानम् । महिषम् । न । सानौ । अंशुम् । दुहंति । उक्षणम् । गिरिऽस्थाम् ।  
> तम् । वावशानम् । मतयः । सचंते । त्रितः । बिभर्ति । वरुणम् । समुद्रे ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> मर्मजानं यष्टृभिः परिचर्यमाणं महिषं न महिषाख्यं मृगमिव सानौ समुच्छ्रिते देशे वर्तमानम् उक्षणं कामानां सेक्तारं गिरिष्ठाम् अभिषवार्थं ग्रावसु निष्ठितं तं तादृशं प्रसिद्धम् अंशुं सोमं दुहंति ऋत्विजो दुहते । ‘ ग्रावाणो वत्सा ऋत्विजो दुहंति' (तै. सं. ६.२.११.४ ) इति तैत्तिरीयब्राह्मणम् । तं तादृशं वावशानं कामयमानं सोमं मतयः मंतव्याः स्तुतयः सचंते समवयंति । सेवंत इति यावत् । ततः त्रितः त्रिषु स्थानेषु वर्तमान इंद्रः वरुणं शत्रूणां निवारकमेनं सोमं समुद्रे अंतरिक्षे बिभर्ति शत्रुवधार्थं धारयति । यद्वा । त्रितस्त्रिषु स्थानेषु द्रोणाधवनीयपूतभृदाख्येषु कलशेषु ततो विततः सोमः शत्रूणां निवारकमिंद्रं द्युलोके बिभर्ति पोषयति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The priests milk (दुहंति (*duhaṃti*)) that well-known Soma, the plant (अंशुं (*aṃśuṃ*)), who is adored (मर्मजानं (*marmajānaṃ*)) by the priests who tend him, who is like a buffalo (महिषं न (*mahiṣaṃ na*)) standing on a high place (सानौ (*sānau*)), who is the sprinkler of desires (उक्षणं (*ukṣaṇaṃ*)), and who is fixed among the pressing stones (गिरिष्ठाम् (*giriṣṭhām*)). The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa says: ग्रावाणो वत्सा ऋत्विजो दुहंति (*grāvāṇo vatsā ṛtvijo duhaṃti*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6.2.11.4). The praises (मतयः (*matayaḥ*)), worthy of thought, attend (सचंते (*sacaṃte*): serve) that Soma, who longs (वावशानं (*vāvaśānaṃ*)). Then Trita (त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)), that is Indra, who is present in three places, bears (बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)) Varuṇa (वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)), this Soma who keeps off enemies, in the ocean (समुद्रे (*samudre*)), the sky, for the slaying of enemies. Or else: Trita is Soma, spread out in three places, the vessels called Droṇa, Ādhavanīya and Pūtabhṛt; he bears, that is nourishes, Indra, the warder-off of enemies, in the world of heaven.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मर्मजानं (*marmajānaṃ*)—the one who has obtained purity
- महिषं न (*mahiṣaṃ na*)—like a buffalo
- सानौ (*sānau*)—who is on a high place
- उक्षणं (*ukṣaṇaṃ*)—the sprinkler of desires
- गिरिष्ठां (*giriṣṭhāṃ*)—who is placed among the pressing stones
- तं अंशुं (*taṃ aṃśuṃ*)—Soma
- दुहंति (*duhaṃti*)—the priests milk
- वावशानं तं (*vāvaśānaṃ taṃ*)—Soma, who longs for praises
- मतयः (*matayaḥ*)—praises
- सचंते (*sacaṃte*)—serve
- त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—Indra, who is present in all three places
- वरुणं (*varuṇaṃ*)—Soma, who keeps off enemies
- समुद्रे (*samudre*)—in the sky
- बिभर्ति (*bibharti*)—bears

### Printed p. 699

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The priests milk Soma, who has obtained purity, who is on a high place like a buffalo, who is the sprinkler of desires and who is placed among the pressing stones. The praises serve Soma, who longs for praises. Indra, who is present in all three places, bears Soma, who keeps off enemies, in the sky.

##### English translation
(The priests) milk forth the Soma cleansed (dwelling) on a high place like a buffalo, the sprinkler, placed between the grinding-stones ; praises attend upon the longing Soma ; (Indra) who dwells in three abodes supports him, the defeater of enemies, in the firmament.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

महिषं न गिरिस्थां अंशुं दुहंति (*mahiṣaṃ na giristhāṃ aṃśuṃ duhaṃti*)—The work of the priests such as the Adhvaryu, crushing and squeezing the soma creepers with stones and taking out the juice, is described by comparison with milking a buffalo. Here the soma creepers are the buffalo, and the stones that crush the creepers are the calf. On this subject there is the sentence of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, ग्रावाणो वत्सा ऋत्विजो दुहंति (*grāvāṇo vatsā ṛtvijo duhaṃti*) (Tai. Saṃ. 6-2-11-4). The purport of the explanation is: as one lets the calf go to the buffalo and milks it, so the priests take the stone to the soma creepers, crush the creeper with that stone, and draw out the soma juice that flows from it, as one milks. **NOTE**

त्रितः (*tritaḥ*)—Two kinds of meaning are given for this word. त्रितः (*tritaḥ*) means त्रिषु स्थानेषु वर्तमान इंद्रः (*triṣu sthāneṣu vartamāna iṃdraḥ*): Indra, who is in the three places, earth, sky and heaven, that is, who rules over them. Such an Indra bears Soma for the slaying of enemies, that is, drinks it; the purport is that Indra, gladdened by the drinking of Soma, destroys the enemies. Or else, for the word त्रितः (*tritaḥ*): त्रिषु स्थानेषु द्रोणाधवनीयपूतभृदाख्येषु कलशेषु (*triṣu sthāneṣu droṇādhavanīyapūtabhṛdākhyeṣu kalaśeṣu*) the soma juice, spread out विततः सोमः (*vitataḥ somaḥ*), nourishes Indra in the world of heaven: that is, the soma juice in the three vessels for holding the soma juice, called Droṇakalaśa, Ādhavanīya and Pūtabhṛt. Such soma juice bears Indra for the warding off of enemies, that is, nourishes him; by the drinking of Soma Indra becomes strong: this is the other kind of meaning. In the first meaning the word त्रितः (*tritaḥ*) is used of Indra, in the second of Soma.

#### Ṛk 5

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> इष्य॒न्वाच॑मुपव॒क्तेव॒ होतुः॑ पुना॒न इं॑दो॒ वि ष्या॑ मनी॒षाम् ।  
> इंद्र॑श्च॒ यत्क्षय॑थः॒ सौभ॑गाय सु॒वीर्य॑स्य॒ पत॑यः स्याम ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> इष्यन् । वाचम् । उपवक्ताऽइव । होतुः । पुनानः । इंदो इति । वि । स्य । मनीषाम् ।  
> इंद्रः । च । यत् । क्षयथः । सौभगाय । सुऽवीर्यस्य । पतयः । स्याम ॥ ५ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम वाचं स्तुतिम् इष्यन् प्रेरयन् होतुः उपवक्तेव यथाध्वर्युः प्रतिगरं कुर्वन् प्रोत्साहयति तद्वत् स्तोतॄणां शंसनाय प्रोत्साहं कुर्वन् पुनानः पूयमानस्त्वं मनीषां बुद्धि वि ष्य विमुंच । किंतु बुद्धिं धनप्रदानाभिमुखीं कुरु । किंच यत् यदा इंद्रश्च त्वं च सह यज्ञे क्षथथः निवसथः तदा स्तोतारो वयं सौभगाय सौभाग्याय स्याम । किंच सुवीर्यस्य शोभनवीर्योपेतस्य धनस्य पतयः स्वामिनः स्याम भवेम ॥ ॥ ५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, sending forth (इष्यन् (*iṣyan*)) speech, praise: as the Adhvaryu, making the response, spurs on the Hotṛ — like the उपवक्तेव (*upavakteva*) — so, encouraging the praisers to recite and being purified, release (वि ष्य (*vi ṣya*)) the thought (मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)), the intellect; that is, turn the intellect towards giving wealth. Further, when you and Indra dwell together at the sacrifice, then may we, the praisers, be for good fortune (सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*)). Further, may we be the lords (पतयः (*patayaḥ*)) of wealth that has excellent heroism.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- होतुः (*hotuḥ*)—to the words of the Hotṛ
- उपवक्ता इव (*upavaktā iva*)—as the Adhvaryu, who speaks the answering words, spurs on the Hotṛ
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—our praise
- इष्यन् (*iṣyan*)—impelling
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who have obtained purity
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—your helpful intellect
- वि ष्य (*vi ṣya*)—make manifest
- यत् (*yat*)—when
- इंद्रश्च (*iṃdraśca*)—Indra and you
- क्षयथः (*kṣayathaḥ*)—you dwell in the house of the sacrifice, then
- सौभगाय (*saubhagāya*)—(we) becoming worthy of welfare
- स्याम (*syāma*)—may we be
- सुवीरस्यॆ (*suvīrasyè*)—for wealth accompanied by heroic sons **NOTE**
- पतयः (*patayaḥ*)—may we become the lords

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, as the Adhvaryu, who speaks the answering words to the words of the Hotṛ, spurs on the Hotṛ, so you, impelling our praise, you who have obtained purity, make manifest your helpful intellect. When Indra and you dwell in the house of the sacrifice, may we become worthy of welfare. May we become the lords of wealth accompanied by heroic sons.

Indu, being purified, stimulating the praise (of the worshippers) like the answerer of the Hotri set free the understanding ; when (you) and Indra are present together (at the sacrifice) may we be prosperous, may we become the possessors of excellent male progeny.

The ninetieth sūkta. **NOTE**

## Sūkta 96 (Maṇḍala 9)

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> प्र सेनानीरिति चतुर्विंशत्यृचमेकादशं सूक्तं दिवोदासपुत्रस्य प्रतर्दनाख्यस्य राजर्षेरिदं त्रैष्टुभं पवमानसोमदेवताकं । तथा चानुक्रम्यते ।
> प्र सेनानीश्च तुर्विंशतिर्दैवोदासिः प्रतर्दन इति ॥ गतः सूक्तविनियोगः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The eleventh sūkta, of twenty-four Ṛks, beginning प्र सेनानीः (*pra senānīḥ*), is the ārṣa of the royal sage Pratardana, the son of Divodāsa. It is in the Triṣṭubh metre and has Pavamāna Soma as its deity. And so the Anukramaṇī says प्र सेनानीश्च तुर्विंशतिर्दैवोदासिः प्रतर्दन इति (*pra senānīśca turviṃśatirdaivodāsiḥ pratardana iti*). The viniyoga has been stated.

##### Anuvāda

Anuvāda— This sūkta, प्र सेनानीः (*pra senānīḥ*), is the eleventh sūkta in the fifth anuvāka. It has twenty-four Ṛks. The seer of this sūkta is Pratardana, the son of Divodāsa; the deity is Pavamāna Soma; the metre is Triṣṭup. In the Anukramaṇikā it is said प्र सेनानीश्चतुर्विशंतिर्द्वैवोदासिः प्रतर्दनः (*pra senānīścaturviśaṃtirdvaivodāsiḥ pratardanaḥ*). The viniyoga has been stated before.

Sūkta 96. Maṇḍala 9, Anuvāka 5, Sūkta 96. Aṣṭaka 7, Adhyāya 4, Varga 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. Number of ṛks in the sūkta: 24. Seer: Pratardana, son of Divodāsa. Deity: Pavamāna Soma. Metre: Triṣṭup.

#### Ṛk 1

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र से॑ना॒नीः शूरो॒ अग्रे॒ रथा॑नां ग॒व्यन्ने॑ति॒ हर्ष॑ते अस्य॒  ॑
> सेना ।  
> भ॒द्रान्कृ॒ण्वन्निं॑द्रह॒वान्स्खि॑भ्य॒ आ सोमो॒ वस्त्रा॑ रभ॒सानि॑ दत्ते॥

### Printed p. 702

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । सेनानीः । शूरः । अग्रे । रथानां । गव्यन् । एति । हर्षते । अस्य । सेना ।  
> भद्रान् । कृण्वन् । इंद्रहवान् । सखिभ्यः । आ । सोमः । वस्त्रा । रभसानि । दत्ते ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> सेनानीः सेनानामग्र उपनेता शूरः शत्रूणां बाधकः सोमो गव्यञ्छत्रूणां
> गा इच्छन् । यद्वा । यजमानानां पश्वादिकमिच्छन् । रथानामग्रे रथानां पुरतः
> प्रैति । प्रकर्षण संग्रामं गच्छति । अस्य सोमस्य सेना च हर्षते । हृष्यति ॥
> वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥ किंच सखिभ्यः समानख्यानेभ्यो यजमानेभ्य इंद्रहवांस्तैः
> कृतानींद्रस्याह्वानानि भद्रान्कल्याणानि यथार्थानि कृण्वन् कुर्वन् । आहूतो हींद्रः
> सोमं पीत्वा कामान्प्रयच्छतीति रभसानींद्रस्य वेगेनागमने निमित्तानि वस्त्राण्याच्छादकानि पयःप्रभृतीन्याश्रयणान्या दत्ते । आगृह्णाति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma is the leader of the host (सेनानीः (*senānīḥ*)), who goes at the head of armies, and a hero (शूरः (*śūraḥ*)), who obstructs enemies. He is desirous of cows (गव्यन् (*gavyan*)): he wishes for the cows of the enemies; or else he wishes for cattle and the like for the sacrificers. He goes forth (प्रैति (*praiti*)) in front of the chariots (रथानां (*rathānāṃ*)), that is, he goes to battle with force; and his army (सेना (*senā*)) rejoices (हर्षते (*harṣate*)). Further, for the friends (सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)), the sacrificers of like fame, he makes (कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)) the invocations of Indra (इंद्रहवान् (*iṃdrahavān*)) made by them auspicious (भद्रान् (*bhadrān*)), that is, effective as intended; for Indra, when invoked, drinks the Soma and grants wishes. The causes of Indra's coming with speed (रभसानि (*rabhasāni*)) are the coverings (वस्त्रा (*vastrā*)), the receptacles such as milk, and these Soma takes (आ दत्ते (*ā datte*)), that is, receives.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सेनानीः (*senānīḥ*)—the general of the army and
- शूरः (*śūraḥ*)—the valiant
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- गव्यन् (*gavyan*)—desiring the cows of the enemies
- रथानां अग्रे (*rathānāṃ agre*)—at the front of the chariots
- प्र एति (*pra eti*)—goes exceedingly
- अस्य सेना (*asya senā*)—his army
- हर्षते (*harṣate*)—becomes joyful with zeal
- सखिभ्यः (*sakhibhyaḥ*)—to the sacrificers who are friends
- इंद्रहवान् (*iṃdrahavān*)—the prayers and praises addressed to Indra
- भध्रान् (*bhadhrān*)—as having auspicious fruit **NOTE**
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—making
- रभसानि (*rabhasāni*)—quickly made for Indra
- वस्त्रा (*vastrā*)—the garments such as milk
- आ दत्ते (*ā datte*)—accepts

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, the general of the army and the valiant, desiring the cows of the enemies, goes exceedingly at the front of the chariots. His army rejoices with zeal. Making the prayers and praises addressed to Indra by the sacrificers, who are friends, auspicious in fruit, he accepts the garments such as milk, quickly made for Indra. (He becomes mixed with milk and the like.)

##### English translation
The leader of the host, a hero, advances in front of the chariots intent on seizing the cattle (of the enemy) ; his army exults : making their oblations

### Printed p. 703

to Indra prosperous for the friendly (worshippers), Soma assumes the hastily made robes (of curds and milk).

#### Ṛk 2

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सम॑स्य॒ हरिं॒ हर॑यो मृजंत्यश्वह॒य्यरनि॑तितं॒ नमो॑भिः ।  
> आ ति॑ष्ठति॒ रथ॒मिंद्र॑स्य॒ सखा॑ वि॒द्वा ए॑ना सुम॒तिं या॒त्यच्छ॑ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सं । अस्य । हरिं । हरयः । मृजंति । अश्वहय्यैः । अनिशितं । नमःभिः ।  
> आ । तिष्ठति रथं इंद्रस्य । सखा विद्वान् । एन । सुमतिं । याति । अच्छ ॥ २ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हरयः हरंत्यभिषुण्वंति सोममित्यृत्वजोऽंगुलयो वा हरिं हरितवर्णमस्य सोमस्य कारणमंशुं सं मृजंति । सम्यगभिषुण्वंति । ततः सोमो नमोभिर्नामयितृभिरश्वहय्वैव्याप्तैरप्यनिशितमसंस्कृतमयुक्तमननुगतं रथं रमणसाधॆनमात्मीयं दशापवित्रमा तिष्ठति । आसीदति । अनंतरमिंद्रस्य सखा सखिभूतो विद्वान्
> प्राज्ञः सोम एनैतेन रथेन पवित्रेण सुमतिं शोभनस्तुतिकं स्तोतारमच्छ याति ।
> अभिगच्छति । तस्मिन्काले तेन क्रियमाणां स्तुतिमभिगच्छतीत्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The हरयः (*harayaḥ*) are the priests, who carry off, that is, press, the Soma; or else the fingers. They rub together, that is, press thoroughly (सं मृजंति (*saṃ mṛjaṃti*)), the green-tinted (हरिं (*hariṃ*)) shoot, the source of this Soma. Then Soma, by the salutations (नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)), those that make one bow, and by the pervading horse-drivers (अश्वहय्यैः (*aśvahayyaiḥ*)) **NOTE**, mounts (आ तिष्ठति (*ā tiṣṭhati*)), that is, sits on, his own chariot (रथं (*rathaṃ*)), the means of delight, the ten-fold filter, which is unsharpened (अनिशितं (*aniśitaṃ*)), that is, unprepared, unyoked, not followed. Afterwards the friend of Indra, the wise Soma, goes (याति (*yāti*)) by this (एन (*ena*)) filter towards (अच्छ (*accha*)) the praiser (सुमतिं (*sumatiṃ*)) who offers good praise; that is, at that time he comes to the praise made by him.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- हरयः (*harayaḥ*)—the priests
- हरिं अस्य (*hariṃ asya*)—the green-hued Soma
- सं मृजंति (*saṃ mṛjaṃti*)—squeeze (afterwards)
- नमोभिः (*namobhiḥ*)—which are obedient and **NOTE**
- अश्वहय्यैः (*aśvahayyaiḥ*)—pervading, from the horses
- अनिशितं (*aniśitaṃ*)—though not yoked
- रथं (*rathaṃ*)—in the daśāpavitra that brings delight
- आ तिष्ठति (*ā tiṣṭhati*)—takes refuge
- इंद्रस्य (*iṃdrasya*)—of Indra
- सखा (*sakhā*)—the friend and
- विद्वान् (*vidvān*)—the wise
- एना (*enā*)—by this daśāpavitra
- सुमतिं अच्छ (*sumatiṃ accha*)—to the excellent praiser
- याति (*yāti*)—goes

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The priests squeeze the green-hued Soma. Afterwards, though not yoked by obedient and pervading horses, he takes refuge in the daśāpavitra that brings delight. Soma, the friend of Indra and the wise, crossing this daśāpavitra, goes to the excellent praiser.

### Printed p. 704

##### English translation
The priests express his green-tinted (juice); he mounts the chariot unyoked by the horse-driving salutions; the wise Soma the friend of Indra goes to meet the worshipper.

#### Ṛk 3

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स नो॑ देव दे॒वता॑ते पवस्व म॒हे सो॑म॒ प्सर॑स इंद्र॒पानः॑ ।  
> कृ॒ण्वन्न॒पो व॒र्षय॒न्द्यामु॒तेमामु॒रोरा नो॑ वरिवस्या  ॒
> पुनानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः । नः । देव । देवताते । पवस्व । महे । सोम । प्सरसे । इंद्रपानः ।  
> कृण्वन् । अपः । वर्षयन् । द्यां । उत । इमां । उरोः । आ । नः । वरिवस्य  
> पुनानः ॥ ३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देव द्योतमान हे सोम स तादृश इंद्रपान इंद्रेण पातव्यस्त्वं
> नोऽस्माकं स्वभूते देवताते देवैस्तते वितते यज्ञे महे महते प्सरसे भक्षणायेंद्रस्य पानाय पवस्व । ग्रहादिषु क्षर । किंचाप उदकानि कृण्वन् कुर्वन् उतापि
> च द्यामिमां द्यावापृथिव्यौ वर्षयन् । भूमिं पर्जन्यरूपेण तर्पयति द्युलोकमग्नि रूपेणेति । भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः ॥ ऋ. १-१६४-५१ । इति
> श्रवणात् । उरोर्विस्तीर्णादंतरिक्षादागच्छंस्त्वं पुनानः पूयमानः सन्नोऽस्मान्वरिवस्य । धनादिप्रदानेन परिचरेति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining (देव (*deva*)) Soma, such as you are, the drink of Indra (इंद्रपानः (*iṃdrapānaḥ*)), to be drunk by Indra, flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)), that is, run into the Graha cups and the rest, at our sacrifice (देवताते (*devatāte*)), which is spread out by the gods, for the great (महे (*mahe*)) food (प्सरसे (*psarase*)), that is, for Indra's drinking. Further, making waters (अपः (*apaḥ*)) and also causing rain to fall (वर्षयन् (*varṣayan*)) on this heaven and earth: he gratifies the earth in the form of Parjanya and the heavenly world in the form of Agni, for it is heard भूमिं पर्जन्या जिन्वंति दिवं जिन्वंत्यग्नयः (*bhūmiṃ parjanyā jinvaṃti divaṃ jinvaṃtyagnayaḥ*) (Ṛ. 1-164-51) **GLOSS**. Coming from the wide (उरोः (*uroḥ*)) firmament, and being purified (पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)), serve us (वरिवस्य (*varivasya*)) by giving wealth and the like.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—of divine nature
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma-deva
- इंद्रपानः (*iṃdrapānaḥ*)—worthy of Indra's drinking
- सः (*saḥ*)—you
- नः (*naḥ*)—our
- देवताते (*devatāte*)—in the sacrifice
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- प्सरसे (*psarase*)—for Indra's drinking
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- अपः (*apaḥ*)—the waters
- कृण्वन् (*kṛṇvan*)—creating
- उत (*uta*)—and
- द्यां (*dyāṃ*)—the heaven
- इमां (*imāṃ*)—this world
- वर्षयन् (*varṣayan*)—drenching with rain
- उरोः (*uroḥ*)—from the wide firmament

### Printed p. 705

- आ (*ā*)—favour (us)
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—having obtained purity
- नः (*naḥ*)—us
- परिवस्य (*parivasya*)—serve with gifts of wealth and the like **NOTE**

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma-deva, of divine nature, worthy of Indra's drinking, flow at our sacrifice for the great drinking of Indra. Creating the waters and drenching heaven and this world with rain, favour us from the wide firmament. Here, having obtained purity, serve us with gifts of wealth and the like.

##### English translation
Divine Soma, who are the beverage of Indra, flow at our sacrifice for (his) abundant food ; sending water, causing rain to fall upon heaven and upon this earth, (come) from the wide (firmament, and) being purified bestow upon us wealth.

#### Ṛk 4

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अजी॑त॒येऽह॑तये पवस्व स्व॒स्तये॑ स॒र्वता॑तये बृह॒ते ।  
> तदु॑शंति॒ विश्व॑ इ॒मे सखा॑य॒स्तद॒हं व॑श्मि पवमान सोम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अजीतये । अहतये । पवस्व । स्वस्तये । सर्वसतातये । बृहते ।  
> तत् । उशंति । विश्वे । इमे । सखायः । तत् । अहं । वश्मि । पवमान । सोम ॥ ४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम अजीतये यथा वयं शत्रुभिरजिता भवेम तथा तेषामजयाय
> अहतये यथा तैरहताः स्याम तस्यॆ च अत एव स्वस्तयेऽविनाशाय किंच बृहते
> सर्वतातये सर्वैरिंद्रादिभिर्देवैः स्तूयमानाय यज्ञाय एतदर्थं पवस्व ।
> अस्मदभिमुखमागच्छ । पविर्गतिकर्मा । विश्वे सर्व इमे मदीयाः सखायः स्तोशारस्तत्त्वदीयं रक्षणमुशंति । कामयंते । हे पवमान सोम तद्रक्षणमहमसि वश्मि
> कामये ॥
> XXVI 45

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, flow (पवस्व (*pavasva*)) for non-defeat (अजीतये (*ajītaye*)), so that we may not be conquered by enemies, that is, for victory over them; for non-slaughter (अहतये (*ahataye*)), so that we may not be slain by them; and hence for welfare (स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)), that is, for freedom from destruction. Further, flow for the great (बृहते (*bṛhate*)) sacrifice (सर्वतातये (*sarvatātaye*)), which is praised by all the gods, Indra and the others; for this purpose come towards us. The root पवि (*pavi*) has the sense of motion. All (विश्वे (*viśve*)) these friends of mine, the praisers, desire (उशंति (*uśaṃti*)) that protection of yours. O Pavamāna Soma, that protection I desire (वश्मि (*vaśmi*)).

- अजीतये (*ajītaye*)—(O Soma) so that enemies may not conquer us
- आहतये (*āhataye*)—for being free from injury **NOTE**
- स्वस्तये (*svastaye*)—for the attainment of welfare, and being accomplished
- बृहते (*bṛhate*)—great
- सर्वतातये (*sarvatātaye*)—for the sacrifice
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- इमे विश्वे सखायः (*ime viśve sakhāyaḥ*)—all these my friends
- तत् (*tat*)—protection from you
- उशंति (*uśaṃti*)—desire
- पवमान (*pavamāna*)—called Pavamāna
- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma
- तत् (*tat*)—that same protection
- अहं (*ahaṃ*)—I too
- वश्मि (*vaśmi*)—desire

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, flow for the great sacrifice, which is accomplished so that enemies may not conquer us, that we may escape injury, and for the attainment of our welfare. All these my friends desire protection from you; O Soma, called Pavamāna, I too desire that same protection.

##### English translation
Flow for our immunity from defeat and slaughter, flow for our welfare, for the great sacrifice for all the gods ; all these my friends desire this ; this I desire, O Soma Pavamana.

> जनिता । अग्नेः । जनिता । सूर्यस्य । जनिता । इंद्रस्य । जनिता । उत । विष्णोः ॥ ५ ॥

> यद्वा मननीयानां स्तुतीनां जनिता जनयिता ॥ जनिता मंत्रे । सा. ६-४-५३ । इति
> निपातनाण्णिलोपः ॥ किंच दिवो द्युलोकस्य जनिता प्रादुर्भावयिता तथा पृथिव्या

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being pressed, flows (पवते (*pavate*)), that is, runs into the vessels. Of what kind is he? He is the begetter (जनिता (*janitā*)) of thoughts (मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)), of intellects, or else of praises worthy of thought. Further, he is the begetter of heaven (दिवो (*divo*)), that is, its manifester; and likewise of the earth (पृथिव्या (*pṛthivyā*)).

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जनयिता अग्नेर्जनयिता प्रकाशयिता सूर्यस्य सर्वस्य प्रेरकस्यादित्यस्य जनिता इंद्रस्य
> जनिता पानेन मदस्य जनयिता उतापि च विष्णोर्व्यापकस्य जनिता जनयिता। एतत्सर्वं
> सोमेऽभिसूयमाणे भवतीति सोमो हि देवानाप्याययतीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

He is the begetter (जनयिता (*janayitā*)) of Agni, that is, its illuminator; the begetter of Sūrya, the Āditya who impels all; the begetter of Indra, begetter of his exhilaration by drinking; and also the begetter of Viṣṇu, the all-pervading. All this happens when Soma is being pressed, for Soma nourishes the gods.

Soma, the generator of praises, the maker of heaven and earth, the illuminator of Agni, the impeller of Sūrya, and the generator of Indra and Viṣṇu, flows.

##### English translation
The Soma flows the generator of praises, the generator of heaven, the generator of the earth, the generator of Agni, the generator of the sun, the generator of Indra and the generator of Vishnu.

### Printed p. 708

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवसुवां हविषु सोमस्य वनस्पतेर्ब्रह्मा देवानामिति याज्या । सूत्र्यते
> च । त्वं च सोम नो वशो ब्रह्मा देवानां पदवीः कवीनां । आ. ४-११ । इति ॥
> सोम एवंरूपो भवति । देवानां स्तोत्रकारिणामृत्विजां ब्रह्मा ब्रह्माख्यर्त्विक्ष्वा नीयो भवति । यद्वा । देवानां द्योतमानानामिंद्रादीनां ब्रह्मा राजा
> भवति । तथा कवीनां क्रांतप्रज्ञानां पदवीः । स्थलंति पदानि साधुत्वेन यो योजयति स पदवीः ॥ वी गत्यादिष्ठित्येतस्मात्कृषि रूपं ॥ तथा विप्राणां मेधाविनां मध्य
> ऋषिर्भवति । यः परोक्षं पश्यति स ऋषिः ऋषिर्दर्शनात् । नि. २-११ । इति । मृगाणां
> महिषो भवति । महिषाख्यो बलवान्राजा भवति । तथा गृध्राणां पक्षिविशेषाणां
> श्येनः शंसनीयः पक्षिराजो भवति । वनानां । वनतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । हिंसकानां
> भेदकानां मध्यॆ स्वधितिरेतन्नामकश्चेदकोऽसि । एवंप्रभावः सोमो रेभञ्चायमानः सन् पवित्रमूर्णास्तुकेन कृतमत्येति । अतिगच्छति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

In the oblations of the Devasuvaḥ, in the one to Soma Vanaspati, ब्रह्मा देवानां (*brahmā devānāṃ*) is the yājyā. And it is stated in the sūtra: त्वं च सोम नो वशो ब्रह्मा देवानां पदवीः कवीनां (*tvaṃ ca soma no vaśo brahmā devānāṃ padavīḥ kavīnāṃ*) (Ā. 4-11). Soma is of such a nature: for the gods (देवानां (*devānāṃ*)), the priests who perform the praise, he is Brahmā, the priest of that name, who is to be honoured **NOTE**; or else, among the shining gods, Indra and the others, he is Brahmā, the king. Likewise he is the पदवीः (*padavīḥ*) of the poets (कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*)), those of far-reaching wisdom: one who joins words correctly. Among the wise (विप्राणां (*viprāṇāṃ*)), the intelligent, he is the seer (ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)): यः परोक्षं पश्यति स ऋषिः ऋषिर्दर्शनात् (*yaḥ parokṣaṃ paśyati sa ṛṣiḥ ṛṣirdarśanāt*) (Ni. 2-11). Among animals (मृगाणां (*mṛgāṇāṃ*)) he is the buffalo (महिषः (*mahiṣaḥ*)), the mighty king so named. Likewise, among vultures (गृध्राणां (*gṛdhrāṇāṃ*)), a species of birds, he is the falcon (श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)), the praiseworthy king of birds. Among the वनानां (*vanānāṃ*), the word वनति (*vanati*) having the sense of injuring, that is, among the injurers and cutters, you are the cutter named स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*). Soma, of such power, roaring (रेभन् (*rebhan*)), passes beyond (अत्येति (*atyeti*)) the filter (पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)) made of a tuft of wool.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देवानां (*devānāṃ*)—to the gods
- ब्रह्मा (*brahmā*)—the one in the form of the priest
- कवीनां (*kavīnāṃ*)—to the poets
- पदवीः (*padavīḥ*)—the guide
- विप्राणां (*viprāṇāṃ*)—among the wise
- ऋषिः (*ṛṣiḥ*)—the one possessed of excellent supersensuous power
- मृगाणां (*mṛgāṇāṃ*)—among beasts
- महिषः (*mahiṣaḥ*)—the king in the form of a buffalo
- गृध्राणां (*gṛdhrāṇāṃ*)—in the flock of vultures
- श्येनः (*śyenaḥ*)—the falcon
- वनानां (*vanānāṃ*)—among the injurers
- स्वधितिः (*svadhitiḥ*)—the cutter called Svadhiti, who is
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- रेभन् (*rebhan*)—making a sound
- पवित्रं (*pavitraṃ*)—the daśāpavitra
- अत्येति (*atyeti*)—goes across

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma-deva, who is for the gods the priest called Brahmā, for the poets the guide, among the wise one of excellent supersensuous power, among beasts the king in the form of a buffalo, in the flock of vultures the falcon, and among the injurers the cutter called Svadhiti (the sword), goes across the daśāpavitra, making a sound.

##### English translation
The Brahma of the gods, the guide of the sages, the rishi of the pious, the buffalo of wild animals, the falcon of the vultures, the hatchet of deadly weapons, the Soma passes through the filter with a roar.

### Printed p. 709

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

When the oblation is made, in the eight homas called Devasuva, to the deity named Soma Vanaspati, this Ṛk ब्रह्मा देवानां (*brahmā devānāṃ*) is to be recited as the yājyā mantra; this is set out in the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra by the sūtra त्वं च सोम नो वशो ब्रह्मा देवानां पदवीः कवीनां (*tvaṃ ca soma no vaśo brahmā devānāṃ padavīḥ kavīnāṃ*) (Ā. 4-11). In this Ṛk, to describe the great nature of Soma-deva, he is compared with many persons.

ब्रह्मा देवानां (*brahmā devānāṃ*)—स्तोत्रकारिणामृत्विजां ब्रह्माख्यर्तिक्षानीयो भवति । (*stotrakāriṇāmṛtvijāṃ brahmākhyartikṣānīyo bhavati |*) In a sacrifice there are many priests, such as the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu and the Udgātṛ. All these perform the duties assigned to them. They have knowledge only in the work that they do; they have no acquaintance with the work of others. For example, the Hotṛ recites the mantras of the Ṛgveda and invokes the deity assigned in the sacrifice; afterwards he praises them and recites the mantras by which oblations and the like are offered to them in the fire: this is his chief function. The Adhvaryu directs by the Praiṣa mantras what work each priest must do at each time, and also takes part in the ancillary rites of the sacrifice, such as pressing the Soma and churning the fire. The mantras that the Adhvaryu must recite are also many. In the same way the Udgātṛ sings the Sāma mantras. The other priests too have many duties to perform. But neither may the Adhvaryu do the work of the Hotṛ, nor the Hotṛ the work of the Adhvaryu. It is the same with the other priests. The Adhvaryu must have studied the Yajurveda, and the Udgātṛ the Sāmaveda. But the priest called Brahman must know well all the ancillary rites of the sacrifice, the duties the other priests have to perform, and the mantras. It is the Brahman's responsibility to see whether the other priests recite the mantras correctly and carry out their duties correctly, without omission or fault. If omissions or faults occur in the sacrifice, the Brahman himself must prescribe the proper expiations and set right those omissions and faults. Therefore the Brahman's duty in the sacrifice is of great importance. For this very reason the glory of Soma is described here as follows: among the priests the Brahman is the foremost, and Soma is the equal of such a Brahman. In the same way the seer has described the glory of Soma-deva by explaining other comparisons.

पदवीः कवीनां (*padavīḥ kavīnāṃ*)—कवीनां क्रांतप्रज्ञानां । स्थलंति पदानि साधुत्वेन यो योजयति स पदवीः । (*kavīnāṃ krāṃtaprajñānāṃ | sthalaṃti padāni sādhutvena yo yojayati sa padavīḥ |*) In praising the gods, according to the occasion, by the joining of words that describe the qualities and the like of the

### Printed p. 710

gods, one who composes sentences in due order and recites them, and is the best among those who do so: such a person is compared with Soma-deva.

विप्राणां ऋषिः (*viprāṇāṃ ṛṣiḥ*)—As among men of wisdom the seer who sees beyond is the best, so Soma-deva is the best among the gods. As to the seer: यः परोक्षं पश्यति स ऋषिः । ऋषिर्दर्शनात् (*yaḥ parokṣaṃ paśyati sa ṛṣiḥ | ṛṣirdarśanāt*) (Ni. 2 11). Ordinary people can see and know only the matters and things that are before their eyes. But the seer can know matters that are not before him, and matters that happened or will happen in the past and future times. For this very reason the seer is said to be better than other intelligent men, and Soma is compared with such a seer.

महिषो मृगाणां (*mahiṣo mṛgāṇāṃ*)—The word mahiṣa has two meanings. Mahiṣa means the wild buffalo. Among all beasts the wild buffalo is the strongest and charges forward with courage. Therefore the buffalo has pre-eminence among beasts; or else, since the word mahiṣa has the meaning "mighty and venerable" (mahiṣaḥ = mahān), Soma is a giver of strength and venerable, like a king who is mighty and venerable.

श्येनो गृध्राणां (*śyeno gṛdhrāṇāṃ*)—Among the species of birds called gṛdhra (strong birds such as the kite), he is like the falcon. It is renowned that the falcon, by its excessive power, flew to the heavenly world and brought the Soma plants there to the earth. Therefore the falcon is regarded as the best among all birds. Soma-deva is equal to such a falcon.

स्वधितिर्वनानां (*svadhitirvanānāṃ*)—वनतिर्हिंसाकर्मा । हिंसकानां भेदकानां मध्ये स्वधितिः एतन्नामकश्चेदकोऽसि । (*vanatirhiṃsākarmā | hiṃsakānāṃ bhedakānāṃ madhye svadhitiḥ etannāmakaścedako 'si |*) Svadhiti means a cutting weapon. It is used in sacrifices and the like to cut animals for the oblation. As the sword called svadhiti is the best among acts of injury, so Soma is the best among other things. The seer describes that Soma, so excellent and venerable, flows with a gurgling sound and enters the vessel called the daśāpavitra, placed for straining.

> प्रावी॑विपद्वा॒च ऊ॒र्मिं न सिंधु॒र्गिरः॒ सोमः॒ पव॑मानो  ॒

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । अवीविपत् । वाचः । ऊर्मिं । न । सिंधुः । गिरः । सोमः । पवमानः । मनीषाः ।  
> अंतरिति । पश्यन् । वृजना । इमा । अवराणि । आ । तिष्ठति । वृषभः । गोषु । जानन्॥७॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> पवमानः सोमो मनीषा मनस ईशिता हृदयंगमा गिरः स्तुतीः प्रावीविपत् । प्रकर्षण वेपयति । प्रेरयति । कथमिव । सिंधुः स्यंदमाना नदीव वाचः
> शब्दस्योर्मिं न संघं यथा प्रेरयति । तद्वत् । किंच वृषभः कामानामुदकानां
> ना वर्षकः सोमोऽंतरंतर्हितं वस्तुजातं पश्यन्नवराणि दुर्बलैर्वारयितुमशक्यानीमा वृजनेमानि बलान्या तिष्ठति । आसीदति । किं कुर्वन् । गोषु जानन् गवां
> जानानः सन् परबलानि प्रविशति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Pavamāna Soma sets in motion (प्रावीविपत् (*prāvīvipat*)) the praises (गिरः (*giraḥ*)), the मनीषा (*manīṣā*), that is, those that rule over the mind and go to the heart: he shakes them forcefully, he impels them. How? As a river (सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*)), a flowing stream, impels the wave (ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)) of sound (वाचः (*vācaḥ*)), the mass of it; so does he. Further, the showerer (वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)), the one who rains the desired waters, Soma, seeing within (अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)) the hidden mass of things, takes his place (आ तिष्ठति (*ā tiṣṭhati*)), sits down, upon these (इमा (*imā*)) lower (अवराणि (*avarāṇi*)) powers (वृजना (*vṛjanā*)), forces that the weak cannot ward off. Doing what? Knowing (जानन् (*jānan*)) the cows (गोषु (*goṣu*)), he enters the forces of others.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सिंधुः (*siṃdhuḥ*)—the flowing river
- वाचः (*vācaḥ*)—of sound
- ऊर्मिं न (*ūrmiṃ na*)—as raising waves
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—called Pavamāna
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma-deva
- मनीषाः (*manīṣāḥ*)—heart-pleasing
- गिरः (*giraḥ*)—praises
- प्रावीविपत् (*prāvīvipat*)—impels
- वृषभः (*vṛṣabhaḥ*)—Soma, the showerer of desires
- अंतः (*aṃtaḥ*)—the things hidden secretly
- पश्यन् (*paśyan*)—seeing
- गोषु (*goṣu*)—the matter of the cows
- जानन् (*jānan*)—having fully known
- अवराणि (*avarāṇi*)—unobstructed by the weak
- इमा वृजना (*imā vṛjanā*)—to all powers
- आ तिष्ठति (*ā tiṣṭhati*)—takes the chief place

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As a flowing river raises waves of sound, so Soma-deva, called Pavamāna, impels heart-pleasing praises. Soma, the showerer of desires, seeing the things hidden secretly, and having fully known the matter of the cows, takes the chief place over all the powers that the weak cannot obstruct.

##### English translation
The purified Soma excites gratifying praises as a river (excites) the wave of sound ; the showerer (of benefits) beholding the hidden (treasure) presides over these irresistible powers, knowing about the cattle.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

सिंधुः ऊर्मिं न पवमानः सोमः गिरः प्र अवीविपत् (*siṃdhuḥ ūrmiṃ na pavamānaḥ somaḥ giraḥ pra avīvipat*)—As a flowing river raises waves by the speed of its current and makes a sound, so Pavamāna Soma impels the priests who have drunk Soma to recite sentences in the form of praise; that is, the priests, delighted by drinking Soma, will praise the gods with zeal: this is the meaning.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma is intoxicating (मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)). In battles (पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*)) he injures (वन्वन् (*vanvan*)) the enemies, and hence is unapproachable (अवातः (*avātaḥ*)), one that others cannot go against; he has a thousand streams of water (सहस्ररेताः (*sahasraretāḥ*)). Such a Soma, go towards (अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)) the strength (वाजं (*vājaṃ*)) of the enemies. O Indu, O Soma, being purified (पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)), you the wise (मनीषी (*manīṣī*)), impelling the cows (गा इषण्यन् (*gā iṣaṇyan*)), an unclear word **NOTE**; or else impelling the cows that are the means of the sacrifice for the sacrificers: for Indra, that is, for Indra's sake, impel (ईरय (*īraya*)) the wave (ऊर्मिं (*ūrmiṃ*)), the mass, of the Soma shoot (अंशोः (*aṃśoḥ*)) that is being pressed.

- मत्सरः (*matsaraḥ*)—(O Soma) the intoxicating
- पृत्सु (*pṛtsu*)—in battles
- वन्वन् (*vanvan*)—injuring the enemies, and
- अवातः (*avātaḥ*)—he who alone is unharmed
- सहस्ररेताः (*sahasraretāḥ*)—having streams of many kinds
- सः (*saḥ*)—you, the renowned
- वाजं (*vājaṃ*)—confronting the strength of the enemies
- अभ्यर्ष (*abhyarṣa*)—advance
- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O Soma-deva
- पवमानः (*pavamānaḥ*)—you the purifier
- मनीषी (*manīṣī*)—

- wise
- गाः इषण्यन् (*gāḥ iṣaṇyan*)—impelling the cows
- इंद्राय (*iṃdrāya*)—for Indra's sake

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O Soma, you who cause exhilaration, who injure the enemies in battles and are yourself unharmed, who have streams of many kinds, and are renowned, confront the strength of the enemies and advance. O Soma-deva, you the purifier, being wise, impelling the cows, cause the mass of the Soma juice to flow for Indra's sake.

##### English translation
(Soma) who are the exhilarator, harming (the foe) in battles, (yourself) unharmed, who have a thousand streams, rush against the :strength (of the enemy); Indu, who are being purified, the sage, uttering cries, urge on for Indra the wave of juice. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

स मत्सरः पृत्सु वन्वन् अवातः (*sa matsaraḥ pṛtsu vanvan avātaḥ*)—Soma, who causes exhilaration, injures the enemies in battles and the like; but he himself is not injured by anyone. That is to say, after drinking Soma, delight arises and zeal is doubled. Therefore it is natural that warriors, made zealous by drinking Soma, rush on the enemies in battles with heroic fervour and slay them. Since the drinking of Soma is the cause of such slaying of enemies, the seer describes in another manner that Soma slays the enemies in battles.

सहस्ररेताः (*sahasraretāḥ*)—सहस्रोदकधारोपेतः । (*sahasrodakadhāropetaḥ |*) When the Soma plants are crushed with a stone and the juice is pressed out, the Soma juice oozes out and flows from many places in the plants. That is described here by the words सहस्ररेताः सहस्रधारः शतधारः (*sahasraretāḥ sahasradhāraḥ śatadhāraḥ*) and so on. The words "thousand" and "hundred" mean "many".
