##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, you who are sufficient for exhilaration, flow at the sacrifice (देवताते (*devatāte*), the sacrifice extended by the gods), together with the stream of flowing currents, on the elevated fleece, the filter. You, with a thousand streams, that is, with many streams, fragrant and unharmed by anyone, flow around in the battle, which is to be endured by men and is for the sake of gaining food.

- देवताते (*devatāte*)—at the sacrifice
- सानौ (*sānau*)—at the elevated place
- अव्ये (*avye*)—in the dashapavitra filter

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are capable of causing exhilaration, flow with the stream at the sacrifice into the dashapavitra filter that stands in the elevated place. You who have many streams and are fragrant, flow, subject to the violence of none, for the gain of food in battle.

#### Ṛk 20

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अ॒र॒श्मानो॒ ये॑र॒था अयु॑क्ता॒ अत्या॑सो॒ न स॑सृजा॒नास॑ आ॒जौ ।  
> ए॒ते शु॒क्रासो॑ धन्वंति॒ सोमा॒ देवा॑स॒स्ता उप॑ याता॒  ॑
> पिबध्यै ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अरश्मानः । ये । अरथाः । अयुक्ताः । अत्यासः । न । ससृजानासः । आजौ ।  
> एते । शुक्रासः । धन्वंति । सोमाः । देवासः । तान् । उप । यात । पिबध्यै ॥ २० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> अरश्मानो रश्मिवर्जिताः । रज्जुरहिता इति यावत्। अरथा रथवर्जिता आयुक्ताः
> कुत्रापि न नियुक्ताः । अबद्धा इत्यर्थः । एतादृशा य आजौ युद्धे सस्यजानासः
> सृज्यमाना अत्यासो नाश्वा यथा त्वरया लक्ष्यं गच्छंति तद्वदाजौ । अजंति
> कर्मकरणार्थमृत्वजोऽत्रेत्याजिर्यज्ञः । तस्मिन्सृज्यमानाः शुक्रा दीप्यमाना एते
> सोमा धन्वंति । क्षिप्रं कलशानभिगच्छंति । अथ प्रत्यक्षः । हे देवासो देवाः
> तानागच्छतः सोमान्पिबध्यॆ पानायोप यात । उपगच्छत ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

These Somas, without reins, that is, without ropes, without chariots, and unyoked, not harnessed anywhere, that is, unbound, being let loose in the battle, run to the goal swiftly like horses. Sāyaṇa explains the battle as the sacrifice, because the officiating priests drive there for the performance of the rites. Let loose in it, these bright, shining Somas run, that is, go quickly to the vessels. Then, in the direct address: O gods, come to those Somas that are arriving, to drink.

- उप यात (*upa yāta*)—come near

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As horses without bridle and not tied to a chariot, if let loose in the battlefield, run freely, so these powerful Soma juices run towards the vessel, that is, they flow. O gods, come near to drink those Soma juices.

##### English translation
These brilliant Soma-juices flow like horses let loose in battle without reins, without chariots, unharnessed ; approach them, you gods, to drink.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In this Ṛk the sentence अरश्मानः........सोमाः (*araśmānaḥ........somāḥ*) is said to be in the indirect form, and the sentence देवासः........ पिबध्यॆ (*devāsaḥ........ pibadhyè*) in the direct form. In many Ṛks there are only indirect sentences; in some Ṛks only direct ones; and in still other Ṛks both indirect and direct. Therefore we shall explain briefly what the indirect and the direct forms are, following what Yāska has explained here.

In dividing the Ṛks of the Ṛgveda according to their sense, Yāska says that there are various kinds, comprising such subjects as the indirect, the direct, the indirect and direct together, the spiritual, praise, blessing, oath, curse, a matter concerning someone, lament, censure and so on, and he has explained them by examples. Thus:

(1) परोक्षकृत (*parokṣakṛta*)—In this Ṛk the deity is thought of as not being before the speaker, that is, as being out of sight, and is praised so. In this case any of the cases of the pronoun may be used, but the verb must be in the third person. For example, इंद्रो दिव इंद्र ईशे पृथिव्याः ॥ (*iṃdro diva iṃdra īśe pṛthivyāḥ ‖*) (nominative case)

### Printed p. 786

इंद्रमिद्दाथिनो बृहत् ॥ (*iṃdramiddāthino bṛhat ‖*) (second case)

इंद्रेणैते तृत्सवो वेविषाणाः ॥ (*iṃdreṇaite tṛtsavo veviṣāṇāḥ ‖*) (third case)

इंद्राय साम गायत ॥ (*iṃdrāya sāma gāyata ‖*) (fourth case)

नेंद्रादृते पवते धाम किंचन ॥ (*neṃdrādṛte pavate dhāma kiṃcana ‖*) (fifth case)

इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्रवोचं ॥ (*iṃdrasya nu vīryāṇi pravocaṃ ‖*) (sixth case)

इंद्रे कामा अयंसत ॥ (*iṃdre kāmā ayaṃsata ‖*) (seventh case)

Here seven examples are given for the seven cases. Only the verb is in the third person.

(2) प्रत्यक्षकृत (*pratyakṣakṛta*)—In this kind of Ṛk the deity who is praised is thought of as present, that is, as standing in front, and that deity may be praised in all the cases as said before. But the second-person pronouns, "you", "your" and so on, and the second-person verbs corresponding to them must be used. For example, त्वमिंद्र बलवादधि ॥ (*tvamiṃdra balavādadhi ‖*) वि न इंद्र मृधो जहि ॥ (*vi na iṃdra mṛdho jahi ‖*) and so on.

(3) Direct and indirect—In some Ṛks which contain both kinds, the people who praise are treated as direct, and the deities who are praised as indirect. For example, मा चिदन्यद्विशंसत ॥ (*mā cidanyadviśaṃsata ‖*) कण्णा अभि प्र गायत ॥ (*kaṇṇā abhi pra gāyata ‖*) **NOTE** उप प्रेत कुशिकाश्चेयध्वं ॥ (*upa preta kuśikāśceyadhvaṃ ‖*) and so on.

(4) आध्यात्मिक (*ādhyātmika*)—The deities who are praised themselves speak, and the sentences are said in the first person. For example, अहं भुवं वसुनः पूर्वस्पतिः ॥ (*ahaṃ bhuvaṃ vasunaḥ pūrvaspatiḥ ‖*) इति ना इति मे मनः ॥ (*iti nā iti me manaḥ ‖*) अहं रुद्रेभिर्वसुभिश्चरामि ॥ (*ahaṃ rudrebhirvasubhiścarāmi ‖*) and so on.

(5) स्तुति (*stuti*)—A Ṛk containing only the praise of deities or of other persons. For example, इंद्रस्य नु वीर्याणि प्रवोचं ॥ (*iṃdrasya nu vīryāṇi pravocaṃ ‖*) and so on.

(6) आशीः (*āśīḥ*)—A blessing, or a mantra that wishes what is good. For example, सुचक्षा अहमक्षिभ्यां ॥ (*sucakṣā ahamakṣibhyāṃ ‖*) and so on.

### Printed p. 787

(7) Oath and curse—a vow, and the giving of a curse wishing another ill. For example, अद्या मुरीय यति यातुधानो अस्मि ॥ (*adyā murīya yati yātudhāno asmi ‖*) **NOTE** अधा स वीरैर्दशभिर्वियूयाः ॥ (*adhā sa vīrairdaśabhirviyūyāḥ ‖*) and so on.

(8) कस्यचिद्भाव (*kasyacidbhāva*)—There is a description or mention of some matter. For example, न मृत्युरासीदमृतं न तर्हि । (*na mṛtyurāsīdamṛtaṃ na tarhi |*) तम आसीत्तमसा गूळ्वमग्रे ॥ (*tama āsīttamasā gūḷvamagre ‖*) and so on.

(9) परिदेवना (*paridevanā*)—Lamenting. For example, सुदेवो अद्य प्रपतेदनावृत् ॥ (*sudevo adya prapatedanāvṛt ‖*) न विजानामि यदि वेदमस्मि ॥ (*na vijānāmi yadi vedamasmi ‖*) and so on.

(10) निंदा (*niṃdā*)—A mantra containing censure or praise. For example, केवलाघो भवति केवलादी ॥ (*kevalāgho bhavati kevalādī ‖*) भोजस्येदं पुष्करणीव वेष्म (*bhojasyedaṃ puṣkaraṇīva veṣma*) (here there is censure of gambling and praise of agriculture) and so on. **NOTE**

The mantras given above as examples are the opening words of the respective Ṛks. The complete Ṛks must be found in the alphabetical index of the Ṛks (Ṛ. Saṃ. Part 1, pp. 717-920). Among the ten kinds of mantras explained above, for an example of a Ṛk of the seventh, the matter of oath and curse, Yāska has recited the Ṛk अद्या मुरीय यदि यातुधानो अस्मि (*adyā murīya yadi yātudhāno asmi*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-104-15, **NOTE**

#### Ṛk 21

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा न॑ इंदो अ॒भि दे॒ववी॑तिं॒ परि॑ स्रव॒ नभो॒ अर्ण॑श्च॒मूषु॑ ।  
> सोमो॑ अ॒स्मभ्यं॒ काम्यं॑ बृ॒हंतं॑ र॒यिं द॑दातु वी॒रवं॑तमु॒ग्रं ॥ २१ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । नः । इंदो इति । अभि । देवनीतिं । परि । स्रव । नभः । अर्णः । चमूषु ।  
> सोमः । अस्मभ्यं । काम्यं । बृहंतं । रयिं । ददातु । वीरवंतं । उग्रं ॥ २१ ॥

### Printed p. 788

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे इंदो सोम नोऽस्मदीयमेव देववीतिं । देवानां वीतिर्भक्षणं
> गमनं वा यस्मिन् स देववीतिर्यज्ञः । तमभिलक्ष्य नभो नभसो द्युलोकादर्ण
> उदकं । अनेन पवित्रान्निर्गतः सोमरसोऽभिधीयते । तं रसं चमूषु चमसेषु
> परि स्रव । परितः क्षर । ततः सोमः काम्यं काम्यमानं बृहंतं प्रवृद्धं वीरवंतं
> पुत्रयुक्तमुग्रमुद्दूर्णबलं रयिं धनमस्सभ्यं ददातु । प्रयच्छतु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Indu, Soma, towards our sacrifice alone (देववीतिं (*devavītiṃ*): the sacrifice in which the gods eat or go) pour the water from the heavenly world, the sky; by this the Soma juice that has come out of the filter is denoted. Pour that juice all around into the cups. Then may Soma give us wealth that is desired, great, accompanied by sons, and of overflowing strength.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- न एव देवनीतिं अभि (*na eva devanītiṃ abhi*)—looking to our sacrifice alone **NOTE**
- नभः (*nabhaḥ*)—from the heavenly world
- अर्णः (*arṇaḥ*)—water
- चमूषु (*camūṣu*)—in the Chamu vessels
- परि स्रव (*pari srava*)—pour
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- काम्यं (*kāmyaṃ*)—attractive
- बृहंतं (*bṛhaṃtaṃ*)—grown great
- नीरवंतं (*nīravaṃtaṃ*)—accompanied by sons **NOTE**
- उग्रं (*ugraṃ*)—possessing exceeding strength **NOTE**
- रयिं (*rayiṃ*)—wealth
- अस्मभ्यं (*asmabhyaṃ*)—to us
- ददातु (*dadātu*)—may he give

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, looking to our sacrifice alone, pour the water from the heavenly world into the Chamu vessels. May Soma give us wealth that is attractive, grown great, accompanied by sons, and possessed of exceeding strength.

##### English translation
So, Indu, at our sacrifice pour the water from the firmament into the vessels; may Soma bestow upon us desirable riches in abundance with male offspring and strength.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

देववीतिं- देवानां वीतिर्भक्षणं गमनं वा यस्मिन् स देववीतिर्यज्ञः । (*devavītiṃ- devānāṃ vītirbhakṣaṇaṃ gamanaṃ vā yasmin sa devavītiryajñaḥ |*) The place where the gods come from heaven and eat the oblation (through the mouth of Agni) is called a sacrifice. In sacrifices the officiating priests, the Hota and the others, invite the deities they favour with the recitation of mantras and offer oblations to them in the fire; this rite, in which the gods accept them, is called a sacrifice, the commentator has explained the meaning.

नभः अर्णः चमूषु परिस्रव- (*nabhaḥ arṇaḥ camūṣu parisrava-*) अनेन पवित्रान्निर्गतः सोमरसोऽभिधीयते । (*anena pavitrānnirgataḥ somaraso 'bhidhīyate |*) O Soma, pour the water that is in heaven into these Chamu vessels. What is meant here by the waters of heaven? In the past the Soma plants were in heaven. Gayatri, in the form of a hawk,

### Printed p. 789

went and brought them to the earth. In the sacrifice the officiating priests crush those plants with stones and squeeze out the juice; the juice squeezed out flows to the vessel called the dashapavitra, placed for filtering. This juice is produced from the Soma plants. The Soma plants were in heaven. Therefore the seer here describes the Soma juice as the juice that was in heaven.

सोमः अस्मभ्यं बृहंतं उग्रं वीरवंतं काम्यं रयिं ददातु (*somaḥ asmabhyaṃ bṛhaṃtaṃ ugraṃ vīravaṃtaṃ kāmyaṃ rayiṃ dadātu*)—The meaning is that the divine Soma should graciously give us the wealth that we desire and sons who are growing in strength and heroic. In many Ṛks of the Ṛgveda, and especially in the last Ṛks, which conclude a hymn, the seers are found praying to the deities to give heroic sons and the like. Wealth is a thing needed by all; but what is the need of heroic sons and the like? In that ancient time the Aryas had to wage fierce wars with the Anaryas, the former inhabitants of this land, who were wicked. These black people, the former inhabitants, used to fall upon the Aryas at night and fight with deceit and crooked devices. They used to cause obstruction to sacrifices and the like. Therefore, to protect themselves, and to advance in the country and settle here and there, the Aryas had to wage terrible wars with the black people. For these reasons the need for heroic warriors was very great at that time. Therefore it was natural to pray to the deities to grant heroic sons and the like; such is the meaning.

#### Ṛk 22

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> तक्ष॒द्यदी॒ मन॑सो॒ वेन॑तो॒ वाग्जेष्ठ॑स्य वा॒ धर्म॑णि॒ क्षोरनी॑के ।  
> आदी॑माय॒न्वर॒मा वा॑वशा॒ना जुष्टं॒ पतिं॑ क॒लशे॒ गाव॒  ॑
> इंदुं ॥ २२ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तक्षत् । यदि । मनसः । वेनतः । वाक् । जेष्ठस्य । वा । धर्मणि । क्षोः । अनीके ।  
> आत् । ईं । आयन् । वरं । आ । वावशानाः । जुष्टं । पतिं । कलशे । गावः । इंदुं ॥

### Printed p. 790

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वेनतः । वेनो वेनतेः कांतिकर्मण इति यास्कः । नि. १०-३८ । कामयमानस्य मनसः । मन्यतेः स्तुतिकर्मणः । स्तोतुर्वाक् स्तुतिलक्षणा यद्येनं तक्षत्
> संस्करोति । वाशब्द उपमार्थे । यथा धर्मणि ॥ निमित्तात्कर्मसंयोगे ।
> पा. २-३-३६-६ । इति सप्तमी ॥ धारकं योगक्षेमविषयं कर्मोद्दिश्य क्षोः
> शब्दायमानस्यानीके मुखे तत्र स्थितस्य जानपदिकस्य वाग्जेष्ठस्य । द्वितीयार्थे
> षष्ट् । प्रशस्यतमं राजानं यथा स्तौति तथा स्तोतुर्वाक् सोमं स्तौतीत्यर्थः ।
> आदनंतरमेव वरं वरणेयं जुष्टं देवानां मदाय पर्याप्तं पतिं सर्वस्य
> पालकं कलशे स्थितमिंदुमीमेनं सोमं वावशानाः कामयमाना गाव आयन् ।
> पयसा स्वीयेन मिश्रयितुमागच्छंति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Sāyaṇa takes वेनतः (*venataḥ*) of the mind that desires, citing Yāska (Ni. 10-38): वेनो वेनतेः कांतिकर्मण इति यास्कः । (*veno venateḥ kāṃtikarmaṇa iti yāskaḥ |*) The root मन्यतेः (*manyateḥ*) is of the sense of praise. If the speech of the worshipper, which consists of praise, fashions him, that is, adorns him; the word वा (*vā*) is in the sense of comparison. As, for the sake of a rite that supports and concerns the acquisition and preservation of goods, the speech of the one who is foremost in speech among the countryfolk standing there, in front of the one who sounds, praises the most praiseworthy king, so the speech of the worshipper praises Soma. Then immediately the cows, desiring this excellent Indu, Soma, who is dear to the gods, sufficient for exhilaration, the lord and protector of all, abiding in the vessel, come to mix him with their own milk.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मनसः (*manasaḥ*)—desiring to praise
- वेनतः (*venataḥ*)—of the praiser who wishes
- वाक् (*vāk*)—the speech of praise
- क्षोः (*kṣoḥ*)—that makes a noise
- अनीके (*anīke*)—in the front of the army
- ज्येष्ठस्य (*jyeṣṭhasya*)—who is the leader **NOTE**
- धर्मणि (*dharmaṇi*)—the king who is the supporter of the people
- वा (*vā*)—in what manner
- यदि तक्षत् (*yadi takṣat*)—in that manner as he praises
- वेनतः वाक् (*venataḥ vāk*)—the speech of the praiser praises Soma
- आत् (*āt*)—afterwards
- ईं (*īṃ*)—this Soma
- वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)—desiring
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—cows
- कलशे (*kalaśe*)—in the Drona vessel
- जुष्टं (*juṣṭaṃ*)—pressed for the satisfaction of the gods
- पतिं (*patiṃ*)—the protector of all
- वरं (*varaṃ*)—needed by all
- इंदु (*iṃdu*)—this divine Soma **NOTE**
- आ अयन् (*ā ayan*)—(in order to mix with their milk and the like) approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the speech of the praisers, the bards and eulogists, praises the king who is the leader of the army at its front and the supporter of the people, that is, of the subjects, so the speech of the officiating priests who are praising praises this Soma. Afterwards the cows, wishing to go to the Soma juice, go to the Soma juice that is needed by all, that has been pressed for the satisfaction of the gods and is in the Drona vessel, in order to mix their milk with it.

##### English translation
When the praise of the zealous worshipper sanctifies him as that of a noisy (crowd) in front (praises) a distinguished (prince) for the support (he affords) ; then the cows come to the excellent exhilarating Indu, the lord (of all, abiding) in the pitcher, eager to gratify him (with their milk).

### Printed p. 791

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

As the bards praise with their words of praise the king who is the leader of the army and the supporter of the subjects, so in the sacrifice the officiating priests praise with various words of praise the Soma juice that has just been pressed for the satisfaction of the gods. Afterwards they mix with that Soma juice the admixtures such as milk obtained from the cows. This is the chief meaning.

#### Ṛk 23

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> प्र दा॑नु॒दो दि॒व्यो दा॑नुपि॒न्व ऋ॒तमृ॒ताय॑ पवते सुमे॒धाः ।  
> ध॒र्मा भु॑वद्वृज॒न्य॑स्य॒ राजा॒ प्र र॒श्मिभि॑र्द॒शभि॑र्भारि॒ भूम॑ ॥२३॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> प्र । दानुदः । दिव्यः । दानुपिन्वः । ऋतं । ऋताय । पवते । सुमेधाः ।  
> धर्मा । भुवत् । वृजन्यस्य । राजा । प्र । रश्मिभिः । दशभिः । भारि । भूम ॥ २३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिव्यो दिवि भवो दानुदो दातृभ्यो धनादीनां दाता। तदेवाह! दानुपिन्वः॥
> पिवि सेचने । कर्मण्यण् । पा. ३-२-१ । इत्यण् ॥ दातृभ्यः कामानां क्षारयिता
> सुमेधाः शोभनप्रज्ञः सोम ऋताय सत्यभूतायेंद्रायर्तं सत्यभूतमात्मीयं रसं पवते । प्रकर्षेण क्षरति । राजा दीप्यमानः सोमो वृजन्यस्य साधुबलस्य धर्मा धारयिता भुवत् । भवति । किंच दशभिरेतत्संख्याकाभी रश्मिभिः कर्मकरणार्थमश्नुवानाभिरंगुलिभिर्भूम प्रभूतं प्र भारि । प्रधार्यते ॥ चिणि रूपं ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma is divine, born in heaven, and दानुदो (*dānudo*), the giver of wealth and the like to the givers; he says this again with दानुपिन्वः (*dānupinvaḥ*), the one who makes the desires flow to the givers. Soma, of good understanding, flows forth his own true juice for Indra, who is of the nature of truth. The shining Soma becomes the upholder of good strength. Further, he is borne forth abundantly by the ten rays, that is, by the ten fingers that are engaged for the performance of the rite.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*)—born in the heavenly world
- दानुदः (*dānudaḥ*)—a benefactor of the givers
- दानुपिन्वः (*dānupinvaḥ*)—the bestower of what they wish on the givers
- सुमेधाः (*sumedhāḥ*)—who has excellent understanding; Soma
- ऋताय (*ṛtāya*)—for Indra, who is of the nature of truth

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who is born in the heavenly world, is a benefactor of the givers, is the bestower on them of what they wish, and has excellent understanding, makes flow his own juice, which is of the nature of truth, for Indra, who is of the nature of truth. The shining Soma is the upholder of excellent strength. He is held abundantly by the ten fingers.

##### English translation

(Soma) distils his true beverage for true (Indra); the radiant (Soma) is the
upholder of strength, he is entirely restrained by the ten fingers.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

दानुदः- दातृभ्यो धनादीनां दाता । (*dānudaḥ- dātṛbhyo dhanādīnāṃ dātā |*) He who gives wealth and the like to those who pray to him.

दानुपिन्नः— (*dānupinnaḥ—*) **NOTE** पिवि सेचने । (*pivi secane |*) दातृभ्यः कामानां क्षारयिता । (*dātṛbhyaḥ kāmānāṃ kṣārayitā |*) One who streams out what is desired to those who wish for wealth and the like, as a rain-giver of desires, that is, one who pours it out. As juice streams from the plants and as rain falls from a cloud, so he pours out the desired objects to the praisers, that is, gives them as much as is wished; such is the meaning.

सुमेधाः ऋतं ऋताय पवते— (*sumedhāḥ ṛtaṃ ṛtāya pavate—*) The Soma, who has excellent knowledge, that is, who is all-knowing, streams his own true juice for Indra, who is of a true nature. That is, for Indra's drinking the juice streams from the plants and comes flowing.

दिव्यः— (*divyaḥ—*) दिवि भवः । (*divi bhavaḥ |*) Grown or existing in heaven; it is well known that the Soma plants were formerly in heaven.

राजा वृजन्यस्य धर्मा भुवत्— (*rājā vṛjanyasya dharmā bhuvat—*) Soma, the lord of all, is the master of excellent strength (power); by drinking Soma strength increases. Therefore he is called the increaser of strength.

रश्मिभिः दशभिः भूम प्र भारि— (*raśmibhiḥ daśabhiḥ bhūma pra bhāri—*) The ten fingers of the officiating priests hold this Soma. That is, the officiating priests squeeze out the Soma juice with the ten fingers of their hands; such is the meaning.

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Soma, being purified with the filters, is the seer of men, the beholder of the fruit and non-fruit of men's acts; and likewise he is the king of the gods, Indra and the others, and of mortals, human beings; thus he is the king of both groups of people. He is रयिपतिः (*rayipatiḥ*), the lord of wealth, not the lord of little but of many riches; Sāyaṇa says that both lordship and abundance are intended. Such a Soma becomes twofold, among the gods as well as among men. This Indu, Soma, bears water that is well borne and auspicious.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

Soma, who is purified by the dashapavitra and the other filters, who watches the dealings of men, who is the lord of the gods and of men and the owner of abundant wealth, exists in two forms. Such a great Soma bears water that is well stored and auspicious.

> ५१-३ । इति सुगागमः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, as a horse goes into battle for the sake of food, so you too, for fame, that is, for our food, go towards the gain of wealth and towards the drink (नीतिं (*nītiṃ*), that is, drinking) of Indra and of Vāyu; approach. In the Aindravāyava cup (graha) the text "Indra and Vāyu drink Soma together" mentions the two together. You, then, give us thousands of foods, of many kinds, great, grown abundant. O Soma, being purified, become for us the one who obtains wealth for us.

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, as a horse acts in battle, so exert yourself and provide for us, for the sake of food and for the gain of wealth, the drink for Indra and for Vāyu; give us foods in thousandfold number and in abundance. O divine Soma, being purified, be the obtainer of wealth.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

इंद्रस्य वायोः नीतिं अभि अर्ष (*iṃdrasya vāyoḥ nītiṃ abhi arṣa*)—Here there is a mention of the Soma-drinking of Indra and Vāyu. There is a narrative about how both of them obtained Soma-drinking in the Aindravāyava cup, and how Vāyu became entitled to Soma-drinking before all others. It is well known that in the sacrifice Vāyu is the first entitled to drink Soma, and that for another reason Indra joined Vāyu and both drink Soma together. On this matter, that is, how the deity Vāyu is entitled to the first Soma-drinking, there is an earlier history in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

देवा वै सोमस्य राज्योऽग्रपेये न समपादयॆन्नहं प्रथमः पिबेयमहं प्रथमः पिबेयमित्येवाकामयंत ते संपादयंतोऽब्रुवन् हंताजिमयाम स यो न उज्जॆष्यति स प्रथमः सोमस्य पास्यतीति तथेति त आजिमयुस्तेषामाजिं यतामभिसृष्टानां वायुर्मुखं प्रथमः प्रत्यपद्यताथेंद्रोऽथ मित्रावरुणावथाश्विन् । (*devā vai somasya rājyo 'grapeye na samapādayènnahaṃ prathamaḥ pibeyamahaṃ prathamaḥ pibeyamityevākāmayaṃta te saṃpādayaṃto 'bruvan haṃtājimayāma sa yo na ujjèṣyati sa prathamaḥ somasya pāsyatīti tatheti ta ājimayusteṣāmājiṃ yatāmabhisṛṣṭānāṃ vāyurmukhaṃ prathamaḥ pratyapadyatātheṃdro 'tha mitrāvaruṇāvathāśvin |*) (Ai. Brā. 9-25)

In former times all the gods together desired to drink Soma, and a dispute arose as to which of them should drink the Soma first; each of them began to insist, "I first, I first shall drink." Since the matter could not be settled in any way, they all gathered, took counsel and came to an agreement, namely: "Let us all arrange a contest together. Whoever wins in it shall be entitled to drink Soma first." When all agreed to this, the contest was fixed thus: running from one place to another place far away, whoever first reached a rock or a tree there should be regarded as the winner. When all consented to the agreement that the one who wins in this way should be victorious among them and drink Soma first, all the gods began to run at the same time.

### Printed p. 796

Among all the running gods, Vāyu reached the appointed place ahead of everyone. Indra came right behind Vāyu and became the second. After that, behind Indra came Mitra and Varuṇa, and behind them the Aśvin gods ran up and reached the appointed place. Therefore among these gods Vāyu ran ahead of everyone and became the victor.

सोऽवेदिंद्रो वायुमुद्वै जयतीति तमनु परापतत्सह नावथोज्जयानेति स नेत्यब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामाति तृतीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति नेति हैवाब्रवीदहमेवोज्जॆष्यामाति तुरीयं मेऽथोज्जयावेति तथेति तं तुरीयेऽत्यार्जत तत्तु रीयभागिंद्रोऽभवत्रिभाग्वायुः ॥ (*so 'vediṃdro vāyumudvai jayatīti tamanu parāpatatsaha nāvathojjayāneti sa netyabravīdahamevojjèṣyāmāti tṛtīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti neti haivābravīdahamevojjèṣyāmāti turīyaṃ me 'thojjayāveti tatheti taṃ turīye 'tyārjata tattu rīyabhāgiṃdro 'bhavatribhāgvāyuḥ ‖*)

While Vāyu was running and Indra behind him, a conversation took place between them in this manner. Indra, who was behind Vāyu, saw him running swiftly and resolved: "This Vāyu will run ahead of everyone and be the victor. Somehow I too must run along with him and win." Using all his strength he ran close to Vāyu. Yet, as there was no sign of leaving Vāyu behind and going ahead himself, Indra then addressed Vāyu: "O Vāyu, we two are ahead of everyone. Therefore let us regard ourselves both as winners and both share the first Soma-drinking: half for me, half for you; thus let us co-operate and gain the victory." Hearing those words Vāyu said: "O Indra, I am ahead of you, if only by a little. Therefore I alone shall be the victor. In the first Soma-drinking everything must belong to me. I cannot give you half." Then Indra said: "Very well, then I do not want a half. Take two out of three parts, and give me only one part." But Vāyu did not agree even to this and said: "Somehow I alone shall win. The whole share will belong to me; I am not willing to give you even one part out of three." Then Indra again entreated Vāyu: "I do not want even one part out of three. Still less, that is, if you give me one part out of four, it is enough. Agree to that at least." When he asked thus, Vāyu agreed, saying "So be it." Therefore it was arranged that in the Aindravāyava cup (that is, the vessel in which Indra and Vāyu together drink Soma) Indra should have one part and Vāyu three parts.

### Printed p. 797

तौ सहैवेंद्रवायू उदजयतां सह मित्रावरुण् सहाश्विन् त एषामेते यथोज्जि तं भक्षा इंद्रवाय्वोः प्रथमोऽथ मित्रावरुणयोरथाश्विनोः स एष इंद्रतुरीयो ग्रहो गृह्यते यद्यैंद्रवायवः । (*tau sahaiveṃdravāyū udajayatāṃ saha mitrāvaruṇ sahāśvin ta eṣāmete yathojji taṃ bhakṣā iṃdravāyvoḥ prathamo 'tha mitrāvaruṇayorathāśvinoḥ sa eṣa iṃdraturīyo graho gṛhyate yadyaiṃdravāyavaḥ |*)

In this way Indra and Vāyu, co-operating, won the contest and reached the appointed place first. Behind them Mitra and Varuṇa came and joined. Behind them the Aśvin gods came. Therefore among these gods, in the order of the place each obtained in the contest, they became entitled to Soma-drinking. That is, the arrangement came about that first Indra and Vāyu, then Mitra and Varuṇa, then the Aśvin gods should drink Soma. Thus the practice of the dvidevatya graha (that is, the practice in which two deities together drink Soma) came into use. Therefore in the Aindravāyava cup only one part out of four is Indra's share in the Soma-drinking.

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> देवाव्यः ॥ अवतेस्तर्पणार्थस्य अवित्यस्तंत्रिभ्य ईरितीप्रत्ययः । उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति जसः स्वरितत्वं ॥ देवानां तर्पयितारः परिषिच्यमानाः परितः

> दिवियजो दिवि द्युलोके स्थितानिंद्रादीन्देवान्यजंतः ॥ दिव्यब्दे तत्पुरुषे कृति
> बहुलमिति सप्तम्या अलुक् ॥ मंद्रतमा अत्यंतं मदकराः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Those who gratify the gods (देवाव्यः (*devāvyaḥ*)), the Somas poured around, that is, poured on all sides into the vessels, are to bring us a dwelling with good heroes, that is, with good sons: may they impel it towards us. Of what kind are they? Like ministrant priests: as the Hotṛs praise the gods Indra and Agni, so these worship the gods Indra and the others who dwell in heaven, in the world of light. They are most exhilarating, that is, in the highest degree intoxicating.

- परिषिच्यमानाः (*pariṣicyamānāḥ*)—and which are poured all around in the vessels

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

May the Soma juices, which give satisfaction to the gods and are poured all around in the vessels, give us a dwelling furnished with excellent heroic sons. Like the Hotṛs, those who worship the gods of the heavenly world, who give gifts visibly, who are worthy of everyone's esteem and most exhilarating, the Soma juices, are to bestow good understanding on us.

##### English translation
May the Soma juices which are gratifying to the gods when poured around (into the vessels) bring us a dwelling and male offspring—(the juices) endeavouring to gain the favour (of the gods), desired by all offering (to the gods) in heaven like the the ministrant priests, most exhilarating. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

The word सुमति (*sumati*) is, by Yāska,

धाता ददातु दाशुषे प्राचीं जीनातुमक्षितां । वयं देवस्य धीमहि सुमतिं सत्यधर्मणः ॥ (*dhātā dadātu dāśuṣe prācīṃ jīnātumakṣitāṃ | vayaṃ devasya dhīmahi sumatiṃ satyadharmaṇaḥ ‖*) (Atha. Saṃ. 7-2-2) **GLOSS**

In this quoted Ṛk and in still other places, Sāyaṇa has explained that the word सुमति (*sumati*) conveys the meaning "auspicious understanding". But the word सुमति (*sumati*) is used not only for the divine, gracious understanding, but also in the sense of a prayer made by man, or the excellent desire of man. For example,

### Printed p. 799

शुभ्यं भरंति क्षितयो यविष्ठ बलिमग्ने अंतित ओत दूरात् । आ भंदिष्ठस्य सुमतिं चिकिद्दि बृहत्ते अग्ने महि शर्म भद्रं ॥ (*śubhyaṃ bharaṃti kṣitayo yaviṣṭha balimagne aṃtita ota dūrāt | ā bhaṃdiṣṭhasya sumatiṃ cikiddi bṛhatte agne mahi śarma bhadraṃ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-1-10) **GLOSS**

प्र वो महे महिवृधे भरध्वं प्रचेतसे प्र सुमतिं कृणुध्वं । विशः पूर्वीः प्र चरा चर्षणिप्राः ॥ (*pra vo mahe mahivṛdhe bharadhvaṃ pracetase pra sumatiṃ kṛṇudhvaṃ | viśaḥ pūrvīḥ pra carā carṣaṇiprāḥ ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-31-10) **GLOSS**

In Ṛks such as these it has been interpreted as स्तोतुः स्तुतिं आ जानीहि (*stotuḥ stutiṃ ā jānīhi*), "listen to the excellent praise of the praiser", and as इंद्राय सुष्टुतिं प्र कुरुत (*iṃdrāya suṣṭutiṃ pra kuruta*), "recite an excellent praise addressed to Indra". And further,

यूयं न उग्रा मरुतः सुचेतुनारिष्टग्रामाः सुमतिं पिपर्तन । यत्रा वो विद्युद्रदति क्रिविर्दती रिणाति पश्वः सुधितेव बर्हणा ॥ (*yūyaṃ na ugrā marutaḥ sucetunāriṣṭagrāmāḥ sumatiṃ pipartana | yatrā vo vidyudradati krivirdatī riṇāti paśvaḥ sudhiteva barhaṇā ‖*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-6) **GLOSS**

In the Ṛk explained earlier, Sāyaṇa has explained सुमतिं पिपर्तन (*sumatiṃ pipartana*) as शोभनबुद्धिं पूरयत (*śobhanabuddhiṃ pūrayata*). Here "excellent understanding" does not mean only the gracious understanding of the gods. Since पिपर्तन (*pipartana*) is said, the meaning "fulfil also our excellent desired aims" arises naturally.

#### Ṛk 27

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा दे॑व दे॒वता॑ते पवस्व म॒हे सो॑म॒ प्सर॑से देव॒पानः॑ ।  
> म॒हश्चि॒द्दि ष्मसि॑ हि॒ताः स॑म॒र्यॆ कृ॒धि सु॑स्था॒ने रोद॑सी पुना॒नः॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । देव । देवताते । पवस्व । महे । सोम । प्सरसे । देवपानः ।  
> महः । चित् । हि । स्मसि । हिताः । समर्यॆ । कृधि । सुस्थाने इति सुस्थाने । रोदसी  
> इति । पुनानः ॥ २७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे देव द्योतमान स्तोतव्य वा हे सोम देवपानो देवैः पातव्यस्त्वं
> देवताते देवैस्तते वितते यज्ञे महे महते प्सरसे भक्षणाय देवानां पानाय्कॆ-

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O shining or praiseworthy Soma, you who are to be drunk by the gods, in the sacrifice spread out by the gods, for the great drinking, for food, for the drinking of the gods. **NOTE**

### Printed p. 800

> यैवैवं पवस्व । क्षर ततो वयं हितास्त्वया प्रेरिताः संतः समर्ये मरणधर्मसहिते संग्रामे महश्चिन्महतो बलाधिकानपि शत्रुन् स्मसि हि । अभिभवेम खलु । किंच
> पुनानः पूयमानस्त्वं रोदसी द्यावापृथिव्य सुस्थाने अस्माकं शोभनावासस्थाने
> सत्यौ कृधि । कुरु ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

So flow, stream forth; then we, impelled by you, in the battle that carries the nature of death, would indeed overcome even enemies who are greater and stronger in might. And further, you who are being purified, make heaven and earth, the two worlds, a good dwelling-place of ours, a true one.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- देव (*deva*)—O shining
- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- देवपानः (*devapānaḥ*)—you who are fit for the drinking of the gods
- देवताते (*devatāte*)—in the sacrifice
- महे (*mahe*)—great
- प्सरसे (*psarase*)—for the drinking of the gods
- एव (*eva*)—in the prescribed manner
- पवस्व (*pavasva*)—flow
- हिताः (*hitāḥ*)—we who are urged on by you
- समर्ये (*samarye*)—in battle
- महश्चित् (*mahaścit*)—even the exceedingly mighty enemies
- स्मसि हि (*smasi hi*)—may we overcome
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—you who have been purified
- रोदसी (*rodasī*)—heaven and earth
- सुस्थाने (*susthāne*)—so that they become a good dwelling-place for us
- कृधि (*kṛdhi*)—make

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O shining Soma, you who are fit for the drinking of the gods, flow in the prescribed manner in the sacrifice for the great drinking of the gods. May we, urged on by you, overcome in battle even the exceedingly mighty enemies. You who have been purified, make heaven and earth a good dwelling-place for us.

##### English translation
Divine Soma, you are the beverage of gods, flow at the sacrifice for (their) abundant food ; urged on (by you) may we overcome even mighty (foes) in battle ; purified do you render heaven and earth happy abodes (for us).

#### Ṛk 28

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> अश्वो॒ न क्र॑दो॒ वृष॑भियुर्जुजा॒नः सिं॒हो न भी॒मो मन॑सो॒  ॑
> जवीयान् ।  
> अ॒र्वा॒चीनैः॑ प॒थिभि॒र्ये रजि॑ष्ठा॒ आ प॑वस्व सौमन॒सं न॑ इंदो ॥

### Printed p. 801

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> अश्वः । न । क्रदः । वृषभिः । युजानः । सिंहः । न । भीमः । मनसः । जवीयान् ।  
> अर्वाचीनैः । पथिभिः । ये । रजिष्ठाः । आ । पवस्व । सौमनसं । नः । इंदो इति ॥२८॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम वृषभिर्युत्विग्भिः सोममभिषुण्वद्भियुर्जानो योज्यमानस्त्वमश्वो नाश्व इव क्रदः । क्रंदसि । शब्दायसे । कीदृशः । सिंहो न सिंह इव भीमः
> शत्रूणां भयंकरः तथा मनसोऽपि जवीयान् वेगवत्तरः । अर्वाचीनैरभिमुख्यः
> पथिभिर्मार्गैर्ये मार्गा रजिष्ठा अत्यंतमृजवो भवंति ॥ विभाषर्जोश्चंदसीत्यृकारस्य रादेशः ॥ हे इंदो दीप्यमान सोम तैर्मार्गैनोर्नोऽस्माकं सौमनसं
> सौमनस्यमा पवस्व । आ प्रापय ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, yoked by the Ṛtviks, who are the bulls, that is, by those who press Soma, you cry like a horse; you make a sound. Of what kind are you? Like a lion, terrible, fearsome to enemies, and also swifter than mind, more swift. By the paths facing us, which are the most straight, O shining Soma, by those paths bring to us good-mindedness; cause it to reach us.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- वृषभिः (*vṛṣabhiḥ*)—by the Ṛtviks
- युजानः (*yujānaḥ*)—you who are yoked for the rite
- अश्वो न (*aśvo na*)—like a horse
- क्रदः (*kradaḥ*)—you make a sound
- सिंहो न (*siṃho na*)—like a lion
- भीमः (*bhīmaḥ*)—you are fearsome to enemies
- मनसः (*manasaḥ*) (अपि (*api*))—than the speed of mind
- जवीयान् (*javīyān*)—you are one of greater speed
- अर्वाचीनैः (*arvācīnaiḥ*)—facing us
- पथिभिः (*pathibhiḥ*)—in the paths
- ये (*ye*)—which
- रजिष्ठाः (*rajiṣṭhāḥ*)—(without crookedness) straight, by those paths
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- सौमनसं (*saumanasaṃ*)—welfare
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—provide

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are yoked by the Ṛtviks for the rite, you make a sound like a horse. You are fearsome to enemies like a lion. You are of greater speed than the speed of mind. By those of the paths facing us which are straight, provide us welfare.

##### English translation
Yoked by the priests, you neigh like a horse, (you are) terrible as a lion, swifter than thought ; Indu, pour happiness upon us by those which are the most direct of the pathes leading hitherward.

#### Ṛk 29

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> श॒तं धारा॑ दे॒वजा॑ता अस्यग्रन्त्स॒हस्र॑मेनाः क॒वयो॑ मृजंति ।  
> इंदो॑ स॒नित्रं॑ दि॒व आ प॑वस्व पुरए॒तासि॑ मह॒तो धन॑स्य ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> शतं । धाराः । देवजाताः । असृग्रन् । सहस्रं । एनाः । कवयः । मृजंति ।  
> इंदो इति । सनित्रं । दिवः । आ । पवस्व, पुरःएता । असि । महतः । धनस्य ॥ २९ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम देवजाता देवार्थं प्रादुर्भूताः शतं शतसंख्याकास्त्वदीया
> धारा असृग्रन् । सृज्यंते । ततः कवयः क्रांतदर्शिन ऋत्विजः सहस्रं बहुविधा
> एनास्त्वदीया धारा मृजंति । अलंकुर्वंति । यद्वा । सहस्रमनेकधा मृजंति ।
> शोधयंति । हे इंदो सनित्रं भजनसाधनं धनं दिवो द्युलोकादस्माकं
> पुत्रादीनां चा पवस्व । आप्रापय । कुतोऽस्य धनमिति चेत् तत्राह । महतः
> प्रभूतस्य धनस्य पुरविता पुरतो गंतासि । भवसि ! तस्माद्देहीति ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, your hundred streams, born for the gods, that is, manifested for the sake of the gods, are released; they are poured forth. Then the sages, the Ṛtvijs who see far, cleanse, that is, adorn, those streams of yours in a thousand, many kinds of ways. Or else: they cleanse, purify, in a thousandfold manner. O Soma, the wealth that is the means of enjoyment, from heaven, from the world of light, bring to us and to our sons and others; cause it to reach us. If it be asked, "Whence has he wealth?", he says: you are the one who goes before, the leader, of great, abundant wealth; therefore give it.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- इंदो (*iṃdo*)—O divine Soma
- देवजाताः (*devajātāḥ*)—produced for the gods
- शतंधारा (*śataṃdhārā*)—your many streams
- अस्यग्रन् (*asyagran*)—have been released freely **NOTE**
- कवयि (*kavayi*)—the wise Ṛtviks **NOTE**
- सहस्रं (*sahasraṃ*)—in many ways
- एनाः (*enāḥ*)—these streams
- मृजंति (*mṛjaṃti*)—they cleanse (adorn)
- सनित्रं (*sanitraṃ*)—wealth fit for enjoyment
- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—from the world of light
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—provide to us
- (त्वं (*tvaṃ*)—you)
- महतः धनस्य (*mahataḥ dhanasya*)—of exceedingly great wealth
- पुरएता (*puraetā*)—as the leader
- असि (*asi*)—you are

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, your many streams, produced for the gods, flow freely. The wise Ṛtviks cleanse these streams in many ways. Provide us from the world of light wealth fit for enjoyment. You are the lord of abundant wealth.

### Printed p. 803

##### English translation
Your hundred streams manifested for the gods are loose ; the sages cleanse those thousand (streams) ; pour wealth upon us, Indu, from heaven ; you are the precursor of abundant riches.

#### Ṛk 30

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒वो न सर्गा॑ अससृग्र॒मह्नां॒ राजा॒ न मि॒त्रं प्र मि॑नाति॒ धीरः॑ ।  
> पि॒तुर्न पु॒त्रः क्रतु॑भिर्यता॒न आ प॑वस्व वि॒शे अ॒स्या अजी॑तिं ॥३०॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिवः । न । सर्गाः । अससृग्रं । अह्नां । राजा । न । मित्रं । प्र । मिनाति । धीरः ।  
> पिशुः । न । पुत्रः । क्रतुभिः । यतानः । आ । पवस्व । विशे । अस्यै । अजीतिं ॥ ३० ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> दिवो न यथा दिवो द्योतमानस्यादित्यस्याह्नां संबंधिनः सर्गा रश्मयोऽसृग्रं विसृज्यंते तद्वत्सोमस्य सर्गाः । सृज्यंत इति सर्गा धाराः । विसृज्यंते ॥
> सृजेर्व्यत्ययेन कर्मार्थे लजि बहुलं छंदसीति शस्य श्लुः । झीरमादेशश्रांदसः ॥
> धीरः प्राज्ञो राजायं सोमो मित्रं सखायं न प्र मिनाति । न हिनस्ति । क्रतुभिः
> कर्मभिर्यतानो यतमानः पुत्रः पितुर्न पितुर्यथापराभवं करोति तद्वत्
> कर्मभिर्यतमानस्त्वमस्यॆ विशे प्रजाया अजीतिमपराभवमा पवस्स । आप्रापय ।
> यथा न पराजिता भवंति तथा कुर्वित्यर्थः ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

As the rays (सर्गाः (*sargāḥ*)) connected with the days of the shining sun are released, so are the streams of Soma released: those that are poured forth are called सर्गाः (*sargāḥ*), the streams; they are let loose. This Soma, wise and a king, does not injure, does not harm, his friend. As a son, striving with rites (क्रतुभिः (*kratubhiḥ*)), does not bring defeat to his father, so you, striving with rites, bring to this people invincibility, absence of defeat; cause it to reach them. The meaning is: act so that they are not defeated.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- दिवः (*divaḥ*)—of the shining Sun
- अह्नां (*ahnāṃ*)—connected with the days
- सर्गाः न (*sargāḥ na*)—like the rays
- अससृग्रं (*asasṛgraṃ*)—the rays of Soma too are released
- धीरः (*dhīraḥ*)—the wise
- राजा (*rājā*)—and lordly Soma
- मित्रं (*mitraṃ*)—his friend
- न प्र मिनाति (*na pra mināti*)—does not give up; (O Soma)
- क्रतुभिः (*kratubhiḥ*)—with his rites
- यशानः (*yaśānaḥ*)—the one who strives **NOTE**
- पुत्रः (*putraḥ*)—a son
- पितुःन (*pituḥna*)—just as he brings no defeat to his father, in the same way
- अस्यॆ विशे (*asyè viśe*)—to us, your people
- अजीतिं (*ajītiṃ*)—freedom from defeat
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—bring about

### Printed p. 804

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

As the rays of the shining Sun among the days spread, so the rays of Soma spread. Soma, wise and lordly, does not give up his friend. O Soma, as a son striving with his rites does not bring defeat to his father, so make us, your people, free from defeat (from being overcome).

##### English translation
As the rays of the days of the sun are let loose (so are the streams of the Soma) : a prudent king doee not obandon his friend ; as a son persevering in pious acts (wins) his father's (safety), so you pour upon this people immunity from defeat. **NOTE**

> अर्कैः ॥ ३१ ॥

> अव्यान् ।  
> पवमान । पवसे । धाम । गोनां । जज्ञानः । सूर्यं । अपिन्वः । अर्कैः ॥ ३१ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> ते तव स्वभूता मधुमतीर्मधुमत्तो धाराः प्रासृग्रन् तदा प्रसृज्यंते
> यद्यदा पूतो वसतीवरीभिस्त्वमव्यानविभवान्वारान्वालान्पवित्राण्यत्येषि । अतीत्य
> गच्छसि । किंच हे पवमान धाम धारकं गोनां गवां पयो लक्ष्मीकृत्य पवसे । ततो
> जज्ञानो जायमानस्त्वमर्कैरर्चनीयैः स्वतेजोभिः सूर्यमादित्यमपिन्नः ।
> पूरयसि ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

Your own honey-laden streams are poured forth when, purified by the Vasatīvarī waters, you pass over the woollen filters, the hairs, which are not abundant. And further, O Pavamāna, you purify, making the milk of the cows, the supporter, your own; then, being born, you fill the Sun with the radiances of yours that are worthy of praise.

(O divine Soma)

- वरान् (*varān*)—the woollen threads **NOTE**
- अत्येषि (*atyeṣi*)—you pass over, then

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, when you, purified by the Vasatīvarī waters, pass over the woollen threads, then your sweet streams flow freely. O divine Soma, you flow towards the supporting milk. As soon as you are produced, you pervade the Sun with your radiances.

##### English translation
Your exhilarating streams are let loose when you pass purified through the woollen fleece ; Pavamana, you flow to the supporting (milk) of the cows, as soon as generated you fill the sun with your radiance.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

अर्कै (*arkai*)—Yāska, giving the etymology of the word अर्क (*arka*), has set out the various meanings of this word.

अर्कः । अर्को देवो भवति यदेनमर्चति । अर्को मंत्रो भवति यदनेनार्चंति । अर्कमन्नं भवत् र्चति भूतानि । अर्को वृक्षो भवति संवृत्तः कटुकिम्ना ॥ (*arkaḥ | arko devo bhavati yadenamarcati | arko maṃtro bhavati yadanenārcaṃti | arkamannaṃ bhavat rcati bhūtāni | arko vṛkṣo bhavati saṃvṛttaḥ kaṭukimnā ‖*) (2. 5-4) **NOTE**

Thus he has stated four kinds of meaning. The explanation of this can be given in this way—

तावत्सर्व एकार्क इत्युच्यते यद्यस्मादेनं देवं अर्चंति स्तोतारः— (*tāvatsarva ekārka ityucyate yadyasmādenaṃ devaṃ arcaṃti stotāraḥ—*)

अर्क (*arka*) means a deity, because it is that by which devotees worship someone; that is, the person or god whom devotees worship, the object (the deity) that devotees worship, is named अर्क (*arka*).

अर्को मंत्रो भवति! यद्यस्मादनेन मंत्रेणार्चंति स्तोतारस्तस्मादर्कः— (*arko maṃtro bhavati! yadyasmādanena maṃtreṇārcaṃti stotārastasmādarkaḥ—*)

अर्क (*arka*) is also understood to mean a mantra, because those who sing praise worship the deity with this (अर्क (*arka*), that is, the mantra). Therefore the word अर्क (*arka*) is also named a mantra.

### Printed p. 806

अर्कमन्नं भवति—तद्धि अर्चति भूतानि यो हि पूज्यः तस्यान्नमपि संस्कारविशेषेण संस्कृतं पूजायां क्रियते, पूज्यं च सर्वस्यॆवान्नं— (*arkamannaṃ bhavati—taddhi arcati bhūtāni yo hi pūjyaḥ tasyānnamapi saṃskāraviśeṣeṇa saṃskṛtaṃ pūjāyāṃ kriyate, pūjyaṃ ca sarvasyèvānnaṃ—*)

अर्क (*arka*) is also understood to mean food. Since food is necessary for all living beings, everyone respects food and desires it; that is, because everyone respects it and longs for it with love and regard, the word अर्क (*arka*) is also understood to mean food.

अर्को वृक्षो भवति य एष प्रसिद्धः । संवृतः हि संगतः संव्याप्तः कटुकिम्ना कटुकभावेन (*arko vṛkṣo bhavati ya eṣa prasiddhaḥ | saṃvṛtaḥ hi saṃgataḥ saṃvyāptaḥ kaṭukimnā kaṭukabhāvena*) Further, the name of a particular tree is well established for the word अर्क (*arka*). The अर्क (*arka*) tree is called ekkada-giḍa (the swallow-wort plant) in the Karnāṭaka language. Because its samits (twigs) are used in the homas and because it is customary to use it in medicines and the like, the अर्क (*arka*) tree is a thing known to all. Because it is bitter it is called कटुकिम्ना (*kaṭukimnā*). In the present Ṛk the commentator has explained the word अर्क (*arka*) as meaning "by a radiance worthy of worship".

The influence of अर्क (*arka*) is exceedingly great, and its glory is praised in many places. In the Aitareya Āraṇyaka,

अथातः शिरः । यद्गायत्रीषु भवत्यग्रं वै छंदसां गायत्र्यग्रमंगानां शिरः । तदर्कवतीषु भवत्यग्निर्वा अर्कः । ता नव भवंति नव कपालं शिरः ॥ (*athātaḥ śiraḥ | yadgāyatrīṣu bhavatyagraṃ vai chaṃdasāṃ gāyatryagramaṃgānāṃ śiraḥ | tadarkavatīṣu bhavatyagnirvā arkaḥ | tā nava bhavaṃti nava kapālaṃ śiraḥ ‖*) (Ai. Ā. 1-4-1)

quoting this sentence, it is stated that the following nine Ṛks, beginning with the Ṛk इंद्रमिद्दाथिनो बृहदिंद्रमर्कॆभिरर्किणः (*iṃdramiddāthino bṛhadiṃdramarkèbhirarkiṇaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-7 1) **NOTE**, are the अर्क (*arka*) mantras, that they are the mantras whose nature is the head, and that, since Gāyatra is the principal principle and these mantras too are in that Gāyatra form, the अर्क (*arka*) mantras hold the principal place above all mantras. In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad, explaining the etymology of the word अर्क (*arka*),

सोऽर्चन्नचरत्तस्यार्चच आपोऽजायंतार्चते वै मे कमभूदिति तदेवार्कस्यार्कत्वं कं ह वा अस्मै भवति य एवमेतदर्कस्यार्कत्वं वेद । (*so 'rcannacarattasyārcaca āpo 'jāyaṃtārcate vai me kamabhūditi tadevārkasyārkatvaṃ kaṃ ha vā asmai bhavati ya evametadarkasyārkatvaṃ veda |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-2-1)

While Death was moving about in search of a body, water came into being. Therefore the name अर्क (*arka*) became established for water. For this very reason,

आपो वा अर्कः तद्यदसां शिर आसीत्तत्समहन्यत । (*āpo vā arkaḥ tadyadasāṃ śira āsīttatsamahanyata |*) (Bṛ. U. 1-2-2)

### Printed p. 807

and so on, it is described. Here अर्क (*arka*) is that which reflects the hidden principle of the universe. The glory of अर्क (*arka*), which expounds the principle of Prajāpati, and the explanation of its nature are described in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, in the context of Āruṇi's instruction, in this manner.

श्वेतकेतुर्वारुणेयः यक्षमाणा आस तग्०ह पितोवाच तानृत्विजोऽवृथा इति स होवाचायं नेव मे वैश्वावसव्यो होतेति तग्०ह पप्रच्छ वेत्थ ब्राह्मणा वैशावसव्य ॥ (*śvetaketurvāruṇeyaḥ yakṣamāṇā āsa tag0ha pitovāca tānṛtvijo 'vṛthā iti sa hovācāyaṃ neva me vaiśvāvasavyo hoteti tag0ha papraccha vettha brāhmaṇā vaiśāvasavya ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-1)

When Śvetaketu Āruṇi, the son of Uddālaka Āruṇi, was engaged in an effort to perform a sacrifice, his father asked him which Ṛtviks he had chosen for the sacrificial rite, and Śvetaketu said that Vaiśvāvasavya was his Hotṛ. Then the father said,

चत्वारि महांतीति । वेद भो ३ इति होवाच..................नेत्थ चत्वारि क्यानीति वेद भो ३ इति होवाच नेत्थ चत्वारि क्यानां क्यानी३इति वेद भो ३ इति होवाच नेत्थ चत्वारि अर्कानिति वेद भो इति होवाच (*catvāri mahāṃtīti | veda bho 3 iti hovāca..................nettha catvāri kyānīti veda bho 3 iti hovāca nettha catvāri kyānāṃ kyānī3iti veda bho 3 iti hovāca nettha catvāri arkāniti veda bho iti hovāca*) (Śa. Brā. 10-1-4-2)

Do you know the four great principles? Do you know the principle related to Ka (Prajāpati)? Among them, do you know the four most hidden principles, have you understood the nature of the four universal lights? Have you meditated on the principle that is the very form of light of the lights? When he asked thus, Śvetaketu said that he knew all of it. Again the father said,

नेत्थार्कमिति । अथ वै नो भवान्वक्ष्यतीति (*netthārkamiti | atha vai no bhavānvakṣyatīti*) (Ka Brā. 10-3-4-3) **NOTE**

Do you know the nature of अर्क (*arka*), the nature of अर्क (*arka*) leaves and अर्क (*arka*) flowers? Do you know the nature of अर्क (*arka*) capsules and अर्क (*arka*) grains? Do you know the root of अर्क (*arka*)? When he asked thus, Śvetaketu said that he knew none of these and asked that they be explained to him. Then the father, explaining अर्क (*arka*), told him also its hidden meaning.

### Printed p. 808

अथ ह वै यत्तदुवाच । वेत्थार्कमिति पुरुषग्ं हैव तदुवाच ! वेत्थार्कपर्णॆ इति कर्णौ हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कपुष्टे इत्यक्षिणी हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्ककोश्याविति नासिके हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कसमुद्गावित्योषौ हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कधाना इति दंतान्हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्काष्ठीलामिति जिह्वाग्ं हैव तदुवाच वेत्थार्कमूलमित्यन्नग्ं हैव तदुवाच (*atha ha vai yattaduvāca | vetthārkamiti puruṣagṃ haiva taduvāca ! vetthārkaparṇè iti karṇau haiva taduvāca vetthārkapuṣṭe ityakṣiṇī haiva taduvāca vetthārkakośyāviti nāsike haiva taduvāca vetthārkasamudgāvityoṣau haiva taduvāca vetthārkadhānā iti daṃtānhaiva taduvāca vetthārkāṣṭhīlāmiti jihvāgṃ haiva taduvāca vetthārkamūlamityannagṃ haiva taduvāca*) स एषोऽग्निरर्को यत्पुरुषः स यो हैतमेवमग्निमर्कं पुरुषमुपास्तेऽयमहमग्निरर्कोऽस्मितिविद्यया हैवासैष आत्मन्नग्निरर्कश्चितो भवति (*sa eṣo 'gnirarko yatpuruṣaḥ sa yo haitamevamagnimarkaṃ puruṣamupāste 'yamahamagnirarko 'smitividyayā haivāsaiṣa ātmannagnirarkaścito bhavati*) (Śa. Brā. 10-3-4-5)

अर्क (*arka*) means the Puruṣa. The अर्क (*arka*) leaves are the ears of the Puruṣa; the अर्क (*arka*) flowers are the eyes. The अर्क (*arka*) capsules are the nostrils; अर्क (*arka*) समुद्ग (*samudga*) means the lips; the अर्क (*arka*) grains are the teeth; the corresponding part of the अर्क (*arka*) is the tongue; the अर्क (*arka*) root is food. The Puruṣa who is expounded by this अर्क (*arka*) is the sacrificial fire. Thus, for one who knows the identity of these three, अर्क (*arka*), fire and Puruṣa, the sacrificial fire becomes manifest on the sacrificial altar; thus he has told the hidden meaning of the word अर्क (*arka*). Explaining again that this अर्क (*arka*) itself is the principle of Parabrahman in the form of the imperishable,

तद्धैतत्पश्यन्नृषिरभ्यनूनाद । भूतं भविष्यत्प्रस्तौमि । महद्ब्रह्मैकमक्षरं बहु ब्रह्मैकमक्षरमित्येतद्दैवाक्षरग्० सर्वे देवाः सर्वाणि भूतान्यभि संपद्यंते तदेतद्ब्रह्म च क्षत्रं चाग्निरेव ब्रह्मेंद्रः क्षत्रमिंद्राग्नी वै विश्वे देवा विडु विश्वे देवास्तदेतद्ब्रह्म क्षत्रं विट् ॥ (*taddhaitatpaśyannṛṣirabhyanūnāda | bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyatprastaumi | mahadbrahmaikamakṣaraṃ bahu brahmaikamakṣaramityetaddaivākṣarag0 sarve devāḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyabhi saṃpadyaṃte tadetadbrahma ca kṣatraṃ cāgnireva brahmeṃdraḥ kṣatramiṃdrāgnī vai viśve devā viḍu viśve devāstadetadbrahma kṣatraṃ viṭ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-4-1-9)

This अर्क (*arka*) is Parabrahman itself, reflecting the past, future and present and being all-pervading. All the gods are included in this Parabrahman, which has the form of अर्क (*arka*) and the form of the imperishable. This one alone reflects the power of Brahma and the power of Kṣatra. It is stated that the principle which the seer explained, saying that all the gods are included in this, is this very अर्क (*arka*)-ness. And,

स एष एवार्कः । योऽयमग्निश्चितस्तस्यैतदन्नं क्यमेष सौम्योऽध्वरस्तदर्क्र्यं ..................सहोदक्रामदेष चंद्रमाः ॥ (*sa eṣa evārkaḥ | yo 'yamagniścitastasyaitadannaṃ kyameṣa saumyo 'dhvarastadarkryaṃ ..................sahodakrāmadeṣa caṃdramāḥ ‖*) (Śa. Brā. 10-4-1-21)

अर्क (*arka*) is this deity of the sacrifice. The principle Kya, that is, the Soma sacrifice, is its food. The harmony of these two becomes अर्क (*arka*). **NOTE**

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

#### Ṛk 33

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> दि॒व्यः सु॑प॒र्णोऽव॑ चक्षि सोम॒ पिन्वं॒धाराः॒ कर्म॑णा दे॒ववी॑तौ ।  
> एंदो॑ विश क॒लशं॑ सोम॒धानं॒ क्रंद॑न्निहि॒ सूर्य॒स्योप॑ र॒श्मिम् ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> दिव्यः । सुऽपर्णः। अव । चक्षि । सोम । पिन्वन् । धाराः ॥ कर्मणा । देवऽवीतौ ।  
> आ । इंदो इति । विश । कलशम् ॥ सोमऽधानम् । क्रंदन् । इहि । सूर्यस्य । उप । रश्मिम् ॥ ३३ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम दिव्यो दिविभवः सुपर्णः सुपतनस्त्वं अवचक्षि अवस्तात् पश्य च । चष्टेर्लटिसिपिव्यत्ययेन परस्मैपदं । किं कुर्वन् देववीतौ देवानां हविर्भक्षणस्थानेयज्ञे कर्मणा धाराः पिन्वन् क्षरन् । किंच हे इंदो सोमधानं कलशं आविश क्रंदन्शब्दायमानस्त्वं सूर्यस्य प्रेरकस्यादित्यस्य रश्मिं कांतिमुपोहि उपगच्छ ॥ ३३ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, celestial, born in heaven, well-winged, good in flight, you look down from below and see. What do you do? In the devavīti, the place where the gods eat the oblation, the sacrifice, you cause the streams to flow by your act. And further, O Indu, enter the vessel that holds Soma; crying out, sounding, approach the ray, the radiance, of Sūrya, the impelling Āditya.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O divine Soma
- दिव्यः (*divyaḥ*)—born in the world of heaven
- सुपर्णः (*suparṇaḥ*)—you who have an excellent course
- देववीतौ (*devavītau*)—in the sacrifice
- कर्मणा (*karmaṇā*)—by your good act

### Printed p. 811

- धाराः (*dhārāḥ*)—the streams of juice
- पिन्वन् (*pinvan*)—causing to flow
- अव चक्षि (*ava cakṣi*)—look down towards us
- सोमुधानं (*somudhānaṃ*)—that holds Soma **NOTE**
- कलशं (*kalaśaṃ*)—into the vessel
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter
- क्रंदन् (*kraṃdan*)—crying out
- सूर्यस्य (*sūryasya*)—of the Sun
- रश्मिं (*raśmiṃ*)—the ray
- उपेहि (*upehi*)—join

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, you who are born in heaven and have an excellent course, causing the streams of juice to flow in the sacrifice by your good act, look down towards us. Enter the vessel that holds the Soma juice. Crying out, join the ray of the Sun and become one with it.

##### English translation
Soma, who are celestial, well-winged, you look down from heaven pouring forth your streams by the pious rite at the sacrifice ; Indu,enter into pitcher the receptacle of the Soma crying aloud approach the sun's rays.

#### Ṛk 34

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ति॒स्रो वाच॑ ईरयति॒ प्र वह्नि॑रृ॒तस्य॑ धी॒तिं ब्रह्म॑णो मनी॒षाम् ।  
> गावो॑ यंति॒ गोप॑तिं पृ॒च्छमा॑नाः॒ सोमं॑ यंति म॒तयो॑ वावशा॒नाः॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> तिस्रः । वाचः। ईरयति । प्र । वह्निः । ऋतस्य । धीतिम् । ब्रह्मणः । मनीषाम् ।  
> गावः । यंति । गोऽपतिम् । पृच्छमानाः । सोमम् । यंति । मतयः। वावशानाः ॥ ३४ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> वह्रिर्वोढा यजमानः [१]तिस्रोवाचः ऋग्यजुःसामात्मिकाः स्तुतीः प्रेरयति । तथा ऋतस्य यज्ञस्य धीतिं धारयित्रीं ब्रह्मणः परिवृढस्य सोमस्य मनीषां मनसईशित्रीं कल्याणीं वाचं च प्रेरयति । किंच गोपतिं वृषभं यथा गावोभिगच्छंति तद्वत् । गवां स्वामिनं सोमं गावः पृच्छमानाः पृच्छंत्यः सत्यो यंति स्वपयसामिश्रयितुमभिगच्छंति । तथा वावशानाः कामयमानाः मतयः स्तोतारः सोमं यंति स्तोतुमभिगच्छंति ॥ ३४ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The bearer, that is, the sacrificer, sends forth the three speeches, the praises consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman. Likewise he sends forth the upholding of the sacrifice (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)) and the मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*) of Brahma, that is, of Soma who is the all-surrounding one: the speech that rules the mind, the auspicious one. And further, as cows go towards the lord of cows, a bull, so the cows, asking, go to Soma, the lord of cows, in order to mingle with their own milk. Likewise the desiring ones (मतयः (*matayaḥ*)), the praisers, go to Soma, go in order to praise.

### Printed p. 812

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- वह्निः (*vahniḥ*)—the sacrificer, the conductor of the sacrifice
- तिस्रः वाचः (*tisraḥ vācaḥ*)—the speeches of three kinds, consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman
- प्रेरयति (*prerayati*)—he recites
- ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)—for the sacrifice
- धीतिं (*dhītiṃ*)—that sustains
- ब्रह्मणः (*brahmaṇaḥ*)—addressed to Soma
- मनीषां (*manīṣāṃ*)—he recites the praise
- गाव (*gāva*)—cows furnished with milk **NOTE**
- गोपतिं (*gopatiṃ*)—the place where Soma, the lord of the cows, is
- पृच्छमानः (*pṛcchamānaḥ*)—asking **NOTE**
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—they approach Soma (as cows seek the bull, the cows seek Soma)
- वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)—those who desired Soma
- मतयः (*matayaḥ*)—the praisers
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- यंति (*yaṃti*)—they approach

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The sacrificer, the conductor of the sacrifice, recites the speeches of three kinds, consisting of Ṛk, Yajus and Sāman. He also recites the praise addressed to Soma, who sustains the sacrifice. As cows furnished with milk seek the bull who is their lord, so they seek Soma, the lord of the cows. The praisers who desire Soma approach Soma.

##### English translation
The bearer (of the oblation) utters the three praises, the thought of Bramhma that sustains the sacrifice ; the cows come to the cowherd asking (to be milked), the praisers proceed to the Soma with eagerness.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

For this Ṛk there are two kinds of explanation in the Nirukta Pariśiṣṭa: one is adhidaivika, the other ādhyātmika. The meaning concerning the deity (adhidaivata) has been explained in Sāyaṇa's commentary. But the explanation given by Yāska is somewhat different. Therefore we indicate here the two kinds of explanation that Yāska has given.

In the adhidaivata view—

वह्निरादित्यो भवति स तिस्रो वाचः प्रेरयत्यृचो यजूंषि सामान्यृतस्यादित्यस्य कर्माणि ब्रह्मणो मतान्येष एव्यैतत् सर्वमक्षरमित्यधिदैवतं ॥ (*vahnirādityo bhavati sa tisro vācaḥ prerayatyṛco yajūṃṣi sāmānyṛtasyādityasya karmāṇi brahmaṇo matānyeṣa evyaitat sarvamakṣaramityadhidaivataṃ ‖*) (Ni. Pariśiṣṭa. 14–19) **NOTE**

Here वह्नि (*vahni*) means Āditya. That Āditya impels the sentences of the three Vedas, the Ṛgveda, Yajurveda and Sāmaveda, that is, the mantras, among the praisers.

### Printed p. 813

The actions of this truth-natured Āditya are in accordance with the rule of Brahma. As the Śruti sentence असौ वा आदित्यो ब्रह्मेति (*asau vā ādityo brahmeti*) says, this Āditya is Parabrahman. According to his rule the actions of all beings go on.

In the ādhyātmika view—

वह्निरात्मा भवति स तिस्रो वाच ईरयति प्रेरयति विद्यामतिबुद्धिमतामृतस्यात्मनः कर्माणि ब्रह्मणो मतान्ययमेव्यैतत् सर्वमनुभवत्यात्मगतिमाचष्टे ॥ (*vahnirātmā bhavati sa tisro vāca īrayati prerayati vidyāmatibuddhimatāmṛtasyātmanaḥ karmāṇi brahmaṇo matānyayamevyaitat sarvamanubhavatyātmagatimācaṣṭe ‖*) (Ni. 14–14) **NOTE**

Here वह्निः (*vahniḥ*) means the Self. That Self, dwelling in the body, is the impeller of the three kinds of activity called तिस्रः वाचः (*tisraḥ vācaḥ*), that is, vidyā, mati and buddhi, and he enjoys, according to the rule of Brahma, the fruits and so on of all the actions done by the various beings.

#### Ṛk 35

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> सोमं॒ गावो॑ धे॒नवो॑ वावशा॒नाः सोमं॒ विप्रा॑ म॒तिभिः॑ पृ॒च्छमा॑नाः ।  
> सोमः॑ सु॒तः पू॑यते अ॒ज्यमा॑नः॒ सोमे॑ अ॒र्कास्त्रि॒ष्टुभः॒ सं न॑वंते ॥ ३५ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सोमम् । गावः । धेनवः । वावशानाः । सोमम् । विप्राः । मतिऽभिः । पृच्छमानाः ।  
> सोमः । सुतः । पूयते । अज्यमानः। सोमे । अर्काः । त्रिऽस्तुभः । सम् । नवंते ॥ ३५॥ १७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> धेनवः प्रीणयित्र्योगावः सोमं वावशानाः कामयमाना भवंति विप्रा मेधाविनः स्तोतारः मतिभिः पृच्छमानाः पृच्छंतो भवंति । अज्यमानः गोभिः सिच्यमानः सुतोभिषुतः सोमः ऋत्विग्भिः परिपूयते । तथा त्रिष्टुभः त्रिष्टुब्रूपाः अर्काः अस्माभिः क्रियमाणाः एते मंत्राः सोमे संनवंते संगच्छंते ॥ ३५ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

The milch cows, the gratifying ones, are desirous of Soma; the wise, the intelligent praisers, are asking with their praises. Soma, pressed and being sprinkled with the milk of the cows, is purified all around by the Ṛtviks. Likewise these Ṛks in Triṣṭubh form, which are made by us, these mantras unite in Soma.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*)—yielding gratifying milk
- गावः (*gāvaḥ*)—the cows
- सोमं (*somaṃ*)—Soma
- वावशानाः (*vāvaśānāḥ*)—they wish to partake
- विप्राः (*viprāḥ*)—the wise praisers
- मतिभिः (*matibhiḥ*)—with praises
- सोमं पृच्छमानाः (*somaṃ pṛcchamānāḥ*)—they ask in order to know the place of Soma
- सुतः (*sutaḥ*)—

### Printed p. 814

- pressed out
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- अज्यमानः (*ajyamānaḥ*)—being refined with milk and the like
- पूयते (*pūyate*)—he is purified
- त्रिष्टुभः (*triṣṭubhaḥ*)—composed in the Triṣṭup metres
- अर्काः (*arkāḥ*)—our praises
- सोमे (*some*)—in Soma
- सं नवंते (*saṃ navaṃte*)—they unite and join together

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The cows that give gratifying milk wish to partake of Soma. The wise praisers ask with their praises in order to know the place of Soma. The pressed Soma, refined with milk and the like, is purified. Our praises, composed in the Triṣṭup metres, unite and join together in Soma.

##### English translation
The milch cows (are) longing for the Soma : wise men (are) inquiring for him with praises ; Soma being effused is purified blended (with the milk), our adorations in the Trishtubh metre are united in the Soma.

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

In the Nirukta Pariśiṣṭa two kinds of meaning, the adhidaivata and the ādhyātma, are explained for this Ṛk.

The adhidaivata view—

एत एव सोमं गावो धेनवो रश्मयो वावश्यमानाः (*eta eva somaṃ gāvo dhenavo raśmayo vāvaśyamānāḥ*) … आदित्यं यंत्येवमेव सोमं विप्रा रश्मयो मतिभिः पृच्छमानाः कामयुमाना आदित्यं यंत्येवमेव सोमः सुतः पूयते अज्यमान एतमेवार्काश्च त्रिष्टुभश्च सन्नवंते तत एतस्मान्नादित्य एकं भवंतीत्यधिदैवतं ॥ (*ādityaṃ yaṃtyevameva somaṃ viprā raśmayo matibhiḥ pṛcchamānāḥ kāmayumānā ādityaṃ yaṃtyevameva somaḥ sutaḥ pūyate ajyamāna etamevārkāśca triṣṭubhaśca sannavaṃte tata etasmānnāditya ekaṃ bhavaṃtītyadhidaivataṃ ‖*) **NOTE** (Ni. 14–15) **NOTE**

Here धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) is explained as the rays of the sun. As cows, longing for the sun's rays (that is, the sunshine), leave their cowshed and go to graze in a meadow made pleasant by the sunshine, so the Ṛtvik priests approach Soma with praises and the like and purify him.

The ādhyātma view—

एत एव सोमं गावो धेनव इंद्रियाणि वावश्यमानानि कामयमानान्यात्मानं यंत्येवमेव सोमं विप्रा इंद्रियाणि मतिभिः पृच्छमानानि कामयमानान्यात्मानं यंत्येवमेव सोमः सुतः पूयते आज्यमान इममेवात्मा च सप्त ऋषयश्च सन्नवंते तानीमान्ये तस्मिन्नात्मन्येकं भवंतीत्यात्मगतिमाचष्टे ॥ ( (*eta eva somaṃ gāvo dhenava iṃdriyāṇi vāvaśyamānāni kāmayamānānyātmānaṃ yaṃtyevameva somaṃ viprā iṃdriyāṇi matibhiḥ pṛcchamānāni kāmayamānānyātmānaṃ yaṃtyevameva somaḥ sutaḥ pūyate ājyamāna imamevātmā ca sapta ṛṣayaśca sannavaṃte tānīmānye tasminnātmanyekaṃ bhavaṃtītyātmagatimācaṣṭe ‖ (*) (Ni. 14–15) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 815

Here धेनवः (*dhenavaḥ*) means the senses. As the senses of the body remain near the self in order to gratify it and are engaged each in its own activity, so the seven sages also approach Soma and engage in the work of purification and the like; this is the meaning intended.

#### Ṛk 36

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> ए॒वा नः॑ सोम परिषि॒च्यमा॑न॒ आ प॑वस्व पू॒यमा॑नः स्व॒स्ति ।  
> इंद्र॒मा वि॑श बृह॒ता रवे॑ण व॒र्धया॒ वाचं॑ ज॒नया॒ पुरं॑धिम् ॥ ३६ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> एव । नः । सोम । परिऽसिच्यमानः । आ । पवस्व । पूयमानः । स्वस्ति ।  
> इंद्रम् । आ । विश । बृहता । रवेण । वर्धय । वाचम् । जनय। पुरम्ऽधिम् ॥ ३६ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> हे सोम परिषिच्यमानः परितः पात्रेषु सिच्यमानः पूयमानस्त्वं नोस्माकमेव स्वस्ति अविनाशमापवस्व आप्रापय । किंच बृहता महता रवेण शब्देन सह इंद्रमाविश प्रविश तथा वाचं स्तुतिलक्षणां वर्धय । किंच पुरंधिं बहुधियं प्रज्ञानं जनय अस्मभ्यं उत्पादय । वाक्यभेदादनिघातः ॥ ३६ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

O Soma, being sprinkled all around, that is, poured round into the vessels, and being purified, flow to us alone and bring us welfare, that is, freedom from destruction. Further, enter Indra with a great sound, and increase our speech, which consists of praise. Further, generate for us पुरंधिं (*puraṃdhiṃ*), that is, abundant wisdom, knowledge.

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- सोम (*soma*)—O Soma, divine one
- परिषिच्यमानः (*pariṣicyamānaḥ*)—poured into the vessels
- पूयमानः (*pūyamānaḥ*)—purified
- नः (*naḥ*)—to us
- एव (*eva*)—as desired
- स्वस्ति (*svasti*)—for the accomplishment of welfare
- आ पवस्व (*ā pavasva*)—flow
- बृहता (*bṛhatā*)—abundant
- रवेण (*raveṇa*)—with sound
- इंद्रं (*iṃdraṃ*)—Indra
- आ विश (*ā viśa*)—enter
- वाचं (*vācaṃ*)—our speech in the form of praise
- वर्धय (*vardhaya*)—strengthen
- पुरंधिं (*puraṃdhiṃ*)—abundant wisdom
- जनय (*janaya*)—produce in us

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

O divine Soma, poured into the vessels and purified, flow for us for the accomplishment of the welfare we desire. Enter Indra with abundant sound. Strengthen our speech in the form of praise. Produce in us abundant wisdom.

### Printed p. 816

##### English translation
Thus poured around (into the vessels), Soma, when purified flow for our welfare, enter with a great noise into Indra, foster our pr:aise, generate abundant knowledge in us. **NOTE**

##### विशेषविषयगळु (Special Topics)

पुरंधिं (*puraṃdhiṃ*)—The use of this word occurs in many contexts, so its meaning has to be explained according to each context; this is understood from the words of the Nirukta author himself.

ते हि यज्ञेषु यज्ञियास ऊमाः (*te hi yajñeṣu yajñiyāsa ūmāḥ*) … विश्वे अभि संति देवाः (*viśve abhi saṃti devāḥ*) … अध्वर (*adhvara*) … यक्ष्यग्ने श्रुष्टी भगं नासत्या पुरंधिं (*yakṣyagne śruṣṭī bhagaṃ nāsatyā puraṃdhiṃ*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-69-4) **NOTE**

In explaining the meaning of the word पुरंधिं (*puraṃdhiṃ*) in this Ṛk, there (in the Nirukta) it is said:

पुरंधिर्बहुधीस्तत्कः पुरंधिर्भगः पुरस्तात्तस्यान्वादेश इत्येकं । इंद्र इत्य-परं स बहुकर्मतमः पुरां च दारयितृतमः । वरुण इत्यपरं तं प्रज्ञया स्तौति । (*puraṃdhirbahudhīstatkaḥ puraṃdhirbhagaḥ purastāttasyānvādeśa ityekaṃ | iṃdra itya-paraṃ sa bahukarmatamaḥ purāṃ ca dārayitṛtamaḥ | varuṇa ityaparaṃ taṃ prajñayā stauti |*) (Ni. 9-13) **NOTE**

The meaning of the word पुरंधि (*puraṃdhi*) is: one possessed of abundant धी (*dhī*), that is, of intellect. But if the question is who such a one is, then, since in the quoted Ṛk the word भग (*bhaga*) stands before this word, some hold that it is an attribute of it. Others hold that, since the word धी (*dhī*) is also read among the names of actions, पुरंधि (*puraṃdhi*) means one of many kinds of action, or one who splits the cities of enemies, and so it is an attribute of Indra. Still others hold that, as in passages such as इमामू नु कवितमस्य मायां (*imāmū nu kavitamasya māyāṃ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-89-4) **NOTE** the supreme resolve of Varuṇa is praised, so in this Ṛk quoted by the Nirukta author also, it may be a synonym of Varuṇa, describing his wisdom. In this way the Nirukta author has stated the differences of opinion. By some further examples the Nirukta author has shown that the word is used both when showing the abundance of the generosity that the gods display towards sacrificers, and when indicating the abundance of the oblations and the like that the sacrificers offer to the gods.

आदाय श्येनो अभरत्सोमं सहस्रं सवा अयुतं च साकं । अत्रा पुरंधिरजहादरातीर्मदे सोमस्य मूरा अमूरः ॥ (*ādāya śyeno abharatsomaṃ sahasraṃ savā ayutaṃ ca sākaṃ | atrā puraṃdhirajahādarātīrmade somasya mūrā amūraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 4-26-6) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 817

For the word in this Ṛk, Durgācārya (Ni. 11-2) **NOTE** explains पुरंधिः बहुधनस्य दाता (*puraṃdhiḥ bahudhanasya dātā*), that is, one who gives wealth in great abundance, and Sāyaṇa explains बहुकर्मा (*bahukarmā*). Here this word is an attribute of Indra. The purport is that he is generous.

नृधूतो अद्रिषुतो बर्हिषि प्रियः पतिर्गवां प्रदिव इंदुर्ऋत्वियः । पुरंधिवान्मनुषो यज्ञसाधनः शुचिर्धिया पवते सोमु इंद्र ते ॥ (*nṛdhūto adriṣuto barhiṣi priyaḥ patirgavāṃ pradiva iṃdurṛtviyaḥ | puraṃdhivānmanuṣo yajñasādhanaḥ śucirdhiyā pavate somu iṃdra te ‖*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 9-22-4) **NOTE**

In this Ṛk the words बहुकर्मवान् मनुष्यः (*bahukarmavān manuṣyaḥ*) are explained as: a man of many kinds of actions for the gratification of the gods, that is, a man who performs actions. And further—

पावीरवी तन्यतुरेकपादजो दिवो धर्ता सिंधुरापः समुद्रियः । विश्वे देवासः शृणवन् वचांसि मे सरस्वती सह धीभिः पुरंध्या ॥ (*pāvīravī tanyaturekapādajo divo dhartā siṃdhurāpaḥ samudriyaḥ | viśve devāsaḥ śṛṇavan vacāṃsi me sarasvatī saha dhībhiḥ puraṃdhyā ‖*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-65-13) **NOTE**

In this Ṛk the Nirukta author (Ni. 12-30) **NOTE** explains this word as पुरंध्या स्तुत्या प्रयुक्तानि (*puraṃdhyā stutyā prayuktāni*), that is, वचांसि (*vacāṃsi*), speeches joined with many kinds of praises. Sāyaṇa has said बहुविधया प्रज्ञया सहिता सरस्वती (*bahuvidhayā prajñayā sahitā sarasvatī*), that is, Sarasvatī endowed with manifold wisdom. But from the explanation made by Durgācārya (Ni. 12-30) **NOTE**, बहुधात्र्या, माध्यमिका वाचा (*bahudhātryā, mādhyamikā vācā*), it is understood that the word पुरंधि (*puraṃdhi*) indicates a particular deity similar to Sarasvatī. Likewise—

शं नो भगः शमु नः शंसो अस्तु शं नः पुरंधिः शमु संतु रायः । शं नः सत्यस्य सुयमस्य शंसः शं नो अर्यमा पुरुजातो अस्तु ॥ (*śaṃ no bhagaḥ śamu naḥ śaṃso astu śaṃ naḥ puraṃdhiḥ śamu saṃtu rāyaḥ | śaṃ naḥ satyasya suyamasya śaṃsaḥ śaṃ no aryamā purujāto astu ‖*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-35-2) **NOTE**

In Ṛks such as this it is understood that पुरंधि (*puraṃdhi*) is itself a separate deity. Sāyaṇa also has not made it an attribute of the words भग (*bhaga*) and the like in this Ṛk. And further,

देवो भगः सविता रायो अंश इंद्रो वृत्रस्य संजितो धनानां । ऋभुक्षा वाज उत वा पुरंधिरवंतु नो अमृतासस्तुरासः ॥ (*devo bhagaḥ savitā rāyo aṃśa iṃdro vṛtrasya saṃjito dhanānāṃ | ṛbhukṣā vāja uta vā puraṃdhiravaṃtu no amṛtāsasturāsaḥ ‖*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 5-42-5) **NOTE**

there this word is a synonym of विघ्न (*vighna*) **NOTE**.

पुराणी देवि युवतिः पुरंधिरसु व्रतं विश्ववारे (*purāṇī devi yuvatiḥ puraṃdhirasu vrataṃ viśvavāre*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-61-1) **NOTE**

### Printed p. 818

In places such as these it is an attribute of Ushas. The meaning is: one who has many praises. Likewise in many places this word is used of the wife and of ordinary women, and gives the meaning of women who are fit to obtain offspring, not barren, and well nourished **NOTE**.

अग्निः सप्तिं वाजंभरं ददात्यग्निर्वीरं श्रुत्य्यर कर्मनिष्ठां । (*agniḥ saptiṃ vājaṃbharaṃ dadātyagnirvīraṃ śrutyyara karmaniṣṭhāṃ |*) … अग्नी रोदसी (*agnī rodasī*) … वीरकुक्षिं पुरंधिं (*vīrakukṣiṃ puraṃdhiṃ*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-80-1) **NOTE**

In Ṛks such as this (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-166-12; 1-117-19) **NOTE** it is understood to mean a wife capable of bearing children, and—

प्र बोधया पुरंधिं जार आ ससतीमिव । प्र चक्षय रोदसी वासयोषसः श्रवसे वासयोषसः ॥ (*pra bodhayā puraṃdhiṃ jāra ā sasatīmiva | pra cakṣaya rodasī vāsayoṣasaḥ śravase vāsayoṣasaḥ ‖*) **GLOSS** (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-134-3) **NOTE**

in Ṛks such as this it is understood to mean a woman fit for enjoyment. Thus Sāyaṇa's commentary has shown that it is a qualifying word describing many kinds of qualities.

#### Ṛk 37

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> आ जागृ॑वि॒र्विप्र॑ ऋ॒ता म॑ती॒नां सोमः॑ पुना॒नो अ॑सदच्च॒मूषु॑ ।  
> सपं॑ति॒ यं मि॑थु॒नासो॒ निका॑मा अध्व॒र्यवो॑ रथि॒रासः॑ सु॒हस्ताः॑ ॥ ३७ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> आ। जागृविः । विप्रः । ऋता । मतीनाम् । सोमः । पुनानः। असदत् । चमूषु ।  
> सपंति । यम् । मिथुनासः । निऽकामाः ॥ अध्वर्यवः । रथिरासः । सुऽहस्ताः ॥ ३७ ॥

##### ॥ सायणभाष्यम् ॥ (Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya)

> जागृविर्जागरणशीलः ऋता सुपांसुलुगिति षठ्या आकारः । ऋतानां सत्यानां मतीनां स्तुतीनां विप्रो ज्ञाता स सोमः पुनानः पूयमानः सन् चमूषु चमसेष्वासदत् आसीदति । मिथुनासः परस्परं संगताः निकामाः नितरां कामयमानाः रथिरासः यज्ञस्य नेतारः सुहस्ताः कल्याणपाणयः अध्वर्यवः पवित्रे यं सोमं सपंति स्पृशंति । षष समवाये। सपतिःस्पृशतिकर्मेति नैरुक्ताः ॥ ३७ ॥

##### Gist of the bhāṣya

जागृविः (*jāgṛviḥ*) means of wakeful nature. ऋता (*ṛtā*) is the genitive plural, with the substitution of ā. Soma, who is the विप्रः (*vipraḥ*), the knower, of the true (ऋतानां (*ṛtānāṃ*)) praises (मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)), being purified, sits down in the चमूषु (*camūṣu*), that is, in the cups. The Adhvaryus, who are मिथुनासः (*mithunāsaḥ*), united with one another, निकामाः (*nikāmāḥ*), intensely desiring, रथिरासः (*rathirāsaḥ*), leaders of the sacrifice, and सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*), of auspicious hands, touch (सपंति (*sapaṃti*), स्पृशंति (*spṛśaṃti*)) that Soma at the filter. The word सपतिः (*sapatiḥ*) is a word for the action of touching, say the followers of the Nirukta.

### Printed p. 819

##### प्रतिपदार्थ (Pratipadārtha)

- मिथुनासः (*mithunāsaḥ*)—those who have gathered together for the sacrificial work
- निकामाः (*nikāmāḥ*)—those who are devoted to the work
- रथिरासः (*rathirāsaḥ*)—leaders of the sacrifice
- सुहस्ताः (*suhastāḥ*)—those who have excellent hands
- अध्वर्यवः (*adhvaryavaḥ*)—the Adhvaryus
- यं (*yaṃ*)—which Soma
- सपंति (*sapaṃti*)—whom they touch
- जागृविः (*jāgṛviḥ*)—the one who is vigilant
- ऋता (*ṛtā*)—of truth
- मतीनां (*matīnāṃ*)—of praises
- विप्रः (*vipraḥ*)—the knower (the one who knows all that)
- सोमः (*somaḥ*)—Soma
- पुनानः (*punānaḥ*)—having obtained purification
- चमूषु (*camūṣu*)—in the Camū vessels
- आ असदत् (*ā asadat*)—he is installed

##### भावार्थ (Bhāvārtha)

The Adhvaryus, who have gathered together for the sacrificial work, who are devoted to the work, leaders of the sacrifice, and have excellent hands, touch Soma. Such a Soma, who is vigilant and knows the truth and the forms of praise **NOTE**, having obtained purification, is installed in the Camū vessels.

##### English translation
The vigilant Soma, the knower of true praises, being purified, has sat down in the vessels—(the Soma) whom the Adhwaryus touch, combined, emulous, leaders of the sacrifice, auspicious-handed.

#### Ṛk 38

##### ॥ संहितापाठः ॥ (Saṃhitā-pāṭha)

> स पु॑ना॒न उप॒ सूरे॒ न धातोभे अ॑प्रा॒ रोद॑सी॒ वि ष आ॑वः ।  
> प्रि॒या चि॒द्यस्य॑ प्रिय॒सास॑ ऊ॒ती स तू धनं॑ का॒रिणे॒ न प्र यं॑सत् ॥ ३८ ॥

##### ॥ पदपाठः ॥ (Pada-pāṭha)

> सः। पुनानः । उप । सूरे । न । धाता । आ । उभे इति । अप्राः । रोदसी इति । वि । सः । आवरित्यावः ।  
> प्रिया । चित् । यस्य । प्रियसासः । ऊती । सः । तु । धनम् । कारिणे । न । प्र ।यंसत् ॥ ३८ ॥
